ftbquests.chapter.act_0.quest149F64C77B5: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Mine iron ore with the stone pickaxe and smelt it.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Four iron and a flower make the </grad><grad from=#F2DDB0 to=#C9A36A f=0.8>Iron Remote</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. That is the Iron Colossus, and he is Act I.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#F2DDB0 to=#B98A4E f=0.6>Ready For Iron</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.act_0.quest19180BF254A: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Four planks. Now you have the big grid and everything else opens up.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.act_0.quest23B5EF52A06: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Flint on top of a stick, right in your inventory grid.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Your first tool. It cuts grass very well!</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.act_0.quest2711F1F4958: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Flint shatters on stone, and there are no wooden tools here. The first stone comes from the </grad><grad from=#F2DDB0 to=#C9A36A f=0.8>loose rocks</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> lying around on the ground and at cave mouths.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Four rocks make one cobblestone, right in your inventory.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.act_0.quest34A86373D67: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Wild life REALLY wants you dead. </grad><grad from=#F2DDB0 to=#C9A36A f=0.8>Some animals attack on sight</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, day or night. Doesn't matter!!</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Don't underestimate them as well, they're genuinely strong.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>Tamed ones and babies leave you alone.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.act_0.quest36A7BD2B303: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Pick up the </grad><grad from=#F2DDB0 to=#C9A36A f=0.8>loose rocks</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> lying around. About 1 in 3 has </grad><grad from=#F2DDB0 to=#C9A36A f=0.8>flint</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> in it. Gravel gives flint now and then too.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Four rocks also make a cobblestone.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.act_0.quest48B8CA04A03: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Twigs lying on the ground give sticks. Leaves work too, about </grad><grad from=#F2DDB0 to=#C9A36A f=0.8>1 in 10</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> drops one.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>Shears and silk touch get you the leaves instead, no sticks.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.act_0.quest4E8D5C99BBD: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>You can't just punch a tree! Your hands will hurt.. Logs need an </grad><grad from=#F2DDB0 to=#C9A36A f=0.8>axe</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, and an axe needs a few things first.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Sticks, flint and some straw..</grad></shadow>
Fine, I will do it properly
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#F2DDB0 to=#B98A4E f=0.6>Sticks and Stones</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.act_0.quest56414A0CEFE: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Nights here are very dark. On a </grad><grad from=#F2DDB0 to=#C9A36A f=0.8>new moon</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> you will not even see your own hands, and a cave with no torch is the same.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A torch in your hand lights up around you as you walk. Carry one.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>If you notice a faint green haze deep underground its a </grad><grad from=#F2DDB0 to=#C9A36A f=0.8>gas!</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. if you are careless with a torch, you could blow yourself up.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Mining under a bare stone ceiling can bring it down on you as well. While mining make sure to be careful or build something above.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>Hanging dripstones might snap off on people who stand under it. Mining makes noise, and things down there definitely hears it.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.act_0.quest58A8B833CC2: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Put a log and your </grad><grad from=#F2DDB0 to=#C9A36A f=0.8>axe</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> in the crafting grid. You get planks and the axe comes back.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A flint or stone axe gives </grad><grad from=#F2DDB0 to=#C9A36A f=0.8>2</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> planks a log. Iron or better gives the full </grad><grad from=#F2DDB0 to=#C9A36A f=0.8>4</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>Chopping usually costs a point of durability. About 3 times in 10 it costs nothing.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.act_0.quest5E0CBCA4368: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Three wool and three planks. Sleep through the night and set your spawn.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>Some zombies and skeletons do not burn in the sun anymore. Morning is not a safe word.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.act_0.quest681BE166510: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Hold the knife and cut grass. About </grad><grad from=#F2DDB0 to=#C9A36A f=0.8>1 in 5</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> gives you </grad><grad from=#F2DDB0 to=#C9A36A f=0.8>straw</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>That is what holds a flint head on a handle.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.act_0.quest69393D6A8FA: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Three cobblestone and two sticks. Planks make sticks now, so no more leaf hunting.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.act_0.quest6F7D4527DAE: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Two flint on top, a stick and a straw below. Fits in your inventory grid.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Now trees are breakable!</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.act_0.questB3FFAF1EE97: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Eight cobblestone. Cook your food, smelt your ore.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Burn a log in it and you get </grad><grad from=#F2DDB0 to=#C9A36A f=0.8>charcoal</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> if you cannot find coal.</grad></shadow>

ftbquests.chapter.act_1.quest17AEDC589AE: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Press </grad><grad from=#F4EEE2 to=#BFB3A0 f=0.8>F</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> just before a hit lands. Time it right and the hit does nothing.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>An attack that glows </grad><grad from=#CFDDEE to=#7C9CC4 f=0.8>blue</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> cannot be dodged. Parry it or eat it.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Pressing parry with nothing coming locks it for a moment, so do not spam it. Every parry you land is counted, and the </grad><grad from=#FFE1A0 to=#E8A22E f=0.8>Study Lectern</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> turns that count into a better parry later.</grad></shadow>

ftbquests.chapter.act_1.quest467CA26A33A: ## <grad from=#B0A28C to=#F8F3E9 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>One act per boss</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Your first boss is </grad><grad from=#F4EEE2 to=#BFB3A0 f=0.8>The Iron Colossus</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. Four iron ingots and a flower make the </grad><grad from=#F4EEE2 to=#BFB3A0 f=0.8>Iron Remote</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> that summons him.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Every boss you kill opens the next part of the pack: better gear, plus new machines, spell books and altars.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Each act shows what is open right now. </grad><grad from=#F4EEE2 to=#BFB3A0 f=0.8>Tech</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> on the left, </grad><grad from=#F4EEE2 to=#BFB3A0 f=0.8>magic</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> on the right. Pick whatever looks fun, none of it is required.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A locked item has a </grad><grad from=#F4EEE2 to=#BFB3A0 f=0.8>padlock</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> in its corner, and the tooltip names the boss that opens it. Until then you cannot craft, place or use it.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Storage, backpacks and drawers are never locked.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#CFC3AE to=#FBF7F0 f=0.6>How The Path Works</grad></shadow>

&8If‌ you‌ have experience with‌ lucky‌ blocks, you already‌ know‌ these‌ outcomes should‌ not be underestimated!&r

ftbquests.chapter.act_1.quest5D3E8E9BCD0: If‌ you noticed your‌ iron tools‌ aren't working, you have officially hit‌ the first‌ major progression lock.
To‌ unlock‌ the ability‌ to‌ use iron equipment, you must‌ summon‌ and defeat

As‌ the‌ leader of‌ the‌ Iron Golems, this boss‌ emits a passive aura‌ that‌ slows you down‌ when you‌ get close, and‌ his‌ direct‌ hits will‌ slow‌ you even further. Time your‌ strikes carefully, utilize‌ your‌ dodge mechanic, and‌ avoid letting‌ him‌ corner‌ you.

Defeat‌ the‌ bosses‌ in order, and‌ carefully study the mechanics‌ detailed‌ in the upcoming‌ quests to‌ ensure you‌ are‌ ready‌ for the challenge.

ftbquests.chapter.act_1.quest757965585FC: The‌ bosses that lie ahead are‌ significantly tougher‌ than anything you‌ have‌ faced so‌ far. Approaching‌ these fights requires patience, strategy, and‌ careful‌ judgment rather than‌ raw‌ force. Take‌ your time‌ progressing‌ through these encounters, and‌ make sure to read‌ the‌ guidance provided for‌ each one.
ftbquests.chapter.act_1.quest78060F4D605: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Your class has one special move on </grad><grad from=#F4EEE2 to=#BFB3A0 f=0.8>G</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. Some fire once, some last a while, a few are always on. The Classes page lists every one.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Picked a class you do not like? Beating the Iron Colossus hands you a </grad><grad from=#FFE1A0 to=#E8A22E f=0.8>Tome of Rebirth</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. Use it and pick again. More can be crafted from a book, crying obsidian, an ender pearl and a Life Essence.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.act_1.quest782E7BEB412: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>One block, thousands of one item.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.act_1.quest79097B7E3E4: High-tier weapons and armor‌ are‌ locked behind specific‌ boss milestones. This‌ questline will‌ guide‌ you‌ through the progression‌ system‌ so you‌ can‌ unlock‌ better equipment‌ tiers.
The Armageddon mod‌ completely overhauls‌ vanilla progression, introducing‌ custom‌ mechanics‌ and unique‌ tiers of‌ ores to discover‌ as you‌ advance.
Every boss features unique combat‌ gimmicks, meaning &nproper preparation&r‌ is vital before‌ jumping‌ into the‌ fight. Take‌ your time, gear up, and don't‌ rush‌ in unprepared.
ftbquests.chapter.act_1.questD8491B5077B: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Waterwheels, belts, presses and mixers. The brass half opens after the Iron Colossus.</grad></shadow>

ftbquests.chapter.act_7.quest41964C08E1E: Additionally, the &eIncarceration&r‌ status‌ effect is incredibly effective‌ here for‌ locking‌ him in‌ place. Look into‌ utilizing‌ a‌ specific &ering&r or &epotion‌ effect&r capable of applying‌ this‌ condition to completely‌ control his‌ movement.
Like‌ every other major‌ encounter, your next‌ boss fight‌ requires‌ strategy‌ over mindless‌ left-clicking. Unless, of‌ course, you are completely overprepared.
Here‌ are the‌ essential‌ mechanics and‌ strategies you‌ need‌ to‌ know before‌ engaging him:
Vaedric possesses the‌ dangerous &bReprint&r‌ trait. This means he‌ will automatically‌ copy the‌ exact‌ enchantments‌ currently active on‌ your‌ equipped gear.
&8(For‌ a‌ complete‌ breakdown of‌ how this mechanic‌ scales, check the‌ L2 Hostility -> Legendary‌ Traits‌ questline).&r

Vaedric utilizes‌ a powerful magic‌ pull to‌ drag you into danger. Utilizing the &eInsulator&r‌ enchantment on‌ your gear can‌ block‌ this pulling‌ effect‌ entirely, allowing you to maintain‌ your‌ spacing.
If you prefer‌ to‌ freestyle‌ the encounter, you‌ can‌ opt out of‌ the enchantment and instead‌ use‌ his pulling mechanic‌ to your‌ advantage to‌ rapidly‌ close‌ the distance.

ftbquests.chapter.act_7.quest4E97AB0CAB1: Vaedric‌ was once a‌ lone traveler‌ of the‌ End‌ dimension. His‌ journey met a‌ dark‌ end, and he‌ now‌ wields‌ the volatile‌ power of the‌ Void itself.

This‌ power allows‌ him‌ to‌ bring forth &nsummons&r‌ that fight‌ by his side. Exercise‌ extreme caution‌ during the battle, as both Vaedric‌ and his‌ minions have the‌ ability‌ to &npull&r you‌ directly‌ into their attack range.
Avoid relying‌ on‌ damage-over-time‌ effects against‌ this‌ boss. He is capable‌ of completely slipping away‌ from‌ or neutralizing most‌ status-based damage.
Defeating‌ him removes‌ the‌ next‌ major progression‌ lock, granting‌ full access to powerful &bVoiderite&r‌ tier items.
&e&nNote:&r‌ Vaedric‌ must be‌ summoned on‌ the‌ Outer‌ End Islands.

ftbquests.chapter.act_8.quest2FC648D9011: This‌ monster‌ forces you into a‌ state‌ of &6constant hunger&r, rapidly draining‌ your‌ food‌ bar throughout‌ the‌ fight.

Be‌ warned that this‌ foe becomes‌ completely immortal‌ for‌ a‌ short duration‌ during its‌ second phase. You will‌ need to‌ play defensively and wait for‌ the status‌ to expire before‌ resuming‌ your assault.
However, if‌ your‌ setup utilizes a &bSoul Flame‌ Blade&r, &bIce‌ Blade&r, or &bSharp Blade&r, your attacks‌ can‌ actually‌ bypass this‌ immortality‌ phase entirely.
&8From this‌ point forward, the hand-holding is‌ over. It‌ is time to‌ optimize your‌ own custom‌ build‌ for‌ what lies‌ ahead.&r

ftbquests.chapter.act_8.quest5C70A89677B: Before you can‌ craft Ankh's‌ Tablet, you must‌ first‌ acquire‌ the Tinkerer's‌ Accessory Template.
To‌ create it, you need‌ to harvest‌ three unique types of &nSpirits&r dropped‌ by vanilla‌ mobs: &cDespair, Dread, and Chaos&r.
Note that‌ different‌ mobs (such as‌ Zombies, Slimes, and‌ Skeletons) drop different spirit types.
Once‌ you‌ have gathered the‌ spirits, complete‌ the‌ crafting process:
&b-&r‌ Utilize‌ the collection of‌ Spirits to craft a‌ Calamitous‌ Core.
&b-&r Combine the‌ Calamitous Core‌ with Khyros's‌ Goldened‌ Tear‌ to successfully‌ create‌ the &dAccessory Template&r.

ftbquests.chapter.advanced_progression.q: # <grad from=#E24B4B to=#FFB4B4 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Archmage Gundalf</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The biological father‌ of‌ the two brats‌ you just‌ turned into‌ loot. Unlike‌ his‌ children he‌ is‌ actually wise, considerably stronger, and has‌ a much‌ better‌ beard.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>His life‌ was already‌ pretty‌ miserable, and‌ the only‌ two things he gave‌ a‌ damn about were‌ taken by‌ YOU. Sure, they were‌ annoying. They‌ were‌ still his damn‌ kids, you‌ monster.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>He is‌ mourning‌ the‌ only way‌ an archmage knows‌ how, which is‌ by being </grad><grad from=#E24B4B to=#FFB4B4 f=0.8>really, really‌ angry</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and‌ making‌ it your‌ problem.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#E24B4B to=#FFB4B4 f=0.8>2000 health</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, and‌ he brings Gatmancers‌ with him.</grad></shadow>
{image:customtextures:textures/gundalf_image.png width:100 height:125 align:center}
<typewriter><grad from=#E24B4B to=#E24B4B>You‌ killed his kids</grad>
&cKill&r Archmage Gunddalf
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#E24B4B to=#FFB4B4 f=0.6>Archmage Gundalf</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>There is no‌ clever trick. You‌ fight‌ a Warden‌ and you‌ win.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>It‌ goes‌ into the </grad><grad from=#7B4BE2 to=#C9B0FF f=0.8>Antimatter‌ Rifle</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, the </grad><grad from=#7B4BE2 to=#C9B0FF f=0.8>Deepward Mask</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and the </grad><grad from=#7B4BE2 to=#C9B0FF f=0.8>Soul Whip</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#7B4BE2 to=#7B4BE2>Kill‌ a‌ Warden. That is the‌ whole method.</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#7B4BE2 to=#C9B0FF f=0.6>Warden Soul</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Dimlite‌ ore‌ sits in‌ a‌ uniform pattern across‌ the overworld between </grad><grad from=#2FB8B0 to=#A8F0EA f=0.8>Y -44</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and </grad><grad from=#2FB8B0 to=#A8F0EA f=0.8>Y -64</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. Mine the‌ untapped‌ dimlite, then combine it‌ with </grad><grad from=#2FB8B0 to=#A8F0EA f=0.8>echo shards</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The‌ smithing template‌ drops‌ from </grad><grad from=#2FB8B0 to=#A8F0EA f=0.8>Gob</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, and‌ it upgrades‌ netherite‌ gear.</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#2FB8B0 to=#A8F0EA f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Set bonus</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A full dimlite‌ set blasts‌ a‌ sonic boom‌ that does‌ light‌ damage‌ and shoves‌ you backwards, on an </grad><grad from=#2FB8B0 to=#A8F0EA f=0.8>8 second</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> cooldown. The‌ shortest‌ set cooldown in‌ the mod, and‌ a genuinely‌ good‌ escape.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Its‌ pickaxe is one‌ of‌ the four‌ that‌ can‌ mine iridium, daemonium, brimslag‌ and decayed black‌ matter.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#2FB8B0 to=#2FB8B0>Something echoes‌ within it</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#2FB8B0 to=#A8F0EA f=0.6>Dimlite</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The Trial Guardian's‌ drop. Point‌ it at bedrock‌ and the‌ bedrock decays‌ into‌ something‌ you can‌ actually‌ mine.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>That is how you‌ get </grad><grad from=#7B4BE2 to=#C9B0FF f=0.8>Black Matter</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and </grad><grad from=#7B4BE2 to=#C9B0FF f=0.8>Decayed‌ Bedrock‌ Dust</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, and without‌ either of‌ those‌ the‌ mod stops‌ here.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#7B4BE2 to=#7B4BE2>It makes bedrock rot</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#7B4BE2 to=#C9B0FF f=0.6>Perish Staff</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Every gem‌ makes‌ a‌ full toolset. They‌ sit above diamond‌ and below‌ the netherite‌ tier‌ metals, so‌ they are‌ the bridge‌ you use while‌ you hunt‌ for the real stuff.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Any one‌ of the‌ five counts here.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#C8AE86 to=#C8AE86>Better‌ than‌ diamond, worse than‌ everything‌ after</grad>
Any gem pickaxe
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#C8AE86 to=#EBD9B8 f=0.6>Gem Tools</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>All three final‌ metals want‌ an antiprism, and the‌ wizards‌ are stingy‌ with‌ them.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Good news: a </grad><grad from=#6E77A8 to=#CDD3F0 f=0.8>Prismatic Jewel</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> duplicates them. That‌ is‌ the whole reason‌ the‌ jewel‌ is worth‌ keeping‌ around from the‌ very first hour of‌ the‌ mod.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#6E77A8 to=#6E77A8>The wizards' drop, and the‌ last bottleneck</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#6E77A8 to=#CDD3F0 f=0.6>Antiprism</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#E24B4B to=#FFB4B4 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Super Sniffer</shadow></grad>
[!warning] Build‌ an arena first. Put‌ obsidian blockades‌ up to‌ break‌ his‌ beam attack. His spirit‌ bomb‌ will go‌ through‌ anything‌ you build‌ anyway, so keep moving.

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>He‌ drops the </grad><grad from=#E24B4B to=#FFB4B4 f=0.8>Cosmilite</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and </grad><grad from=#E24B4B to=#FFB4B4 f=0.8>Virentium</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> smithing‌ templates.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>You‌ have‌ always found sniffers </grad><grad from=#E24B4B to=#FFB4B4 f=0.8>WEAK</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and </grad><grad from=#E24B4B to=#FFB4B4 f=0.8>USELESS</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>We‌ can‌ fix that with‌ a little‌ motivational electricity.</grad></shadow>

<typewriter><grad from=#E24B4B to=#E24B4B>Super Saiyan‌ Sniffer!</grad>
Slay &cThe Super Sniffer&r
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#E24B4B to=#FFB4B4 f=0.6>Super Sniffer</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>One of‌ each‌ gem, crushed together. The jewel‌ is the key to‌ most‌ of the good‌ accessories and‌ it is‌ the‌ only‌ thing that‌ duplicates </grad><grad from=#7FD8C8 to=#D6F5EE f=0.8>antiprisms</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> later‌ on, so never throw one‌ away.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Sleeping with‌ a‌ prismatic jewel‌ in your‌ inventory‌ drops‌ a </grad><grad from=#7FD8C8 to=#D6F5EE f=0.8>Music Sheet‌ of Time</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. It does not‌ consume‌ the jewel, so that‌ is a‌ free sheet‌ every‌ night‌ you bother.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#7FD8C8 to=#7FD8C8>All five, squeezed‌ into‌ one</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#7FD8C8 to=#D6F5EE f=0.6>Prismatic Jewel</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Drink‌ it for </grad><grad from=#7FD8C8 to=#D6F5EE f=0.8>Speed‌ II</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. Cheap, common, and fine‌ to‌ burn.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Three‌ fairy bottles‌ of different‌ colours build the </grad><grad from=#7FD8C8 to=#D6F5EE f=0.8>Fairy‌ Staff</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#7FD8C8 to=#7FD8C8>Use it‌ for Speed II</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#7FD8C8 to=#D6F5EE f=0.6>Blue Fairy</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#E24B4B to=#FFB4B4 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>The Virtue</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A biblically‌ accurate angel, and‌ it‌ is very‌ clearly upset‌ that‌ you‌ decided to‌ chuck an unholy lance‌ into‌ its sky.</grad></shadow>
[gap=5]
[gap=5]
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#E24B4B to=#FFB4B4 f=0.8>4000 health</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, the‌ second toughest‌ thing in‌ the‌ mod.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>It‌ drops </grad><grad from=#E24B4B to=#FFB4B4 f=0.8>Angel Feathers</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> for Reverium, and‌ it‌ is a‌ somewhat‌ common‌ source of‌ the </grad><grad from=#E24B4B to=#FFB4B4 f=0.8>Music Sheet of‌ Cleansing</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>
{image:customtextures:textures/virtue_image.png width:100 height:75 align:center}
<typewriter><grad from=#E24B4B to=#E24B4B>Biblically accurate‌ and extremely‌ annoyed</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#E24B4B to=#FFB4B4 f=0.6>Virtue</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Iridium, black matter‌ and </grad><grad from=#3BD8E2 to=#A8F2FF f=0.8>circuit boards</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. Template‌ from the </grad><grad from=#3BD8E2 to=#A8F2FF f=0.8>Trial Guardian</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#3BD8E2 to=#A8F2FF f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Set‌ bonus</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Factory‌ Reset. Clears every‌ status‌ effect you have, good and‌ bad, on‌ a </grad><grad from=#3BD8E2 to=#A8F2FF f=0.8>180 second</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> cooldown. The longest‌ cooldown‌ of‌ the three‌ and‌ the only real‌ answer to a stack‌ of‌ debuffs.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Its pickaxe mines </grad><grad from=#3BD8E2 to=#A8F2FF f=0.8>Profaned‌ Ore</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, and the‌ metal itself‌ is‌ what‌ the </grad><grad from=#3BD8E2 to=#A8F2FF f=0.8>Railgun</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and the </grad><grad from=#3BD8E2 to=#A8F2FF f=0.8>Conductite‌ Laser‌ Rifle</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> are made of.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#3BD8E2 to=#3BD8E2>Harbors the‌ power of‌ electricity</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#3BD8E2 to=#A8F2FF f=0.6>Conductite</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Iridium, black‌ matter‌ and empty‌ essence. Template from the </grad><grad from=#7B4BE2 to=#C9B0FF f=0.8>Trial‌ Guardian</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#7B4BE2 to=#C9B0FF f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Set bonus</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Phasing‌ for </grad><grad from=#7B4BE2 to=#C9B0FF f=0.8>5 seconds</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> on‌ a </grad><grad from=#7B4BE2 to=#C9B0FF f=0.8>60‌ second</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> cooldown. Phasing‌ means invulnerable‌ to everything. Not‌ resistant. Invulnerable.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Its pickaxe mines </grad><grad from=#7B4BE2 to=#C9B0FF f=0.8>Profaned‌ Ore</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#7B4BE2 to=#7B4BE2>Harbors the‌ power of the void</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#7B4BE2 to=#C9B0FF f=0.6>Void Alloy</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Villagers drop‌ them. So‌ do </grad><grad from=#7B4BE2 to=#C9B0FF f=0.8>Hellroks</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, which have </grad><grad from=#7B4BE2 to=#C9B0FF f=0.8>250‌ health</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and‌ are‌ a much‌ less awkward conversation.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Goes‌ into the </grad><grad from=#7B4BE2 to=#C9B0FF f=0.8>Asphodel</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, the </grad><grad from=#7B4BE2 to=#C9B0FF f=0.8>Withered‌ Visage</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and the </grad><grad from=#7B4BE2 to=#C9B0FF f=0.8>Spireguard‌ Mask</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#7B4BE2 to=#7B4BE2>Slay‌ villagers, or‌ farm Hellroks</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#7B4BE2 to=#C9B0FF f=0.6>Spiteful Soul</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Right click and‌ play it‌ through. If‌ the overworld‌ sky is‌ visible‌ the‌ whole time, it‌ sends you back to‌ your‌ spawn point.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>It leaves‌ a tornado‌ behind for </grad><grad from=#9B6BFF to=#DCC9FF f=0.8>15‌ seconds</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, and‌ anything‌ that steps on‌ the‌ tornado goes‌ to‌ your‌ spawn too. Including‌ other players, which is‌ either a‌ rescue or‌ a‌ prank.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#9B6BFF to=#9B6BFF>Play‌ the whole‌ tune under‌ open sky</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#9B6BFF to=#DCC9FF f=0.6>Warp Whistle</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Drink it for </grad><grad from=#7FD8C8 to=#D6F5EE f=0.8>Jump‌ Boost II</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Also‌ one third of‌ the‌ Fairy Staff‌ recipe.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#7FD8C8 to=#7FD8C8>Use‌ it for Jump Boost‌ II</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#7FD8C8 to=#D6F5EE f=0.6>Green Fairy</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Fairies‌ spawn all‌ over‌ the‌ overworld and they‌ are‌ absurdly easy‌ to‌ miss. Right‌ click one‌ holding an </grad><grad from=#7FD8C8 to=#D6F5EE f=0.8>empty bottle</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and‌ it is‌ yours.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Every fairy‌ also‌ drops </grad><grad from=#7FD8C8 to=#D6F5EE f=0.8>Fairy‌ Dust</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, which a‌ surprising number‌ of good items‌ want.</grad></shadow>
[!warning] You can‌ carry more than two fairy‌ bottles, but if‌ you die holding‌ more‌ than two, all‌ but‌ one of them get‌ burned‌ at once. Keep exactly‌ two.
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>Bottling‌ a‌ fairy also‌ has‌ a decent chance‌ of dropping the Music‌ Sheet‌ of Life.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#7FD8C8 to=#7FD8C8>Right click‌ one with‌ an empty‌ bottle</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#7FD8C8 to=#D6F5EE f=0.6>Fairies</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#E24B4B to=#FFB4B4 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>The Trial Guardian</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#E24B4B to=#FFB4B4 f=0.8>3000‌ health</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. The spire‌ is a long‌ dungeon, so‌ go in‌ stocked.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>It‌ drops the </grad><grad from=#E24B4B to=#FFB4B4 f=0.8>Perish Staff</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, which is‌ the‌ single most important‌ item‌ in‌ Terramity, and the </grad><grad from=#E24B4B to=#FFB4B4 f=0.8>Hellspec</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, </grad><grad from=#E24B4B to=#FFB4B4 f=0.8>Void</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and </grad><grad from=#E24B4B to=#FFB4B4 f=0.8>Conductite</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> smithing‌ templates.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A‌ wealthy king‌ once ran‌ cruel‌ trials‌ in his‌ enormous‌ chamber, and his Guardian was‌ famously ruthless‌ with‌ anyone who‌ entered.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Time got‌ the‌ king‌ anyway. The Guardian‌ is still down there, alone, waiting‌ for‌ one more contestant.</grad></shadow>
[gap=5]
[gap=5]
## <grad from=#E24B4B to=#FFB4B4 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Summoning‌ it</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#E24B4B to=#FFB4B4 f=0.8>Trial Spires</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> generate‌ in any‌ ocean. Work‌ your‌ way down to‌ the‌ basement, find the‌ lock, and‌ insert‌ a </grad><grad from=#E24B4B to=#FFB4B4 f=0.8>Spire Key</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. Keys‌ are scattered through‌ the spire‌ itself.</grad></shadow>
[!danger] It is‌ immune‌ to‌ all projectile‌ damage. Every gun‌ you own is‌ decoration for‌ this fight. Bring a melee weapon.
{image:customtextures:textures/trial_guardian_image.png width:100 height:65 align:center}
{image:customtextures:textures/trialspire.png width:250 height:100 align:center}
Trial Spire locator
<typewriter><grad from=#E24B4B to=#E24B4B>Immune‌ to every projectile‌ you own</grad>
Slay &cThe Trial Guardian&r
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#E24B4B to=#FFB4B4 f=0.6>Trial Guardian</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Terramity‌ is full of‌ things‌ that‌ are not‌ gear‌ and not progression‌ and are still worth‌ an‌ afternoon.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Two of these‌ are genuinely‌ required later, so‌ do‌ not‌ skip the‌ whole‌ cluster on sight.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#8FCB3F to=#8FCB3F>The fluids, the‌ blocks and‌ the‌ toys</grad>
Go on then
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#8FCB3F to=#DDF5A8 f=0.6>Odds And Ends</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Three‌ sources, so this‌ is the easy‌ one. </grad><grad from=#7B4BE2 to=#C9B0FF f=0.8>Mausoleums</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> are full‌ of them, </grad><grad from=#7B4BE2 to=#C9B0FF f=0.8>Duskroks</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> drop them at </grad><grad from=#7B4BE2 to=#C9B0FF f=0.8>150 health</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, and‌ so does‌ everything living inside‌ a‌ Trial Spire.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#7B4BE2 to=#7B4BE2>Mausoleums, Duskroks, and‌ the‌ Trial Spire</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#7B4BE2 to=#C9B0FF f=0.6>Lost Soul</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Bedrock‌ black‌ matter ore sits‌ on the‌ Nether roof, blended‌ into‌ the‌ bedrock so well‌ that‌ you will‌ walk‌ over‌ it a‌ hundred times.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Hit it‌ with the </grad><grad from=#7B4BE2 to=#C9B0FF f=0.8>Perish‌ Staff</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> to decay‌ it, then‌ mine‌ the decayed‌ ore with‌ a Terramity pickaxe. Netherite‌ will not‌ do it.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Every alloy from here‌ up needs‌ this.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#7B4BE2 to=#7B4BE2>Harbors the power‌ of ???</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#7B4BE2 to=#C9B0FF f=0.6>Black Matter</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Iridescent‌ shards hide‌ deep underground, anywhere‌ in‌ the‌ overworld. If you‌ have been‌ strip mining for‌ diamonds you‌ have probably walked past a‌ dozen.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Each of‌ the five gems‌ makes‌ a full‌ toolset, a‌ full armour set and‌ a‌ fistful of accessories. They‌ are‌ the‌ cheapest real‌ upgrade‌ in the mod, so‌ grab a stack of‌ every‌ one before you‌ move on.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#7FD8C8 to=#7FD8C8>Harbors‌ the power‌ of‌ light</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#7FD8C8 to=#D6F5EE f=0.6>Iridescent Shard</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Iridium, black matter‌ and‌ chthonic‌ crystals. Template from‌ the </grad><grad from=#E2683B to=#FFC0A8 f=0.8>Trial‌ Guardian</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, applied to iridium gear.</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#E2683B to=#FFC0A8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Set‌ bonus</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Lifesteal for </grad><grad from=#E2683B to=#FFC0A8 f=0.8>25‌ seconds</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> on‌ a </grad><grad from=#E2683B to=#FFC0A8 f=0.8>60 second</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> cooldown. Every‌ hit heals‌ you‌ for‌ part of‌ the damage, up to one‌ heart‌ per swing.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Its pickaxe‌ is one‌ of the‌ three‌ that‌ can mine </grad><grad from=#E2683B to=#FFC0A8 f=0.8>Profaned Ore</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#E2683B to=#E2683B>Harbors‌ the‌ power of‌ hell</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#E2683B to=#FFC0A8 f=0.6>Hellspec Alloy</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Terramity‌ runs‌ on‌ accessories. Rings, charms, talismans, scarves, belts, gauntlets, all of‌ it goes into‌ Curios slots‌ and stacks‌ with‌ whatever‌ armour you‌ happen to‌ be wearing.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>If a‌ fight feels‌ impossible, the answer is usually a‌ better loadout‌ and not a‌ better‌ sword.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The Cardboard‌ Necklace‌ from the first quest‌ is‌ your starter. It is‌ cardboard. Do‌ not‌ get attached.</grad></shadow>
The full accessory catalogue
<typewriter><grad from=#C8AE86 to=#C8AE86>Accessories‌ beat‌ armour more often‌ than you think</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#C8AE86 to=#EBD9B8 f=0.6>Wear Something</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The‌ one soul‌ that matters‌ most. It‌ duplicates </grad><grad from=#C8AE86 to=#EBD9B8 f=0.8>black‌ matter</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and goes‌ into a long list‌ of‌ late crafts.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>The other‌ souls are‌ covered over‌ in‌ the‌ structures chapter.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#C8AE86 to=#C8AE86>Duplicates black‌ matter, which‌ is the‌ whole‌ point</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#C8AE86 to=#EBD9B8 f=0.6>Spectral Soul</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Rubies‌ are‌ all‌ over the‌ Nether. This is‌ the easy one.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Each‌ of the‌ five gems makes a full‌ toolset, a full‌ armour set and‌ a‌ fistful of‌ accessories. They‌ are the cheapest real‌ upgrade‌ in the mod, so‌ grab‌ a‌ stack of‌ every‌ one before you‌ move on.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#E23B3B to=#E23B3B>Harbors the power‌ of‌ fire</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#E23B3B to=#FFB0B0 f=0.6>Ruby</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Any spawner at‌ all, from‌ any mod. Break it‌ and‌ an‌ accursed soul‌ pops‌ out.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>It is the‌ whole spider line in‌ Summonity‌ and the </grad><grad from=#7B4BE2 to=#C9B0FF f=0.8>Necromantic Scroll</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> on‌ top of‌ that, so break‌ every‌ spawner‌ you find.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#7B4BE2 to=#7B4BE2>Break‌ any‌ mob spawner</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#7B4BE2 to=#C9B0FF f=0.6>Accursed Soul</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Passively you gain </grad><grad from=#E24B4B to=#FFB4B4 f=0.8>Hyper‌ Crit</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> on any‌ form of‌ damage. Hyper‌ Crits‌ do </grad><grad from=#E24B4B to=#FFB4B4 f=0.8>2x damage</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> with‌ a‌ base chance of </grad><grad from=#E24B4B to=#FFB4B4 f=0.8>25 percent</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, and‌ unlike every‌ other‌ crit in‌ the mod‌ it‌ does‌ not scale‌ off Luck at all.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The‌ active‌ forces Hyper Crit‌ chance to </grad><grad from=#E24B4B to=#FFB4B4 f=0.8>100‌ percent</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> for </grad><grad from=#E24B4B to=#FFB4B4 f=0.8>10 seconds</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, on‌ a </grad><grad from=#E24B4B to=#FFB4B4 f=0.8>45‌ second</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> cooldown.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#E24B4B to=#E24B4B>Hyper‌ Crits, and they do‌ not‌ care about‌ Luck</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#E24B4B to=#FFB4B4 f=0.6>Ultra Sniffer Fur</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Chthonic‌ crystals‌ come‌ out of </grad><grad from=#E2683B to=#FFC0A8 f=0.8>brimslag</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, which‌ generates anywhere‌ in the Nether‌ that blackstone‌ does. Basalt deltas are thick with‌ it.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Brimslag needs‌ a virentium, cosmilite, dimlite or‌ iridium‌ pickaxe. Anything weaker‌ just‌ bounces off.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>It goes into‌ hellspec‌ alloy and into‌ most‌ of‌ the genuinely‌ powerful‌ Terramity items.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#E2683B to=#E2683B>Dig the‌ purple rock in the‌ basalt‌ deltas</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#E2683B to=#FFC0A8 f=0.6>Chthonic Crystal</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Gnomes wander‌ the‌ world and will‌ trade with‌ you if‌ you‌ right‌ click them‌ holding‌ the right thing.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Hand one‌ a </grad><grad from=#C8AE86 to=#EBD9B8 f=0.8>diamond</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and it‌ gives‌ you its‌ hat.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Hand one‌ any </grad><grad from=#C8AE86 to=#EBD9B8 f=0.8>Terramity‌ boss‌ drop</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and it‌ gives you a random‌ valuable‌ back.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>Their hats are‌ also the‌ summoning item‌ for‌ the‌ first boss, so this‌ is‌ not just‌ a‌ novelty.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#C8AE86 to=#C8AE86>They‌ will take‌ literally anything shiny</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#C8AE86 to=#EBD9B8 f=0.6>Bartering With Gnomes</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Profanum, antiprism‌ and‌ opaline moonstone.</grad></shadow>
[!info] The three‌ final metals‌ have no‌ smithing‌ template. You‌ craft the tools‌ and‌ the armour‌ straight‌ out‌ of the‌ ingots.
## <grad from=#9B6BFF to=#DCC9FF f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Nyxium Knight set‌ bonus</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Casts a‌ ring of‌ fire‌ at‌ your feet‌ that inflicts </grad><grad from=#9B6BFF to=#DCC9FF f=0.8>Shadowflame</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, on‌ a </grad><grad from=#9B6BFF to=#DCC9FF f=0.8>45 second</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> cooldown. The full‌ set also‌ grants immunity to fire and‌ Shadowflame and‌ cuts ability cooldowns‌ by </grad><grad from=#9B6BFF to=#DCC9FF f=0.8>20‌ percent</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#9B6BFF to=#9B6BFF>Harbors the‌ power‌ of the moon</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#9B6BFF to=#DCC9FF f=0.6>Nyxium</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#E24B4B to=#FFB4B4 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Circe‌ and‌ Merlin</shadow></grad>
[!warning] Keep‌ them‌ inside the‌ arena. They‌ break in odd ways‌ if‌ they wander too‌ far.
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Two spoiled brats who‌ are convinced‌ the‌ Nether belongs‌ to them.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Their‌ egos‌ are‌ so far‌ through the roof that‌ they‌ will legit ignore‌ you at‌ first, because they‌ do‌ not‌ think you are‌ worth‌ the effort.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Merlin‌ has </grad><grad from=#E24B4B to=#FFB4B4 f=0.8>600‌ health</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, Circe‌ has </grad><grad from=#E24B4B to=#FFB4B4 f=0.8>900</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. They both‌ summon help, so the‌ fight is‌ much bigger‌ than‌ those‌ numbers look.</grad></shadow>
[gap=5]
[gap=5]
## <grad from=#E24B4B to=#FFB4B4 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Summoning‌ them</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Find the </grad><grad from=#E24B4B to=#FFB4B4 f=0.8>Chthonic‌ Cathedral</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> on the roof‌ of the‌ Nether. There is an offering pedestal‌ inside. Right click‌ it with </grad><grad from=#E24B4B to=#FFB4B4 f=0.8>Occult Fabric</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>
{image:customtextures:textures/cathedral.png width:250 height:100 align:center}
Chthonic Cathedral locator
<typewriter><grad from=#E24B4B to=#E24B4B>Two‌ spoiled‌ brats who‌ think‌ they own the‌ Nether</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#E24B4B to=#FFB4B4 f=0.6>The Shadow Wizards</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Revive‌ with </grad><grad from=#7FD8C8 to=#D6F5EE f=0.8>6‌ hearts</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> when you‌ die, and‌ unlike almost every other‌ revive in‌ the‌ pack you‌ do not‌ have‌ to‌ be holding‌ it.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Fairy fountains are stuffed‌ with‌ them. Otherwise they turn‌ up anywhere‌ in the‌ overworld, rarely.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>They‌ also‌ rarely drop the </grad><grad from=#7FD8C8 to=#D6F5EE f=0.8>Music‌ Sheet‌ of Rejuvenation</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#7FD8C8 to=#7FD8C8>The‌ rarest‌ one, and‌ the only‌ one that matters</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#7FD8C8 to=#D6F5EE f=0.6>Pink Fairy</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Terramity‌ takes Minecraft‌ past netherite and‌ keeps going. New‌ gems, new metals, five bosses, a pile of‌ guns and‌ more accessories than‌ you‌ will ever‌ wear‌ at once.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The whole thing‌ is‌ a ladder. Every metal‌ sits‌ on‌ a rung, and‌ you‌ cannot skip one. Two‌ metals on the same‌ rung‌ are equals, so pick‌ whichever you‌ like the‌ look‌ of.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The‌ tier graph‌ pinned‌ on the right is‌ the mod's‌ own. Higher‌ is better, same‌ height is‌ the‌ same‌ tier.</grad></shadow>
[gap=5]
[gap=5]

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>This chapter holds the‌ metals‌ and the bosses. The‌ rest is‌ split off‌ so‌ it‌ stays readable:</grad></shadow>
Structures
Arsenal
Accessories
Brutality
Lethality
Summonity
<typewriter><grad from=#8FCB3F to=#8FCB3F>Everything above‌ netherite‌ starts here</grad>
Aite
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#8FCB3F to=#DDF5A8 f=0.6>Terramity</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Five kinds‌ of‌ soul, each‌ with its‌ own‌ source, and every one of‌ them feeds‌ something‌ you will‌ want later.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Collect‌ them‌ as‌ you go. Backtracking‌ for souls at the‌ end‌ of the mod‌ is miserable.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#7B4BE2 to=#7B4BE2>They‌ look like‌ junk.. but‌ they‌ are not!</grad>
Noted
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#7B4BE2 to=#C9B0FF f=0.6>Souls</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The red hat‌ is what‌ wakes up the‌ Gold‌ Gnome Statue. You‌ can‌ beg a gnome for‌ one, or‌ you can just‌ buy‌ it‌ here.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#C8AE86 to=#C8AE86>For when‌ the‌ gnomes stop cooperating</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#C8AE86 to=#EBD9B8 f=0.6>Red Gnome Hat Shop</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Profanum, antiprism‌ and angel‌ feathers.</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#F2D98A to=#FFF7DC f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Reverium‌ Paladin‌ set bonus</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Fires a‌ holy‌ beam wherever‌ you‌ are‌ looking. It damages‌ and inflicts </grad><grad from=#F2D98A to=#FFF7DC f=0.8>Vulnerable</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, which is‌ a flat </grad><grad from=#F2D98A to=#FFF7DC f=0.8>1.33x</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> to‌ all damage‌ the‌ target‌ takes. </grad><grad from=#F2D98A to=#FFF7DC f=0.8>30 second</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> cooldown.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Pair‌ the beam‌ with anything that‌ hits hard‌ and watch the numbers get‌ silly.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#F2D98A to=#F2D98A>Harbors the‌ power of the‌ heavens</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#F2D98A to=#FFF7DC f=0.6>Reverium</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>You are not drilling‌ into‌ the moon. You are‌ shooting‌ the‌ moon and‌ catching‌ the bits.</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#9B6BFF to=#DCC9FF f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Using it</shadow></grad>

1. <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Place‌ a </grad><grad from=#9B6BFF to=#DCC9FF f=0.8>battery</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> underneath the cannon. It gets‌ eaten‌ and the cannon‌ charges.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
2. <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Wait until‌ the cannon‌ glows‌ yellow.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]

3. <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Fire‌ it at </grad><grad from=#9B6BFF to=#DCC9FF f=0.8>midnight</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, when‌ the‌ moon is directly overhead. Any‌ other time‌ and‌ nothing happens.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Moonstone‌ rocks rain‌ down. Those‌ become </grad><grad from=#9B6BFF to=#DCC9FF f=0.8>Opaline‌ Moonstone</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, and that‌ becomes Nyxium.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#9B6BFF to=#9B6BFF>Yeah the moon, u‌ heard‌ it right</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#9B6BFF to=#DCC9FF f=0.6>Moondrill Cannon</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Terramity's own‌ cooking, sitting quietly‌ between‌ the guns‌ and the‌ gods.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Worth‌ having‌ a stack‌ before any boss.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#F2D98A to=#F2D98A>Food, but the‌ good‌ kind</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#F2D98A to=#FFF7DC f=0.6>Ambrosia</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A dash on the V‌ key. You teleport‌ a short way‌ in‌ the direction‌ you‌ are looking, and the spot‌ you‌ left explodes a‌ moment‌ later.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Offence‌ and escape‌ in‌ the same button.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#E24B4B to=#E24B4B>Blink‌ forward and leave a‌ bomb‌ behind</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#E24B4B to=#FFB4B4 f=0.6>Ultra Sniffer's Pelt</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Set off‌ a </grad><grad from=#6E77A8 to=#CDD3F0 f=0.8>Black‌ Hole Bomb</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, then throw </grad><grad from=#6E77A8 to=#CDD3F0 f=0.8>Empty‌ Essence</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> into‌ the‌ black hole‌ it‌ leaves behind.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>What comes‌ out is a cracked‌ microcosm, and‌ that is the‌ Exodium ingredient.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#6E77A8 to=#6E77A8>Feed‌ a black‌ hole‌ an‌ empty essence</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#6E77A8 to=#CDD3F0 f=0.6>Cracked Microcosm</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Standing in it </grad><grad from=#E2683B to=#FFC0A8 f=0.8>Hexes</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> you and‌ hurts a‌ lot. Hexed does nothing‌ until‌ it ends, and‌ then‌ it halves your health.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Throwing‌ an‌ unenchanted but enchantable‌ item‌ in‌ gives it‌ Curse‌ of Vanishing.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>You still‌ need it: </grad><grad from=#E2683B to=#FFC0A8 f=0.8>black matter</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> thrown into‌ stygian‌ blood is the‌ only source‌ of </grad><grad from=#E2683B to=#FFC0A8 f=0.8>empty essence</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. The </grad><grad from=#E2683B to=#FFC0A8 f=0.8>Stygian‌ Safety‌ Talisman</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> makes‌ you immune‌ to‌ Hexed, so get one first.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#E2683B to=#E2683B>It‌ hexes you‌ and‌ it is‌ required anyway</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#E2683B to=#FFC0A8 f=0.6>Stygian Blood</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Fire‌ the charged </grad><grad from=#9B6BFF to=#DCC9FF f=0.8>Moondrill‌ Cannon</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> at‌ the‌ moon while‌ it‌ is directly overhead. Moonstone rocks‌ come down. Refine‌ them‌ into opaline‌ moonstone.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>This is‌ the‌ Nyxium‌ ingredient.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#9B6BFF to=#9B6BFF>Shot off‌ the moon at midnight</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#9B6BFF to=#DCC9FF f=0.6>Opaline Moonstone</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Iridium‌ ore‌ is deep‌ in </grad><grad from=#B9C6D2 to=#EFF5FA f=0.8>any</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> dimension, and a‌ normal‌ netherite‌ pickaxe will‌ not touch it. You need‌ a‌ dimlite, cosmilite or virentium‌ pickaxe.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>This is‌ the pinch‌ point‌ of‌ the whole mod. Every‌ alloy‌ above this‌ line‌ is‌ iridium plus‌ something nasty.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#B9C6D2 to=#B9C6D2>Wasn't it‌ white? Or... nevermind, that's Industrial‌ Craft 2</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#B9C6D2 to=#EFF5FA f=0.6>Iridium</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Stellar‌ remnants‌ generate‌ in a‌ uniform pattern through the‌ End‌ between </grad><grad from=#5B6BD8 to=#BEC6F5 f=0.8>Y 50</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and </grad><grad from=#5B6BD8 to=#BEC6F5 f=0.8>Y 0</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. Break‌ them for‌ cosmic scrap, then‌ combine‌ the‌ scrap with </grad><grad from=#5B6BD8 to=#BEC6F5 f=0.8>gold ingots</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The‌ smithing‌ template drops‌ from‌ the </grad><grad from=#5B6BD8 to=#BEC6F5 f=0.8>Super‌ Sniffer</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#5B6BD8 to=#BEC6F5 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Set bonus</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Toggle‌ your own gravity‌ upside down. It‌ is exactly‌ as‌ disorienting‌ as it‌ sounds and‌ it trivialises a‌ lot of‌ vertical terrain.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#5B6BD8 to=#5B6BD8>Calamity reference</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#5B6BD8 to=#BEC6F5 f=0.6>Cosmilite</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Standing‌ in it‌ gives‌ Regeneration. Throwing‌ a cursed‌ item in strips‌ the curse‌ right off.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Ponds‌ of‌ it‌ are rare‌ and deep. Bucket‌ some and keep‌ it.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#7FD8C8 to=#7FD8C8>Regeneration, and it‌ eats curses</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#7FD8C8 to=#D6F5EE f=0.6>Prism Solution</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The‌ metals‌ are done. Everything‌ Terramity actually does‌ with them‌ is somewhere‌ below.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>Big‌ swords. Twenty tiers of‌ one‌ big‌ sword, plus the‌ special‌ ones.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>Whips, minions, and never swinging‌ a sword again.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>Court‌ of‌ Gnomes, Trial Spire, the‌ Chthonic pair, fairies, souls, slot‌ machines and warp‌ pipes.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>Every gun, every‌ ammo type, and the whole Ocarina‌ of Power.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>The‌ rings, charms, talismans and cursed‌ trinkets.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>Rage, seals, anklets, nine‌ schools of‌ magic‌ and a lot of‌ cutlery.</grad></shadow>

# <grad from=#E24B4B to=#FFB4B4 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Gob, The‌ King Of Gnomes</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>He drops the </grad><grad from=#E24B4B to=#FFB4B4 f=0.8>Dimlite</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and </grad><grad from=#E24B4B to=#FFB4B4 f=0.8>Virentium</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> smithing templates, which‌ is the‌ whole reason you‌ are‌ here.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>An ambitious‌ little‌ gnome who never‌ let his‌ height stop‌ him.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>With‌ the‌ help of‌ some‌ very unnatural substances, Gob grew‌ taller and‌ bigger‌ than every‌ other gnome‌ and‌ took‌ the crown‌ by being the loudest‌ thing‌ in the room.</grad></shadow>
[gap=5]
[gap=5]
## <grad from=#E24B4B to=#FFB4B4 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Summoning‌ him</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Find a </grad><grad from=#E24B4B to=#FFB4B4 f=0.8>Court‌ of Gnomes</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, which‌ only‌ generates‌ in dark forests‌ and‌ swamps. There is‌ a‌ Gold‌ Gnome Statue‌ in it. Right click‌ the statue‌ with a </grad><grad from=#E24B4B to=#FFB4B4 f=0.8>Red‌ Gnome‌ Hat</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>He‌ has </grad><grad from=#E24B4B to=#FFB4B4 f=0.8>1350 health</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. Bring‌ diamond or‌ netherite armour and‌ something that‌ hits hard.</grad></shadow>

{image:customtextures:textures/courtgnome.png width:250 height:100 align:center}
{image:customtextures:textures/courtgnome2.png width:250 height:100 align:center}
Court of Gnomes locator
<typewriter><grad from=#E24B4B to=#E24B4B>I really‌ hate‌ these little goblins</grad>
Kill &cGob, King Of The Gnomes
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#E24B4B to=#FFB4B4 f=0.6>Gob, King Of Gnomes</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Stygian‌ blood pools‌ sit in Terramity‌ structures, the Trial‌ Spire included. Toss </grad><grad from=#7B4BE2 to=#C9B0FF f=0.8>black‌ matter</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> into‌ one‌ and it‌ comes back‌ as empty essence.</grad></shadow>
[!warning] Stygian‌ blood hexes‌ you and hurts a lot. It‌ also slaps‌ Curse of Vanishing‌ on‌ anything unenchanted‌ you‌ drop in. The {Stygian Safety Talisman} makes this survivable.

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Empty‌ essence‌ goes into void‌ alloy, and‌ much‌ later it‌ becomes‌ a </grad><grad from=#7B4BE2 to=#C9B0FF f=0.8>Cracked Microcosm</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> when you‌ throw it into a‌ black‌ hole.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#7B4BE2 to=#7B4BE2>Throw black matter‌ into stygian‌ blood</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#7B4BE2 to=#C9B0FF f=0.6>Empty Essence</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Gaianite‌ ore‌ generates‌ in a‌ triangle pattern‌ through lush caves‌ between </grad><grad from=#4FC26A to=#B8F0C6 f=0.8>Y 20</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and </grad><grad from=#4FC26A to=#B8F0C6 f=0.8>Y -64</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. Gaia‌ lilies drop it too if‌ you would‌ rather farm than‌ dig.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Combine‌ gaianite with </grad><grad from=#4FC26A to=#B8F0C6 f=0.8>netherite‌ scrap</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> for‌ the ingot.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Both </grad><grad from=#4FC26A to=#B8F0C6 f=0.8>Gob</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and the </grad><grad from=#4FC26A to=#B8F0C6 f=0.8>Super Sniffer</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> drop‌ its‌ smithing template, so it‌ is‌ the‌ easiest of‌ the‌ three to actually‌ finish.</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#4FC26A to=#B8F0C6 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Set bonus</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Dripleaf Step. The full‌ set‌ drops temporary dripleaf‌ blocks under‌ your feet, which‌ means‌ you‌ can walk‌ on‌ air whenever you feel‌ like it.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#4FC26A to=#4FC26A>Lush‌ caves‌ finally have‌ a purpose</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#4FC26A to=#B8F0C6 f=0.6>Virentium</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#E24B4B to=#FFB4B4 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Ultra‌ Sniffer</shadow></grad>
## <grad from=#E24B4B to=#FFB4B4 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Before you‌ try</shadow></grad>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A‌ flat, solid‌ arena out‌ of obsidian or something‌ equally‌ stubborn.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Pillars and blockades‌ to eat‌ his lasers.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Endgame‌ armour, high‌ mobility‌ accessories, and a weapon‌ you‌ trust.</grad></shadow>
[!danger] He is‌ nigh‌ unkillable‌ and it‌ is genuinely not‌ recommended. If you‌ do it‌ anyway, he‌ drops‌ some of‌ the best‌ gear in the‌ game.
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The hardest‌ thing‌ in Terramity, and it does‌ not‌ sit anywhere in‌ the‌ progression. It‌ sits after‌ it.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#E24B4B to=#FFB4B4 f=0.8>9001‌ health</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. Yes, really.</grad></shadow>
[gap=5]
[gap=5]
## <grad from=#E24B4B to=#FFB4B4 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Summoning him</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Get a </grad><grad from=#E24B4B to=#FFB4B4 f=0.8>Super‌ Sniffer</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> into his </grad><grad from=#E24B4B to=#FFB4B4 f=0.8>second phase</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and down‌ to </grad><grad from=#E24B4B to=#FFB4B4 f=0.8>10‌ percent</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> health, then strike him‌ with lightning‌ again.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Doing that‌ while‌ he‌ is nearly‌ dead‌ and still shooting at‌ you is‌ most‌ of the‌ challenge.</grad></shadow>

ftbquests.chapter.ae2.quest1824ABB8F7FA3: Create Engineering‌ Processors by merging Diamond, Printed Engineering‌ Circuits, and Redstone‌ in the Inscriber. These‌ processors‌ are needed‌ for‌ powering your most advanced‌ AE2‌ machines.
ftbquests.chapter.ae2.quest18F89BE5ADFFC: Use the‌ Network Tool‌ to‌ monitor‌ channel usage‌ and power‌ consumption. Perfect for troubleshooting.
ftbquests.chapter.ae2.quest1B1835BC63E5B: Now that‌ you‌ have‌ crafted your‌ ME‌ Drive, ME Controller, ME Terminal‌ or Crafting Terminal, and Energy‌ Acceptor, it's‌ time to put‌ everything together‌ to build‌ a‌ working‌ AE2 storage‌ system!
-Place the ME Drive‌ and install‌ some‌ storage cells (start‌ with 1k‌ or‌ 4k‌ cells).
-Attach the‌ Energy Acceptor and provide‌ it‌ with power from‌ your energy‌ source to‌ power‌ the‌ network.
-Connect the ME‌ Drive‌ and Energy‌ Acceptor‌ with‌ AE2 cables (Glass, Covered, or‌ Smart).
-Place the ME‌ Controller nearby‌ to manage‌ your‌ network‌ channels.
-Connect the‌ ME Terminal‌ or Crafting Terminal‌ to the‌ network for easy access to‌ stored items.
-Insert‌ storage cells into‌ the‌ ME Drive‌ and‌ start storing your items‌ digitally.
Get‌ Your Digital Storage‌ Up‌ and‌ Running
AE2 Storage Setup: Your First ME Network
ftbquests.chapter.ae2.quest1BB8D4C2ABC37: The covered‌ cable‌ variant‌ offers no‌ gameplay‌ benefits over its‌ Fluix ME Glass Cable‌ counterpart. It‌ can however be‌ used as‌ an alternate‌ aesthetic‌ choice‌ if you‌ prefer‌ the covered look.
Can be‌ colored in‌ the‌ same manner‌ as Fluix‌ ME‌ Glass‌ Cable. Four Fluix‌ ME Covered Cable can‌ be‌ crafted with redstone‌ and glowstone‌ to make‌ Fluix‌ ME‌ Dense Covered Cable.
ftbquests.chapter.ae2.quest1D839C76FD495: Applied‌ Energistics is‌ a huge storage‌ mod that‌ will make you replace tom's‌ simple storage‌ for sure!
You can‌ hold "G" to‌ an item‌ to‌ see what it does. Just‌ like‌ create ponder mechanic :D
&8(If‌ you‌ want to contribute‌ like dex, u can always‌ dm‌ me on discord!)
ftbquests.chapter.ae2.quest1DBBB7D3AC587: With‌ the‌ Engineering Press‌ and‌ Diamonds, create Printed Engineering‌ Circuits in the Inscriber. These‌ are‌ crucial for Engineering‌ Processors and‌ high-level AE2‌ components.
ftbquests.chapter.ae2.quest1F60D6F90DBB1: Other‌ power‌ sources also work‌ with‌ ae2, for‌ example you‌ can‌ use Mekanism windmill‌ to power up your‌ ae2‌ system which i‌ recommend.
ftbquests.chapter.ae2.quest1FE482282D4E3: Create‌ ME‌ Drives and‌ Terminals‌ to start storing items‌ digitally — the‌ core of AE2‌ storage.
The‌ Drive is‌ the &bdevice&r‌ you plug your &bstorage‌ cells&r into in order‌ to‌ use them for &bnetwork‌ storage&r. It has‌ 10 slots‌ which‌ each‌ accept a‌ cell.
If‌ for some reason you‌ want to, you‌ can‌ push and‌ pull the‌ cells‌ from‌ its inventory‌ with any item logistics‌ like‌ hoppers or ae2‌ busses.
It can‌ be rotated‌ with‌ a‌ Certus Quartz Wrench.
Your‌ basic terminal, allowing‌ you‌ to‌ view and‌ access the contents‌ of your &bnetwork's‌ storage&r and‌ request‌ things‌ from your &bautocrafting&r‌ setup.
ftbquests.chapter.ae2.quest2144A344B1769: Create Energy‌ Cells to‌ store‌ power for‌ your network. Dense‌ cells‌ hold‌ more power — perfect‌ for bigger setups.
It works‌ by‌ putting it right‌ next to‌ an Energy‌ Acceptor‌ or‌ connect it via‌ energy‌ cable!
Stores up‌ to‌ 200‌ kAE amount‌ of energy per‌ cell. Multiple can‌ be placed‌ around‌ the‌ Acceptor
ftbquests.chapter.ae2.quest2822F59A793F6: Use your‌ Charger‌ to‌ turn ordinary‌ Certus Quartz‌ into Charged Certus‌ Quartz — a key‌ ingredient for many AE2 recipes.
ftbquests.chapter.ae2.quest2B9672616C93D: Use‌ the Logic‌ Press‌ to craft‌ Logic Processors, designed‌ for‌ basic‌ computations in‌ your ME system. These are‌ the‌ simplest processors you'll‌ use.
ftbquests.chapter.ae2.quest30715AAE9C04F: Make‌ Calculation‌ Processors‌ by combining‌ Pure‌ Certus Quartz Crystal, Printed‌ Calculation Circuits, and Redstone in‌ the‌ Inscriber. Use these for‌ high-level automation, storage‌ cells, and crafting‌ upgrades.
ftbquests.chapter.ae2.quest3162C46FCFC99: The‌ quartz fiber is used to‌ share power‌ between networks, while keeping‌ them‌ separate. This allows‌ you‌ to power subnetworks without‌ needing‌ to put energy‌ acceptors‌ and‌ power cables‌ everywhere.
Can‌ be used to‌ keep cables from connecting, although‌ using‌ cables of different‌ colors or‌ using Cable‌ Achor‌ is‌ cheaper
ftbquests.chapter.ae2.quest33C0FE15CA881: Craft‌ an AE2 wrench‌ to‌ rotate devices, remove‌ cables, and‌ safely dismantle blocks without‌ losing‌ materials. A must-have as‌ your‌ network‌ grows.
ftbquests.chapter.ae2.quest34993A77A7CBB: Craft‌ the Crafting‌ Terminal to craft items anywhere‌ directly from‌ your ME Network.

The‌ Crafting Terminal‌ is‌ similar to a regular‌ terminal, with‌ all the same‌ settings‌ and‌ sections, but with‌ an‌ added crafting grid‌ that will be automatically‌ refilled‌ from &bnetwork storage&r. Be careful‌ when shift-clicking‌ the output!
You‌ should‌ upgrade‌ your terminal‌ into‌ a crafting terminal &l&bASAP&r&r.
ftbquests.chapter.ae2.quest364250500493C: Craft‌ Logic‌ Processors by combining Gold‌ Ingots, Printed Logic‌ Circuits, and‌ Redstone in‌ the Inscriber. Logic‌ Processors‌ are‌ the backbone‌ of basic AE2 machines‌ and‌ automation features.
Simple Automation‌ for Your‌ ME System
ftbquests.chapter.ae2.quest3D27AAE3D52B1: The Inscriber‌ is where AE2‌ magic happens — use‌ it with‌ the‌ presses‌ found from‌ meteorites to‌ craft processors and‌ other important‌ parts. Get started crafting the brains‌ of your‌ network.
Same as the‌ Charger, not‌ required to‌ input‌ power via a special‌ AE2‌ way.
ftbquests.chapter.ae2.quest416F3D8D06837: Charger has‌ multiple uses‌ in the‌ mod, but‌ for‌ now we‌ will‌ use it to make‌ a meteorite‌ compass.
Needs‌ power, but we‌ recently got‌ into‌ the‌ mod.. so we‌ use a &ewooden crank!
Place it‌ on‌ side of a‌ charger and‌ then crank‌ it‌ till‌ it powers up.
&8Wooden‌ cranks‌ will break‌ after‌ some‌ use.
ftbquests.chapter.ae2.quest41BD8ED441485: So, you've started‌ expanding‌ on your network, and‌ you've probably got a‌ handle‌ on resource generation, great, but‌ what next? Setting‌ up auto-crafting‌ is‌ what's‌ next! Auto-crafting is‌ probably‌ one of the most‌ essential parts‌ of‌ the mod‌ and for‌ creating‌ large‌ quantities of‌ items, or any recipe you‌ need.
AE2‌ Auto-crafting can allow‌ you to‌ request items‌ on‌ demand, keep‌ a certain specific‌ amount‌ of item
in‌ stock, automatically‌ craft‌ items and‌ export them
ftbquests.chapter.ae2.quest42E31E44908BD: With‌ the‌ Calculation Press, create‌ Calculation‌ Processors, essential for performing‌ complex calculations and automation‌ tasks‌ in AE2.
ftbquests.chapter.ae2.quest43B937DE1F432: Use‌ the‌ Logic Press and Gold‌ Ingots in‌ the‌ Inscriber to‌ make Printed‌ Logic‌ Circuits. These‌ are key‌ for building Logic Processors‌ and‌ several important AE2‌ parts.
ftbquests.chapter.ae2.quest43E8D547EABE0: &6Quantum Bridges&r‌ offer‌ a solution to‌ long range, interdimensional networks.
For example, creating‌ a‌ link between the‌ Overworld and‌ the Nether‌ systems, you‌ should‌ link two‌ Quantum‌ Bridges.
They transfer only 32‌ channels in‌ total, mostly‌ functions as‌ a wireless‌ Dense‌ Cable.
They‌ are constructed‌ of 8 ME Quantum‌ Ring‌ blocks, surrounding one ME‌ Quantum Link‌ Chamber.
ftbquests.chapter.ae2.quest444A508DA7B4B: This‌ was the most basic‌ way‌ of explaining Aut-Crafting, it‌ has an‌ monstrous amount‌ of‌ complexity‌ behind it.
There‌ are‌ a few tips I‌ can give‌ you‌ so far:
2. I‌ suggest using‌ Acceleration cards on them, to‌ make‌ them work faster.
3. Many‌ of the‌ components in‌ this‌ quest‌ line have an "Extended" variant, they‌ improve‌ on their‌ original's‌ functionality‌ by storing‌ more, moving more, more jobs‌ and etc.
4. When‌ using the‌ pattern‌ terminal‌ to make‌ patterns, there will‌ be 3 buttons:
- The "X" button - simply‌ clears the‌ pattern
- The Ingot Button - enables / disables Substitutions (for recipes‌ that use‌ items like an‌ Ore‌ Hammer)
- The Bucket‌ Button - will‌ enable / disable using just a‌ fluid‌ instead of a‌ bucket‌ or‌ other item‌ like‌ that
ftbquests.chapter.ae2.quest4BE2E14DC30BA: It is‌ very important‌ to read the‌ guide, since this‌ questline is only touching the‌ basic ground‌ of AE2 and‌ its‌ capabilities!
Feedback appreciated‌ via‌ the discord feedback channel! (tag @!dex)
ftbquests.chapter.ae2.quest4D8229386678C: The‌ best‌ way to use‌ P2P, is to use them‌ to‌ create, technically, portable Controller Faces. It‌ is important‌ in creating‌ large‌ networks.
Just‌ put them‌ on‌ each side of a‌ controller and‌ use‌ them for‌ machines.
ftbquests.chapter.ae2.quest4FF1275D6D5F2: Use the‌ Silicon Press‌ to‌ create‌ Silicon Presses needed‌ in‌ processor recipes. This‌ press‌ helps‌ you build‌ electronic parts essential‌ for your‌ machines.
ftbquests.chapter.ae2.quest525845E9EFAC5: Mine‌ Certus Quartz‌ Crystals and‌ Dust‌ from‌ meteorites.
Be careful‌ to‌ protect budding quartz blocks‌ for an‌ endless‌ resource supply.
&eTip: Use‌ cardboard boxes‌ from‌ Mekanism‌ to move‌ easily
You also‌ have‌ to make some‌ Certus Quartz‌ Dust, either by‌ mining‌ again‌ from budding blocks‌ or‌ putting normal‌ Certus‌ Quartz‌ Crystals in‌ an Inscriber.
Certus Quartz‌ Dust can‌ be used‌ for‌ making‌ Pipes, Quartz Glass‌ or smelted‌ into silicon!
ftbquests.chapter.ae2.quest56FC37AEC8ED5: Mostly clear‌ glass‌ made with Certus Quartz‌ Dust. Used to‌ make‌ many AE2‌ machines and‌ items.
ftbquests.chapter.ae2.quest59DDEECB0D3FA: Use the Calculation‌ Press and‌ Pure Certus Quartz Crystal in‌ the Inscriber‌ to make Printed‌ Calculation‌ Circuits. These form‌ the‌ core of Calculation Processors‌ and‌ automation upgrades.
ftbquests.chapter.ae2.quest61041A9BF25A5: Craft the‌ ME‌ Controller — the brain of‌ your ME‌ Network! It manages‌ all‌ connections, controls‌ channel limits, and keeps‌ everything‌ running smoothly. Place‌ it‌ carefully: your‌ network devices‌ connect through it‌ to communicate‌ and function.
- The size of‌ the controller‌ must be‌ within‌ 7x7x7; else‌ it will‌ turn red.
- A‌ controller can have‌ 2 adjacent‌ blocks in at most 1‌ axis; if a‌ block violates this‌ rule, it‌ will disable‌ and‌ turn red.
Now‌ this‌ one‌ is a‌ bit tough, so‌ stay with me.
The‌ controller is‌ the routing hub of a &bME‌ Network&r. Without it, a‌ network is "ad-hoc" and can‌ only‌ have a‌ max‌ of 8 channel-using &bdevices&r total.
It‌ is‌ not possible to‌ have‌ 2‌ controllers in‌ one‌ ME Network.
The‌ controller‌ requires 6 AE/t‌ per controller‌ block to‌ function. Each‌ controller‌ block can‌ store‌ 8000 AE, so larger networks‌ might require‌ additional‌ energy storage.
Multiblock‌ Controllers can‌ be‌ built‌ in a‌ fairly free form.
However, there are‌ a‌ few rules that‌ must be‌ followed:
- All controller‌ blocks‌ on‌ a ME Network‌ must‌ be connected; else‌ the‌ blocks‌ will turn‌ red.
Manage and Expand‌ Your‌ AE2 Network
Heart of the Network: ME Controller
ftbquests.chapter.ae2.quest6252BC9282ACC: Your AE2 network‌ needs power! Build the Energy‌ Acceptor‌ to connect your‌ system to‌ energy sources‌ and‌ keep‌ everything running‌ smoothly.
ftbquests.chapter.ae2.quest65EBEFBFF0138: So far, we have‌ set-up a basic AE2‌ network, maybe‌ not so basic, depends‌ on how‌ you play‌ this‌ mod.

You‌ might realize, by‌ expanding‌ the network, everything is starting‌ to take‌ maybe‌ a little‌ too much‌ channels‌ on‌ the cables? Do‌ not worry! AE2 has a‌ few‌ solutions for this‌ in the‌ form of‌ P2P‌ and‌ Quantum Bridges.

Point to‌ Point‌ tunnels, or‌ P2P Tunnels, act‌ as a way‌ to move‌ a lot‌ of‌ things‌ throughout your‌ network, without interacting‌ with the network‌ directly. That's kind‌ of confusing, so imagine P2P Tunnels‌ as a‌ Portal, connecting two location‌ through‌ the use‌ of‌ Fluix Cabels.
(make sure to‌ also‌ check the AE2‌ guide‌ for‌ detailed explenation)
ftbquests.chapter.ae2.quest66EF071A5EDBB: Storage‌ Components‌ are the‌ core of‌ all‌ AE2‌ cells, determining the‌ capacity of the cells. Each‌ tier‌ increases the capacity‌ by 4x‌ and costs‌ 3‌ of‌ the previous tier.
Begin‌ by‌ creating the‌ first‌ 1k‌ Storage Component, ideally‌ creating a maxed‌ out 1k‌ Storage Cell‌ ME‌ Drive‌ would currently‌ the best‌ thing.
Storage Cells‌ are one‌ of the primary methods of‌ storage in‌ Applied Energistics. They go‌ in &bME‌ Drives&r or &bME‌ Chests&r.
Storage‌ components can be removed‌ from‌ the housing if‌ the‌ cell‌ is empty‌ by‌ shift-right clicking with‌ the cell in your‌ hand.
The‌ upfront cost of‌ types is‌ such that‌ a‌ cell‌ holding 1‌ type‌ can hold 2x as‌ much as‌ a‌ cell with‌ all 63‌ types‌ in‌ use.
ftbquests.chapter.ae2.quest677C7E63E071D: Craft the‌ Meteorite Compass to find meteorites‌ around the‌ world.
Meteorites are how‌ you‌ start the‌ mod, they‌ include essential items!
Dig inside‌ the‌ meteor and break‌ the‌ blocks‌ you find‌ in‌ it.
ftbquests.chapter.ae2.quest69C0B0AF6B0A3: While‌ ME‌ networks are‌ also created by adjacent‌ ME-capable‌ machines, cables are the‌ primary way‌ of extending‌ an‌ ME‌ network over larger‌ areas.

&eIf‌ you‌ are‌ new to‌ AE2 and unfamiliar‌ with channels, use‌ smart cable‌ and‌ dense‌ smart cable‌ wherever you‌ can. It will show‌ how channels‌ are routed through your network, making‌ their behavior‌ more understandable.&r

&5Fluix‌ ME‌ Glass Cable&r‌ is‌ the simplest cable to‌ make, transfers‌ power and up‌ to‌ 8 &bchannels&r. It‌ comes in‌ 17‌ diffrent colors, the default‌ being Fluix, and can be‌ dyed‌ any color using‌ any of‌ the 16‌ dyes.

To‌ craft‌ colored cables‌ surround‌ a dye of any‌ type with‌ 8‌ cables of‌ the same‌ type ( color‌ of‌ the cables‌ dosn't matter, but they must‌ be‌ the same type, glass, smart, etc ). You‌ can also‌ paint cables‌ with‌ any‌ forge compatible paint‌ brush‌ in world.
You‌ can‌ craft‌ any colored‌ cable with a‌ water bucket‌ to remove‌ the‌ dye.
You‌ can cover‌ the cable‌ with wool to‌ create Fluix‌ ME Covered Cable, and craft Fluix‌ ME Smart‌ Cable to get‌ a‌ better idea‌ of‌ what is going on‌ with‌ your channels.
ftbquests.chapter.ae2.quest6ABC5228466A1: There‌ are‌ two‌ main terminals‌ used for Auto-crafting:

- uses Blank Patterns‌ to create‌ Patterns, most Commonly‌ Crafting‌ and‌ Processing Patterns. Crafting Patterns‌ will‌ go into‌ the‌ providers‌ that connect‌ to your Molecular‌ Assemblers, while Processing‌ Patterns will‌ go‌ to‌ the provider‌ that connects‌ to a machine‌ or other‌ inventory.
- gives you‌ a way‌ to access all‌ providers‌ on your‌ network‌ remotely. It is handy, but only‌ for‌ a lot of‌ providers, not‌ handy‌ when your‌ system‌ is still small
ftbquests.chapter.ae2.quest6ABCA58C8E5B6: As‌ you may have‌ guessed, Providers‌ and Assemblers‌ do‌ exactly‌ the same‌ as the name‌ suggests.

When requested, a‌ Pattern Provider‌ will‌ read‌ a pattern‌ inside itself, and‌ push the ingredients‌ written on‌ the pattern into any adjacent‌ inventories. These inventories‌ can be almost‌ anything, allowing‌ for you‌ to‌ create a truly staggering‌ variety‌ of things with‌ your‌ Auto-crafting‌ system.

The Molecular‌ Assembler‌ is the wrokhorse‌ of the Auto-crafting system. Best‌ way‌ to use them‌ is by‌ putting them‌ next‌ to‌ a single‌ Pattern‌ Provider, they are the machines‌ that do‌ the‌ crafting for‌ the system.
ftbquests.chapter.ae2.quest700DE6D96334E: Use‌ the‌ Silicon‌ Press in the‌ Inscriber‌ to make‌ Printed‌ Silicon‌ from Silicon. Printed‌ Silicon is needed‌ in every‌ processor recipe‌ and‌ is‌ a staple‌ item for‌ AE2 crafting.
ftbquests.chapter.ae2.quest73BE55CE529F4: Any auto-crafting‌ system requires‌ 3 Main‌ Modules:
Craft‌ Processing‌ Units, The Providers/Assemblers, and‌ the Terminals
Or CPUs, define‌ how large‌ your craft can be, and how‌ many steps‌ can be performed‌ at‌ once. They consist‌ of‌ two parts: Co-processors, and Crafting Storage

The‌ Co-Processor‌ is responsible for‌ telling‌ your‌ network to‌ send‌ more ingredients more‌ often. While technically it is‌ not‌ required, it would be‌ unwise to‌ not have‌ an‌ abundance‌ of these...

The‌ Crafting‌ Storage allows your crafts‌ to be‌ bigger, and‌ contain more‌ steps. Crafting storage‌ blocks‌ use‌ the same‌ ingredients used in storage‌ cells, and‌ can be un-crafted‌ back into‌ their parts‌ by‌ hand
ftbquests.chapter.ae2.quest7403EE5D0E354: Through the‌ use‌ of‌ a Memory‌ Card, we can Connect our‌ P2P‌ Tunnels. P2P Tunnels wont‌ work while‌ not configured.

Shift + Right-Click‌ on‌ a‌ P2P Tunnel to‌ create‌ a new‌ frequiency, or‌ copy‌ the existing‌ Frequency if there‌ is one, then‌ Right-Click the‌ P2P‌ end‌ tunnel you‌ want to‌ use to set‌ it's frequency.
&n&6The‌ item will not be lost‌ if used!&r&r
A‌ P2P Tunnel system‌ may‌ have only‌ one‌ input, but as many outputs‌ as‌ the cable you‌ use‌ allow‌ for.
ftbquests.chapter.ae2.quest79C499E5E6130: Make‌ Fluix‌ Dust‌ and Crystals by‌ combining‌ Certus Quartz‌ and‌ Redstone, required‌ by many‌ recipes from now‌ on
ftbquests.chapter.ae2.quest79EBEC31BC907: Start‌ with‌ the‌ ME Chest‌ for your first digital‌ storage‌ before advancing to‌ ME Drives.

The ME‌ Chest‌ acts‌ like a miniature‌ network‌ with a‌ ME‌ Terminal, ME‌ Drive, and Energy‌ Acceptor. While it can‌ be used‌ as a‌ tiny‌ storage‌ network, its capacity‌ for just‌ one single storage‌ cell means‌ it has limited utility as‌ such.
ftbquests.chapter.ae2.quest7F8CB607C5418: The Quantum‌ Link‌ Chamber‌ has only one‌ slot, for‌ a &6Quantum Entagled‌ Singularity&r.
One‌ is‌ needed for‌ each Link Chamber, however‌ you get‌ 2 from‌ a‌ sigle‌ explosion :)
ftbquests.chapter.ae2.quest7FBE856FF3F46: The Engineering‌ Press crafts‌ Engineering Processors, used‌ for‌ advanced‌ circuit crafting‌ and‌ powering complex machine operations.
ftbquests.chapter.ae2.questD59AB28BAD4E3: While‌ bearing‌ some similarity‌ to‌ Fluix‌ ME Covered‌ Cable in appearance, they‌ provide diagnostic‌ function by‌ visualizing‌ the‌ channel usage‌ on the‌ cables, the channels appear‌ as lit‌ colored lines that run along‌ the black‌ stripe on the‌ cables‌ giving you‌ an‌ understanding of how your‌ channels‌ are being used‌ on‌ your‌ network. For regular‌ smart‌ cables, the first four‌ channels show as lines‌ matching‌ the color of‌ the cable, the‌ next four‌ show‌ as‌ white lines. For‌ dense‌ smart cable, each stripe represents‌ 4 channels (will‌ talk‌ further on‌ that later).
On‌ networks‌ with a &bME‌ Controller&r (fruther down the quest‌ line), the‌ lines on the‌ cables show‌ the exact‌ path‌ the‌ channels take.
These can‌ also‌ be colored‌ in‌ the‌ same manner‌ as Fluix ME‌ Glass Cable.
ftbquests.chapter.ae2.questD9DBD9835CEA9: Higher‌ Capacity cable, can‌ carry‌ 32 &bchannels&r‌ unlike standard‌ cable which‌ can only carry‌ 8, however it &4doesn't‌ support buses&r so you must‌ first step‌ down from dense‌ to‌ a smaller‌ cable (such‌ as Fluix ME Glass‌ Cable‌ or Fluix ME‌ Smart‌ Cable) before‌ using buses‌ or‌ panels. (explained a bit‌ later)

Dense cables slightly override‌ the "shortest‌ path" behavior of channels, channels‌ will take‌ the shortest‌ path‌ to‌ a dense‌ cable, and‌ then the shortest path‌ through that‌ dense‌ cable to‌ a controller.
