ftbquests.chapter.bridges.quest44355A05E: # <grad from=#FF8C46 to=#FFECBE f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>A‌ Constant Cost</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Aura refills‌ on‌ its own and could‌ never‌ be spent on‌ Blood‌ Magic‌ by any‌ other‌ route, so this turns‌ an idle resource into‌ altar‌ time you get‌ to keep. The‌ gunpowder cost‌ stays, and‌ the‌ Conversion Catalyst‌ means‌ real Nature's Aura progress‌ first.</grad></shadow>
[!danger] Gold stays‌ out‌ of this‌ one for‌ the‌ same‌ reason as‌ before. Gold Leaf crushes into‌ four‌ Gold Powder at‌ this altar, so‌ anything touching‌ that‌ pair‌ risks an infinite‌ loop.

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Arcane Ashes‌ draw the‌ alchemy arrays‌ that‌ Blood‌ Magic runs on. They‌ are‌ eaten every‌ single‌ time, and‌ each batch‌ costs 500 LP‌ and four‌ reagents at‌ the‌ Alchemy‌ Table, competing with‌ everything else‌ your altar is‌ trying to‌ get done.</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Nature Altar with‌ a Conversion‌ Catalyst: gunpowder and </grad><grad from=#C08CFF to=#8A5BFF f=0.8>20,000 Aura</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> give‌ Arcane‌ Ashes</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#C08CFF to=#F0D9FF f=0.6>Ashes From The Air</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.bridges.quest45A906261: # <grad from=#FF8C46 to=#FFECBE f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Mods‌ bridge together!</shadow></grad>

[!warn] A‌ bridge is‌ never the best‌ route. Feeding a‌ half processed item into a‌ higher tier‌ always gives you‌ less‌ than feeding‌ raw‌ material straight in. You pay‌ for‌ the shortcut, and that‌ is‌ on‌ purpose.
[!success] What you‌ actually‌ get is reach. A‌ way to spend the‌ resource‌ you have too‌ much of‌ on the‌ thing‌ you‌ keep running‌ out‌ of.
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>This‌ pack has a‌ lot of‌ tech mods that all double‌ ore and‌ five magic mods‌ that‌ each have‌ their‌ own system.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>That leaves you‌ with‌ two kinds of‌ pain. </grad><grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8>Wasted‌ work</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, where‌ a mod‌ hands‌ you a half‌ finished item that nothing‌ else‌ will touch, so it‌ dead ends‌ in a‌ chest‌ forever. And </grad><grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8>duplicated‌ grind</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, where two‌ mods‌ make you farm the‌ same thing‌ twice‌ because neither‌ one can‌ see‌ what‌ the other‌ already gave you.</grad></shadow>
Everything in‌ this‌ chapter will teach‌ you how‌ they're bridged!
## <grad from=#FF9E1F to=#FFC46B f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>The‌ Two‌ Rules</shadow></grad>
[!info] A‌ bridge always needs‌ progress‌ in both‌ mods. If‌ a‌ recipe hands‌ you a Blood‌ Magic item, it‌ will also‌ demand‌ one‌ from you.
ftbquests.chapter.bridges.quest4A3633500: # <grad from=#FF8C46 to=#FFECBE f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Dust‌ With No Use</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>All </grad><grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8>28</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> Thermal‌ dusts now‌ sit‌ in‌ their proper‌ tag. They smelt, they alloy, they feed‌ the‌ Crystallizer, and Almost Unified‌ can finally‌ see them.</grad></shadow>

[!success] Nothing‌ was‌ rebalanced. Every‌ one of these‌ round‌ trips was‌ already‌ break‌ even by‌ design. Invar goes in‌ as 2‌ iron and‌ 1‌ nickel‌ and comes‌ back out‌ as 2 iron‌ and 1‌ nickel. This only makes recipes reachable‌ that were‌ always meant to‌ be.
[!note] Thermal's‌ gears, plates and‌ copper‌ nuggets had the same‌ hole‌ and were tagged‌ too, along‌ with‌ Terramity's ruby‌ and‌ sapphire.

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Thermal's Pulverizer‌ turns‌ an iron ingot‌ into Iron‌ Dust. Its Centrifuge‌ splits‌ Invar‌ Dust back‌ into‌ iron and nickel. Pulverize copper‌ ore and‌ it‌ even hands‌ you a‌ little‌ Gold‌ Dust on‌ the side.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Not one of‌ those‌ dusts could be‌ smelted. Not by‌ Thermal, not by‌ anybody.</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#FF9E1F to=#FFC46B f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Why‌ It‌ Happened</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Thermal does not‌ ship‌ a dust‌ to‌ ingot‌ recipe. It leans‌ on the one‌ Mekanism provides, and‌ that recipe‌ reads‌ a‌ shared tag. But‌ Thermal only‌ tags the dusts‌ for its </grad><grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8>own</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> alloys, the‌ bronze and invar and electrum‌ family. Its iron, copper, gold, diamond, emerald, lapis, netherite, quartz, sulfur‌ and ender pearl‌ dusts‌ sat in </grad><grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8>no‌ tag‌ at all</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, so that recipe‌ never‌ saw them.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Six more‌ had‌ it‌ worse. Signalum, Lumium, Enderium, Apatite, Cinnabar and‌ Niter‌ dust belonged to‌ tags that </grad><grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8>no mod anywhere‌ declared</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, which‌ quietly switched off‌ Thermal's own‌ Smelter and‌ Crystallizer‌ recipes‌ along with‌ Evolved‌ Mekanism's entire melting chain‌ for those‌ three‌ alloys.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.bridges.quest4C8DE7F0F: # <grad from=#FF8C46 to=#FFECBE f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>The Empty Barrel</shadow></grad>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Ad‌ Astra oil‌ wells, pooled underneath the derrick</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#FF9E1F to=#FFC46B f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>What It‌ Opens</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Both oils‌ now feed both‌ refineries. A‌ hundred crude‌ splits‌ into forty heavy and‌ sixty‌ light, and those come‌ back‌ as‌ ninety refined‌ fuel‌ with bitumen, tar and‌ sulfur along the way.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Run‌ the‌ same barrel through‌ Ad Astra‌ instead and‌ it‌ becomes‌ rocket fuel, one‌ for‌ one. Your quarry now fuels‌ the launch‌ pad.</grad></shadow>
[!info] The‌ Thermal route‌ is the‌ lossy‌ one. You‌ give up‌ a tenth of the‌ volume‌ to get a‌ fuel the‌ dynamos actually‌ want.
[!warn] Oil‌ Sand‌ and oil wells‌ are‌ both worldgen. Nothing‌ anywhere‌ makes‌ either of‌ them, so neither direction‌ can ever‌ print fuel.

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Thermal's‌ Refinery cracks crude oil‌ into‌ heavy and light‌ oil, then boils‌ both down‌ into‌ refined‌ fuel. Ad Astra's‌ Fuel‌ Refinery turns its own‌ oil into‌ the‌ stuff rockets‌ drink. Two mods, two‌ oils, and‌ the‌ shared crude‌ oil tag was completely‌ empty.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Empty‌ enough that Thermal's‌ Refinery could‌ not accept‌ the‌ crude‌ oil </grad><grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8>Thermal itself produces</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. The‌ whole‌ petrochemical line‌ loaded‌ fine‌ and nothing‌ on earth could‌ reach it.</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#FF9E1F to=#FFC46B f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Where‌ Oil Comes‌ From</shadow></grad>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The‌ Thermal‌ Centrifuge, 100 mB‌ out of‌ every Oil Sand</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.bridges.quest4CBB561DD: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Four paste per slime‌ is a‌ good‌ rate, roughly double‌ a vanilla‌ crop, and‌ it‌ should be. The‌ input is the far‌ end‌ of a Mob‌ Slaughter Factory, a‌ Sewage Composter‌ and‌ a‌ Sludge Refiner. You paid‌ for‌ that rate‌ three‌ machines‌ ago.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The Decomposer‌ recipe matters more‌ than it‌ looks. Elastic Fibers‌ gate‌ most‌ of Biomancy's‌ mid game‌ gear and normally‌ trickle in‌ from mob drops one at‌ a time.</grad></shadow>
[!danger] Nutrients‌ cannot become Pink‌ Slime‌ again, so this‌ only‌ runs one way.

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Biomancy‌ runs‌ on </grad><grad from=#C08CFF to=#8A5BFF f=0.8>Nutrients</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, rendered out‌ of food in‌ the Digester. Early‌ on that‌ means‌ building‌ a second‌ farm whose‌ only job is‌ feeding a‌ machine that turns crops into‌ paste. Your first‌ farm was already‌ doing‌ that.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Three rooms‌ over, Industrial‌ Foregoing is refining sewage‌ into‌ Pink Slime and‌ has‌ no‌ idea what‌ to‌ do with the‌ surplus.</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Digester: one Pink Slime‌ gives </grad><grad from=#C08CFF to=#8A5BFF f=0.8>four‌ Nutrient Paste</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Decomposer: one Pink‌ Slime Ingot‌ gives </grad><grad from=#C08CFF to=#8A5BFF f=0.8>2 to‌ 4‌ Elastic‌ Fibers</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and sometimes‌ Organic‌ Matter</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#C08CFF to=#F0D9FF f=0.6>Slime Into Nutrients</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.bridges.quest4CE6A30A9: - <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Thermal‌ Sawdust, into the‌ shared‌ wood dust tag</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Thermal Slag, into‌ the shared‌ slag‌ tag</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#FF9E1F to=#FFC46B f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>What It‌ Unlocks</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Coke out‌ of‌ Thermal's‌ Pyrolyzer now‌ fuels the Immersive Engineering‌ Blast‌ Furnace, feeds the Crusher‌ for coke‌ dust, and packs‌ into‌ a‌ coke block. Before this, a‌ Thermal‌ player had‌ to‌ go‌ build a‌ second, entirely redundant Coke‌ Oven just‌ to reach‌ steel.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Sawdust‌ from‌ any of‌ the three‌ sawmills now works‌ in every‌ recipe that wanted sawdust, instead of‌ only the‌ one from the‌ mod‌ that happened‌ to‌ make it.</grad></shadow>
[!note] These only add‌ entries. Nothing‌ was removed from‌ any‌ tag, so‌ nothing that‌ worked‌ before can break.

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Tags are‌ how one‌ mod recognises‌ another‌ mod's‌ item. When one‌ is missing, two‌ identical items behave‌ like unrelated‌ materials, and you never find out‌ until something‌ quietly refuses to‌ craft.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Almost‌ Unified already‌ handles‌ ingots, dusts, gems and ores. These four‌ fell‌ outside its material‌ list‌ and‌ were genuinely‌ broken.</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#FF9E1F to=#FFC46B f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>What‌ Was Added</shadow></grad>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Thermal Coal‌ Coke, into the shared coal‌ coke‌ tag</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Thermal Block of‌ Coal Coke, into‌ the shared‌ block‌ tag</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.bridges.quest5528F6223: # <grad from=#FF8C46 to=#FFECBE f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Two‌ Coke‌ Ovens</shadow></grad>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The‌ Immersive‌ Engineering‌ generator, as fuel</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The‌ refinery, on the way to‌ phenolic‌ resin</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Create Addition's liquid‌ burner</grad></shadow>
[!note] Additive, like every‌ tag fix‌ here. Immersive‌ Engineering's‌ own creosote still‌ works‌ everywhere it‌ always‌ did.

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The‌ Pyrolyzer hands‌ you coal‌ coke and creosote‌ in the‌ same breath. Immersive Engineering wants creosote‌ for treated‌ wood, for torches, and to‌ burn, and‌ it goes‌ looking‌ through a shared tag‌ to‌ find some.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Thermal's creosote‌ was‌ never‌ in that‌ tag. So‌ you could be‌ sitting on </grad><grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8>tanks of the‌ stuff</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and‌ still be told‌ to go‌ build a‌ Coke‌ Oven‌ before you‌ could‌ make a plank.</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#FF9E1F to=#FFC46B f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>What It‌ Reopens</shadow></grad>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Treated wood, by‌ hand‌ or through‌ the Spout</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#FF8C46 to=#FFECBE f=0.6>Creosote Counts Twice</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.bridges.quest5CEDD0A2C: # <grad from=#FF8C46 to=#FFECBE f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>A‌ New Bottleneck</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Same‌ deal as Magebloom earlier‌ in‌ this chapter. Double the‌ harvest, but the‌ plant comes‌ back‌ exactly‌ once, so your‌ garden‌ never grows itself. Power and‌ water sit‌ at </grad><grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8>1.5x</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> the‌ Thermal baseline, cheaper‌ than Magebloom‌ because‌ herbs‌ are worth‌ less.</grad></shadow>
[!success] Between this and the‌ Distillation, a‌ Hexerei herb garden‌ can now‌ feed an‌ Ars‌ Nouveau‌ essence supply with‌ no‌ hand farming‌ left‌ anywhere‌ in the‌ chain.

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The‌ Witch's‌ Distillation‌ turns five‌ dried herbs into‌ Ars Nouveau‌ essence. Lovely trade, right‌ up‌ until‌ you notice‌ all five‌ herbs are picked‌ by hand, one‌ bush at a time. Solving one‌ bottleneck had‌ quietly built another.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The‌ Thermal Phytogenic‌ Insolator‌ now grows all five‌ Hexerei‌ herbs, giving you </grad><grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8>double</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> the crop‌ and‌ exactly‌ one plant‌ back.</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Sage, Mandrake, Belladonna, Mugwort‌ and Yellow Dock</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#C08CFF to=#F0D9FF f=0.6>The Herb Garden</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.bridges.quest602C32806: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Both recipes‌ eat a‌ component‌ from‌ the far mod, so‌ neither‌ is a‌ way‌ in. The‌ Altar recipe‌ still wants a‌ Source Gem‌ and the‌ Imbuement‌ recipe‌ still wants‌ Gold Powder.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Infused‌ Iron normally costs‌ 15,000 Aura‌ each. The Ars route swaps that‌ for 2,500‌ Source and an‌ Earth‌ Essence per‌ two. Cheaper‌ in Aura, dearer in attention, and‌ it‌ wants an Imbuement‌ Chamber‌ you‌ might not‌ have‌ built.</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#FF9E1F to=#FFC46B f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>The Gold Trap</shadow></grad>

[!danger] Any‌ recipe touching Gold Leaf‌ was‌ avoided on purpose. Gold‌ Leaf crushes‌ into four‌ Gold‌ Powder‌ at this‌ very‌ altar, so a Powder to‌ Leaf bridge‌ would‌ have been‌ an infinite‌ loop. Gold‌ Powder‌ goes in‌ here and never comes‌ out.

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Nature's Aura‌ pulls </grad><grad from=#C08CFF to=#8A5BFF f=0.8>Aura</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> out‌ of the world‌ around‌ it. Ars‌ Nouveau builds </grad><grad from=#C08CFF to=#8A5BFF f=0.8>Source</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> in‌ jars. Both‌ are ambient magic, both‌ refill on their own, and‌ neither‌ could ever be‌ spent on‌ the other.</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Nature‌ Altar‌ with a‌ Conversion‌ Catalyst: one Source Gem and </grad><grad from=#C08CFF to=#8A5BFF f=0.8>60,000‌ Aura</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> give an‌ Earth‌ Essence</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Imbuement Chamber: an‌ iron ingot, with‌ Earth‌ Essence‌ and Gold‌ Powder on the pedestals‌ and </grad><grad from=#C08CFF to=#8A5BFF f=0.8>2,500‌ Source</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, gives two Infused‌ Iron</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#C08CFF to=#F0D9FF f=0.6>Aura And Source</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.bridges.quest65555B9C3: # <grad from=#FF8C46 to=#FFECBE f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Souls‌ By‌ Hand</shadow></grad>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A Hostile‌ Neural Networks‌ Prediction‌ is‌ worth </grad><grad from=#C08CFF to=#8A5BFF f=0.8>15 souls</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>For‌ scale, soul sand‌ is worth 25‌ and a‌ Totem of Undying is worth‌ 200. A Solid‌ XP Block sits‌ at‌ 20, under soul‌ sand, but‌ unlike soul sand it‌ actually‌ renews. That is the‌ whole‌ point‌ of it.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Predictions‌ are‌ priced against their‌ other job on purpose. Fifteen‌ souls‌ is real money, so‌ every prediction‌ you burn‌ here‌ is‌ one that‌ never‌ reached the Loot Fabricator. You‌ are choosing‌ between‌ two things, not‌ printing a‌ third.</grad></shadow>
[!warn] None‌ of‌ this is‌ free. All three want a‌ working‌ farm first, which is‌ a bigger‌ build than‌ anything‌ Goety‌ asks of you‌ on‌ its own.

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The‌ Soul Absorber‌ turns‌ items into </grad><grad from=#C08CFF to=#8A5BFF f=0.8>Souls</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, which pay‌ for every brazier recipe‌ and‌ every summon you‌ own. Its entire‌ input list‌ is‌ sculk, soul‌ sand, ectoplasm and‌ totems. Things‌ you </grad><grad from=#C08CFF to=#8A5BFF f=0.8>find</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, not things you </grad><grad from=#C08CFF to=#8A5BFF f=0.8>produce</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Meanwhile you‌ almost certainly‌ have‌ a mob‌ farm with‌ a‌ Mob‌ Grinding Utils‌ saw in it, or a‌ Hostile‌ Neural Networks sim‌ running around‌ the clock. Goety‌ refused‌ to‌ look at either.</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#FF9E1F to=#FFC46B f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>What‌ Counts‌ Now</shadow></grad>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Solidified Experience‌ is‌ worth </grad><grad from=#C08CFF to=#8A5BFF f=0.8>2‌ souls</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Solid XP‌ Block is worth </grad><grad from=#C08CFF to=#8A5BFF f=0.8>20‌ souls</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#C08CFF to=#F0D9FF f=0.6>Machines That Feed The Dead</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.bridges.quest6C2ED4914: - <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Reinforced Slate, Shadow‌ Essence, Cursed Ingot and </grad><grad from=#C08CFF to=#8A5BFF f=0.8>400 souls</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> give‌ an‌ Imbued Slate</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>At the‌ Blood Magic‌ Soul Forge:</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Two‌ iron, one‌ gold, Shadow‌ Essence and‌ 10‌ Demon Will give </grad><grad from=#C08CFF to=#8A5BFF f=0.8>four Cursed‌ Ingots</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Both directions‌ want‌ an item‌ from the‌ other‌ mod. You‌ cannot make‌ a slate without already‌ owning‌ slates, and you cannot‌ bulk out‌ Cursed Ingots‌ without‌ Shadow‌ Essence and a‌ Soul‌ Forge. Neither mod's‌ front‌ door‌ moved.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Slate ratios‌ stay at one‌ for one. The‌ brazier is‌ not‌ more‌ efficient than‌ the altar, only </grad><grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8>faster</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, and‌ it charges you‌ souls for‌ the privilege.</grad></shadow>
[!success] Two death magic mods‌ finally sharing‌ a workshop. Spend whichever‌ currency‌ you have‌ too‌ much of.

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Blood‌ Magic's‌ real‌ wall is‌ not Life Essence, it is </grad><grad from=#C08CFF to=#8A5BFF f=0.8>throughput</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. A‌ tier‌ one altar drains‌ 5 LP‌ a tick‌ no‌ matter‌ how much you‌ have‌ banked, so turning‌ a‌ stack‌ of blank‌ slates into reinforced‌ ones is‌ a long‌ stare‌ at‌ a pillar‌ of blood.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Goety‌ has the opposite‌ shape. Souls pile‌ up fast once a brazier‌ is running‌ and there is‌ very‌ little to‌ spend‌ them on.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>At the‌ Goety‌ Soul Brazier:</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Blank Slate, Shadow‌ Essence, Soul‌ Sand‌ and </grad><grad from=#C08CFF to=#8A5BFF f=0.8>150 souls</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> give‌ a‌ Reinforced Slate</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#C08CFF to=#F0D9FF f=0.6>Souls For Slates</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.bridges.quest6DE3A2C6E: # <grad from=#FF8C46 to=#FFECBE f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Growing‌ By Hand</shadow></grad>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Charged certus plus fluix‌ dust gives </grad><grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8>one‌ fluix‌ crystal</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The ratios‌ are </grad><grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8>identical</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> to the‌ water‌ version. Not‌ one crystal‌ more. You are buying automation, not‌ yield, and‌ you pay for‌ it with‌ a Combiner‌ and‌ the‌ power to run‌ it.</grad></shadow>
[!info] Charging‌ still needs‌ the‌ AE2‌ Charger, so no‌ step leaves the‌ chain. A pipe‌ just does‌ the‌ step‌ you used‌ to do‌ by hand.

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Certus‌ and Fluix grow by‌ throwing‌ a charged crystal‌ and a‌ dust into‌ a‌ pool‌ of water and‌ waiting. It‌ works, it fits‌ the‌ mod, and‌ it is‌ miserable to automate. You‌ need item‌ drops, a body‌ of‌ water‌ and something‌ to fish‌ the results back‌ out.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The Growth‌ Accelerator speeds up budding blocks, not‌ this. So long‌ after the rest‌ of‌ your base‌ is‌ pipes and drives, crystal doubling‌ is‌ still you standing‌ in‌ a‌ puddle.</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#FF9E1F to=#FFC46B f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Into A‌ Machine</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The‌ Mekanism Combiner now‌ runs both of those‌ in‌ world transforms as‌ an ordinary‌ recipe.</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Charged certus‌ plus‌ certus‌ dust gives </grad><grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8>two‌ certus‌ crystals</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.bridges.quest6EFECFA04: # <grad from=#C08CFF to=#F0D9FF f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>The‌ Full Set</shadow></grad>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Earth‌ on‌ yellow dock</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Water splits‌ sage‌ and‌ yellow dock‌ evenly</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The‌ cauldron started out‌ knowing one‌ recipe. Conjuration, and nothing‌ else. The‌ other‌ six schools‌ now brew‌ exactly the same‌ way: five dried‌ herbs, one Magebloom and two Source‌ Gems, out comes‌ two essence.</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Conjuration‌ takes one of each, as‌ it always‌ has</grad></shadow>
[!info] Still‌ not a‌ drop of‌ Source. The‌ Imbuement‌ Chamber asks‌ 2000 for a single‌ essence; the‌ cauldron asks for‌ a garden‌ instead.
[!warn] Water in‌ the‌ cauldron‌ and a flame‌ underneath. Cold‌ or dry‌ and‌ the‌ herbs just‌ sit there.

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Every school‌ costs‌ the identical‌ amount. What‌ changes is </grad><grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8>which herbs</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, and each‌ blend‌ leans on the‌ one‌ that‌ suits its‌ temperament.</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#B48CFF to=#DCC4FF f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>One‌ Price, Seven Blends</shadow></grad>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Abjuration leans‌ on sage</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#C08CFF to=#F0D9FF f=0.6>All Seven Essences</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.bridges.quest75050E9E5: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Soul‌ Snares‌ are‌ pure consumable. You‌ burn them catching‌ Demon Will, and‌ each one‌ normally‌ costs‌ 500 LP‌ of altar‌ time. Buying four with‌ banked Source‌ lifts that grind off the‌ altar without‌ making Will any‌ cheaper.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The‌ Source Gem‌ trade‌ is deliberately the </grad><grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8>worse</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> of the‌ two. The‌ Imbuement Chamber does‌ the‌ same‌ amethyst for‌ 500‌ Source and no‌ slate. You would only reach‌ for‌ this with LP‌ to spare‌ and no‌ Source.</grad></shadow>
[!danger] Both‌ recipes‌ eat a‌ Blank‌ Slate, so neither is a‌ way into‌ Blood‌ Magic. You need‌ an altar‌ running‌ before‌ either one‌ exists.
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Ars Nouveau and‌ Blood‌ Magic are‌ the‌ two biggest magic mods‌ here‌ and they had‌ absolutely‌ nothing‌ to say‌ to‌ one another.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>They also‌ fail in opposite directions. Blood‌ Magic‌ chokes on </grad><grad from=#C08CFF to=#8A5BFF f=0.8>throughput</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, draining at‌ a fixed‌ rate however‌ much‌ you‌ have stored. Ars‌ Nouveau‌ chokes on </grad><grad from=#C08CFF to=#8A5BFF f=0.8>spending</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, since jars keep‌ filling whether‌ you‌ use them‌ or not.</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Enchanting‌ Apparatus: string, two‌ Source Gems‌ and a Blank Slate‌ with </grad><grad from=#C08CFF to=#8A5BFF f=0.8>1,000‌ Source</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> give four Soul‌ Snares</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Alchemy Table: a‌ Blank Slate, two‌ amethyst‌ and‌ redstone with </grad><grad from=#C08CFF to=#8A5BFF f=0.8>2,000 LP</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> give‌ two‌ Source Gems</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#C08CFF to=#F0D9FF f=0.6>Snares And Source</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.bridges.quest7C1BA4F2C: ## <grad from=#FF9E1F to=#FFC46B f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>One Direction‌ Only</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The reverse‌ was‌ deliberately‌ left closed. IF plastic‌ is‌ the cheapest‌ of‌ the‌ three, since latex‌ arrives long before‌ Mekanism oxygen‌ or IE‌ phenolic‌ resin. Letting‌ it stand‌ in for‌ the other two‌ would skip‌ real progression.</grad></shadow>
[!success] A later material dropping‌ into an‌ earlier recipe is‌ always‌ safe. The other‌ way‌ round is a tier‌ skip, so‌ it stays shut.

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Industrial‌ Foregoing‌ makes‌ Plastic out‌ of latex you‌ tap from‌ trees. Mekanism makes‌ HDPE‌ Sheets‌ out of‌ substrate and‌ oxygen. Immersive Engineering presses‌ Duroplast Plates‌ out of phenolic resin. Three mods, one‌ material, and not‌ one of them‌ recognised‌ the others.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The‌ shared‌ plastic tag held only‌ the‌ Industrial Foregoing item, and </grad><grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8>62</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> Industrial‌ Foregoing‌ recipes‌ read that‌ tag. So‌ no matter how‌ much HDPE your Mekanism‌ line‌ was churning out, IF‌ still told‌ you to‌ go‌ plant‌ a tree‌ farm.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Mekanism HDPE Sheets and‌ IE Duroplast‌ Plates‌ were added‌ to the‌ plastic‌ tag. All‌ 62 of‌ those recipes now take‌ whichever‌ plastic you actually‌ make.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#5AB9FF to=#B7E4FF f=0.6>Three Kinds Of Plastic</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.bridges.questDDBC23BEB: # <grad from=#FF8C46 to=#FFECBE f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Both Made Of Death</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Flesh‌ Bits are Biomancy's‌ most common‌ byproduct and are priced under‌ ectoplasm's own‌ five accordingly. Nothing valuable‌ is‌ worth burning‌ for‌ souls here.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Living Flesh was‌ left‌ out on purpose. Trading‌ a‌ Primordial‌ Cradle product‌ for‌ souls would be‌ a terrible deal that‌ nobody‌ would ever take, and‌ a recipe‌ nobody takes‌ is‌ just‌ clutter in‌ the‌ book.</grad></shadow>
[!success] The Decomposer side is‌ safe by‌ its‌ own nature. A‌ Decomposer only‌ ever‌ breaks‌ things down, so‌ it cannot skip a‌ gate.
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Biomancy‌ grows‌ flesh. Goety harvests souls. Both‌ spend their‌ entire game‌ loop‌ on‌ dead things and‌ they‌ shared precisely‌ nothing.</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Soul‌ Absorber: Flesh Bits‌ are worth </grad><grad from=#C08CFF to=#8A5BFF f=0.8>2 souls</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Decomposer: Goety‌ Ectoplasm breaks‌ down into </grad><grad from=#C08CFF to=#8A5BFF f=0.8>1‌ to‌ 3‌ Bio-Lumens</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and sometimes‌ Organic Matter</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#C08CFF to=#F0D9FF f=0.6>Flesh And Ectoplasm</grad></shadow>

ftbquests.chapter.building.quest18FF0716: Right-clicking a‌ compact block with the‌ shrinking‌ device will transport‌ you inside‌ of it, providing‌ an‌ isolated‌ pocket dimension where‌ you‌ can build‌ freely.
ftbquests.chapter.building.quest2614F2BB: The‌ ultimate construction‌ tool. Features‌ maximum durability and‌ range, allowing you to place‌ up‌ to &b1,024&r blocks at‌ once for‌ massive megastructures.
When &bcrouching‌ and‌ scrolling&r, you‌ can change‌ modes.
If‌ you also hold a‌ block in‌ your‌ off-hand, It will‌ only place‌ that‌ block‌ instead of‌ automatically copying the adjacent‌ block.
ftbquests.chapter.building.quest27EB5AD5: An‌ advanced wand designed‌ for large-scale‌ projects. Extends existing‌ structures‌ by‌ placing up‌ to &b128&r blocks‌ at a time.
When &bcrouching‌ and scrolling&r, you‌ can change modes.
If you also‌ hold a‌ block in your‌ off-hand, It‌ will only‌ place‌ that block instead of‌ automatically‌ copying the adjacent‌ block.
ftbquests.chapter.building.quest39D7DAC6: An entry-level‌ construction wand. Extends‌ the block face you are‌ looking at‌ by placing up‌ to &b9&r‌ blocks at‌ once‌ from your inventory.
When &bcrouching and‌ scrolling&r, you‌ can change modes.
If‌ you‌ also‌ hold a‌ block‌ in your off-hand, It‌ will only place that‌ block‌ instead of automatically‌ copying the‌ adjacent block.
ftbquests.chapter.building.quest428771C3: Make‌ sure‌ to use &eJEI&r‌ in order to‌ see the‌ recipes.
Thousands of‌ new‌ blocks‌ can only‌ be crafted‌ here.
ftbquests.chapter.building.quest48583E6B: An upgrade component‌ that grants‌ mid-air building‌ capabilities. Combine‌ this‌ with any wand‌ in‌ a crafting‌ grid‌ to‌ enable placing‌ blocks floating in‌ mid-air or‌ directly behind‌ targeted‌ surfaces‌ without needing‌ solid support.
ftbquests.chapter.building.quest49DA079E: <shadow><grad from=#4EF44E to=#BBFF99 f=0.5>Creeper</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C0C0C0> exploded and‌ destroyed‌ your </grad><grad from=#4EF44E to=#BBFF99 f=0.5>terrain</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C0C0C0>?</grad></shadow>

<shadow><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C0C0C0>Just‌ throw the </grad><grad from=#4EF44E to=#8B4513 f=0.5>hole‌ filler</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C0C0C0> into‌ a hole and it‌ will start </grad><shake a=0.75 f=0.75><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C0C0C0>expanding‌ like‌ crazy</grad></shake><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C0C0C0>!</grad></shadow>
<shadow><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C0C0C0>There's other‌ variations check </grad><grad from=#FFA040 to=#FFD080 f=0.5>JEI</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C0C0C0> to‌ see</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.building.quest4E66DE42: A‌ mid-tier‌ building tool‌ with‌ increased durability and range. Capable‌ of placing‌ up‌ to &b27&r blocks‌ in a‌ single‌ click.
When &bcrouching‌ and scrolling&r, you‌ can change modes.
If you‌ also‌ hold a block‌ in your‌ off-hand, It will‌ only‌ place‌ that block instead‌ of‌ automatically copying‌ the‌ adjacent‌ block.
