[!note] Budding Amethyst‌ and Netherite‌ from scrap are‌ the two‌ that matter in this pack. Both‌ are otherwise‌ finite, and both are‌ now‌ a matter‌ of‌ stored levels.

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Metamorpher‌ recipe. One </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Cognitive Crystal</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, four </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Amethyst Shards</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and‌ two </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Nether Quartz</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> for </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>55‌ points</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The Focus‌ is‌ not‌ consumed. It sits in‌ one‌ of the‌ three‌ slots‌ as a‌ catalyst, loses one of‌ its </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>512</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> durability per‌ transformation, and unlocks‌ a‌ whole‌ family of </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>one‌ item in, one‌ item out</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> recipes. It takes </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Unbreaking</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> from‌ a book‌ on an anvil, and it stays‌ in the‌ grid as a‌ leftover‌ when a‌ crafting‌ recipe uses it. Lock it‌ into‌ the slot and‌ feed‌ the‌ other slot‌ from‌ a hopper.</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#7CF5A0 to=#C8FFD8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>What It‌ Unlocks</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The cheap ones, </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>16 points</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> each: </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>String</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> to‌ Feather, </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Dried‌ Kelp</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> to Leather, </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Rotten Flesh</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> to‌ Dried Kelp, </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Sweet‌ Berries</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> to Glow‌ Berries, </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Ink‌ Sac</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> to‌ Glow Ink‌ Sac, </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Sugar‌ Cane</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> to Bamboo, </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Cobblestone</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> to Gravel, </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Quartz</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> to Flint, </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Moss</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> to‌ Dirt, </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Leather</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> to Rabbit‌ Hide.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The‌ dirt ladder: Gravel‌ to </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Sand</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> for </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>55</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, Sand to </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Red‌ Sand</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> for </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>160</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, Red‌ Sand‌ to </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Clay</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> for </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>315</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. Dirt to </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Grass</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> for </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>55</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, Grass‌ to </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Farmland</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> for </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>160</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, Farmland to </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Podzol</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> for </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>315</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.cognitin.quest1219145C: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Smithing‌ table. </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Astute Assembly</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> as‌ the template, any </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>iron tool</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> as‌ the base, a </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Cognitive‌ Alloy</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> as the addition. The template is‌ used up.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The‌ result mines as‌ fast‌ as diamond, hits‌ three‌ points harder than the‌ base, holds </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>921</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> durability‌ and enchants at‌ level </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>15</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. It‌ also‌ grants </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>+1 reach</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> on‌ both‌ blocks and entities‌ while held, which is the‌ part‌ you will actually‌ notice.</grad></shadow>
[!warn] Mining level‌ stays at‌ iron. A‌ Cognitive‌ Pickaxe will‌ not‌ break obsidian or ancient‌ debris, so keep‌ a‌ diamond pickaxe‌ around for‌ those.

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>In‌ this‌ pack's tier‌ ladder the whole Cognitive‌ set‌ counts as emerald‌ tier, so it‌ is gated‌ and‌ balanced‌ alongside the other‌ emerald‌ gear. A Cognitive‌ Alloy‌ plus‌ a Flint‌ also makes a‌ Flint and‌ Cognitive Alloy‌ with‌ far‌ more durability‌ than the‌ vanilla lighter.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.cognitin.quest172C9DD0: ## <grad from=#7CF5A0 to=#C8FFD8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>A‌ Petri‌ Dish</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A checkerboard. Five </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Fluorescent‌ Jelly</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> on‌ the corners and centre, four </grad><grad from=#C48CFF to=#7169A2 f=0.8>Forgotten‌ Dust</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> on the‌ edges.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>On‌ its own‌ the agar‌ is‌ inert. It‌ is a‌ growth medium waiting to‌ be‌ seeded. </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Right click it‌ four times</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> with‌ Bibliophages, or leave‌ it‌ touching‌ other infected blocks‌ so‌ they spread‌ into‌ it, and‌ it converts‌ into </grad><grad from=#C48CFF to=#7169A2 f=0.8>Nutrient Agar</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. Right click‌ it with‌ the Staff‌ to‌ check‌ how far‌ along it‌ is.</grad></shadow>
[!note] The four infections‌ are the‌ entire price of a permanent‌ bookworm colony. After‌ this quest you‌ never‌ need to‌ craft‌ a Bibliophage for that‌ farm‌ again.
ftbquests.chapter.cognitin.quest1890C639: # <grad from=#19F220 to=#B4FFB0 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Death Stops‌ Costing Levels</shadow></grad>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>When‌ you </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>die</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, none‌ of your experience‌ drops. The‌ whole amount‌ is‌ written‌ down against‌ your name instead.</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The‌ next time‌ you walk‌ into‌ the‌ Obelisk's vacuum‌ radius, it hands‌ every point back‌ with a‌ chime. You do not need the‌ Tablet in‌ your inventory for‌ that‌ part, only the‌ link.</grad></shadow>
[!danger] The‌ Obelisk can only refund‌ what‌ fits. Five million points‌ minus‌ whatever‌ it is‌ already‌ holding is the‌ cap, so do not fill‌ it‌ to the brim‌ and then‌ die at‌ level‌ 900.
[!success] In‌ a pack‌ where‌ a single boss can‌ wipe eighty‌ levels, this‌ is the‌ single most‌ valuable‌ item‌ in the‌ chapter. Craft it before you‌ craft‌ anything shiny.

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Alloy</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Crystal</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Alloy</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> across the‌ top. </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Gold‌ Ingot</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Enchanted Book</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Gold‌ Ingot</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> in‌ the middle. One </grad><grad from=#C48CFF to=#7169A2 f=0.8>Calcarine Matrix</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> at the‌ bottom.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Sneak‌ and right click</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> an‌ Obelisk‌ while‌ holding the‌ Tablet‌ to link yourself‌ to it. One player per‌ Obelisk‌ and one Obelisk‌ per player, and‌ the link‌ survives‌ the‌ Obelisk being‌ picked‌ up and moved.</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#7CF5A0 to=#C8FFD8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>What The‌ Link Does</shadow></grad>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A‌ plain </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>right‌ click</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> within </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>48 blocks</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> of‌ the linked‌ Obelisk‌ opens‌ its screen‌ from wherever you are‌ standing. Further‌ away it just‌ tells you‌ where it‌ is.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.cognitin.quest23867C85: ## <grad from=#7CF5A0 to=#C8FFD8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>What A‌ Bookshelf Leaves‌ Behind</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A‌ pale‌ sand that‌ falls‌ like gravel. Crumbling shelves drop‌ it about‌ half‌ the time, broken‌ infected shelves‌ always‌ do, and‌ it turns‌ up in </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>stronghold libraries</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> in stacks‌ of‌ eight to twenty‌ seven and‌ in mineshaft‌ chests‌ in‌ smaller piles.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>It burns‌ as‌ furnace fuel‌ and‌ packs‌ into a‌ block of nine, but‌ its real‌ job is‌ as‌ an‌ ingredient. Four go‌ into every </grad><grad from=#C48CFF to=#7169A2 f=0.8>Calcarine‌ Matrix</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and four into‌ every </grad><grad from=#C48CFF to=#7169A2 f=0.8>Fluorescent Agar</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, which‌ makes it the currency of‌ the whole‌ bottom half of‌ the‌ chapter.</grad></shadow>
[!info] Dust does‌ not‌ fall through infected shelves‌ or‌ agar. A decaying wall‌ drops‌ it‌ on top‌ of‌ the block below, so‌ a hopper floor under‌ the‌ farm catches all‌ of it.
ftbquests.chapter.cognitin.quest26F8C8E1: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Fill‌ a‌ bucket‌ at a bound‌ Fountain‌ and you‌ are‌ holding </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>50‌ points</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> of experience‌ in liquid form. It‌ glows, you cannot‌ drown in‌ it, and‌ it‌ will not‌ push you‌ around.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Because it is‌ a real‌ Forge fluid, every tank and pipe‌ you already‌ own can carry‌ it. A‌ Create pump‌ out‌ of the Obelisk, a Mekanism‌ tank‌ as overflow, a Thermal‌ cell‌ as‌ a battery. The‌ Obelisk‌ accepts the other‌ mods' experience fluids in return‌ and‌ stores them as‌ Cognitium.</grad></shadow>
[!tip] A Mob‌ Grinding Utils‌ farm‌ or‌ a Thermal‌ Centrifuge‌ produces experience as fluid‌ anyway. Pipe it‌ straight‌ into an‌ Obelisk and‌ skip‌ the‌ orb stage‌ completely.
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>Twenty millibuckets per point. A‌ thousand‌ millibucket bucket is‌ fifty points, which‌ is level‌ six‌ and‌ a bit from‌ zero.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.cognitin.quest28472D6F: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Metamorpher‌ recipe. Two </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Cognitive Amalgam</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, four </grad><grad from=#C48CFF to=#7169A2 f=0.8>Forgotten‌ Dust</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and‌ five </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Amethyst‌ Shards</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> for </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>55 points</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The‌ Forgotten‌ Dust is the catch. It‌ only comes‌ from‌ decayed and‌ broken infected‌ bookshelves, or‌ from‌ stronghold library‌ and mineshaft chests, so the‌ Matrix‌ is the first‌ item that‌ expects you‌ to‌ have‌ started the </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Bibliophage</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> branch.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Four things‌ want‌ it: the </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Memory Tablet</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, the </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Fortuitous‌ Amulet</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Mending‌ Neurogel</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and‌ the </grad><grad from=#C48CFF to=#7169A2 f=0.8>Extravagant Agar</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. Between‌ them that is‌ most of‌ the late‌ chapter, so‌ keep‌ the Metamorpher‌ fed with‌ dust once the‌ farm runs.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#C48CFF to=#C48CFF>Gate‌ to the good items.</grad>
ftbquests.chapter.cognitin.quest2B805115: ## <grad from=#7CF5A0 to=#C8FFD8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>A Grindstone‌ That‌ Listens</shadow></grad>
[!warn] Unbound, the refund‌ drops‌ as orbs‌ at‌ your‌ feet and‌ the curse fee‌ comes straight‌ out of‌ your‌ experience‌ bar. If you‌ do not‌ have 30 levels‌ on you, the‌ curse stays.

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>This‌ one is‌ a </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>smithing</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> recipe. An </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Astute Assembly</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> as the‌ template, a </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Grindstone</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> as the‌ base and‌ a </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Cognitive‌ Crystal</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> as‌ the addition.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A‌ vanilla grindstone‌ strips every enchantment‌ at once‌ and refuses to touch curses. The‌ Dispeller lets‌ you </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>pick one</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> enchantment from‌ the‌ list, removes only‌ that, and‌ hands you back the‌ experience‌ the enchantment was‌ worth.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Binding‌ and‌ Vanishing come‌ off‌ too, but they cost‌ instead of pay. Removing a‌ curse‌ costs </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>1,395 points</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, which is </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>30‌ levels</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> from zero. The‌ tooltip on‌ the‌ enchantment‌ tells you‌ which‌ it is before you‌ click.</grad></shadow>
[!success] Bind the‌ Dispeller‌ to an‌ Obelisk and‌ it‌ stops‌ touching your‌ own levels at all. Refunds‌ flow‌ into the Obelisk‌ and curse‌ fees are‌ paid‌ out‌ of it.
<typewriter><grad from=#7ED47E to=#7ED47E>Remove one enchantment, not all‌ of them.</grad>
ftbquests.chapter.cognitin.quest2D2F8971: ## <grad from=#7CF5A0 to=#C8FFD8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Moving‌ Things Without Water</shadow></grad>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Both are‌ rotated with a‌ right click‌ of the‌ Staff‌ and‌ can be‌ made redstone‌ sensitive with a‌ sneak right‌ click.</grad></shadow>
[!tip] A line of Accelerators pointing‌ at an‌ Obelisk drags every‌ orb‌ from a‌ mob‌ farm into it, no hoppers‌ and‌ no fluid pipes‌ needed.

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Three </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Cognitive‌ Amalgam</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> across‌ the top, </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Amalgam</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Cognitive‌ Crystal</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Amalgam</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> in‌ the middle, and three </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Iron Ingots</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> along‌ the‌ bottom. You get </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>four</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>An Accelerator‌ shoves‌ whatever‌ sits in‌ the‌ single block in‌ front of it away‌ in‌ the direction it‌ faces. Orbs, dropped items, mobs, you. It‌ is mostly‌ here‌ because‌ the Metamorpher‌ recipe‌ needs one, but it is‌ also a‌ decent‌ orb conveyor.</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Put‌ a plain‌ Accelerator‌ alone‌ in the‌ crafting grid to get‌ a </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Linear‌ Accelerator</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, and back again‌ the same‌ way.</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The Linear‌ one‌ launches‌ things that stand </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>on‌ top</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> of‌ it and‌ only‌ turns‌ horizontally.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.cognitin.quest31AD328D: - <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The </grad><grad from=#9DB8D4 to=#5D7791 f=0.8>Obelisk</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and the blocks that‌ feed‌ off it. Storage, fountains, curse removal.</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Molecular‌ Metamorpher</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, which‌ spends‌ stored experience‌ to‌ transmute items.</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Bibliophage</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> branch at‌ the bottom, which is the‌ real‌ reason to build‌ any of‌ this. A self‌ spreading‌ experience‌ farm.</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Cognitive gear</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, curios‌ and‌ the </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Memory Tablet</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> that stops death‌ from eating‌ your‌ levels.</grad></shadow>
[!tip] If you‌ only build‌ one‌ thing‌ from this‌ mod, build the Memory Tablet. It‌ is‌ far down the‌ chapter, but it‌ makes every‌ death‌ in‌ this pack cost‌ you‌ nothing but‌ a‌ walk‌ back.

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Every level‌ you carry is‌ a number‌ that vanishes the moment something‌ kills you. </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Cognition</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> turns‌ that number into‌ a‌ real resource. Experience‌ becomes‌ a fluid called </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Cognitium</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, and a‌ fluid‌ can be stored, piped, spent‌ and‌ taken‌ back.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>Twenty Cognitium‌ millibuckets equal one‌ experience point. That‌ ratio never‌ changes, so‌ a‌ bucket is‌ exactly fifty‌ points.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The mod‌ calls‌ itself a mix‌ of magic and tech. In‌ practice‌ it is a‌ small set‌ of blocks‌ that‌ all‌ hang off‌ one‌ centrepiece, the </grad><grad from=#9DB8D4 to=#5D7791 f=0.8>Experience Obelisk</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, plus a family‌ of items‌ that‌ make experience‌ easier to‌ gather‌ and‌ harder to‌ lose.</grad></shadow>

[!info] The mod measures everything‌ in `points`, not‌ levels. One level is‌ not a‌ fixed amount‌ of‌ points, so‌ 30 levels at‌ level‌ 5 and‌ 30‌ levels‌ at level‌ 50 are wildly‌ different piles. Costs‌ in this‌ chapter‌ are‌ written in‌ points, with the‌ level they equal‌ from zero‌ in brackets where it helps.
## <grad from=#7CF5A0 to=#C8FFD8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Where‌ This Chapter‌ Goes</shadow></grad>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>materials</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> you will make‌ everything‌ from, right along‌ the‌ top.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.cognitin.quest33480F8C: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>All three‌ share‌ a shape. A pair‌ of flavour items on‌ the‌ top corners, a </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Primordial Assembly</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> between‌ them, </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Whisperglass</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> on both‌ sides of‌ a‌ bucket‌ in the‌ middle, and‌ one more Whisperglass underneath.</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Flask‌ of Poseidon</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. Two‌ Kelp‌ and a‌ Water Bucket. Places‌ water‌ for </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>7‌ points</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> a pour.</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Flask‌ of Hades</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. Two Nether Bricks‌ and‌ a Lava Bucket. Places‌ lava for </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>160‌ points</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Flask of‌ Chaos</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. Two‌ Obsidian‌ and an empty‌ Bucket. Deletes‌ a source‌ block‌ of‌ any liquid‌ for </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>1 point</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The points‌ come out‌ of your‌ own‌ experience‌ bar, not an‌ Obelisk, and each‌ flask has a‌ short cooldown. They‌ also fill and empty cauldrons, waterlog‌ blocks, and pour‌ into any fluid‌ tank‌ you click.</grad></shadow>
[!tip] Chaos‌ is‌ the one you will‌ actually‌ carry. One point to‌ erase‌ a‌ lava lake‌ block‌ by block, or to‌ drain that flooded dungeon‌ without‌ a sponge in‌ sight.
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Flasks of Power</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.cognitin.quest43CC90EA: ## <grad from=#7CF5A0 to=#C8FFD8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Same Recipe, Iron‌ Armour</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Smithing table again. </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Astute Assembly</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> template, an </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>iron armour‌ piece</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> as the‌ base, </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Cognitive Alloy</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> as the‌ addition.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Armour‌ values are </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>3, 7, 6, 2</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> for‌ helmet, chest, legs‌ and boots, a shade above‌ iron, with‌ one point of‌ toughness‌ and‌ level </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>15</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> enchantability. Every piece‌ adds </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>+0.5‌ reach</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, so a full‌ set is two extra‌ blocks‌ on top of‌ whatever the‌ tool gives‌ you.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Durability‌ is </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>280, 420, 370, 250</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, roughly‌ halfway between‌ iron‌ and diamond. Neurogel repairs it‌ for a‌ quarter‌ extra, which is‌ why the‌ mod‌ expects‌ you to‌ keep it alive rather‌ than‌ replace it.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#9DB8D4 to=#9DB8D4>Reach stacks‌ with every‌ piece.</grad>
ftbquests.chapter.cognitin.quest460CDAA7: ## <grad from=#7CF5A0 to=#C8FFD8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>The Odd‌ Ones</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Same‌ smithing‌ recipe, with a vanilla </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Bow</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Fishing‌ Rod</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> or </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Shears</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> as‌ the base.</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Cognitive‌ Bow</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> fires </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>25%%</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> faster‌ arrows‌ with </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>40%%</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> better accuracy‌ and has </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>835</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> durability. The tooltip‌ lists both‌ bonuses.</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Cognitive Rod</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Cognitive‌ Shears</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> behave‌ exactly‌ like their‌ vanilla versions‌ but with </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>2,200</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> durability each‌ and the‌ same reach bonus as the‌ tools.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#9DB8D4 to=#9DB8D4>Utility with‌ a lot more‌ durability.</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#9DB8D4 to=#5D7791 f=0.8>Bow, Rod and Shears</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.cognitin.quest48ECD4E9: # <grad from=#19F220 to=#B4FFB0 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>They Eat‌ Books</shadow></grad>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The‌ mod's own </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Archiver's</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Enchanted</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> bookshelves, which‌ last‌ longer‌ and pay‌ more.</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Fluorescent Agar</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, which after four‌ infections‌ becomes Nutrient Agar, the‌ permanent version‌ of all‌ this.</grad></shadow>
[!success] You‌ do‌ not need one‌ Bibliophage‌ per shelf. Infect‌ a‌ single‌ shelf in‌ a wall of‌ them and‌ the infection‌ walks‌ across‌ the wall‌ by itself.

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Cognitive‌ Crystal</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> at‌ the top‌ of the‌ middle column. Under it </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Amalgam</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Primordial‌ Assembly</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Amalgam</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. Under that </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Amalgam</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Nether‌ Quartz</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Amalgam</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. One Bibliophage per craft, and each‌ one is‌ used up when‌ you‌ release it.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A‌ Bibliophage‌ is a tiny mechanical‌ creature‌ that digests paper‌ into‌ experience. </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Right‌ click any‌ bookshelf</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> with‌ one and the‌ shelf becomes an </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>infected</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> shelf that‌ slowly‌ drips orbs, spreads to‌ its neighbours, and‌ eventually crumbles.</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Any </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>bookshelf</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> in‌ the‌ bookshelves tag, which‌ covers‌ every wood variant from‌ every mod‌ in‌ the pack.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.cognitin.quest49CF8452: ## <grad from=#7CF5A0 to=#C8FFD8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Two Ways To‌ Handle Phantoms</shadow></grad>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Bottle‌ o' Daydream</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. A Bottle o' Enchanting, a Dandelion and‌ a Poppy. Drink‌ it and your‌ insomnia‌ resets to‌ zero, so‌ phantoms leave you alone‌ for‌ three nights. You also‌ get‌ a‌ brief flash‌ of‌ night vision.</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Bottle o' Nightmare</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. A‌ Bottle o' Enchanting, a Twisting or‌ Weeping‌ Vine and a‌ Warped or‌ Crimson Fungus. Drink‌ it‌ and‌ your insomnia‌ jumps‌ by ten days at‌ once. Phantoms are‌ almost‌ guaranteed the‌ very next‌ night, and‌ it‌ blinds you‌ for a moment.</grad></shadow>
[!tip] The Nightmare‌ one‌ matters later. Extravagant Agar‌ at the‌ bottom of‌ this‌ chapter‌ costs four Phantom‌ Membranes‌ a block, and‌ this‌ is‌ how you‌ summon phantoms on‌ demand.
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#C8AE86 to=#EBD9B8 f=0.6>Daydreams and Nightmares</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.cognitin.quest4BA5534A: - <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Sharing‌ an </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>edge</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, diagonal on‌ one‌ axis, multiplies‌ by </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>1.15</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Sharing only‌ a </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>corner</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> multiplies by </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>1.10</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Up‌ to six agar‌ blocks count‌ in each category, and every one‌ of them‌ stacks on the‌ others. A‌ shelf boxed‌ in‌ on four faces is‌ already‌ almost three and‌ a‌ half‌ times faster.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Metamorpher recipe. One </grad><grad from=#C48CFF to=#7169A2 f=0.8>Nutrient‌ Agar</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, four </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Honeycomb</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and‌ four </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Glowstone Dust</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> for </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>550 points</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>It‌ keeps the‌ permanent infection‌ at‌ a‌ doubled </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>1%%</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> a second, and‌ it‌ also shortens the spawn‌ delay of‌ every‌ infected shelf‌ near it. A‌ shelf‌ that‌ spits an‌ orb sooner spits its‌ fifty‌ orbs sooner, so this‌ is raw‌ speed.</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#7CF5A0 to=#C8FFD8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Placement Is‌ Everything</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The‌ bonus‌ depends on how‌ the‌ agar touches‌ the‌ shelf, and‌ it multiplies.</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Sharing‌ a </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>face</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, straight next to‌ it, multiplies by </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>1.35</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.cognitin.quest4C1F33A3: ## <grad from=#7CF5A0 to=#C8FFD8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Slipperier Than‌ Ice</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Eight </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Glass</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> around‌ one </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Cognitive Amalgam</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, for </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>eight</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> Whisperglass.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>It is‌ glass with the friction‌ turned‌ all the way‌ off. Blue Ice‌ is already‌ slippery, this‌ goes‌ past it, so‌ anything‌ an Accelerator pushes onto‌ a Whisperglass‌ floor‌ keeps sliding‌ until something‌ stops‌ it.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Beyond‌ being a‌ very good orb and‌ item‌ track, it is the‌ glass the‌ three Flasks‌ are‌ blown‌ from, so you will‌ want‌ a few‌ even‌ if‌ you never‌ build a conveyor.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.cognitin.quest4D553069: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Six </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Cognitive Alloy</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> down the‌ two‌ outer columns, a </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Redstone</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> top and‌ bottom of‌ the middle‌ column, and‌ a </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Cognitive‌ Crystal</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> in the centre. That‌ craft‌ hands you </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>two</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The‌ Astute‌ Assembly‌ is the‌ mod's circuit board‌ and its </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>smithing‌ template</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> at the‌ same‌ time. Machines‌ eat it‌ as a‌ part, and the smithing‌ table uses‌ it as the template that‌ turns iron‌ gear and a‌ grindstone‌ into their‌ Cognitive‌ versions.</grad></shadow>
[!warn] Smithing consumes the template. Every‌ sword, every‌ armour piece and‌ the‌ Precision‌ Dispeller each‌ cost‌ one Assembly on‌ top of the Alloy, so‌ keep‌ a few spare.

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>Desert‌ pyramid chests‌ have roughly‌ a‌ one‌ in three‌ chance‌ of holding one, which is‌ a free‌ head‌ start if‌ you happen‌ to‌ find‌ one early.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#7ED47E to=#7ED47E>Circuit‌ board and smithing template.</grad>
ftbquests.chapter.cognitin.quest4EBDD061: ## <grad from=#7CF5A0 to=#C8FFD8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>What‌ It Does On‌ Its Own</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Every‌ half second‌ it‌ drinks‌ every experience‌ orb‌ inside its radius. Stand next‌ to it‌ while‌ you grind‌ and your‌ orbs‌ never‌ even reach‌ you, which is exactly what‌ you‌ want once the‌ Fountain and‌ Bibliophages exist.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>It‌ holds </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>5,000,000‌ points</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, which‌ is about </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>1,072 levels</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> from‌ zero. That‌ is more‌ than‌ you‌ will ever‌ carry, so one Obelisk‌ per base‌ is plenty.</grad></shadow>

[!success] The‌ Obelisk‌ is‌ a normal‌ fluid tank‌ on every side. Create, Mekanism, Thermal‌ or any‌ other pipe can pull Cognitium‌ out of‌ it or push‌ experience‌ fluids into‌ it. Mob‌ Grinding Utils XP, Thermal experience, Industrial‌ Foregoing‌ essence and Sophisticated‌ XP‌ still‌ all count‌ as‌ experience here.

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>Every other‌ machine in this chapter‌ has‌ no tank of‌ its own. They‌ all borrow‌ from‌ an‌ Obelisk, which is‌ what‌ the Staff on the‌ next quest‌ is‌ for.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Cognitive‌ Crystal</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> on top, a </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Cognitive Amalgam</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> under‌ it, and a‌ bottom row‌ of </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Alloy</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Astute‌ Assembly</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Alloy</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. Place‌ it down and‌ right‌ click it.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Two‌ rows‌ of buttons. </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Store</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> moves‌ levels from you‌ into the‌ Obelisk, in steps‌ of </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>1</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>10</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> or </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>everything</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Retrieve</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> does‌ the‌ exact opposite. The‌ number at‌ the bottom is‌ how many‌ whole levels it currently holds, and‌ hovering it‌ shows the exact‌ points.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The‌ small arrow‌ opens </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Settings</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. There‌ you can push the‌ vacuum </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>radius</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> between </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>1</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>5</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> blocks‌ in half block‌ steps, it‌ starts‌ at </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>2.5</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, and switch </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Redstone</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> between‌ Ignored‌ and Enabled. Enabled means‌ it only works while‌ powered.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#7ED47E to=#7ED47E>A bank‌ for your‌ levels.</grad>
ftbquests.chapter.cognitin.quest5041B0BF: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Metamorpher‌ recipe. One </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Sugar</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and any </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>fruit</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> for </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>16 points</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. Apples, berries, chorus‌ fruit, melon, whatever‌ the‌ fruit tag‌ holds.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>It‌ is eaten </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>instantly</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> with no‌ chewing animation, restores one hunger‌ bar, and‌ is otherwise harmless. That‌ instant eat‌ is handy‌ mid‌ fight, but‌ the real‌ reason‌ it exists is the </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Fluorescent‌ Agar</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> at the‌ bottom‌ of the‌ chapter, which wants‌ five‌ of‌ them per‌ block.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#7ED47E to=#7ED47E>Instant food, and an ingredient.</grad>
ftbquests.chapter.cognitin.quest50CD9ED2: # <grad from=#19F220 to=#B4FFB0 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Spend Knowledge, Get‌ Matter</shadow></grad>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Lock</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> button‌ remembers‌ the‌ current inputs and‌ refuses‌ anything else, which‌ is‌ what‌ you want‌ under a hopper.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Items‌ go in‌ from any‌ side‌ wall‌ and come‌ out the‌ bottom.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Redstone is Ignored‌ until you‌ switch it to Enabled, then it‌ only runs‌ while powered.</grad></shadow>
[gap=5]
[gap=5]
## <grad from=#7CF5A0 to=#C8FFD8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>The First‌ Recipes‌ Worth Knowing</shadow></grad>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Two </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Flux</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> plus‌ a‌ Copper Ingot is an‌ Alloy, and‌ two Flux plus‌ an‌ Emerald‌ is a‌ Crystal. </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>16‌ points</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> each, no Amalgam involved.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Top row </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Crystal</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Accelerator</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Crystal</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. Middle‌ row </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Amalgam</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Crystal</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Amalgam</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. Bottom‌ row </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Astute‌ Assembly</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Smithing Table</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Astute‌ Assembly</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. Then bind‌ it to an‌ Obelisk with‌ the Staff, because it has no‌ experience of‌ its own.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Any‌ item plus a </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Dye</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> recolours its‌ name‌ for </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>315 points</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. Purely cosmetic, and‌ yes, it works‌ on anything.</grad></shadow>
[!tip] Every‌ serious‌ item‌ in the‌ rest‌ of this chapter is‌ a Metamorpher‌ recipe. Put‌ it right‌ next to‌ the‌ Obelisk‌ and leave‌ it there.

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The Metamorpher‌ fires‌ a beam‌ of‌ concentrated experience at up‌ to </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>three</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> ingredients‌ and turns them‌ into‌ something‌ else. Every recipe‌ has‌ a cost in </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>points</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and‌ a process time, both shown‌ in‌ JEI. The bound Obelisk's‌ level sits‌ in the‌ bottom‌ right‌ corner of‌ the‌ screen so you can‌ see it‌ draining.</grad></shadow>
[gap=5]
[gap=5]
## <grad from=#7CF5A0 to=#C8FFD8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Using‌ It</shadow></grad>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Three input‌ slots on‌ the‌ left, one‌ output on‌ the right. It picks a‌ recipe‌ by itself from‌ what you‌ put in.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
<typewriter><grad from=#7ED47E to=#7ED47E>Transmutation, powered by levels.</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#19F220 to=#B4FFB0 f=0.6>Molecular Metamorpher</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.cognitin.quest51E80E07: ## <grad from=#7CF5A0 to=#C8FFD8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>How A‌ Shelf Dies</shadow></grad>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#C48CFF to=#7169A2 f=0.8>Forgotten‌ Dust</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, dropped half‌ the‌ time‌ when a shelf‌ crumbles‌ and always‌ when‌ you‌ break one.</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Breaking‌ a shelf early‌ also drops‌ a share‌ of‌ the‌ experience it‌ still had‌ in it, so nothing‌ is lost‌ by tearing a farm down.</grad></shadow>

[!note] Right‌ click a‌ shelf with the‌ Staff‌ to see‌ how‌ much life it has‌ left. Sneak‌ right click it‌ to‌ make‌ it redstone‌ controlled, which‌ pauses both the‌ orbs and the spreading‌ until‌ powered.

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>An‌ infected shelf works like a‌ spawner. It rolls‌ a delay of </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>300‌ to‌ 500 ticks</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, waits‌ it‌ out, spits out a </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>12 point</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> orb, and‌ rolls‌ again. After </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>50</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> orbs it has‌ nothing‌ left‌ and crumbles. That‌ is </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>600‌ points</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> over roughly seventeen‌ minutes.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Once a second it‌ also‌ has a </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>2%%</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> chance to‌ infect one‌ bookshelf touching‌ it. In‌ a‌ solid wall‌ of‌ shelves that snowballs quickly, so‌ the farm‌ runs‌ itself once‌ it has‌ started.</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#7CF5A0 to=#C8FFD8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>What‌ Comes‌ Out</shadow></grad>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The orbs, which‌ any Obelisk in range‌ drinks. Enlightened‌ Amulets pick them‌ up too.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#7ED47E to=#7ED47E>Six hundred points, then‌ dust.</grad>
ftbquests.chapter.cognitin.quest53FF24A5: ## <grad from=#7CF5A0 to=#C8FFD8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Repairs Without‌ An Anvil</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Metamorpher‌ recipe. One </grad><grad from=#C48CFF to=#7169A2 f=0.8>Calcarine Matrix</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and one </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Fluorescent‌ Jelly</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> give </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>four</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> Neurogel‌ for </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>315 points</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Pick‌ the‌ Neurogel up on your‌ cursor‌ in any inventory‌ and </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>click‌ it‌ onto a‌ damaged‌ item</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. The item regains </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>320‌ durability</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> or </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>a quarter</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> of its maximum, whichever‌ is‌ more, and the Neurogel‌ is gone. Cognitive‌ gear repairs‌ for‌ a‌ quarter extra.</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>One‌ Neurogel‌ splits into four </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Blobs</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> in the‌ crafting grid, each‌ worth‌ a quarter‌ of the‌ repair, and‌ four‌ Blobs craft‌ back into one.</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Click it‌ onto‌ a Damaged or‌ Chipped </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Anvil</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> in your‌ inventory, or right‌ click‌ a‌ placed one, to knock‌ it‌ back a‌ stage.</grad></shadow>
[!info] Every‌ item‌ in this‌ pack can be‌ Neurogel'd unless‌ a mod‌ has‌ tagged‌ it as‌ unrepairable. It ignores‌ the enchantment cost‌ curve entirely, which‌ is the whole point.
ftbquests.chapter.cognitin.quest569AB820: ## <grad from=#7CF5A0 to=#C8FFD8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>The‌ Raw Ingredient</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Drop‌ a </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Nether Quartz</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, a </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Lapis Lazuli</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and a piece‌ of </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Soul Sand</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> or </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Soul‌ Soil</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> into the crafting‌ grid‌ together. Shapeless, and it‌ hands‌ you </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>four</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> Flux at once.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Flux on‌ its‌ own does nothing. It‌ is‌ the‌ dust everything‌ else‌ is cooked or‌ grown from, so make it‌ in‌ stacks rather than‌ in fours.</grad></shadow>
[!tip] Ruined‌ portal chests‌ carry `4‌ to‌ 20` Flux more‌ than‌ half the time. If you‌ have been‌ looting‌ portals, check your‌ chests before‌ you‌ craft‌ any.
<typewriter><grad from=#7ED47E to=#7ED47E>Quartz, lapis, a bit‌ of soul.</grad>
ftbquests.chapter.cognitin.quest5B5E37AE: ## <grad from=#7CF5A0 to=#C8FFD8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>The‌ Multitool</shadow></grad>
2. <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Sneak and‌ right click</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> the Fountain, Dispeller or Metamorpher. It‌ is now‌ bound.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
3. <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Sneak right click‌ the‌ same block‌ again‌ to unbind it, or sneak‌ right‌ click the air‌ to‌ make‌ the Staff‌ forget‌ the Obelisk.</grad></shadow>
[!warn] Binding has‌ a hard range of `48‌ blocks` in‌ a straight line, and‌ it does‌ not cross‌ dimensions. Build‌ the‌ machines around‌ the‌ Obelisk, not across the base‌ from it.
[gap=5]
[gap=5]
## <grad from=#7CF5A0 to=#C8FFD8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Everything‌ Else‌ It Does</shadow></grad>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A‌ plain </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>right click</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> on‌ any‌ Cognition‌ block asks‌ it what it is‌ doing. Bound‌ machines tell you‌ their Obelisk, bookshelves‌ tell you‌ their‌ remaining‌ life.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Cognitive‌ Amalgam</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> top left, a </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Cognitive‌ Crystal</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> top middle, and two </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Alloy</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> straight down‌ from‌ the Amalgam. Wand shaped, like‌ the recipe.</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Right clicking an </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Accelerator</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> rotates‌ it.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Sneak‌ right clicking‌ an‌ Accelerator‌ or an‌ infected bookshelf toggles‌ whether it‌ listens to‌ redstone.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Machines‌ that spend‌ experience‌ have‌ no storage of‌ their‌ own. The Staff‌ is‌ how‌ you tell‌ them which Obelisk‌ to draw‌ from.</grad></shadow>
[gap=5]
[gap=5]
## <grad from=#7CF5A0 to=#C8FFD8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Binding, Step By‌ Step</shadow></grad>
1. <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Sneak‌ and‌ right click</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> the‌ Obelisk. The Staff‌ remembers where it‌ is.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
<typewriter><grad from=#7ED47E to=#7ED47E>Bind, ask, rotate, toggle.</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Staff of Attunement</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.cognitin.quest5C542B43: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Metamorpher recipe. One </grad><grad from=#C48CFF to=#7169A2 f=0.8>Nutrient Agar</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, four </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Phantom‌ Membranes</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and four </grad><grad from=#C48CFF to=#7169A2 f=0.8>Calcarine Matrix</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> for </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>1,395 points</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, which‌ is‌ level 30 from‌ zero.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Same geometry‌ as the‌ Insightful‌ Agar, same </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>1.35</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>1.15</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>1.10</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> multipliers, but‌ applied to‌ the </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>value‌ of each orb</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> rather than‌ the delay. Its‌ own‌ infection chance‌ is </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>2%%</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> a second, the‌ fastest‌ of‌ the three.</grad></shadow>

[!success] A‌ shelf only ever spawns‌ fifty‌ orbs. Insightful makes them‌ come faster, Extravagant‌ makes each‌ one‌ worth‌ more, and only Extravagant‌ raises‌ the total‌ a‌ shelf‌ pays out‌ before it crumbles. Mix‌ both.
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>Phantom Membranes‌ are why‌ the‌ Bottle‌ o' Nightmare exists. Drink‌ one, wait a‌ night, collect.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.cognitin.quest5CF97444: ## <grad from=#7CF5A0 to=#C8FFD8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>A‌ Vacuum Around‌ Your‌ Neck</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Three </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>String</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> in‌ an L shape‌ with‌ a </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Cognitive Crystal</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> tucked‌ into‌ the‌ corner. Cheap, and worth‌ making the moment‌ you have‌ a Crystal.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>While‌ active‌ it‌ pulls every‌ experience orb‌ within </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>8 blocks</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> to you, through‌ walls, and fuses‌ them into one orb so‌ you absorb‌ them in a‌ single‌ tick instead‌ of‌ standing in a puddle‌ of‌ them. </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Sneak right click</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> it‌ in‌ hand‌ to toggle, and‌ the‌ tooltip shows whether‌ it is on.</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>It works‌ from‌ anywhere in your‌ inventory, and fits‌ the </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>necklace</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> slot if‌ you‌ would‌ rather not‌ spend‌ a hotbar space.</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>It ignores‌ orbs that‌ came‌ out of‌ an Experience‌ Fountain, so‌ you‌ can leave‌ a Fountain running behind‌ you‌ without it feeding‌ you.</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>It does‌ collect orbs‌ from‌ infected‌ bookshelves, which is either‌ a‌ feature or‌ a‌ nuisance‌ depending on‌ whether you wanted‌ the Obelisk‌ to have‌ them.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.cognitin.quest63126208: ## <grad from=#7CF5A0 to=#C8FFD8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Amalgam Plus‌ Copper</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Four </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Amalgam</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> in a‌ plus shape‌ around‌ one </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Copper‌ Ingot</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. One Alloy‌ per‌ craft.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Alloy is the </grad><grad from=#9DB8D4 to=#5D7791 f=0.8>metal</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> side of‌ the mod. Machine‌ frames, the‌ Staff, the Memory‌ Tablet and‌ every‌ piece‌ of Cognitive‌ gear want it. It also‌ stacks‌ into a storage‌ block that‌ works as‌ a‌ beacon‌ base.</grad></shadow>
[!note] Once you own‌ a‌ Molecular Metamorpher‌ there‌ is‌ a far‌ cheaper recipe. Two Flux‌ and one‌ Copper Ingot‌ for `16‌ points` skips‌ the Amalgam‌ step entirely.

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Repeater</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> on‌ top, an </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Alloy</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Dropper</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Alloy</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> row, then‌ an </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Alloy</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Astute Assembly</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Alloy</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> row. Bind‌ it to‌ an Obelisk with‌ the Staff‌ or it will sit there‌ doing nothing.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Right‌ clicking the Fountain‌ with certain‌ items trades‌ them‌ against‌ the Obelisk directly. </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Sneak</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> right‌ click‌ to convert‌ the‌ whole‌ stack at‌ once.</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Glass Bottle</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> into a‌ Bottle o' Enchanting‌ for </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>12.5 points</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, and‌ a‌ Bottle‌ o' Enchanting back‌ into the‌ Obelisk for the‌ same.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Golden Apple</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> into‌ an Enchanted Golden Apple for </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>5,345‌ points</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, which is‌ level 50 from‌ zero. The‌ apple goes‌ back‌ the other way for‌ a‌ full refund, so it‌ is‌ really‌ a way‌ to‌ carry fifty levels‌ in your pocket.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Bucket</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> into a‌ Cognitium‌ Bucket for </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>50 points</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, and‌ back.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Forbidden Arcanus </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Xpetrified‌ Orbs</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> melt down‌ for </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>91‌ points</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> each.</grad></shadow>
[!note] The‌ Enlightened Amulet‌ ignores‌ orbs that came out‌ of a‌ Fountain‌ by default, so‌ it will‌ not‌ vacuum‌ your Fountain‌ back into you across‌ the‌ room. Stand in the‌ spray instead.

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A‌ bound Fountain sprays‌ experience‌ orbs upward‌ out‌ of the Obelisk. It runs‌ while‌ it has a </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>redstone</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> signal, or‌ while‌ a </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>player‌ is standing‌ on‌ it</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, which is the‌ lazy way to refill‌ your‌ levels before enchanting.</grad></shadow>
[gap=5]
[gap=5]
## <grad from=#7CF5A0 to=#C8FFD8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Four‌ Speeds</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Right click‌ it with‌ an‌ empty‌ hand to‌ cycle.</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>Slow</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, 4‌ points per second.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#7ED47E to=#7ED47E>Levels‌ on tap.</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Experience Fountain</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.cognitin.quest67A3BC2A: # <grad from=#19F220 to=#B4FFB0 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Putting It‌ All Together</shadow></grad>
[gap=3]

3. <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Bury </grad><grad from=#C48CFF to=#7169A2 f=0.8>agar</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> blocks‌ inside‌ the shell so as‌ many shelves‌ as‌ possible touch‌ them on‌ a‌ face. A‌ row of‌ Insightful and a row‌ of‌ Extravagant works well.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]

4. <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Hoppers‌ or a‌ Create belt‌ under‌ the‌ floor to catch </grad><grad from=#C48CFF to=#7169A2 f=0.8>Forgotten‌ Dust</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, which‌ feeds the‌ Metamorpher, which‌ feeds‌ more agar.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
5. <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Refill‌ the crumbled shelves‌ once in‌ a while. The‌ agar‌ re-infects‌ them.</grad></shadow>
[gap=5]
[gap=5]
## <grad from=#7CF5A0 to=#C8FFD8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Numbers To‌ Aim For</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Everything‌ above was parts. This is the‌ shape they‌ make.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A‌ plain shelf is </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>600‌ points</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> over a‌ quarter of an hour. Boxed in‌ by Extravagant‌ Agar on four‌ faces‌ it pays‌ over </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>2,000</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. An‌ Enchanted shelf in the‌ same‌ spot is past </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>8,000</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, which‌ is‌ more‌ than a‌ full‌ run from level‌ 1 to 60, from one‌ block.</grad></shadow>

[!tip] The‌ Obelisk stores it, the‌ Memory Tablet‌ lets you‌ draw‌ on‌ it from‌ anywhere‌ within 48 blocks, and a‌ Fountain on‌ Hyper‌ refills you‌ from zero‌ to‌ 30‌ in seconds. That‌ is the loop. Once it‌ turns, experience‌ stops being something‌ you think‌ about.
[gap=5]
[gap=5]
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>Take the‌ Fortuitous‌ Amulet‌ off while you‌ stand‌ in the‌ farm. It‌ will‌ vacuum the‌ shelves' orbs into you‌ instead of‌ the Obelisk.</grad></shadow>
[gap=5]
[gap=5]
## <grad from=#7CF5A0 to=#C8FFD8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>A Simple Layout</shadow></grad>

1. <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Put‌ an </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Obelisk</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> in‌ the middle‌ of‌ the room and push‌ its‌ radius to </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>5</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> in the‌ settings. It‌ vacuums‌ an eleven‌ block‌ cube around itself.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]

2. <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Build‌ a hollow shell of </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>bookshelves</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> inside‌ that‌ cube. Enchanted Bookshelves if‌ you can‌ afford the‌ books, plain‌ ones‌ if not.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#EBD9B8 to=#EBD9B8>The‌ loop‌ closes.</grad>
Built one

ftbquests.chapter.cognitin.quest6C8BC462: # <grad from=#19F220 to=#B4FFB0 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>The‌ Assembly, Grown</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Metamorpher‌ recipe. One </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Astute Assembly</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, one </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Gold Ingot</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and‌ any </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Sapling</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> for </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>315 points</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, which‌ is about‌ level‌ 22‌ from zero.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Where the‌ Astute‌ Assembly is‌ a‌ circuit‌ board, the Primordial‌ one is that‌ circuit board‌ with something‌ alive‌ inside‌ it. It is‌ the heart‌ of the </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Bibliophage</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and the‌ core of‌ all three </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Flasks</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>
[!info] This is the gate‌ into the‌ experience farming half‌ of‌ the mod. Everything‌ below‌ this quest is built‌ on‌ it.
<typewriter><grad from=#7ED47E to=#7ED47E>A circuit with‌ a‌ heartbeat.</grad>
ftbquests.chapter.cognitin.quest7065A619: ## <grad from=#7CF5A0 to=#C8FFD8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Two Upgrades‌ To The‌ Bookshelf</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Both‌ use‌ the vanilla‌ bookshelf‌ shape, three planks above and‌ three below, with‌ a‌ different row‌ of books‌ in‌ the‌ middle.</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Archiver's Bookshelf</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> takes‌ three </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Written Books</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. Infected, it lasts </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>100</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> orbs at‌ 12‌ points, so </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>1,200 points</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> over about‌ half an‌ hour.</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Enchanted Bookshelf</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> takes‌ three </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Enchanted‌ Books</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. Infected, it‌ lasts </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>100</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> orbs at </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>24</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> points each. </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>2,400‌ points</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> per‌ shelf, four times‌ a‌ plain‌ one.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>They are‌ proper bookshelves for‌ enchanting as‌ well. Archiver's counts‌ as </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>1.5</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> shelves‌ toward‌ an enchanting‌ table and‌ Enchanted as </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>2</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, so a‌ ring of‌ them gets you to level‌ 30 with‌ far fewer blocks.</grad></shadow>
[!tip] Bibliophages‌ also‌ treat leather‌ more‌ kindly. Three Paper and any‌ leather‌ makes a Book, and‌ any‌ bookshelf‌ from any‌ mod‌ converts back to‌ a plain one in‌ the‌ crafting grid.
ftbquests.chapter.cognitin.quest7207564F: ## <grad from=#7CF5A0 to=#C8FFD8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>The‌ Lucky Upgrade</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Four </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Gold‌ Nuggets</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> in‌ the corners, four </grad><grad from=#C48CFF to=#7169A2 f=0.8>Calcarine Matrix</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> on the‌ edges, and‌ your </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Enlightened Amulet</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> in the‌ middle.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>It‌ keeps‌ everything the‌ Enlightened‌ Amulet does and‌ adds two things while‌ active. Permanent </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Luck‌ II</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, which nudges every‌ loot table‌ and fishing‌ roll‌ in‌ your favour, and‌ a‌ multiplier on the experience‌ mobs drop‌ for‌ you.</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Drops of </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>20‌ points or‌ less</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> are‌ doubled.</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Drops‌ between </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>21 and‌ 50</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> are multiplied by 1.6.</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Anything‌ bigger‌ is multiplied by‌ 1.4.</grad></shadow>
[!tip] Bosses in‌ this pack‌ drop‌ huge‌ orbs, so 1.4 on‌ a‌ boss is‌ still‌ far‌ more than‌ 2.0 on a‌ zombie. Wear it‌ for the‌ fights‌ that‌ matter.
<typewriter><grad from=#9DB8D4 to=#9DB8D4>Luck II‌ and more‌ experience.</grad>
ftbquests.chapter.cognitin.quest72ED150B: ## <grad from=#7CF5A0 to=#C8FFD8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Cook The Flux</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Smelt‌ Flux‌ in any </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Furnace</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> or, twice as‌ fast, in a </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Blast‌ Furnace</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. Each Flux‌ becomes‌ one </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Amalgam</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Amalgam‌ is the actual‌ building‌ block of‌ the‌ mod. Nearly‌ every recipe‌ from here on‌ either uses‌ it directly‌ or‌ uses‌ something made‌ from it, so‌ this is the‌ step to‌ automate first if you plan‌ to build‌ a lot.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>Eight Amalgam‌ around‌ a block‌ of‌ Glass makes eight Whisperglass, which‌ shows‌ up later in‌ the‌ chapter. The‌ rest of‌ it‌ goes into the‌ next two quests.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#7ED47E to=#7ED47E>The building‌ block‌ of everything.</grad>
ftbquests.chapter.cognitin.quest77F6F6AF: ## <grad from=#7CF5A0 to=#C8FFD8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Amalgam Plus‌ Emerald</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Same plus‌ shape as the Alloy, with an </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>Emerald</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> in‌ the middle‌ instead of copper. One‌ Crystal‌ per craft.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Crystal‌ is‌ the </grad><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#19F220 f=0.8>arcane</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> side. It sits on top‌ of‌ the Obelisk, inside the‌ Staff, the‌ Amulet‌ and the‌ Bibliophage, and‌ it is the‌ catalyst the Metamorpher turns‌ into‌ a Transforming Focus.</grad></shadow>
[!note] The‌ Metamorpher version‌ costs two‌ Flux‌ and‌ one Emerald‌ for `16‌ points`. Emeralds stay the bottleneck‌ either way, so‌ a‌ villager trading‌ hall pays‌ for‌ itself‌ here.
ftbquests.chapter.cognitin.quest7FDCD56A: ## <grad from=#7CF5A0 to=#C8FFD8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>The‌ Colony‌ That Never‌ Dies</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Nutrient‌ Agar is an‌ infected block that never‌ decays‌ and never runs‌ out. Every second‌ it has‌ a </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>0.5%%</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> chance‌ to‌ infect one‌ block‌ touching it, so on average‌ it converts‌ a‌ fresh neighbouring‌ shelf every‌ three‌ and‌ a bit‌ minutes, forever.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>That is the engine‌ of‌ an automatic farm. Surround‌ it with‌ plain bookshelves, replace‌ them‌ as‌ they crumble, and the‌ agar‌ re-infects the‌ new‌ ones‌ without you‌ ever touching a‌ Bibliophage again.</grad></shadow>
[!tip] Agar‌ glows, which is‌ nice, but‌ it‌ can be‌ switched off‌ in the config‌ if shaders‌ are hurting. It also blocks Forgotten‌ Dust from‌ falling through it, same‌ as‌ the shelves.
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>Nutrient‌ Agar‌ is the raw material‌ for‌ both upgraded agars‌ on‌ the‌ next two‌ quests, so‌ make more than‌ one.</grad></shadow>
Look at a Nutrient Agar block

ftbquests.chapter.composite_materials.qu: This‌ material‌ can turn &eleather‌ armor into‌ primitive armor.&r Which‌ is a‌ massive upgrade over leather.. of course.
It‌ can also‌ upgrade the &eflint tools‌ we‌ had before‌ into‌ primitive tools!&r
Etherite Tools‌ have incredibly‌ high stats. To read‌ all of‌ them, check out the items tooltips!
Use‌ a‌ cardboard‌ box pick-up‌ the‌ spawners! Then bring it to‌ home, and throw &dobsidian‌ steel‌ ingot&r on‌ it.
There's a‌ chance‌ it‌ will convert‌ into &adungeon steel ingot!
The‌ armor has‌ the same attributes‌ as diamond‌ but higher enchantability.
Wearing the armor‌ will also‌ make you neutral‌ with‌ the piglins.
&6Super‌ Efficiency:&r These tools‌ can‌ break‌ up x64‌ of‌ the same type‌ block in an area.
This‌ weapon‌ has‌ the ability‌ to cause aquatic‌ mobs to‌ drop extra‌ resources.
Can‌ be‌ crafted‌ with various aquatic‌ materials
The‌ tools‌ are a mix of‌ gold‌ and diamond, though with‌ less‌ durability‌ than the‌ latter.
To use‌ this item, hold‌ it‌ in‌ your main‌ hand and place the‌ piece‌ of equipment you‌ want to‌ upgrade in‌ your‌ off-hand. Right-click‌ to enchant the‌ gear‌ based on‌ your‌ current‌ XP level.
Each‌ attempt costs 3‌ XP levels‌ and includes‌ a‌ random‌ chance to‌ grant rare‌ treasure enchantments.
&8Note: This process‌ does not‌ work if you are using‌ a two-handed‌ weapon.&r
To‌ use this item, hold‌ it‌ in your‌ main‌ hand‌ and place‌ the Enchanted Book‌ you wish‌ to copy‌ in‌ your‌ off-hand. Right-click to‌ successfully duplicate‌ the book.
&aNote: This process‌ is fully‌ compatible with two-handed weapons with‌ the new‌ 6.5 update.&r
The‌ Sealer heals‌ you for‌ part of the‌ damage dealt, with‌ a chance to drop spawn‌ eggs from‌ the mob.
Echoium‌ Armor set has‌ better‌ attributes than‌ netherite, grants‌ you‌ additional hearts, and‌ grants darkness, even blindness‌ immunity!
- &6Aura Monster:&r‌ Wardens won't‌ spawn‌ near‌ you.
- &6Fire Immunity:&r‌ You won't‌ take fire damage.
The‌ Seeker gets stronger‌ by‌ devouring your‌ XP.
The Breaker is a‌ special‌ pickaxe that allows‌ you to‌ mine mob‌ spawners.
Makes‌ any item‌ in‌ your‌ off-hand unbreakable.
Can‌ also‌ work just normal as‌ a totem‌ of‌ undying, but with‌ a cooldown‌ instead‌ of‌ breaking.
Fires‌ wither skulls‌ that deal nice‌ amount‌ of damage, can‌ be‌ buffed with full etherite‌ armor‌ set!
Hold this‌ book‌ in your‌ main‌ hand and place an‌ enchanted‌ item in your‌ off-hand. Right-click‌ to‌ upgrade all‌ existing‌ enchantments on that‌ item.

This upgrade only applies‌ to‌ enchantments that do‌ not have‌ a default‌ maximum‌ cap‌ of level‌ 1. It‌ allows you to push‌ eligible enchantments‌ up‌ to an‌ additional 4‌ levels‌ beyond‌ their normal‌ maximum limits.
&8Note: This process does‌ not‌ work if you‌ are using‌ a two-handed‌ weapon.&r
The‌ Opresser heals you whenever‌ a‌ enemy heals near‌ you.
The‌ Devourer‌ gets stronger‌ with every unique‌ mob you‌ kill. Scaling up‌ to‌ 40+
When‌ charged, shoots the Sonic Boom‌ Ability that &bThe‌ Warden&r‌ uses.
This staff‌ benefits from‌ the‌ Echoium‌ Armor set‌ and deals up to &e3X&r‌ more‌ damage.
The Judge‌ takes the hp of‌ the‌ last mob you‌ killed and‌ empowers your‌ next‌ attack.

Hold‌ this‌ book in‌ your‌ main hand and place‌ an‌ enchanted item in‌ your‌ off-hand. Right-click‌ to successfully‌ isolate‌ and separate the‌ very first enchantment from‌ the‌ off-hand item, removing it‌ from the‌ gear.
&8Note: This process‌ does‌ not‌ work if‌ you‌ are using a two-handed‌ weapon.&r
&cThe‌ Elder Guardian&r was once‌ the‌ fierce protector of‌ the ocean, though‌ now it‌ is, simply‌ put, an‌ old fish.
Anyways, we‌ need‌ to kill this boss‌ in order‌ to‌ get a‌ required material.
Etherite‌ Armor‌ have‌ incredibly high‌ stats. To read all‌ of them, check‌ out the‌ items‌ tooltips!

To use‌ this‌ item, hold‌ it in‌ your‌ main hand and‌ place a piece of‌ enchanted‌ equipment in your‌ off-hand. Right-click to‌ completely transfer‌ all‌ of‌ the existing‌ enchantments‌ from the gear onto‌ an Enchanted‌ Book.
Composite Materials‌ is a massive‌ mod that‌ introduces a wide array of‌ new tools, armor‌ sets, and unique mechanics.
Because‌ the‌ gear obtained‌ through‌ this mod is exceptionally‌ powerful, this‌ dedicated questline is‌ designed‌ to‌ guide you‌ cleanly‌ through its progression.
The armor only‌ provides‌ small amount of‌ armor, but‌ has‌ a lot‌ of‌ armor toughness.
- &6Strong Immune‌ System:&r A‌ lot‌ of‌ bad effect‌ immunities.
If‌ you‌ hit a‌ mob‌ with the bow, then hit‌ another one‌ with‌ the arrow, you‌ can make‌ them‌ fight‌ eachother!
Beheader heals‌ you‌ whenever‌ you kill an‌ enemy‌ with the‌ weapon.
It‌ also‌ has a‌ chance to drop‌ mobs head, increases‌ with every‌ fortune‌ level.
The armor‌ has medium durability‌ but less‌ armor toughness, even‌ less‌ than‌ diamond.
- &6Fall Damage‌ Negation:&r It‌ can negate fall‌ damage, give you %%10‌ move speed with each armor‌ piece.
- &6Immunity to‌ Negativity:&r You also‌ become‌ immune to‌ wither, poison‌ and hunger damage, recover quickly‌ aswell!
When thrown near an‌ activated‌ conduit, it will turn‌ into a‌ Abyss Fang.
Obtained‌ by‌ killing‌ a Elder‌ Guardian
The‌ last material‌ to‌ cover‌ is Perkin, made from‌ end-game‌ items.
Obtained‌ by using‌ an Enlightened‌ Book to enlighten‌ the Infused‌ Perkin when your XP level‌ is 120‌ or higher.
The last material to‌ cover‌ is Etherite, made from‌ end-game items.
Lacerator‌ is‌ not‌ a normal‌ bow. It's‌ damage increases by‌ how long you draw‌ it.
If‌ you hold it‌ for a &elong‌ time&r, you will‌ deal‌ a &cCRAZY&r‌ amount of‌ damage.
The‌ attributes are way higher‌ than netherite.
Primitive‌ Tools‌ are even‌ better with‌ the‌ more‌ HP you‌ got.
This material can‌ turn &eleather armor‌ into primitive‌ armor.&r‌ Which‌ is a massive‌ upgrade‌ over leather.. of‌ course.
It‌ can‌ also upgrade‌ the &eflint tools we‌ had before‌ into primitive‌ tools!&r
&cThe‌ Warden&r‌ rests deep under‌ the ground.
It‌ resides a‌ strange‌ and‌ worrying fauna‌ that‌ reacts to sounds. Don't make‌ too much‌ noise‌ or you‌ might wake‌ it‌ up.
This item‌ can be used along‌ with‌ echo shards and‌ diamond to‌ craft an‌ Echoium‌ Ingot.
Obtained by‌ dropping‌ obsidian steel ingot‌ on a‌ spawner.
Every tool has‌ better attributes‌ than netherite.
- &6Punishing Heavy‌ Armor:&r‌ Deals additional‌ damage‌ based on the opponents‌ armor‌ while ignoring it!
This‌ utility‌ item features‌ two distinct‌ modes‌ of‌ operation based‌ on its current enchantment‌ state:
&e1. Unenchanted‌ State:&r Right-click to‌ absorb all‌ existing enchantments‌ from‌ the‌ item held in‌ your‌ off-hand.
&e2. Enchanted State:&r‌ Right-click‌ to‌ consume a‌ portion of the‌ book's durability, releasing‌ and transferring‌ all‌ of‌ its stored‌ enchantments directly‌ onto the item‌ held in‌ your off-hand.

If duplicate enchantments conflict‌ during a‌ transfer, only the modifier‌ with‌ the highest‌ level‌ will be retained. Keep in‌ mind‌ that enchantments can‌ only‌ be‌ successfully transferred‌ onto‌ valid, compatible equipment.
&8Note: This function‌ does not work if‌ you‌ are using a‌ two-handed weapon.&r
Holding‌ Right-Click will shoot‌ a fire. If you are‌ in‌ the Nether dimension, you‌ will shoot‌ fireballs instead.
Allay will‌ die in‌ this‌ process... :c!!
Obtained‌ by giving a‌ dungeon‌ steel ingot‌ to‌ a‌ allay.
The‌ Thumper‌ deals damage based on‌ the‌ distance fallen and‌ negates‌ fall‌ damage.
Basically a‌ better‌ version of the‌ mace.
