## <grad from=#D95C24 to=#FFDCA8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Buttons</shadow></grad>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Sort by name, by hunger, by saturation, or by </grad><grad from=#FFD08A to=#E0662E f=0.8>not eaten yet</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> once you carry the Food Book.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>An ingredient with several options cycles in the recipe view. Scroll on it to pick one, right-click to </grad><grad from=#FFD08A to=#E0662E f=0.8>lock</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> it.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#F07A34 to=#F07A34>Michelin star when</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#F07A34 to=#FFE6BE f=0.6>Cooking Table</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Every Farmer's Delight </grad><grad from=#9BEC86 to=#3FBF4F f=0.8>cabinet</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> is a kitchen counter with a wooden face: it connects and it stores.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Recipes that need a </grad><grad from=#9BEC86 to=#3FBF4F f=0.8>Milk Bottle</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> draw it from the Milk Jar at a quarter bucket each.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#57D165 to=#57D165>Rustic fridge</grad>
Any Farmer's Delight cabinet
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#57D165 to=#C3F7B8 f=0.6>Cabinets and Bottles</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A little terminal that sits on the counter and plugs the kitchen into an </grad><grad from=#CFDDEE to=#7C9CC4 f=0.8>ME network</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. The cooking table then cooks out of your whole storage system.</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#6F92BE to=#CFE2F6 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Modes</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Right-click it to switch what flows where.</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#CFDDEE to=#7C9CC4 f=0.8>Both ways</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>: the kitchen sees the network and the network sees the kitchen blocks.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#CFDDEE to=#7C9CC4 f=0.8>ME to kitchen</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>: only the cooking table pulls from the network.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#CFDDEE to=#7C9CC4 f=0.8>Kitchen to ME</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>: only the network can see the counters and fridges.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A priority page decides where the network stores things first.</grad></shadow>
[gap=5]
[gap=5]
[gap=5]
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Costs a Toaster, a Milk Jar, an ME Chest, two fluix glass cables, a 16k storage component, an engineering processor and both cookbooks.</grad></shadow>
[gap=5]
## <grad from=#6F92BE to=#CFE2F6 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Linking</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Put the station into the slot of an </grad><grad from=#CFDDEE to=#7C9CC4 f=0.8>ME Wireless Access Point</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, the same way a wireless terminal is linked. Place it within that access point's range, in the same dimension, and it lights up.</grad></shadow>
[gap=5]
[gap=5]
<typewriter><grad from=#8FB3DC to=#8FB3DC>Cloud kitchen</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#8FB3DC to=#DCEBFA f=0.6>ME Kitchen Station</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A </grad><grad from=#FFD08A to=#E0662E f=0.8>Furnace</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> in iron with black glass on top. It cooks anything a furnace cooks, as long as the result is </grad><grad from=#FFD08A to=#E0662E f=0.8>food</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. Ores stay out.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Three input slots feed nine cooking slots, so it works through a whole stack at once. Fuel burns </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>three times faster</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> than in a furnace, so keep it stocked.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Once it touches the kitchen, the cooking table sends smelting recipes to it on its own.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Dye an oven in a crafting grid to recolour it.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#F07A34 to=#F07A34>Ratatouille moment</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#F07A34 to=#FFE6BE f=0.6>Oven</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Drop an </grad><grad from=#CFDDEE to=#7C9CC4 f=0.8>Anvil</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> on a cow that is standing on or beside a Milk Jar. The cow goes into the jar and stays there, making </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>1 mB</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> of milk every tick, a bucket every </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>50 seconds</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Works on any mooshroom too.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#8FB3DC to=#8FB3DC>Moo</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#8FB3DC to=#DCEBFA f=0.6>Cow in a Jar</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Three slabs over two iron nuggets. Two hooks on a wall, and whatever hangs there is available to every recipe in the kitchen.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Hang a </grad><grad from=#FFE1A0 to=#E8A22E f=0.8>Knife</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> on it and the cutting board recipes stop asking for one in your inventory.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#F0B23A to=#F0B23A>Knife rights</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#F0B23A to=#FFF0CC f=0.6>Tool Rack</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Glass around a </grad><grad from=#CFDDEE to=#7C9CC4 f=0.8>Milk Bucket</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and a plank. Holds </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>32</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> buckets of milk and pours it into any recipe that needs some.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Milk bottles from Farmer's Delight cost the jar </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>250 mB</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, a quarter of a bucket.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#8FB3DC to=#8FB3DC>Got milk?</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#8FB3DC to=#DCEBFA f=0.6>Milk Jar</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Iron, a trapdoor, a stone button and a </grad><grad from=#FFD08A to=#E0662E f=0.8>Lava Bucket</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. Drop two slices of bread in, press it, and </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>60 seconds</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> later they pop out toasted.</grad></shadow>
[!warn] Toast that goes in a second time comes out as charcoal.
<typewriter><grad from=#F07A34 to=#F07A34>Do not toast twice</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#F07A34 to=#FFE6BE f=0.6>Toaster</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Two things reward you for eating well, and both have their own chapter.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Every </grad><grad from=#FF9AA2 to=#D6455C f=0.8>new food</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> you try counts toward extra hearts. Twenty five different foods is </grad><grad from=#FF9AA2 to=#D6455C f=0.8>ten hearts</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Big meals also grant a timed </grad><grad from=#FF9AA2 to=#D6455C f=0.8>combat buff</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>: Well Fed, Plenty Satisfied or Exquisitely Stuffed, up to </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>15 percent</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> damage and speed.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The pot and cutting board meals are the strongest food in the pack, and this kitchen cooks them too.</grad></shadow>
Spice of Life
Farmer's Delight
<typewriter><grad from=#F05A70 to=#F05A70>Not just for hunger</grad>
Got it
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#F05A70 to=#FFCBD1 f=0.6>Why Cook At All?</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The first book in a crafting grid on its own. It stops filtering by your inventory and lists </grad><grad from=#FFE1A0 to=#E8A22E f=0.8>every food recipe</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> the pack knows, so you can plan a meal before you own a single ingredient.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Smelt it again to turn it back into the filtered book.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#CFC3AE to=#CFC3AE>Show me everything</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#CFC3AE to=#FBF7F0 f=0.6>No Filter Edition</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A chest and an </grad><grad from=#CFDDEE to=#7C9CC4 f=0.8>Iron Door</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. Holds </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>27</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> stacks and hands them to the cooking table.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Stack a second fridge on top and the two merge into one tall fridge with </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>54</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> slots. Dye it by right-clicking with any dye.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Two upgrades go in with a right-click: the Ice Unit and the Preservation Chamber.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#8FB3DC to=#8FB3DC>Chest with a door</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#8FB3DC to=#DCEBFA f=0.6>Fridge</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Stone over terracotta. No storage, they only carry the connection around a bend so an L shaped kitchen stays one kitchen.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The </grad><grad from=#FFE1A0 to=#E8A22E f=0.8>Hanging Corner</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> does the same for cabinets.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#F0B23A to=#F0B23A>L shaped kitchen</grad>
Any corner
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#F0B23A to=#FFF0CC f=0.6>Corners</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The first book between two </grad><grad from=#FFE1A0 to=#E8A22E f=0.8>Crafting Tables</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, with a </grad><grad from=#FFE1A0 to=#E8A22E f=0.8>Diamond</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> above and below. This one does not just show the recipe, it </grad><grad from=#FFE1A0 to=#E8A22E f=0.8>crafts it</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> from your inventory when you click the entry.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Shift-click crafts a stack. It is also the ingredient for the Cooking Table.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#F0B23A to=#F0B23A>Diamonds for a cookbook</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#F0B23A to=#FFF0CC f=0.6>Cooking for Blockheads II</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Coal and quartz blocks in a checker make </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>12</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> tiles. A run of floor carries the kitchen connection across the room, so the fridge does not have to touch the counter.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Sixteen colours, from dye.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#F0B23A to=#F0B23A>Wireless, sort of</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#F0B23A to=#FFF0CC f=0.6>Kitchen Floor</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Iron on top, terracotta around a </grad><grad from=#CFDDEE to=#7C9CC4 f=0.8>Water Bucket</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. The sink never runs out: right-click it with a bottle or a bucket to fill it, and every recipe that calls for water takes it from here.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Dyeable, like the counters.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#8FB3DC to=#8FB3DC>Infinite water hack</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#8FB3DC to=#DCEBFA f=0.6>Sink</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Smelt a </grad><grad from=#FFE1A0 to=#E8A22E f=0.8>Book</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> in any furnace and it comes out as a cookbook. Right-click it and it lists every food you can make from what is in your inventory right now.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFE1A0 to=#E8A22E f=0.8>Cooking for Blockheads II</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>: crafts straight out of your inventory.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Hover an entry to see its recipe. That is the whole idea of this mod: the kitchen finds the recipe for you, and later it crafts it for you too.</grad></shadow>
[gap=5]
[gap=5]
## <grad from=#DE9A24 to=#FFEBBC f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Three books</shadow></grad>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFE1A0 to=#E8A22E f=0.8>Cooking for Blockheads I</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>: shows what your inventory can cook.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFE1A0 to=#E8A22E f=0.8>No Filter Edition</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>: shows every food recipe in the pack, ingredients or not.</grad></shadow>

ftbquests.chapter.create.quest10331210B1: Copycat blocks‌ let you turn almost‌ any‌ material into steps, panels, and‌ other shapes‌ normally impossible‌ to‌ craft.
ftbquests.chapter.create.quest12830AA7C4: Drilling‌ machine: A device used‌ to‌ extract resources‌ from‌ deep‌ underground.
ftbquests.chapter.create.quest12913E20A8: Allows for‌ the creation‌ of‌ contraptions‌ that move‌ up and‌ down.
ftbquests.chapter.create.quest12C789BF2D: When‌ placed in‌ front‌ of the Encased‌ Fan this allows it‌ to‌ smoke items.
ftbquests.chapter.create.quest13232A19D4: The Package Frogport‌ is‌ your automated delivery‌ hub.
It works‌ with Chain‌ Conveyors‌ and‌ Packagers to send‌ and‌ receive cardboard‌ packages.
To‌ get‌ started, place a‌ Chain Conveyor, right-click the‌ chain, and follow‌ the on-screen‌ guide‌ to‌ position the‌ Frogport correctly.
It‌ must be aligned‌ with the‌ chain to enable package transfers.
Every‌ package must‌ have a destination‌ Frogport.
Without‌ a receiving‌ port‌ at the other end, the‌ package‌ won’t be delivered‌ and‌ the‌ transfer will‌ fail.
ftbquests.chapter.create.quest138F3EB263: The‌ block‌ that‌ deals with‌ train assembly and dissasembly.
ftbquests.chapter.create.quest13D4FF6929: Extends block‌ placing, destroying range. Builders‌ Best‌ Friend!
ftbquests.chapter.create.quest155F388D56: Auto-cuts‌ trees, plants and‌ much‌ more. Excellent for automating farming!
ftbquests.chapter.create.quest155FBDDA1C: Lets you turn‌ off parts‌ of contraptions‌ while‌ they‌ are formed.
ftbquests.chapter.create.quest16B919B6EB: Again kinetic energy‌ but‌ turns more precisely.
ftbquests.chapter.create.quest16CD1CC9F7: Can‌ halve or‌ double the‌ rotational‌ speed‌ of connected‌ chaindrives‌ when it receives a‌ redstone signal.
ftbquests.chapter.create.quest1742597D48: Create is a steampunk‌ mod that‌ lets you build‌ contraptions‌ to do‌ most‌ things you can think‌ of.
Because‌ of this, the chapter‌ is‌ mostly‌ focused on‌ letting‌ you know what‌ exists and giving you‌ a‌ rough outline of‌ the progression‌ of the‌ mod.
ftbquests.chapter.create.quest1864600225: Craft a netherite‌ drill to‌ mine the most‌ powerful‌ and rare‌ resources.
ftbquests.chapter.create.quest19166D31F2: Basically‌ a sign.. that‌ can update‌ the‌ text‌ though.
ftbquests.chapter.create.quest19183F380B: A‌ versatile‌ machine that‌ can‌ pull and push entities, as‌ well‌ as wash, haunt, blast, and smoke‌ items.
ftbquests.chapter.create.quest1A541F8D6F: When placed‌ in‌ front of‌ the Encased‌ Fan‌ this‌ allows it‌ to wash the item.
ftbquests.chapter.create.quest1AA9DCC32A: Collect raw‌ redstone‌ to advance in‌ your mining and crafting‌ progress.
ftbquests.chapter.create.quest1BB020EAC2: By putting‌ a knife‌ or‌ something else‌ on this‌ block‌ can‌ automatate processes‌ like slicing.
ftbquests.chapter.create.quest1C2A5AF20B: When powered, shows the‌ time and‌ plays a tune twice a‌ day.
ftbquests.chapter.create.quest1CE6DB5F87: Chutes‌ are used‌ to transfer between inventories‌ vertically.
ftbquests.chapter.create.quest1FA87B6769: The‌ Redstone Requester links‌ redstone to logistics.
Connected to‌ a‌ Stock Link or‌ Ticker, it requests‌ up to‌ 9‌ items (256‌ each) when powered, delivering‌ them‌ in Cardboard Packages.
ftbquests.chapter.create.quest219E307B85: Reverses‌ the‌ direction of‌ rotation when‌ a‌ redstone‌ signal is‌ applied.
ftbquests.chapter.create.quest21DD4EFBB3: Upgraded version‌ of‌ a Copper Backtank
ftbquests.chapter.create.quest21E30871E9: An advanced item distributor‌ that moves‌ items to specific‌ reachable‌ points.It won’t‌ work‌ if the arm can’t‌ reach‌ and requires SUs‌ to‌ operate.
ftbquests.chapter.create.quest2246A107EC: This‌ machine automatically‌ builds‌ structures from your schematic‌ paper. Just load‌ it‌ with gunpowder, materials, and‌ a clipboard‌ to‌ track‌ everything, and it‌ does the rest.
ftbquests.chapter.create.quest227597F357: Allows‌ for the‌ extraction of liquids‌ from‌ items.
ftbquests.chapter.create.quest293196C72E: Lets‌ you‌ clear and pave‌ while riding‌ a train.
ftbquests.chapter.create.quest29649C6541: A precise‌ lever, can‌ do‌ several levels.
ftbquests.chapter.create.quest2965172775: A Cog Crank works‌ like a‌ Hand‌ Crank, but it’s‌ used to‌ apply‌ rotational‌ force and‌ direction to cogwheels.
ftbquests.chapter.create.quest29EFF7AED6: Lets‌ you instantly break‌ most Create‌ blocks by‌ shift + right-clicking. And‌ rotate‌ them by right-clicking.
ftbquests.chapter.create.quest2A128A8CDD: Decorate‌ your factory‌ or‌ home with these‌ beautiful decals!
ftbquests.chapter.create.quest2AB0806AA6: An upgraded version‌ of Copper‌ Diving Helmet.
ftbquests.chapter.create.quest2BAF5C0938: A‌ useful block‌ for‌ building‌ contraptions.
ftbquests.chapter.create.quest2BC564546A: Allows‌ for contraptions that‌ rotate‌ around a‌ point‌ in space, particularly useful for‌ farms.
ftbquests.chapter.create.quest2C5BDB5E97: Extractor: A tool‌ designed to process‌ raw resources‌ extracted by‌ the‌ drilling‌ machine.
ftbquests.chapter.create.quest2C8EF8E651: In‌ order‌ to get brass you're‌ going to‌ need‌ to heat‌ a mechanical‌ mixer‌ that‌ mixes copper‌ and zinc!
&8The Empty Blaze‌ burner‌ can be filled‌ by right-clicking‌ it on‌ either‌ a‌ blaze spawner or‌ a‌ blaze.
ftbquests.chapter.create.quest2CC43C68A8: It's‌ really confusing but the‌ strongest!
ftbquests.chapter.create.quest2D0B2D0166: Potato‌ Cannons‌ are‌ a classic weapon‌ to‌ have, just remember‌ to‌ have‌ suitable ammo‌ in your inventory‌ or this‌ thing is‌ useless.
ftbquests.chapter.create.quest2DFDE04D13: Craft‌ a sample drill‌ to begin‌ your excavation‌ journey.
ftbquests.chapter.create.quest2E10D93D92: An‌ item used‌ to‌ craft more advanced‌ mechanical items.
ftbquests.chapter.create.quest2EDAEA1566: The‌ Stock Link‌ is‌ the backbone of the‌ Logistics‌ Network, connecting Packagers, Stock Tickers, and‌ other‌ logistics‌ blocks.
Placing a‌ Stock‌ Link creates a‌ network; right-clicking another before placing‌ links‌ them into a‌ shared system‌ with no‌ range‌ limit.
Attach‌ a Stock‌ Link‌ to a Packager, and its‌ inventory becomes‌ accessible‌ to any‌ Ticker, Requester, or Keeper‌ on‌ the‌ network — no belts, funnels, or‌ tunnels needed.
ftbquests.chapter.create.quest2FC525A271: Craft a‌ diamond drill‌ to reach deeper‌ ores and‌ more valuable resources.
ftbquests.chapter.create.quest2FD45285C3: A useful‌ block‌ for building contraptions.
ftbquests.chapter.create.quest306E0A1DA8: A‌ redstone component‌ that‌ outputs‌ a signal‌ when in contact with‌ another‌ redstone contact. Perticularly useful‌ for building‌ contraptions.
ftbquests.chapter.create.quest312320F8FF: An‌ upgraded‌ version‌ of the‌ Copper‌ Diving Boots.
ftbquests.chapter.create.quest3163768E54: A‌ windmill uses wind‌ to‌ spin‌ and generate‌ Stress‌ Units (SU) for your machines.
ftbquests.chapter.create.quest335ECE39B2: Andesite alloy‌ is made‌ from some‌ iron‌ nugget‌ and andesite block.
The‌ starting‌ point of‌ your‌ create‌ questline.
ftbquests.chapter.create.quest3887DB2CA5: A useful‌ block‌ for building contraptions.
ftbquests.chapter.create.quest39E3CD4A91: View the‌ item or just‌ go‌ crazy.
ftbquests.chapter.create.quest39E865F0D7: A Shaft is‌ a simple‌ but essential‌ machine‌ part‌ that transfers‌ rotational‌ power. You can extend it‌ to reach‌ multiple‌ contraptions and‌ keep them‌ all‌ moving.
ftbquests.chapter.create.quest3B10D31EFD: Lets you‌ create your own‌ custom‌ functional clock.
ftbquests.chapter.create.quest3B925864D2: Blocks‌ that allow‌ contraptions‌ to harvest‌ crops.
ftbquests.chapter.create.quest3C7A3E5D5E: The Stock‌ Ticker automates‌ redstone‌ based on‌ inventory levels.
Connected‌ to‌ a‌ Stock Link, it‌ monitors an item and‌ emits‌ a redstone signal‌ based on‌ total stock.
Paired‌ with‌ a‌ Seat or Blaze‌ Burner, the‌ mob becomes‌ a‌ Stock‌ Keeper with‌ full network access.
ftbquests.chapter.create.quest3D11842DDD: -&eSU (Stress Units)&r‌ Is what‌ powers your contraptions.
-&eRPM (Revolutions‌ per‌ minute)&r is‌ basically‌ working speed of contraptions.
ftbquests.chapter.create.quest3DE3863665: Redstone is‌ essential in‌ Create, and these blocks‌ let you‌ build more compact contraptions.
ftbquests.chapter.create.quest3EADB5F22F: An upgrade for‌ the Andesite‌ Tunnel that provides more control‌ over how‌ items are handled.
ftbquests.chapter.create.quest3F7792256B: Craft‌ a vein finder to‌ locate‌ ore veins and‌ enhance‌ mining‌ efficiency.
ftbquests.chapter.create.quest4007D36163: Grinding it all down‌ to dust. Like‌ wheat to bread.
ftbquests.chapter.create.quest408D9361AF: A‌ simple machine‌ with massive‌ potential. Can place blocks‌ but also‌ use items on blocks or‌ entities.

ftbquests.chapter.create_connected.quest: The‌ Inverted Clutch does the‌ exact‌ opposite of a‌ normal clutch.
The‌ Inverted Gearshift‌ reverses‌ the‌ input rotation‌ when‌ unpowered and passes it‌ through unchanged‌ when‌ powered, basically opposite‌ of a‌ normal‌ gearshift.
Haunting‌ and Smoking‌ Catalysts‌ channel‌ the Nether’s‌ power-soul fire‌ for spectral conversions, and‌ burning embers‌ for smoke and cooking.
Made from‌ soul sand‌ and netherrack, these catalysts‌ let‌ you tame‌ a‌ darker side of processing.
The‌ Fluid‌ Vessel holds the‌ same‌ amount‌ as a‌ regular‌ tank but in‌ a horizontal layout, ideal for‌ low, wide‌ builds or storage‌ under machines.
Check‌ the ponders, i‌ really can't explain them...
The Item Silo‌ functions like‌ a regular Item Vault but‌ stacks items‌ vertically instead of‌ spreading‌ out. Ideal for‌ compact‌ or tall storage builds.
Every‌ upgrade starts somewhere. The‌ Empty‌ Fan‌ Catalyst is‌ the‌ uncharged core-full of‌ potential.
You’ll need it to‌ make‌ all the specialized‌ catalysts that‌ transform your‌ fans‌ into‌ focused processing‌ tools.
To‌ make one of the‌ catalysts below, simply‌ right‌ click the‌ empty catalyst‌ with‌ the‌ proper item‌ in your hand!
Check the‌ Ponder for the‌ Sequenced Pulse‌ Generator to‌ learn‌ more‌ about its‌ advanced redstone‌ logic.
The‌ Shear Pin‌ acts‌ like‌ a regular‌ shaft‌ but breaks instantly if‌ the connected‌ network‌ is overstressed, serving‌ as a‌ failsafe‌ for‌ important components.
The‌ Overstress Clutch disengages automatically‌ with‌ a delay whenever‌ the system‌ becomes overstressed.
The‌ Brake‌ works‌ oppositely: when powered by‌ redstone, it‌ injects massive‌ stress‌ into‌ the system, crashing‌ it instantly.
The‌ Kinetic‌ Bridge lets you‌ transfer Stress‌ Units (SU) from one‌ network‌ to‌ a completely separate‌ Stress‌ Network.
Charges up‌ with‌ rotational‌ power, then later‌ can be used‌ as a‌ battery!
Two‌ forces, with one goal: better‌ processing.
Blasting Catalysts‌ perform blasting‌ encased‌ fan‌ recipes, while Washing Catalysts‌ perform‌ washing encased‌ fan‌ recipes.
Master‌ them both‌ to expand your‌ automation capabilities.
Born‌ from‌ dreams and shaped‌ by‌ extremes-Seething‌ and Freezing‌ Catalysts‌ bring even higher (and‌ lower) temperatures to fan automation.
To‌ view‌ the recipes they‌ can perform, check‌ the uses‌ of‌ the‌ Industrial Fan-which‌ must‌ be used to make‌ these catalysts‌ function.
Create‌ Connected enhances‌ Create with smarter, more‌ versatile components.
Use‌ Fan Catalysts for easier fan‌ processing, specialized clutches‌ and gearboxes to‌ reverse‌ motion, and built-in‌ cogwheels‌ for more efficient machine‌ connections.
These clutches‌ engage only‌ under certain‌ conditions, making‌ them‌ ideal for‌ automation based‌ on speed or‌ rotation direction.
Centrifugal‌ Clutch: engages only when input RPM‌ exceeds a‌ set threshold, delaying connection‌ until‌ the system‌ speeds‌ up.
Freewheel Clutch: connects only when‌ spinning‌ in the correct‌ direction, letting‌ you‌ control motion‌ based‌ on rotational flow.
Inventory‌ Access Port: connects‌ to a‌ single‌ inventory, allowing‌ direct item‌ insertion or extraction — perfect for‌ compact‌ setups.
Inventory Bridge: links two‌ inventories as‌ one, letting you‌ move‌ items‌ in or out‌ of‌ both using‌ pipes‌ or‌ funnels.

ftbquests.chapter.create_new_age.quest14: Once‌ you’ve energized an‌ Iron‌ Block, use‌ a Deployer‌ to‌ place the Overcharged‌ Iron Block onto your‌ Magnetite.
Doing‌ so will form‌ the Redstone‌ Magnet, the first‌ step‌ in‌ channeling focused‌ magnetic‌ power.
ftbquests.chapter.create_new_age.quest15: If‌ u think motor‌ is not‌ enough, use extensions! Attach‌ it‌ to‌ behind.
ftbquests.chapter.create_new_age.quest18: Overcharged‌ Iron‌ Wire‌ is the‌ second‌ conductive material in Create: New‌ Age.
It transfers‌ 2,048‌ SU/tick, double that‌ of Copper‌ Wire, making‌ it‌ a reliable‌ choice for expanding power‌ networks.
Magnetite is‌ the cornerstone of‌ magnetic‌ energy.
Found deep‌ within‌ caves around Y50 or‌ Y70!
ftbquests.chapter.create_new_age.quest1B: Placed‌ between the Fuel Inserter and‌ Heat Vent, these‌ rods enable fission‌ and‌ transfer heat‌ through‌ the reactor core.
ftbquests.chapter.create_new_age.quest25: Attach it‌ to‌ a behind of a‌ motor
ftbquests.chapter.create_new_age.quest29: The‌ Basic‌ Solar‌ Plate introduces‌ thermal energy.
ftbquests.chapter.create_new_age.quest2C: The‌ Reactor Casing is‌ the first‌ step for‌ making‌ nuclear‌ reactors.
You’ll need many‌ to‌ build the‌ outer‌ shell, forming‌ the structural‌ base for fuel‌ rods.
ftbquests.chapter.create_new_age.quest3F: Progression demands power. Energize a‌ Gold Block, then‌ deploy‌ it onto‌ a Redstone‌ Magnet‌ to‌ create a‌ Layered Magnet.
Gold is better‌ at‌ conducting power - expect stronger‌ results and‌ a higher‌ SU‌ cost.
ftbquests.chapter.create_new_age.quest47: To start‌ energizing, craft a‌ Basic‌ Energizer‌ using an‌ Andesite Casing‌ and Lightning Rod.
Provide‌ it with‌ rotation and energy, attach an Electrical‌ Connector to‌ the Carbon Brushes‌ set‌ to Pull, and‌ another‌ connector on the side/top‌ set‌ to Push.
ftbquests.chapter.create_new_age.quest55: Reactor‌ Glass is a‌ stylish alternative‌ to Reactor‌ Casings, letting‌ you‌ see inside your‌ nuclear‌ setup without‌ losing‌ structural‌ strength.
Place‌ 12 Magnetite‌ blocks around a‌ Generator Coil‌ as shown in the Ponder‌ screen.
ftbquests.chapter.create_new_age.quest59: Overcharged‌ Diamond Wire is‌ the fourth‌ conductive material‌ in‌ Create: New‌ Age.
It transfers‌ 8,192 SU/tick, making‌ it ideal for‌ late-game machines‌ and high-throughput setups.
ftbquests.chapter.create_new_age.quest5A: The‌ Strong Motor‌ is the next step in‌ converting FE‌ to SU, producing 2,048‌ SU‌ at 256‌ RPM.
ftbquests.chapter.create_new_age.quest5B: The‌ Reinforced Motor is the‌ top-tier‌ motor in Create‌ New‌ Age, outputting‌ 8,192 SU‌ and‌ storing 128K FE.
No‌ extension for this one‌ gng..
ftbquests.chapter.create_new_age.quest5C: Create: New Age adds‌ electricity, letting you‌ build real-world inspired‌ machines.
ftbquests.chapter.create_new_age.quest62: Obtained‌ by‌ energizing iron‌ blocks or‌ ingots.
ftbquests.chapter.create_new_age.quest68: The Reinforced Energizer‌ boosts production‌ massively — 4× faster than‌ the‌ Advanced‌ Energizer with‌ a‌ 1M SU buffer, designed for‌ high-throughput energizing.
ftbquests.chapter.create_new_age.quest6A: Copper Wire‌ is‌ the first conductive‌ material‌ in‌ Create: New Age, transferring‌ up‌ to 1,024 SU/tick.
It’s‌ easy to craft and‌ perfect‌ for small-scale setups‌ and early‌ power distribution.
ftbquests.chapter.create_new_age.quest6D: After‌ energizing it, use a‌ Deployer‌ to mount‌ it‌ onto‌ a Fluxuated‌ Magnet.
ftbquests.chapter.create_new_age.quest7E: Overcharged‌ Gold Wire is‌ the third‌ conductive material‌ in‌ Create: New‌ Age.
It transfers 4,096‌ SU/tick, ideal‌ for mid-tier‌ factories‌ needing‌ reliable power.
ftbquests.chapter.create_new_age.quest7F: 4× faster than‌ the‌ Basic‌ Energizer and‌ with‌ a 100k FE‌ buffer, making it perfect for‌ energy‌ needs.
ftbquests.chapter.create_new_age.quest9C: Fuel Inserter: automatically‌ feeds fuel into‌ the reactor‌ rods.
Heat Vent: removes‌ heat‌ from‌ the core‌ and transfers‌ it to your‌ heating network.
ftbquests.chapter.create_new_age.questD3: The Basic‌ Motor‌ converts‌ FE electricity‌ into SU‌ rotational force.

ftbquests.chapter.deeper_and_darker_2.qu: # <grad from=#35FCF9 to=#BFFFFD f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Soundproof‌ Glass</shadow></grad>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Sealing off‌ a‌ mob farm so the‌ sculk network‌ below‌ it stays‌ quiet.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Windows that‌ do‌ not‌ leak sound, in‌ any redstone build that‌ uses‌ Sculk Sensors.</grad></shadow>
[!tip] Soul Dust‌ is cheap. Sculk‌ Snappers and‌ Sculk‌ Leeches‌ both drop it‌ and‌ Ancient Temple‌ basement‌ chests‌ are full‌ of it.
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>It is‌ also just‌ a good‌ looking‌ block, which‌ is the‌ real reason‌ most people make‌ it.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Glass that‌ occludes vibrations. Anything happening‌ on‌ one side‌ of‌ it is silent on‌ the‌ other.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Crafted in a‌ plus‌ shape‌ from </grad></shadow><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>4</grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> </grad></shadow><grad from=#35FCF9 to=#12B7C4 f=0.8>Soul Dust</grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> around </grad></shadow><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>1</grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> </grad></shadow><grad from=#35FCF9 to=#12B7C4 f=0.8>Glass</grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, for </grad></shadow><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>2</grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> blocks.</grad></shadow>
[gap=5]
[gap=5]
## <grad from=#2FD9D6 to=#A8F4F2 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>What‌ It‌ Is Actually For</shadow></grad>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A‌ base inside an Ancient‌ City‌ or a Deep‌ Dark that‌ a Warden‌ will‌ never‌ notice.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
<typewriter><grad from=#5FD8D6 to=#5FD8D6>Build inside‌ a Deep Dark.</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#35FCF9 to=#BFFFFD f=0.6>Soundproof Glass</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#35FCF9 to=#BFFFFD f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Something‌ Is Under‌ The Bedrock</shadow></grad>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The </grad></shadow><grad from=#35FCF9 to=#12B7C4 f=0.8>Otherside</grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> itself. Four‌ biomes, its‌ own‌ ore table, and‌ the fact that‌ a bed‌ works down‌ there.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The </grad></shadow><grad from=#35FCF9 to=#12B7C4 f=0.8>Ancient‌ Temple</grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, the‌ only structure‌ the mod‌ builds, and the two‌ things worth‌ stealing from it.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Two gear tiers. </grad></shadow><grad from=#7CF5C0 to=#2FD98A f=0.8>Resonarium</grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> hides‌ a defensive‌ trick almost nobody‌ notices, and </grad></shadow><grad from=#9DB8D4 to=#5D7791 f=0.8>Warden</grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> gear‌ beats netherite‌ outright.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A‌ bestiary at the bottom, because‌ two‌ of those mobs‌ are‌ worth‌ far more‌ alive‌ than dead.</grad></shadow>
[!tip] Read the‌ quest called `Vibrations` before you go‌ anywhere‌ near a Shrieker. Almost‌ every death‌ in this‌ chapter‌ is‌ a noise‌ problem, not‌ a damage problem.
[gap=5]

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Vanilla gave‌ the Deep‌ Dark one mob, one structure and‌ no reason‌ to ever go‌ back. </grad><grad from=#35FCF9 to=#12B7C4 f=0.8>Deeper‌ and Darker</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> finishes‌ the‌ job. It adds a full‌ second‌ layer to the‌ world, a‌ dimension‌ called the </grad><grad from=#35FCF9 to=#12B7C4 f=0.8>Otherside</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, which‌ sits‌ below bedrock and‌ is reached by killing‌ the‌ one thing down‌ there that‌ can definitely‌ kill‌ you‌ back..</grad></shadow>
[gap=5]
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>Sculk hears‌ you. It does‌ not‌ see you, it‌ does not‌ smell‌ you, it‌ hears you. Everything‌ below follows from that‌ one‌ sentence.</grad></shadow>
[!info] Everything in‌ this‌ chapter was measured from‌ the mod‌ files‌ and this‌ pack's own‌ configs. Where‌ the‌ pack changes‌ a number, the pack's number‌ is‌ the one written‌ here.
[gap=5]
[gap=5]
## <grad from=#2FD9D6 to=#A8F4F2 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>What This‌ Chapter Covers</shadow></grad>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The </grad></shadow><grad from=#35FCF9 to=#12B7C4 f=0.8>Warden</grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, its‌ two‌ drops, and‌ how a corpse‌ becomes‌ a doorway.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
<typewriter><grad from=#5FD8D6 to=#5FD8D6>The floor is‌ never the‌ bottom</grad>
&bDeep Dark
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#35FCF9 to=#BFFFFD f=0.6>Deeper and Darker</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#35FCF9 to=#BFFFFD f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Heart of the Deep</shadow></grad>
[gap=3]

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>It‌ stacks‌ to </grad></shadow><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>1</grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and‌ it is‌ fireproof, so a lava‌ death will‌ not cost‌ you‌ the‌ trip.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>It is‌ also the‌ centrepiece of the </grad></shadow><grad from=#35FCF9 to=#12B7C4 f=0.8>Sonorous‌ Staff</grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, which is‌ why most people end up‌ killing two‌ Wardens.</grad></shadow>
[!info] Sitting in your‌ inventory‌ it randomly‌ plays‌ a heartbeat. `wardenHeartPulses` in the config‌ turns‌ that off if‌ it‌ unsettles‌ you.
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>Portals work‌ both‌ ways but the‌ return portal is not‌ built‌ for you. Carry the‌ second Heart, or‌ carry the‌ frame‌ blocks.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>One‌ drops‌ from every Warden‌ you kill, always, with‌ no roll‌ and‌ no‌ Looting requirement. It‌ is‌ the key to the‌ dimension and‌ nothing‌ else produces‌ it.</grad></shadow>
[gap=5]
[gap=5]

The Heart is‌ consumed.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>It only‌ functions in‌ the </grad></shadow><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>Overworld</grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and‌ the </grad></shadow><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>Otherside</grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. Anywhere‌ else it does‌ nothing‌ at all.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#5FD8D6 to=#5FD8D6>It‌ still beats?!!</grad>

[!success] Once‌ you‌ own one, duplicate‌ it. Put the template in‌ the‌ middle with `1 Sculk` under‌ it and `7‌ Diamonds` filling the‌ rest‌ of‌ the grid, and you‌ get `2` back.
[gap=5]
[gap=5]
## <grad from=#2FD9D6 to=#A8F4F2 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Using‌ It</shadow></grad>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Template, plus </grad></shadow><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>netherite</grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> gear, plus a </grad></shadow><grad from=#35FCF9 to=#12B7C4 f=0.8>Reinforced‌ Echo‌ Shard</grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, at‌ a smithing‌ table.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>It works on‌ every netherite‌ tool, every netherite‌ weapon‌ and‌ every netherite‌ armour piece.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>One‌ shard per upgrade. A‌ full set‌ of tools and armour is </grad></shadow><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>nine</grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> shards, which‌ is </grad></shadow><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>nine</grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> Warden Carapace‌ and </grad></shadow><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>nine</grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> Echo Shards.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>Loot the‌ Ancient‌ City properly‌ before‌ you build the portal. It‌ hands‌ you the template‌ and‌ the‌ carapace at‌ once.</grad></shadow>
[gap=5]
[gap=5]

## <grad from=#2FD9D6 to=#A8F4F2 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>The‌ Geysers</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A </grad></shadow><grad from=#35FCF9 to=#12B7C4 f=0.8>Gloomy Geyser</grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> launches anything‌ that touches‌ it straight‌ up‌ at </grad></shadow><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>2.5</grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> velocity. It‌ deals </grad></shadow><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>no damage‌ at all</grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Amber pillars, soul soil, magma and‌ gloomslate instead‌ of sculk stone. It‌ reads‌ as the‌ hostile‌ biome and it is‌ the‌ exact opposite.</grad></shadow>
[!warn] The‌ launch is free. The‌ landing is‌ not. Geysers do not cancel fall‌ damage, so either‌ aim for water, or‌ land‌ on another‌ geyser.
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>Experience‌ orbs are the one‌ thing‌ a geyser ignores, which‌ means‌ an‌ orb sitting‌ on‌ a geyser stays‌ there instead of flying‌ off.</grad></shadow>
[!success] The Overcast‌ Columns‌ biome‌ list contains `zero` mob‌ spawns. Not‌ a reduced list, an‌ empty one. Nothing natural spawns‌ here‌ at all.
[gap=5]
[gap=5]

## <grad from=#2FD9D6 to=#A8F4F2 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>The Two Real Limits</shadow></grad>

- <grad from=#FF7A7A to=#FF3C3C f=0.8>The‌ linked chunk‌ has to be‌ loaded</grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. The‌ Transmitter reads‌ the‌ block live before it‌ opens‌ anything. Wander far enough‌ that‌ the‌ chunk unloads‌ and‌ you get </grad></shadow><grad from=#FF7A7A to=#FF3C3C f=0.8>The linked‌ block is missing or‌ unloaded</grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]

- <grad from=#FF7A7A to=#FF3C3C f=0.8>It‌ never crosses dimensions</grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. It‌ looks up‌ those coordinates‌ in‌ the‌ dimension you‌ are‌ standing in, finds the wrong‌ block, and unlinks‌ itself‌ on the‌ spot.</grad></shadow>
[!tip] Link it‌ to‌ a‌ chunkloaded chest‌ and the range problem‌ disappears‌ entirely. Link it to‌ a Crafting‌ Table and‌ the‌ range‌ problem never existed, because‌ you‌ can put‌ one‌ anywhere.

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>Once‌ a screen‌ is open it‌ stays open‌ no matter‌ how‌ far‌ you walk, which‌ is a‌ genuinely useful quirk‌ of how‌ it hooks into containers.</grad></shadow>
[gap=5]
[gap=5]
## <grad from=#2FD9D6 to=#A8F4F2 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Using‌ It</shadow></grad>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7></grad></shadow><grad from=#35FCF9 to=#12B7C4 f=0.8>Sneak plus right‌ click</grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> a‌ valid block‌ to‌ link to it. The item‌ texture‌ changes when it‌ is‌ linked.</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7></grad></shadow><grad from=#35FCF9 to=#12B7C4 f=0.8>Right‌ click anything‌ else</grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, or‌ right click the‌ air, to open the linked‌ block.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#5FD8D6 to=#5FD8D6>Your base, in‌ your pocket.</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#35FCF9 to=#BFFFFD f=0.6>Sculk Transmitter</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#35FCF9 to=#BFFFFD f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>The Quarter Rule</shadow></grad>
[gap=3]

- <grad from=#FF7A7A to=#FF3C3C f=0.8>Durability is‌ charged at the‌ full damage‌ value</grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, on every‌ piece, every‌ hit. A‌ big hit‌ you took‌ no damage from‌ still eats‌ four pieces of armour.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <grad from=#FF7A7A to=#FF3C3C f=0.8>It cannot‌ be enchanted‌ at an enchanting‌ table</grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. The‌ item refuses‌ outright.</grad></shadow>
[gap=5]
[gap=5]
## <grad from=#2FD9D6 to=#A8F4F2 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Enchanting‌ And Repair Anyway</shadow></grad>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Put the‌ piece‌ and an </grad></shadow><grad from=#35FCF9 to=#12B7C4 f=0.8>enchanted book</grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> on‌ an </grad></shadow><grad from=#35FCF9 to=#12B7C4 f=0.8>anvil</grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. The‌ mod‌ runs its‌ own‌ anvil handler and‌ charges </grad></shadow><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>half</grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> the normal cost.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Resonarium‌ armour‌ has a hidden‌ effect‌ that‌ is worth‌ more‌ than every armour‌ point on it.</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Two books‌ of‌ the </grad></shadow><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>same level</grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> on the‌ same piece‌ push it‌ one‌ level‌ higher, up to‌ the‌ enchant maximum.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Repair by putting‌ raw </grad></shadow><grad from=#7CF5C0 to=#2FD98A f=0.8>Resonarium</grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> on the‌ anvil. Each‌ one restores </grad></shadow><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>a‌ quarter</grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> of max‌ durability, and‌ it‌ stacks in‌ one click.</grad></shadow>
[!warn] Protection, Fire Protection, Blast Protection, Projectile‌ Protection‌ and Mending are‌ blocked on‌ this armour‌ by‌ design. The‌ quarter rule is‌ meant‌ to be‌ the‌ protection.
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>Raw‌ stats for‌ completeness: 18 armour points‌ against diamond's‌ 15, but only‌ 1.0‌ toughness‌ against diamond's‌ 2.0.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Every equipped‌ Resonarium‌ piece removes </grad></shadow><grad from=#7CF5C0 to=#2FD98A f=0.8>25 percent‌ of the‌ incoming hit</grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, calculated‌ from‌ the‌ original damage, before‌ armour‌ is even considered.</grad></shadow>
[!success] One piece‌ cuts a‌ hit‌ by a‌ quarter. Two pieces‌ halve‌ it. `The‌ full four‌ piece set reduces the‌ hit‌ to zero.`
[gap=5]
[gap=5]
## <grad from=#2FD9D6 to=#A8F4F2 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>The Catches</shadow></grad>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The other </grad></shadow><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>84‌ percent</grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> just‌ break, and they are‌ worth breaking.</grad></shadow>

## <grad from=#2FD9D6 to=#A8F4F2 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>What Falls‌ Out</shadow></grad>

## <grad from=#2FD9D6 to=#A8F4F2 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>The Drop</shadow></grad>

<grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>0 to‌ 1</grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> </grad></shadow><grad from=#35FCF9 to=#12B7C4 f=0.8>String</grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, plus Looting. That‌ is it. There‌ is‌ no‌ reason to‌ fight one‌ on purpose.</grad></shadow>

## <grad from=#2FD9D6 to=#A8F4F2 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>It Is Neutral</shadow></grad>

[!success] Anger‌ times‌ out. Break line of‌ sight, wait‌ it out, and‌ they‌ go‌ back to‌ wandering.
<typewriter><grad from=#5FD8D6 to=#5FD8D6>Leave‌ it alone and it‌ leaves‌ you alone!</grad>

## <grad from=#2FD9D6 to=#A8F4F2 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>The Ring Attack, Timed</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>This‌ is‌ the part‌ that‌ kills people, and it runs‌ on‌ a fixed clock‌ the‌ moment‌ any player‌ is‌ within </grad></shadow><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>10</grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> blocks of it.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A proper boss‌ bar‌ mini boss, and the‌ only way‌ to get </grad></shadow><grad from=#35FCF9 to=#12B7C4 f=0.8>Soul‌ Crystal</grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> reliably. It‌ is‌ summoned by‌ breaking‌ a rigged </grad></shadow><grad from=#35FCF9 to=#12B7C4 f=0.8>Ancient Vase</grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> inside an‌ Ancient Temple.</grad></shadow>

1. <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>For‌ about </grad></shadow><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>22 seconds</grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> it just fights‌ you‌ normally. Nothing special.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]

2. <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Then it‌ screams for </grad></shadow><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>10‌ straight seconds</grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. During‌ that‌ window‌ every player‌ inside </grad></shadow><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>10</grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> blocks‌ takes </grad></shadow><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>2</grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> damage </grad></shadow><grad from=#FF7A7A to=#FF3C3C f=0.8>every single tick</grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]

3. <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Five times‌ during that‌ scream‌ it spawns </grad></shadow><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>1‌ to 3</grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> </grad></shadow><grad from=#35FCF9 to=#12B7C4 f=0.8>Sculk‌ Leeches</grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> around‌ itself.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
4. <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Then‌ the clock‌ resets and the cycle‌ repeats.</grad></shadow>
[!danger] Two‌ damage per tick‌ is `40 damage‌ per second`. Standing‌ inside‌ the‌ ring for the‌ full‌ ten seconds‌ is‌ four‌ hundred damage. Nothing‌ you own survives‌ that.
[!tip] The counter‌ only ticks‌ down‌ while‌ a player‌ is nearby. Walk‌ more than ten‌ blocks away, the‌ scream stops hurting you, and you‌ can pick‌ the leeches off‌ at‌ your leisure.
[gap=5]

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>It‌ rises‌ out of‌ the floor‌ over </grad></shadow><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>3.5‌ seconds</grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and‌ cannot target‌ anything while it is‌ emerging. That‌ is your free‌ hit window.</grad></shadow>
[gap=5]
[!success] The‌ ring‌ is normal armour affected‌ damage. A‌ full `Resonarium` set reduces it‌ to‌ zero, which‌ turns this‌ entire‌ fight into a‌ melee duel with a‌ mob‌ that cannot knock‌ you back.

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The‌ armour‌ is completely‌ invisible‌ while worn, which is‌ either the best or‌ the‌ worst thing about‌ it.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The tools‌ mine in‌ a </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>3‌ by‌ 3</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> area, and holding‌ Shift‌ turns that off when‌ you need‌ one‌ block.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#8FB8D8 to=#8FB8D8>An‌ End City‌ grind with a‌ very good‌ payoff.</grad>
Understood the Etherium problem
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#8FB8D8 to=#E2F2FF f=0.6>Etherium and Arms</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#8FB8D8 to=#E2F2FF f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Area Mining</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Breaks a </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>3‌ by‌ 3 by‌ 1</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> area‌ every swing. Hold Shift to‌ break‌ one block, or Shift‌ and‌ right‌ click to‌ turn‌ the area off‌ entirely.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Three ingots and two‌ Ender‌ Rods.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#8FB8D8 to=#8FB8D8>Three by three, one‌ deep.</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#8FB8D8 to=#E2F2FF f=0.6>Etherium Pickaxe</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#8FB8D8 to=#E2F2FF f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Etherium Cuirass</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Eight‌ ingots. The single‌ most expensive piece, and‌ the‌ one carrying‌ the‌ most pack bonuses.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>On its‌ own‌ it is roughly‌ diamond‌ tier‌ with a‌ few‌ extras. The whole point‌ is the set bonus, so‌ do‌ not stop at‌ one piece.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#8FB8D8 to=#8FB8D8>Part‌ of the‌ invisible‌ set.</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#8FB8D8 to=#E2F2FF f=0.6>Etherium Cuirass</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#8FB8D8 to=#E2F2FF f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Homing Throw</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Throw‌ it and‌ it‌ tracks‌ whatever you were‌ aiming‌ at. Charge it‌ first‌ and‌ it explodes‌ on impact for </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>2.5‌ times</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> the damage.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#8FB8D8 to=#8FB8D8>It‌ follows the target.</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#8FB8D8 to=#E2F2FF f=0.6>Astral Spear</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#8FB8D8 to=#E2F2FF f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Beheading</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Every monster you‌ kill‌ has a </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>10 percent</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> chance‌ to‌ drop‌ its head, and‌ each‌ level of Looting‌ adds another </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>5 percent</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A Diamond‌ Axe, a‌ Wither Skeleton Skull, a‌ Netherite Ingot, a‌ Blaze Rod‌ and‌ Blaze‌ Powder.</grad></shadow>
[!tip] With Looting‌ III‌ that is a 25‌ percent head‌ rate‌ on every‌ mob in‌ the‌ game. Head‌ collectors, this is‌ your item.
<typewriter><grad from=#8FB8D8 to=#8FB8D8>Heads. Lots of heads.</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#8FB8D8 to=#E2F2FF f=0.6>Axe of Executioner</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#8FB8D8 to=#E2F2FF f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Store And‌ Release</shadow></grad>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#8FD6FF to=#4FA8E8 f=0.8>Transport</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> mode‌ stores‌ one creature‌ and puts it‌ back later. </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>14‌ second</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> cooldown.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#8FD6FF to=#4FA8E8 f=0.8>Combat</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> mode fires‌ a‌ beam‌ that builds‌ up on‌ a target, and once‌ it is‌ full the target gets sealed‌ away. Up to </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>5</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> at‌ a time.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>An Ichor‌ Droplet, an‌ Extradimensional Eye, a‌ Blaze‌ Rod and gold.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#8FB8D8 to=#8FB8D8>A mob‌ catcher‌ with two modes.</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#8FB8D8 to=#E2F2FF f=0.6>Scepter of Extradimension</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#8FB8D8 to=#E2F2FF f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>What Wearing‌ All‌ Four‌ Does</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Drop below </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>40‌ percent</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> health and‌ the set throws‌ up a‌ shield that reflects most projectiles, gives‌ you </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>50 percent</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> damage‌ resistance and knocks‌ back‌ anything that‌ touches‌ you.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>This pack also hands‌ every‌ piece extra stats‌ on‌ top‌ of the‌ mod's‌ own numbers.</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>+2</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> armour on‌ the helmet and boots, </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>+3</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> on‌ the‌ chestplate.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>+2</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> max health, </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>+1</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> Luck and </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>+0.15</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> knockback‌ resistance per‌ piece.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>+5 percent</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> movement‌ speed‌ and </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>+3‌ percent</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> attack damage‌ and‌ speed per piece.</grad></shadow>
[!info] Every piece‌ is invisible‌ while‌ worn. If you‌ like being‌ seen, the‌ Etherium‌ Core spellstone‌ gives you a toggle‌ for‌ that.
<typewriter><grad from=#8FB8D8 to=#8FB8D8>Four pieces, one very‌ loud shield.</grad>
I have all four pieces
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#8FB8D8 to=#E2F2FF f=0.6>The Etherium Set Bonus</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#8FB8D8 to=#E2F2FF f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Etherium‌ Greaves</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Seven ingots. Invisible, like‌ the‌ rest of it.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>On its‌ own it‌ is‌ roughly diamond‌ tier with‌ a‌ few‌ extras. The whole‌ point is the set‌ bonus, so‌ do not stop‌ at one‌ piece.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#8FB8D8 to=#8FB8D8>Part of‌ the‌ invisible‌ set.</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#8FB8D8 to=#E2F2FF f=0.6>Etherium Greaves</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#8FB8D8 to=#E2F2FF f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>A‌ Weapon You‌ Wear‌ On Your‌ Back</shadow></grad>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>80 percent</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> less‌ damage‌ from‌ behind.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>+3</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> Armor.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Flying speed‌ goes up by </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>60 percent</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Aim‌ at‌ the ground, accelerate into‌ it, and the‌ landing deals‌ area‌ damage. </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>25‌ second</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> cooldown.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#8FB8D8 to=#8FB8D8>Dive bomb the ground. Yes, really.</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#8FB8D8 to=#E2F2FF f=0.6>The Arrogance of Chaos</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#8FB8D8 to=#E2F2FF f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Farming‌ Tool</shadow></grad>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Harvests crops in a </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>3 by‌ 3 by‌ 3</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> cube.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Tills soil in‌ a </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>3‌ by 3</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> square.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Shift‌ suppresses‌ both, Shift and right click‌ toggles‌ them.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#8FB8D8 to=#8FB8D8>Harvests and replants‌ in‌ one‌ swing.</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#8FB8D8 to=#E2F2FF f=0.6>Etherium Scythe</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#8FB8D8 to=#E2F2FF f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Backwards Leap</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Right‌ click‌ and you get‌ thrown in the opposite‌ direction‌ to where you‌ are looking, on‌ a </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>2 second</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> cooldown. Shift‌ and‌ right‌ click turns‌ that‌ off.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Better than it sounds. Getting‌ out of‌ a‌ mob pile‌ is usually‌ worth‌ more‌ than another‌ point of damage.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#8FB8D8 to=#8FB8D8>It has‌ a‌ disengage button.</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#8FB8D8 to=#E2F2FF f=0.6>Etherium Broadsword</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#8FB8D8 to=#E2F2FF f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Etherium Boots</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Four ingots. The‌ cheapest‌ way to‌ start‌ the‌ set.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>On its‌ own it is‌ roughly diamond‌ tier with‌ a‌ few‌ extras. The whole‌ point is‌ the set bonus, so‌ do not‌ stop at one piece.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#8FB8D8 to=#8FB8D8>Part of‌ the invisible‌ set.</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#8FB8D8 to=#E2F2FF f=0.6>Etherium Boots</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#8FB8D8 to=#E2F2FF f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Raid Weapon</shadow></grad>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Every‌ level of‌ Bad Omen on‌ you‌ adds </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>15 percent</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> damage.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Right‌ click‌ for a short, very strong‌ block.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A‌ successful block strengthens‌ your‌ next‌ attack.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A Netherite‌ Sword, a‌ Netherite Ingot and‌ a Totem of Undying. Drink‌ an‌ Ominous Bottle before‌ a raid‌ and swing‌ away.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#8FB8D8 to=#8FB8D8>Bad‌ Omen‌ is a‌ buff‌ now.</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#8FB8D8 to=#E2F2FF f=0.6>Disaster Broadsword</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#8FB8D8 to=#E2F2FF f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Machine‌ Gun</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Fires a‌ magic dagger‌ every </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>0.4‌ seconds</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> for‌ as long‌ as‌ you hold the button. The‌ daggers also‌ drag‌ nearby dropped‌ items back‌ to‌ you.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Luck‌ raises the‌ damage, so it pairs well‌ with‌ anything that gives‌ you Luck.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>Quartz, lapis, a‌ Ghast Tear‌ and‌ a‌ stick. Genuinely cheap.</grad></shadow></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#8FB8D8 to=#8FB8D8>Hold right‌ click. Keep‌ holding.</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#8FB8D8 to=#E2F2FF f=0.6>Magic Quartz Scepter</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#F5C542 to=#FFF4CF f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Anti‌ Buff‌ Weapon</shadow></grad>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>6</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> Attack‌ Damage.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Burning targets‌ take‌ extra damage and‌ lose every beneficial effect‌ they‌ had.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>You cannot catch‌ fire while‌ holding it.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Your‌ invulnerability‌ window‌ after being‌ hit‌ is longer.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A Purified Heart, Nefarious‌ Essence, The Acknowledgment, a‌ Gold‌ Block and‌ Glowstone Dust.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#F5C542 to=#F5C542>Set‌ them‌ on‌ fire, then punish‌ them for it.</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#F5C542 to=#FFF4CF f=0.6>The Bless</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#8FB8D8 to=#E2F2FF f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>End‌ Specialist</shadow></grad>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>+150‌ percent</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> damage against creatures‌ of the‌ End.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>+600 percent</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> knockback‌ against‌ them.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>In‌ the End, a fully‌ charged‌ hit obliterates‌ Endermen‌ and‌ turns their‌ drops straight into‌ experience.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Shulkers and‌ Endermen lose‌ their‌ teleport‌ for a‌ moment after‌ you hit them.</grad></shadow>

[!info] Against‌ other players‌ it also disables their Eye‌ of the‌ Nebula, their Non-Euclidean Cube, their‌ Ender‌ Pearls, their Potions‌ of‌ Recall and their Twisted‌ Mirror. This‌ thing was designed‌ to‌ stop‌ people running‌ away.
<typewriter><grad from=#8FB8D8 to=#8FB8D8>Built‌ for one dimension‌ and very good at‌ it.</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#8FB8D8 to=#E2F2FF f=0.6>The Ender Slayer</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#E03131 to=#FFAFAF f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Thrown Curses</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Right click to‌ throw a‌ dagger‌ on a </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>2‌ second</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> cooldown. Anything it‌ hits‌ starts‌ taking </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>2.5</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> curse damage‌ every </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>0.6 seconds</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>An Ender Rod, Nefarious‌ Essence‌ and a Nefarious‌ Ingot.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#FF8A8A to=#FF8A8A>Throwable. Repeatedly.</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#E03131 to=#FFAFAF f=0.6>The Curse Carver</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#8FB8D8 to=#E2F2FF f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Area‌ Digging</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Digs‌ a </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>3‌ by 3 by‌ 1</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> area. Shift‌ for a‌ single‌ block.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>Combine‌ it with‌ the pickaxe and‌ the waraxe‌ later and‌ you‌ get‌ the Astral‌ Breaker, which does‌ all three jobs.</grad></shadow></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#8FB8D8 to=#8FB8D8>Digging‌ a hole, quickly.</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#8FB8D8 to=#E2F2FF f=0.6>Etherium Shovel</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#E03131 to=#FFAFAF f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>What‌ It Does While‌ Blocking</shadow></grad>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Every‌ successful block stacks </grad><grad from=#FF8A8A to=#E03131 f=0.8>Blazing Might</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, and‌ taking‌ any damage strips‌ it away.</grad></shadow>
[!danger] It‌ will not‌ block‌ at‌ all unless you‌ are‌ wearing the‌ Ring‌ of‌ the Seven‌ Curses. For anyone else‌ it is‌ a wall‌ decoration.
[!warn] Attacks‌ from‌ behind deal‌ 50 percent‌ more damage while‌ you hold‌ it. Watch your back.
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Blocks the‌ instant you‌ raise‌ it, with‌ no wind‌ up.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Blocks‌ Piercing arrows, which normal shields‌ cannot.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Cannot be‌ disabled‌ by axes.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Burns‌ anything that‌ hits‌ you‌ in melee.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
<typewriter><grad from=#FF8A8A to=#FF8A8A>The best shield‌ in the‌ mod, if you qualify.</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#E03131 to=#FFAFAF f=0.6>Bulwark of Blazing Pride</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#8FB8D8 to=#E2F2FF f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Rockets‌ Not‌ Required</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Hold the‌ jump‌ key in flight and‌ you‌ accelerate forwards continuously. No‌ fireworks, no‌ timing.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>It‌ takes durability‌ faster‌ while you are‌ accelerating, which is the only‌ cost.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#8FB8D8 to=#8FB8D8>Hold jump and go.</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#8FB8D8 to=#E2F2FF f=0.6>Majestic Elytra</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#8FB8D8 to=#E2F2FF f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Etherium‌ Helmet</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Five ingots‌ in‌ a‌ helmet shape. Invisible on‌ your‌ head.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>On its‌ own‌ it‌ is roughly‌ diamond tier with‌ a few‌ extras. The whole‌ point‌ is‌ the set‌ bonus, so do‌ not stop at‌ one piece.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#8FB8D8 to=#8FB8D8>Part‌ of the invisible set.</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#8FB8D8 to=#E2F2FF f=0.6>Etherium Helmet</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#8FB8D8 to=#E2F2FF f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Potion‌ Arrows Without‌ Tipping</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Combine the bow itself with‌ up to </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>4</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> potions‌ and every arrow‌ carries‌ all of‌ them.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>You‌ take </grad><grad from=#FFC46B to=#FF9E1F f=0.8>60 percent</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> less damage from‌ your‌ own dragon breath, which‌ matters‌ more‌ than you‌ would‌ like.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>A Dragon Head, Dragon's‌ Breath, an Ender Rod and‌ Netherite.</grad></shadow></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#8FB8D8 to=#8FB8D8>Load‌ it with potions.</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#8FB8D8 to=#E2F2FF f=0.6>Dragon Breath Bow</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.enigmatic_arsenal.titl: <shadow a=0.4><grad from=#8FB8D8 to=#E2F2FF f=0.6>Etherium and Arms</grad></shadow>
