ftbquests.chapter.hexerei.quest116AF0295: The Owls can‌ be‌ tamed with‌ a‌ raw cod or salmon, just‌ like‌ the crow, you either‌ throw‌ the‌ fish on‌ the‌ ground or you‌ can just right-click to‌ them.
If‌ you wanna breed‌ them, you can‌ give Raw‌ rabbit‌ meat!
How Do I Tame a Owl?
ftbquests.chapter.hexerei.quest12B5E3921: Hexerei‌ is a‌ witchery and magic‌ mod that‌ includes really beautiful things!
To start‌ with the‌ questline, i suggest using‌ Book‌ of The‌ Shadows‌ for in-game wiki and‌ putting‌ it on the‌ altar.
&8How‌ am‌ i going‌ to‌ find the wood‌ type for it?
Hexerei mod‌ generates‌ some trees around‌ the world, it's‌ really not‌ hard‌ to‌ find them!
ftbquests.chapter.hexerei.quest19C6E7916: Broom‌ Neterite Tip will allow‌ you to‌ fly‌ through lava‌ and fire‌ without‌ getting‌ damaged!
ftbquests.chapter.hexerei.quest1D3A8218B: - <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Ingredients‌ into‌ the </grad><grad from=#C79BFF to=#7B3FD1 f=0.8>Item‌ Port</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, eight slots each‌ way</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7></grad><grad from=#C79BFF to=#7B3FD1 f=0.8>Water‌ or lava</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> into‌ the‌ Brew‌ Port, two tanks‌ of ten buckets</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7></grad><grad from=#C79BFF to=#7B3FD1 f=0.8>5000‌ FE</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> per craft, two‌ and a‌ half‌ seconds</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The‌ liquid is </grad><grad from=#C79BFF to=#7B3FD1 f=0.8>not‌ used up</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. It‌ has to be‌ in the‌ tank and it has to‌ be the‌ right one, and that‌ is‌ all. Keep water‌ and‌ lava loaded side by‌ side‌ and the Retort‌ will‌ switch‌ between them‌ on‌ its own.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Everything the cauldron‌ already‌ brews, </grad><grad from=#C79BFF to=#7B3FD1 f=0.8>without the eight‌ right‌ clicks</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The three‌ brooms are the exception. They‌ turn‌ their bucket of‌ water into </grad><grad from=#C79BFF to=#7B3FD1 f=0.8>blood</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, which‌ comes out‌ of‌ the‌ Brew Port's‌ other‌ side, so give that one‌ somewhere to‌ drain.</grad></shadow>
[!warn] Three‌ recipes stay‌ on the‌ real‌ cauldron. Moon‌ Dust wants‌ a full moon, and the‌ Ankh‌ Amulet and Replacer‌ Satchel are‌ brewed in‌ potion‌ rather‌ than water.
[!note] Look the‌ controller‌ up in‌ JEI‌ for‌ the full‌ list.

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Base‌ of </grad><grad from=#C79BFF to=#7B3FD1 f=0.8>Mahogany Planks</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, three‌ by‌ three. Five of those‌ tiles are the controller‌ and‌ its ports.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A </grad><grad from=#C79BFF to=#7B3FD1 f=0.8>Magma Block</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> goes‌ in the‌ middle of‌ the‌ base, directly‌ under a‌ real </grad><grad from=#C79BFF to=#7B3FD1 f=0.8>Mixing‌ Cauldron</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. Corners on top are </grad><grad from=#C79BFF to=#7B3FD1 f=0.8>Selenite‌ Blocks</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, edges are </grad><grad from=#C79BFF to=#7B3FD1 f=0.8>Witch‌ Hazel‌ Planks</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>
[!info] The magma‌ is the‌ fire‌ you‌ would have‌ lit under it anyway. Recipes‌ that‌ want heat get‌ it for‌ free here.
ftbquests.chapter.hexerei.quest22961E333: The‌ mixing cauldron is one‌ of the‌ main‌ tools in‌ hexerei.
Mixing up‌ all‌ sorts‌ of items‌ and potions!
Cauldron can hold‌ items, fluids‌ and these systems‌ integrate with‌ other mods‌ such‌ as‌ create.
It will help‌ us‌ create some‌ items‌ and‌ blocks!
The‌ mixing cauldron when‌ heated can‌ brew up‌ to‌ two‌ buckets worth‌ of potions‌ at a time.
To‌ do this, fill‌ it with water, then add two‌ of the‌ ingredient needed to‌ make‌ the potion!
ftbquests.chapter.hexerei.quest37B8692BF: The coffer‌ is a‌ very‌ useful‌ storage method in‌ hexerei, it‌ uses crows‌ to‌ automate‌ storage!
On the‌ right side of‌ the coffer's‌ GUI is‌ a‌ crow‌ icon.
While toggled, the‌ crow button‌ will allow crows‌ on gather‌ mode to check items inside‌ the coffer‌ and look in‌ the‌ area for‌ items‌ matching its contents to‌ deposit.
Crows‌ with a perch‌ located‌ on‌ a coffer‌ will‌ pick up any‌ item in the area‌ and‌ return it to‌ that coffer!
ftbquests.chapter.hexerei.quest3ADA80DFC: Courier packages‌ are perfect‌ for‌ sending items‌ to other‌ players‌ or‌ depots.
Delivered by‌ owls, your parcels will always‌ reach‌ their destination!
ftbquests.chapter.hexerei.quest411D1E658: Packing peanuts‌ are not‌ only perfect‌ for‌ cushioning‌ your Courier packages, but‌ also‌ make for‌ a‌ delightful‌ light snack!
ftbquests.chapter.hexerei.quest439C7D4A7: Broom‌ whistle is‌ a handy‌ tool‌ for‌ any witch.
Bind‌ it to‌ your broom and‌ with a‌ simple blow, your broom will come‌ flying to‌ you!
ftbquests.chapter.hexerei.quest445F7EAAD: The‌ Crow can‌ be‌ tamed with a seed‌ mixture.
&8If you‌ throw‌ the mixture‌ to ground‌ you‌ have‌ lower chance‌ of taming them than‌ giving‌ them by hand.
Once‌ tamed crows‌ can be‌ set‌ to‌ different commands.
The player‌ can‌ change these‌ commands‌ by‌ simply right-clicking‌ the crow!
Crows contain‌ 3 slots‌ that are‌ Hand, Hat‌ and‌ Misc.
Misc slot‌ can be‌ equip with weapons‌ or storage‌ items!
If you right-click to your‌ crow with‌ a dye you‌ can‌ add a‌ colored‌ bandanna!
ftbquests.chapter.hexerei.quest448DDF682: Brushes are‌ one of‌ the most important‌ attachments, as they‌ allow the broom to fly.
Eventually‌ the brush‌ will be damaged, and‌ will‌ break.
&8All brushes‌ can‌ be enchanted by the‌ way.
ftbquests.chapter.hexerei.quest4665C4EBA: Unlike‌ the candles, Candelabras wont go‌ out‌ on their own.
They‌ can‌ be‌ placed on‌ top‌ of a block, or‌ under a block. Including chains‌ and‌ more.
ftbquests.chapter.hexerei.quest480570240: The candles‌ are‌ a‌ dyeable, decorative block‌ which‌ can be used for‌ lightning or‌ magic.
Up‌ to 4‌ different candles‌ can‌ be‌ placed in‌ the same block.
A candle‌ can‌ be lit with‌ a flint‌ and stell‌ and‌ will‌ typically stay lit‌ for‌ 35 minutes.
&8Candles‌ are‌ lit‌ individually, in the‌ order of they‌ were placed‌ in.
&8When placed‌ near‌ an‌ altar and‌ lit, the candles‌ will start floating‌ around it.
&8You‌ can also craft several items‌ with candle‌ to add a‌ decorative‌ base to‌ it!
ftbquests.chapter.hexerei.quest54240BF12: The‌ Herb Jar‌ is‌ perfect‌ for keeping‌ ingredients‌ in bulk.
It can hold‌ up to‌ 1024‌ items of‌ only one‌ type.
Like‌ coffers, herb‌ jars also‌ have a crow icon, letting‌ your‌ crows keep your‌ herb collection‌ tidy!
ftbquests.chapter.hexerei.quest550EED2B2: Courier‌ letters are great for‌ sending‌ secret messages to‌ other‌ players‌ or depots.
Whether‌ you're‌ sharing important information‌ or just keeping in‌ touch.
Delivered‌ by our witch‌ trusty owls;
Your‌ words will‌ always‌ find‌ their way‌ to‌ the intended recipient!
ftbquests.chapter.hexerei.quest5A487F862: A witch's‌ main tool‌ of transportation!
&8The willow is the‌ slowest but‌ also the most‌ common‌ one.
&8The mahogany‌ being‌ the fastest but rarest‌ to‌ find one.
Brooms have‌ three‌ slots‌ for upgrades: Misc, Satchel, and‌ Brush.
The‌ brush is what‌ allows the broom to‌ fly‌ and it comes‌ with every‌ broom you‌ make!
ftbquests.chapter.hexerei.quest5D3BA46F1: Crow‌ flute is‌ an‌ essential item‌ that controls‌ your‌ crow‌ companions.
It has‌ a menu for assigning‌ commands, selecting‌ crows and setting‌ a crow's‌ perch position!
ftbquests.chapter.hexerei.quest61DB44DC9: Blood‌ is a‌ key‌ ingredient‌ in the‌ creation of flying‌ brooms.
Can be‌ acquired by‌ using‌ blood‌ sigil!
ftbquests.chapter.hexerei.quest6405BF216: Cuorier depots‌ serve as‌ a crucial‌ center‌ for‌ managing all‌ your deliveries.
With‌ this efficient design‌ and charming‌ aesthetics, it ensures that every parcel‌ and massage‌ is delivered with‌ utmost‌ care and‌ precision!
ftbquests.chapter.hexerei.quest6829096FF: The pestle‌ and‌ mortar is used for‌ smashing‌ and grinding items‌ to‌ paste.
This‌ will be‌ used‌ for making the‌ blends and pastes for‌ infusing‌ your candles to‌ give them‌ effects!
ftbquests.chapter.hexerei.quest688E3BBF4: The broom‌ seat‌ is a mix‌ between a‌ satchel and‌ a‌ cosmetic‌ seat, making the‌ rider‌ face forwards.
ftbquests.chapter.hexerei.quest6C47E7849: The‌ dowsing‌ rrod‌ is able‌ to loacte certain biomes‌ containing‌ the need for‌ plants.
Sneak Right-click‌ to flip‌ between‌ searching‌ for swamps or‌ jungles.
ftbquests.chapter.hexerei.quest70630186B: The Dipper‌ is‌ an attachment for the‌ mixing cauldron, mainly‌ used‌ for making‌ candles by‌ dipping‌ string‌ into the‌ tallow.
Sneak Right-Click to put‌ attachment‌ on cauldron!
ftbquests.chapter.hexerei.quest721C181D9: Sage burning‌ plate‌ can‌ protect your home‌ from‌ monsters.
Simply place‌ one‌ down, fill‌ it with‌ bundle of dried‌ sage, then light‌ it to‌ prevent‌ monster‌ spawns.
By default, it's‌ effect can‌ reach in a‌ 48 block‌ radious around the plate!
Can also‌ use dried‌ sage bundle to‌ stop‌ spawns!
ftbquests.chapter.hexerei.quest73D552422: The crystal ball‌ is a‌ useful tool, able‌ to‌ reveal‌ the phase‌ of‌ the moon, or the sun‌ if it's‌ daytime.
ftbquests.chapter.hexerei.quest774532320: Satchels allow‌ the‌ broom to‌ store‌ items.
It‌ has few‌ variants including a‌ bigger satchel‌ for more‌ storage!
ftbquests.chapter.hexerei.questA34AE3D5E: The‌ Blood‌ Sigil is a sigil‌ for‌ the mixing cauldron, able‌ to‌ extract‌ blood from‌ entities‌ who jump in‌ the cauldron.
The blood can‌ then‌ be used in‌ recipes later, bottled‌ or bucketed‌ aswell.
ftbquests.chapter.hexerei.questBCC02F443: This broom‌ brush‌ makes‌ the broom‌ faster, especialy‌ during the full‌ moon!
ftbquests.chapter.hexerei.questCF29512E4: It's‌ quite‌ good‌ for bashing things‌ in‌ the face.

ftbquests.chapter.how_stats_work.quest10: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Every mob has a level. Yours decides theirs, and yours comes from kills and from the bosses you have beaten.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#9A7CFF to=#DDD2FF f=0.6>Mobs Level Up</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.how_stats_work.quest15: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Spell power is linear: </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>+0.10</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> is 10 percent more. Cooldown reduction compounds: </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>1 / (1 - c)</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, so 0.5 is twice the casts. Mana regen caps at </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>100</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.how_stats_work.quest17: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Your damage is the weapon's tier floor, times crits, times how much of the target's armour you get through.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.how_stats_work.quest1E: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Eaten once each: </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>300, 500, 800 percent</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> spell power and Ars spells hitting 3, 6, 9 harder. Death keeps it.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.how_stats_work.quest1F: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A parry catches hits for </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>3 ticks</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. Footwork ranks add more.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Perfect parries need </grad><grad from=#FFD08A to=#E0662E f=0.8>Cold Read</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> rank 1, which costs </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>30</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> parries. At most half the window can ever count as perfect.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.how_stats_work.quest22: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Every weapon family has one art. Learn it on the </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>Weapon Arts</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> page of a Study Lectern, then press the art key, </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>Mouse 5</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> by default, with that weapon in hand.</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>Iaido</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> (Katanas): draw and sheathe. Everything in front is cut on the click.</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>Pinpoint Flurry</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> (Rapiers): a burst of stabs that fills your element fast.</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>Mark and Blink</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> (Daggers): throw to mark an enemy, press again to appear behind it and stab.</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>Skewer</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> (Spears): lunge and carry the first enemy into a wall or another enemy.</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>Sweep the Legs</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> (Glaives and halberds): a low sweep that trips and roots.</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>Pillar</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> (Staffs): slam the staff and let it grow along the ground.</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>Harvest</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> (Scythes): throw a crescent that marks, then rip the marked back to you.</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>Ricochet</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> (Chakrams and warglaives): a throw that bounces between enemies and comes back.</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>Pounce</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> (Fists and bare hands): leap at the enemy you look at and land on it.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>Arts take your weapon's element. The slot next to your hotbar shows the cooldown.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>All arts share one cooldown of </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>3 minutes</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. Every swing that lands on an enemy takes time off it, so about </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>15 seconds</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> of steady fighting refills it, with a fast weapon or a slow one.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Each art has </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>3</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> ranks. Rank 1 teaches it, rank 2 changes how it works, rank 3 adds a last stage.</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>Gathering Cut</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> (Greatswords): hold to charge, release for a rising cut. You cannot be knocked back while charging.</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>Fault Line</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> (Great hammers): smash the ground and send a crack forward that launches what it passes.</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>Headsman</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> (Axes): hook the nearest enemy, pull it in, chop. Hits harder the more health it is missing.</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>Bell Toll</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> (Maces and hammers): slam, daze, and a ring that spreads outward.</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>Blade Dance</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> (Swords): blink between up to 3 enemies and cut each.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#F05A5A to=#F05A5A>Mouse 5</grad>
Noted
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#F05A5A to=#FFC8A0 f=0.6>Weapon Arts</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.how_stats_work.quest25: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A Somber Smithing Stone adds </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>0.5</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> damage to a weapon, up to </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>10</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> stones. A Smithing Stone adds a 10 different durability health, no cap.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.how_stats_work.quest26: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Every level of a protection enchantment on your gear cuts </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>2.5 percent</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, capped at </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>85 percent</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. That cap is 34 levels across four pieces.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>It multiplies with armour, it is not added to it.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.how_stats_work.quest27: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>13 percent</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> of any hit from an attacker lands no matter what you wear. Armour, protection, curios, all of it stops at 87 percent.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The other way round too: no single hit from an attacker takes more than </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>half</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> your max health.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>A parry or a dodge cancels the hit outright. The floor never sees those. Falls and lava are not attackers.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#8FB3DC to=#8FB3DC>The Balance.. yin and yang</grad>
ftbquests.chapter.how_stats_work.quest29: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Killing mobs at your level raises your level every </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>5</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> kills. Mobs below your level count for far less.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.how_stats_work.quest2C: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Every weapon does at least its tier's damage: iron </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>6</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, golden </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>8</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, emerald </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>11</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, diamond </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>14</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, netherite </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>18</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, elvenite </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>24</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, voiderite </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>31</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, bloody </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>40</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, helionite </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>50</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>It is a damage per second budget of </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>(floor + 1) x 1.8</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, so a fast weapon settles below its floor and a slow one sits on it. Pickaxes and shovels get 40 percent.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.how_stats_work.quest3D: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Each Armageddon Keeper you beat adds levels straight to yours: </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>2, 5, 13, 25, 43, 69, 102, 146, 200</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> at the tenth. It shows as Item Level in the difficulty tab.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>It is back loaded on purpose. The early game barely moves.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.how_stats_work.quest3E: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Bosses have their own fixed level. Your level never touches them.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.how_stats_work.quest41: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Elemental hits fill a meter on the target. When it fills, it goes off. Jade shows the meters on whatever you look at.</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#74D452 to=#74D452>Nature</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>: Overgrowth, rooted, then rots, and the rot spreads to a neighbour</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#E384FF to=#E384FF>Arcane</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>: Unravel, </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>6%%</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> max health to it and around it, </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>20%%</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> more elemental damage, some mana back</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>After it goes off, the next one takes longer. Bosses fill at half speed, take smaller bursts and never get stunned or rooted.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>Weapon tooltips say which one a weapon builds.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>About </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>5</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> sword hits. Slow weapons fill it faster per hit, weaknesses fill it faster, resistances never fill it.</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FF7A2E to=#FF7A2E>Fire</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>: Scorch, set alight, </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>15%%</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> more fire damage</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#86DCFF to=#86DCFF>Frost</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>: Frostbite, </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>8%%</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> max health, slowed, </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>15%%</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> more damage</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFE14D to=#FFE14D>Lightning</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>: Overcharge, jumps to </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>3</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> nearby mobs, stuns</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFF0A0 to=#FFF0A0>Holy</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>: Judgement, a beam for </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>+50%%</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, double on undead, no healing</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#9575E0 to=#9575E0>Dark</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>: Dread, deals </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>30%%</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> less, and a quarter of the damage it took hits again when it ends</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#E0303F to=#E0303F>Blood</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>: Hemorrhage, </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>12%%</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> max health, then bleeds, more while moving</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#F05A5A to=#F05A5A>Numbers go brrr</grad>
Noted
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#F05A5A to=#FFC8A0 f=0.6>Status Effects</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Every number below is the one the game actually uses. Six topics, read whichever one bit you last.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A8ECF4 to=#3FC2D6 f=0.8>The Roll</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>: dash, roll, red attacks.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#C7B8FF to=#7B5CE6 f=0.8>Mobs Level Up</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>: kills, your gear, death, traits.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#9BEC86 to=#3FBF4F f=0.8>Buffs</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>: food, spell power, summons, mana shards.</grad></shadow>
[gap=5]
[gap=5]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#CFDDEE to=#7C9CC4 f=0.8>Taking Damage</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>: armour, protection, the floor, dodge.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFB3B3 to=#E04B4B f=0.8>Dealing Damage</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>: tier floors, crits, penetration, lifesteal.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFD08A to=#E0662E f=0.8>The Parry</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>: window, whiff, heavy hits, payoff.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#F0B23A to=#F0B23A>Numbers, no fluff</grad>
Okay
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#F0B23A to=#FFF0CC f=0.6>How Stats Work</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A hit worth </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>25 percent</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> of your max health or more only half parries: </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>30 percent</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> of it leaks, capped at </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>15 percent</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> of your max health.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Braced ranks cut the leak. A perfect parry ignores it.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#F07A34 to=#F07A34>Brace</grad>
Noted
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#F07A34 to=#FFE6BE f=0.6>Heavy Hits</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.how_stats_work.quest42: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Summon Damage multiplies every summon you own: Iron's, Ars, Goety, Summonity, and tamed pets. A full build reaches about </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>3x</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.how_stats_work.quest46: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Any parry makes the attacker stumble for </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>14 ticks</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, then leaves it Exposed for </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>60 ticks</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. It takes </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>20%%</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> more damage and every hit you land makes it flinch. Bosses skip the stumble.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A perfect parry makes both last </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>1.5x</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> as long and resets your parry cooldown. There is no special follow up, you just hit it.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.how_stats_work.quest4A: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Four multipliers on top of gear. Food is the one nobody uses.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.how_stats_work.quest4B: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>One key, two moves. A tap is a dash, a second tap is the roll. Both make you untouchable for a moment.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.how_stats_work.quest51: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Some reforges add a damage type. The name tells you: </grad><grad from=#FFE14D to=#FFE14D>Lightning</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> for Storm Cleaver, </grad><grad from=#E0303F to=#E0303F>Blood</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> for Crimson Verdict.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>A glass bottle and two of the element's ingredient make two. JEI lists them.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Some reforges are only a type, no other stats. Every stone can roll them.</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Same type as the weapon: weakness hits get </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>+5%%</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> at common up to </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>+25%%</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> at mythic, doubled while boosted. Stars raise it.</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Different type: it works at half strength, unless the reforge is only a type.</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Each hit uses whichever type is best against the target, so a reforge never makes it worse.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Imbuements coat a weapon in an element for </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>90 seconds</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. On a weapon that already has that element, every hit counts as boosted.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#F05A5A to=#FFC8A0 f=0.6>Reforges and Imbuements</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.how_stats_work.quest53: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Heals </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>damage x (lifesteal - 1)</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. Lifesteal 1.2 heals 20 percent of every hit you land.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.how_stats_work.quest54: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The Study Lectern has a tab for the roll. Every dodge and every red attack you roll through is banked there and buys ranks.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A8ECF4 to=#3FC2D6 f=0.8>Sidestep</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> widens the untouchable part of a dodge, </grad><grad from=#A8ECF4 to=#3FC2D6 f=0.8>Stride</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> lengthens it, </grad><grad from=#A8ECF4 to=#3FC2D6 f=0.8>Second Wind</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> adds charges and </grad><grad from=#A8ECF4 to=#3FC2D6 f=0.8>Breath</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> refills them faster. </grad><grad from=#A8ECF4 to=#3FC2D6 f=0.8>Momentum</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> hands charge back for a dodge that actually slipped a hit, </grad><grad from=#A8ECF4 to=#3FC2D6 f=0.8>Punish</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> makes the next swing land harder and </grad><grad from=#A8ECF4 to=#3FC2D6 f=0.8>Opening</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> keeps the mob staggered longer.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A8ECF4 to=#3FC2D6 f=0.8>Air Step</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, </grad><grad from=#A8ECF4 to=#3FC2D6 f=0.8>Featherfall</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and </grad><grad from=#A8ECF4 to=#3FC2D6 f=0.8>Bash</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> are new moves. </grad><grad from=#A8ECF4 to=#3FC2D6 f=0.8>Mirror Step</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> answers a dodged red attack on the spot. </grad><grad from=#A8ECF4 to=#3FC2D6 f=0.8>Last Straw</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> sharpens the dodge when you are close to death.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.how_stats_work.quest58: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>If you miss the parry it locks it for </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>140 ticks</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and gives you Slowness II for </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>60</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Recovery ranks cut the lockout. Sure Footing cuts the slow by 20 ticks a rank and removes it at full rank.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.how_stats_work.quest5A: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Dodge chance from gear and curios caps at </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>40 percent</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. A dodged hit never EVER lands, so it's better than every other layer.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.how_stats_work.quest61: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Two crit systems roll on every hit and both can land.</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFB3B3 to=#E04B4B f=0.8>Brutality</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>: crit chance is a multiplier capped at </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>2x</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, crit damage caps at </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>3x</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFB3B3 to=#E04B4B f=0.8>Apothic</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>: </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>5 percent</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> base chance, </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>1.5x</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> damage.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Perfect Hits are a third thing: </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>5 percent</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> of melee swings deal </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>1.5x</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> with </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>4x</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> knockback and a flash.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.how_stats_work.quest64: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Every hit has a type. Weapons show theirs under the name.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#B8916E to=#B8916E>Blunt</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>: boosted by heavy armour.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#E8C99A to=#E8C99A>Pierce</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>: boosted by a target in the air.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#D9D9D9 to=#D9D9D9>Slash</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>: boosted by no armour.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FF7A2E to=#FF7A2E>Fire</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>: boosted by hot places and the Nether.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#86DCFF to=#86DCFF>Frost</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>: boosted by the cold or a frozen target.</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Physical: </grad><grad from=#D9D9D9 to=#D9D9D9>Slash</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, </grad><grad from=#E8C99A to=#E8C99A>Pierce</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, </grad><grad from=#B8916E to=#B8916E>Blunt</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. Swords and axes slash. Spears, bows and guns pierce. Hammers, staffs and fists are blunt.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFE14D to=#FFE14D>Lightning</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>: boosted by rain or a wet target.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFF0A0 to=#FFF0A0>Holy</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>: boosted by daylight.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#E0303F to=#E0303F>Blood</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>: boosted by a wounded target.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#E384FF to=#E384FF>Arcane</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>: boosted by the End or a full moon.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#9575E0 to=#9575E0>Dark</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>: boosted by darkness.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#74D452 to=#74D452>Nature</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>: boosted by a poisoned target.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>Every boss on The Path is weak to something different. The boss damage ceiling still applies.</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Elements: </grad><grad from=#FF7A2E to=#FF7A2E>Fire</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, </grad><grad from=#86DCFF to=#86DCFF>Frost</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, </grad><grad from=#FFE14D to=#FFE14D>Lightning</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, </grad><grad from=#FFF0A0 to=#FFF0A0>Holy</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, </grad><grad from=#9575E0 to=#9575E0>Dark</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, </grad><grad from=#E0303F to=#E0303F>Blood</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, </grad><grad from=#74D452 to=#74D452>Nature</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, </grad><grad from=#E384FF to=#E384FF>Arcane</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. An elemental weapon hits with its element.</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Spells hit with their school, burning is </grad><grad from=#FF7A2E to=#FF7A2E>Fire</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, and arrows take the type of whatever shot them.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Mobs can be weak to a type, </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>x1.25</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, or resist it, </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>x0.75</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. Look at a mob to see which.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Each type has a boost. While it is on, a weakness takes </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>x1.5</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and a resistance holds at </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>x0.5</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.how_stats_work.quest67: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A meal's score is </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>hunger + hunger x saturation x 2</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. Score 12 is </grad><grad from=#9BEC86 to=#3FBF4F f=0.8>Well Fed</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, 24 is </grad><grad from=#9BEC86 to=#3FBF4F f=0.8>Plenty Satisfied</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, 30 is </grad><grad from=#9BEC86 to=#3FBF4F f=0.8>Exquisitely Stuffed</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>They give </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>5, 10, 15 percent</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> attack damage, spell power, summon damage, arrow damage and speed, plus 10, 20, 30 percent mining speed, for </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>10, 15, 20</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> minutes. A higher tier replaces a lower one.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.how_stats_work.quest68: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Dying drops your level to </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>30 percent</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> of what it was.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.how_stats_work.quest6B: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Your hit sees the target's armour </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>x (2 - penetration) - lethality</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. Penetration caps at </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>1.95</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Against a 450 armour boss, a 150 hit does </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>14 percent</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> at base and </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>77 percent</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> at the cap. The last 0.05 is worth five times the first.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>Lethality subtracts a flat amount. A few points do nothing against boss armour.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.how_stats_work.quest6D: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Every parry, perfect parry and level you have is banked at the Study Lectern and buys ranks in the parry tab.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFD08A to=#E0662E f=0.8>Footwork</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> holds the window open longer, </grad><grad from=#FFD08A to=#E0662E f=0.8>Cold Read</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> is what makes a parry perfect, </grad><grad from=#FFD08A to=#E0662E f=0.8>Recovery</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> shortens the whiff, </grad><grad from=#FFD08A to=#E0662E f=0.8>Anchor</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> takes the shove out of heavy hits, </grad><grad from=#FFD08A to=#E0662E f=0.8>Mend</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> heals, </grad><grad from=#FFD08A to=#E0662E f=0.8>Stagger</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> decides what the mob eats.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFD08A to=#E0662E f=0.8>Deflection</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> sends shots back, </grad><grad from=#FFD08A to=#E0662E f=0.8>Unbinding</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> catches attacks that cannot normally be parried, </grad><grad from=#FFD08A to=#E0662E f=0.8>Siphon</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, </grad><grad from=#FFD08A to=#E0662E f=0.8>Soul Tithe</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and </grad><grad from=#FFD08A to=#E0662E f=0.8>Blood Tithe</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> pay you in mana, souls and life essence. </grad><grad from=#FFD08A to=#E0662E f=0.8>Ironhand</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> parries with empty hands.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.how_stats_work.quest6E: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A mob level is </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>+1 percent</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> health and damage. A level 100 mob has double both.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>One of your levels is about </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>1.2</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> mob levels in the Overworld and Nether, </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>1.5</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> in the End.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.how_stats_work.quest77: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Damage you take is </grad><grad from=#CFDDEE to=#ff030b f=0.8>A</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> divided by </grad><grad from=#CFDDEE to=#ff030b f=0.8>A + your armour</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. </grad><grad from=#CFDDEE to=#ff030b f=0.8>A</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> is 10 for a hit under 20 damage and grows with bigger hits. So, big hits cut through armour and small ones do not!</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Armour </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#03ff25 f=0.8>67</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> already takes chip/small damage down to the floor. Every point past that only matters against boss level hits.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>Armour toughness does nothing to incoming damage. It only blunts an attacker's armour shred.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#8FB3DC to=#8FB3DC>67 is the magic number</grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A mob spends its level on traits, up to </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>15</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. A trait's rank caps at the highest rank you have already killed, plus one.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A Bottle of Curse adds </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>50</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> levels to the mobs around you. Hostility orbs drop as your level climbs.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.how_stats_work.quest78: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>5 tick</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> step at 40 percent of a roll's distance, invulnerable for the first </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>2 ticks</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, back every </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>1.6</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> seconds.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A mob winding up a red heavy attack cannot be parried. Roll through it and the mob eats a </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>60 tick</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> posture break instead.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.how_stats_work.quest79: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Fill two element meters on the same enemy to </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>half</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> or more and they react. Both meters empty, and that enemy cannot react again for </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>10 seconds</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>Eclipse</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>: ignores the target's resistances to damage types for 4 seconds. Armour still counts.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>Fester</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>: Bleeding II and Rot II, and both spread to 2 nearby enemies.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>Wildfire</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>: sets the target and enemies within 5 blocks on fire.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>Crimson Ice</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>: frozen in place for 2 seconds, then 12%% of max health.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>Smite</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>: a lightning strike for 10%% of max health, 16%% on undead.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>Bloodletting</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>: 8%% of max health, and you heal 12%% of yours.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>Frostbloom</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>: roots the target and enemies within 4 blocks, with Frostbite.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>Arterial Surge</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>: 6%% of max health, and Bleeding jumps to 3 nearby enemies.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>Sunfire</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>: 8%% of max health, 14%% on undead, and burns undead nearby.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>Resonance</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>: Arcane plus any other element: that element goes off at once, and you get mana back.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>Bosses take half of everything here.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Two elements come from an imbuement on an elemental weapon, a typed reforge, or a different weapon in each hand.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>Shatter</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>: 14%% of max health. Clears freezing and fire.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>Detonation</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>: 10%% of max health to the target and up to 10%% to enemies within 4 blocks. Never hurts you or blocks.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>Superconduct</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>: Exposed II for 8 seconds and a short stun.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.how_stats_work.quest7A: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Press again within </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>10 ticks</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> of the dash: an </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>8 tick</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> roll, invulnerable for the first </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>2 ticks</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, back every </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>4</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> seconds at the base Roll Recharge of 20.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Needs more than </grad><grad from=#FFD98A to=#FFB347 f=0.8>6</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> food and costs 0.1 exhaustion. You cannot attack or use items until it ends. No direction held rolls you backwards at 60 percent distance.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.how_stats_work.quest7F: Four things stand between a hit and your health bar. They multiply etc..
ftbquests.chapter.how_stats_work.questCC: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Raise a shield or press "F" with a weapon at the right moment and boom. Ranks at the Study Lectern change every number here.</grad></shadow>

ftbquests.chapter.ice_element.quest49184: Hold to cast out‌ a cone‌ of cold energy, freezing‌ creatures‌ in its‌ path.

ftbquests.chapter.ice_element.quest5BF66: Fire‌ a beam of‌ cold‌ energy, dealing low‌ damage‌ but immediately applying freeze‌ to‌ the creature hit.
ftbquests.chapter.ice_element.quest6D46B: The‌ Ice school‌ is centered around‌ damage and‌ crowd control.
ftbquests.chapter.ice_element.quest77EDF: Cascade a‌ wave‌ of‌ frost magic‌ in‌ a radius around you, afflicting‌ creatures with‌ chilled. Chilled‌ creatures are‌ slowed, and have‌ their‌ incoming‌ freeze time‌ doubled.

The Crusher‌ multiblock from‌ Immersive‌ Engineering‌ lets us‌ crush materials‌ on a larger‌ scale.
It breaks‌ items down, sometimes producing materials we‌ couldn’t get‌ before
The‌ Industrial‌ Squeezer is used‌ to‌ extra‌ oil from‌ seeds.
It‌ can also be‌ used to squeeze Coke‌ Dust‌ into Graphite Dust.
With electricity‌ available, we can add‌ Blast‌ Furnace Preheaters‌ to‌ boost our Improved Blast‌ Furnace.
This the‌ Lightning Rod, we can harness‌ this‌ power and generate‌ energy from‌ it.
The lightning‌ will‌ strike‌ the rod and‌ generate‌ power.
Steel fences‌ can‌ be‌ used to‌ increase the height‌ of the‌ rod.
The Fermenter‌ multiblock is used to produce‌ Ethanol.
Ethanol can‌ be made from‌ various‌ crops and‌ used‌ to create other resources
This‌ machine allows for continuous, automated Steel‌ output.
Now‌ we‌ can dive‌ into‌ the mod!
Applying Creosote Oil‌ to‌ regular‌ planks gives‌ us‌ access to Treated‌ Planks. Treated Planks are used‌ to‌ make higher end‌ equipment and‌ machinery. We want‌ to‌ keep‌ a steady‌ supply‌ of these.
&7I don't really‌ know the‌ mod‌ btw, so here's‌ a tutorial‌ video.
The Sawmill‌ cuts‌ logs‌ into planks faster‌ than‌ the Create‌ saw.
It‌ also‌ produces Sawdust, which‌ can be used‌ to make‌ cardboard boxes.
Connecting‌ Water Wheels‌ to a Kinetic‌ Dynamo lets‌ you passively‌ generate‌ power‌ from flowing‌ water.
Make sure‌ the water isn’t‌ flowing against‌ parts of the wheel it‌ shouldn’t, or it‌ will slow down‌ the‌ rotation.
With‌ Biodiesel‌ ready, we can build a‌ Diesel Generator‌ to‌ produce much‌ more power.
This‌ is‌ one‌ of our‌ first major steps toward‌ large-scale‌ power production.
Set it‌ up, supply the materials, and it‌ will‌ craft the recipes‌ you’ve assigned‌ automatically.
With‌ Coke‌ Dust ready, we‌ can start building a‌ Coke‌ Oven. It takes some‌ time to‌ make, but it‌ lets‌ us‌ produce Coal Coke‌ and‌ Creosote.
Building a‌ Blast‌ Furnace‌ lets you‌ use the Coal‌ Coke we’ve‌ been producing‌ to‌ superheat‌ Iron into‌ Steel.
It also‌ creates Slag as‌ a byproduct!
With‌ a Metal‌ Press, you‌ can‌ use electricity to‌ create‌ plates, rods, and wires.
It’s‌ faster‌ and‌ more automatable‌ than the Create‌ Press.
This‌ book‌ is‌ a life‌ saver if‌ you are confused!
It‌ shows tons‌ of information about multi-block structures‌ and more.
The Arc Furnace‌ provides‌ us with‌ a‌ simpiler way to be‌ able‌ to produce HOP‌ Graphite‌ without‌ having to‌ loose‌ so many resources.
It‌ also opens up the‌ ability‌ to begin processing‌ all of‌ the Osmium‌ we‌ had‌ been gathering.
The‌ main tool‌ in Immersive Engineering‌ is the‌ Engineer’s Hammer. It’s used to rotate‌ machines and‌ assemble multiblock structures.
With the‌ Refinery, we can‌ create new‌ resources‌ by‌ refining what we‌ already‌ have.
Combine Ethanol‌ and‌ Plant‌ Oil to‌ make Biodiesel for‌ power generation.
You‌ can also‌ produce‌ Phenolic‌ Resin, which is‌ needed for‌ other materials later‌ on.
You can‌ harness‌ wind power using Windmills‌ connected‌ to a Kinetic‌ Dynamo.
Simply‌ place‌ a Windmill‌ on‌ the Dynamo, and the‌ wind will generate power‌ automatically.
Windmill‌ Sails improve the‌ efficiency of‌ your windmills.
Attach‌ them‌ to‌ a windmill‌ to‌ generate more energy from‌ the wind.
The Mixer‌ is‌ used to create‌ Redstone Acid, which‌ is essential‌ for‌ progressing‌ in Mekanism.
It‌ can‌ also combine experience with‌ mob drops‌ to‌ produce Mob‌ Essence for‌ crafting‌ special‌ resources.
LV, MV, and‌ HV‌ Accumulators&r are‌ a compact‌ way‌ to‌ store power.
Use‌ the Engineer’s Hammer to‌ configure‌ their input and‌ output sides.
The Thermoelectric‌ Generator‌ produces‌ power from‌ heat‌ differences.
Just place different heat‌ blocks around‌ it‌ and the‌ energy will‌ start‌ flowing.
Check‌ your Engineer’s‌ Manual for details on‌ how‌ much each block‌ contributes.
Building and‌ designing the‌ same‌ thing‌ repeatedly can be‌ frustrating, that’s‌ where Schematicannon‌ comes‌ in.
The‌ Bottling Machine‌ is essential‌ for‌ producing‌ advanced resources.
Phenolic‌ Resin‌ can be turned into‌ Duroplast and‌ Grinding‌ Disks.
It can‌ also create‌ Redstone‌ Acid‌ Dusts.
Excavators are‌ machines‌ that‌ gather resources‌ from the‌ world.
They work chunk‌ by chunk, digging‌ and collecting materials until the‌ resources in‌ the area are‌ fully‌ depleted.
You can‌ make‌ Rough Rods with a‌ Metal‌ Press, or get the‌ recipe‌ from‌ a trader‌ to‌ craft them in‌ an Engineer’s Table.

ftbquests.chapter.industrial_foregoing.q: # <grad from=#5DBE5D to=#BCEDBC f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Closing The‌ Loop</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Plastic, a furnace, two‌ pistons, two bricks, an iron gear and‌ a Pity‌ frame.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Every </grad><grad from=#5DBE5D to=#BCEDBC f=0.8>1000 sewage</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> becomes one </grad><grad from=#5DBE5D to=#BCEDBC f=0.8>Fertilizer</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, in‌ five‌ seconds. Twenty cow-cycles‌ per‌ fertilizer.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>That fertilizer goes into‌ the‌ Plant Fertilizer, which grows‌ the‌ crops, which‌ feed the‌ Bioreactor, which‌ powers all of‌ it. The cows are the‌ engine.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#5DBE5D to=#5DBE5D>1000‌ sewage, one fertilizer</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#5DBE5D to=#BCEDBC f=0.6>Sewage Composter</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#4FD9CE to=#BFF5F0 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Burns‌ Enchanted Books</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Eight‌ books‌ around a grindstone, on an </grad><grad from=#4FD9CE to=#BFF5F0 f=0.8>Advanced‌ frame</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Feed‌ it enchanted books. Burn‌ time‌ comes‌ from the‌ enchantment's </grad><grad from=#4FD9CE to=#BFF5F0 f=0.8>rarity</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and‌ power from its </grad><grad from=#4FD9CE to=#BFF5F0 f=0.8>level</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, at‌ 160 per level. It gives‌ the‌ plain book back‌ afterwards.</grad></shadow>
[!tip] Point an‌ Enchantment Sorter‌ at‌ a‌ Mob Crusher‌ and‌ route the enchanted pile‌ straight in‌ here. Free‌ power from‌ junk drops.
<typewriter><grad from=#4FD9CE to=#4FD9CE>Burns‌ your‌ bad‌ loot</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#4FD9CE to=#BFF5F0 f=0.6>Disenchantment Generator</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#E8A33D to=#FFDCA8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Range</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Twelve of‌ them, numbered from‌ 0 to 11, each‌ one‌ a bigger‌ box‌ than the last. Every one‌ is‌ a Dissolution Chamber‌ recipe.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>They‌ go‌ in farms, mob‌ machines, sewers, fertilisers‌ and anything else‌ with a coloured area. Hold‌ the‌ machine and place‌ a bigger‌ addon to‌ watch‌ the‌ box grow.</grad></shadow>
[!warn] The‌ biggest‌ range addon is also‌ a required‌ ingredient‌ in every‌ Infinity tool. Do‌ not‌ use‌ your only‌ one on a plant‌ gatherer.
<typewriter><grad from=#E8A33D to=#E8A33D>Twelve‌ sizes, all in the‌ chamber</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#E8A33D to=#FFDCA8 f=0.6>Range Addons</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#A85A46 to=#E3A794 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Counting</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Plastic, a comparator, two‌ observers, two repeaters‌ and‌ a‌ Simple frame.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>It emits‌ a‌ redstone signal‌ based‌ on‌ how many‌ mobs are in‌ its area, and‌ it can‌ be‌ filtered‌ to only‌ care about‌ one type.</grad></shadow>
[!tip] Wire it‌ to a‌ Mechanical Dirt so the spawner‌ shuts off‌ when the killing‌ floor‌ is already‌ backed‌ up.
<typewriter><grad from=#A85A46 to=#A85A46>Redstone that counts heads</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#A85A46 to=#E3A794 f=0.6>Mob Detector</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#FFCE3D to=#FFEEB0 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Carrying Things</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Two </grad><grad from=#FFCE3D to=#FFEEB0 f=0.8>common‌ Black Hole‌ Units</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, two </grad><grad from=#FFCE3D to=#FFEEB0 f=0.8>common‌ Black‌ Hole Tanks</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, a‌ diamond gear and three‌ gold‌ gears, in 2,000 pink‌ slime.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>It picks‌ items up‌ off‌ the‌ floor into itself, holds‌ far‌ more per‌ slot‌ than‌ a chest‌ would, and can feed‌ the rest‌ of your‌ Infinity‌ gear‌ directly.</grad></shadow>
[!tip] It is‌ the cheapest‌ Infinity item to‌ make and‌ probably the one you will‌ use most.
<typewriter><grad from=#FFCE3D to=#FFCE3D>Black‌ holes you can‌ wear</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#FFCE3D to=#FFEEB0 f=0.6>Infinity Backpack</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#D2503C to=#F5A99B f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Two Fluids‌ At Once</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Plastic, an‌ iron sword, an‌ iron‌ axe, a‌ gold gear, redstone‌ and‌ a Pity frame.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>It kills‌ one mob‌ per‌ cycle and‌ fills both‌ its‌ tanks. It‌ gives no‌ items and no experience, only </grad><grad from=#D2503C to=#F5A99B f=0.8>Liquid‌ Meat</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and </grad><grad from=#D2503C to=#F5A99B f=0.8>Pink‌ Slime</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, and how much‌ of each‌ depends entirely‌ on‌ what‌ you killed.</grad></shadow>
[!danger] This is‌ where‌ Advanced Machine‌ Frames‌ come‌ from. Everything past‌ the halfway point‌ of this‌ mod runs‌ through‌ this‌ block.
<typewriter><grad from=#D2503C to=#D2503C>The pink‌ slime tap</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#D2503C to=#F5A99B f=0.6>Mob Slaughter Factory</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#5DBE5D to=#BCEDBC f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Automatic Fishing</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Plastic, a fishing‌ rod, a bucket, two‌ iron gears, redstone and a Simple‌ frame.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>It needs‌ at least </grad><grad from=#5DBE5D to=#BCEDBC f=0.8>nine water‌ source‌ blocks</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> in its‌ area. Then‌ it rolls the same‌ fishing‌ table you would, and </grad><grad from=#5DBE5D to=#BCEDBC f=0.8>2‌ percent</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> of‌ the‌ time it‌ rolls‌ the </grad><grad from=#5DBE5D to=#BCEDBC f=0.8>treasure</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> table instead.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Treasure means‌ enchanted books, enchanted rods and‌ bows, name‌ tags and nautilus‌ shells, with no‌ luck enchantment‌ needed.</grad></shadow>
[!warn] It‌ costs‌ 5000 energy‌ a‌ cast and only holds‌ 20,000, so it‌ drinks. Give‌ it a‌ proper feed.
<typewriter><grad from=#5DBE5D to=#5DBE5D>Nine‌ water‌ blocks‌ and a‌ fishing rod</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#5DBE5D to=#BCEDBC f=0.6>Marine Fisher</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#4FD9CE to=#BFF5F0 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Burns Nether‌ Plants</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Eight‌ nether‌ wart blocks‌ around a crimson fungus, on‌ an </grad><grad from=#4FD9CE to=#BFF5F0 f=0.8>Advanced‌ frame</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#4FD9CE to=#BFF5F0 f=0.8>Fungus, roots, vines and sprouts</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> burn‌ 200 ticks‌ at 20.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#4FD9CE to=#BFF5F0 f=0.8>Shroomlight</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> burns‌ 200‌ ticks‌ at 40.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#4FD9CE to=#BFF5F0 f=0.8>Nether wart‌ blocks</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> burn‌ 400 ticks‌ at‌ 40.</grad></shadow>
[!tip] A‌ Plant Gatherer‌ over a warped‌ forest floor‌ keeps this‌ fed‌ and‌ gives you‌ the fungus‌ for a hydroponic‌ bed at‌ the same time.
<typewriter><grad from=#4FD9CE to=#4FD9CE>The nether's weeds</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#4FD9CE to=#BFF5F0 f=0.6>Crimed Generator</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#C8AE86 to=#EBD9B8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>The‌ Inversion</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The Slaughter Factory‌ gives you‌ both fluids from every kill, but‌ the ratio‌ flips depending on‌ the‌ victim.</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Kill an </grad><grad from=#C8AE86 to=#EBD9B8 f=0.8>animal</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and‌ you‌ get meat equal to‌ its‌ health, and pink slime‌ equal‌ to‌ its health </grad><grad from=#C8AE86 to=#EBD9B8 f=0.8>times‌ twenty</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Kill‌ a </grad><grad from=#C8AE86 to=#EBD9B8 f=0.8>hostile mob</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and you‌ get meat equal to‌ its‌ health </grad><grad from=#C8AE86 to=#EBD9B8 f=0.8>times twenty</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, and pink‌ slime equal‌ to its‌ health.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>So‌ a‌ cow with‌ 10‌ health gives 10 meat‌ and </grad><grad from=#C8AE86 to=#EBD9B8 f=0.8>200 pink‌ slime</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. A‌ zombie with‌ 20 health‌ gives </grad><grad from=#C8AE86 to=#EBD9B8 f=0.8>400‌ meat</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and‌ 20 pink‌ slime.</grad></shadow>
[!tip] Want pink slime for‌ Advanced‌ frames? Farm cows. Want liquid‌ meat for‌ the ore‌ chain? Farm‌ a‌ mob spawner.
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>One Advanced‌ frame‌ needs 500‌ pink‌ slime, which‌ is roughly‌ three cows. The tanks‌ hold 8,000‌ each, so plumb‌ both‌ out.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#C8AE86 to=#C8AE86>The‌ split is‌ backwards from‌ what you'd guess</grad>
Huh. Okay.
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#C8AE86 to=#EBD9B8 f=0.6>Meat Or Slime, Pick One</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#F2C14E to=#FFE6A8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Burning‌ Things, Badly</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Cobblestone, gold, iron bars, a‌ furnace‌ and‌ a Pity‌ frame. It burns‌ any normal furnace‌ fuel and‌ produces </grad><grad from=#F2C14E to=#FFE6A8 f=0.8>30 energy a tick</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The mod‌ ships this‌ at 400 a‌ tick. This‌ pack cut‌ it‌ to 30, so treat it‌ as‌ a starter battery‌ and‌ not‌ as a‌ power‌ plant.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>It does hold </grad><grad from=#F2C14E to=#FFE6A8 f=0.8>100,000‌ energy</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and pushes out up‌ to‌ 1000 a tick, which‌ makes it‌ a decent‌ buffer‌ next‌ to something‌ better.</grad></shadow>
[!info] Real‌ Industrial Foregoing power is‌ the Biofuel‌ Generator, then‌ the Mycelial‌ generators much‌ later.
<typewriter><grad from=#F2C14E to=#F2C14E>It‌ is‌ called pitiful‌ for a reason</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#F2C14E to=#FFE6A8 f=0.6>Pitiful Generator</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#5DBE5D to=#BCEDBC f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Fertilizer</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Behaves exactly like bone‌ meal‌ in your hand‌ and in‌ the Plant‌ Fertilizer‌ machine.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>You‌ cannot craft it. It‌ comes‌ out of‌ the </grad><grad from=#5DBE5D to=#BCEDBC f=0.8>Sewage‌ Composter</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, which‌ is further‌ down this chapter‌ and involves‌ a lot‌ of‌ cows.</grad></shadow>
[!tip] Until‌ then, ordinary bone‌ meal works‌ fine in the‌ Plant Fertilizer. Nothing‌ is gated on this item.
<typewriter><grad from=#5DBE5D to=#5DBE5D>Bone‌ meal, but from‌ sewage</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#5DBE5D to=#BCEDBC f=0.6>Fertilizer</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#A85A46 to=#E3A794 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Nothing‌ Moves</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Three‌ soul sand, two ghast‌ tears, two‌ gold‌ gears, a piston‌ and‌ an </grad><grad from=#A85A46 to=#E3A794 f=0.8>Advanced frame</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Every mob‌ in its area stops‌ thinking. No‌ pathing, no attacking, no despawning, and‌ it slowly‌ heals them. In‌ this‌ pack‌ it also </grad><grad from=#A85A46 to=#E3A794 f=0.8>hides‌ their‌ boss bars</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, which makes a‌ room full‌ of‌ frozen bosses‌ actually usable.</grad></shadow>
[!danger] Players‌ in‌ the‌ area get‌ hit with a slowness‌ effect‌ so strong you‌ cannot move‌ at all. Do‌ not‌ build‌ the working area‌ over‌ your own‌ walkway.
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>The‌ standard‌ trick is‌ a Stasis Chamber‌ holding a‌ duplicated boss‌ still‌ while‌ a Mob‌ Crusher works‌ on it.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#A85A46 to=#A85A46>Freeze everything, including‌ yourself</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#A85A46 to=#E3A794 f=0.6>Stasis Chamber</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#FFCE3D to=#FFEEB0 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Shooting Things</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Two diamond blocks, a‌ bow, a </grad><grad from=#FFCE3D to=#FFEEB0 f=0.8>Mob‌ Imprisonment Tool</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, the biggest‌ range‌ addon‌ and three‌ gold‌ gears, in 2,000 pink‌ slime.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>It shoots arrows, and it‌ has‌ a </grad><grad from=#FFCE3D to=#FFEEB0 f=0.8>plunger</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> setting that yanks‌ entities toward‌ you instead. Yes, the‌ mob‌ imprisonment‌ tool in‌ the‌ recipe is a hint.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#FFCE3D to=#FFCE3D>A‌ bow that‌ fires‌ mobs</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#FFCE3D to=#FFEEB0 f=0.6>Infinity Launcher</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#D8C9A8 to=#F3EBD8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Dry Rubber</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>One comes out‌ of‌ the Latex Processing‌ Unit per‌ cycle. Get eight‌ before‌ you‌ go further, because everything‌ after‌ this eats‌ plastic‌ and‌ plastic eats‌ these.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>There is a‌ Tiny Dry‌ Rubber item‌ lying‌ around‌ in the‌ mod files‌ with nine of‌ them making‌ one of these. It is marked‌ deprecated and‌ nothing makes it‌ any‌ more, so ignore‌ it.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#D8C9A8 to=#D8C9A8>The‌ middle step nobody remembers</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#D8C9A8 to=#F3EBD8 f=0.6>Dry Rubber</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#D8C9A8 to=#F3EBD8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Curing The‌ Sap</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Latex on‌ its own is‌ useless. Pour </grad><grad from=#D8C9A8 to=#F3EBD8 f=0.8>750 latex</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and </grad><grad from=#D8C9A8 to=#F3EBD8 f=0.8>500‌ water</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> into this and five seconds‌ later you‌ get one Dry‌ Rubber.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>This‌ pack runs‌ it‌ at 20 energy a‌ tick‌ instead of the‌ mod's‌ usual‌ 400, so it‌ is‌ cheap to leave‌ running forever. Its two tanks‌ were‌ doubled to 16,000‌ each as‌ well.</grad></shadow>
[!tip] Feed it‌ water‌ from‌ a Water‌ Condensator‌ or an infinite water‌ source. It drinks‌ more‌ water than‌ you expect.
<typewriter><grad from=#D8C9A8 to=#D8C9A8>750‌ latex‌ and‌ 500 water, five‌ seconds</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#D8C9A8 to=#F3EBD8 f=0.6>Latex Processing Unit</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#D2503C to=#F5A99B f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Never‌ Eat Again</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Plastic, three‌ iron ingots and two glass‌ bottles.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Fill it‌ with Liquid Meat‌ and‌ carry it. When‌ your‌ hunger drops it spends </grad><grad from=#D2503C to=#F5A99B f=0.8>400‌ meat</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and‌ tops you back‌ up, with‌ no‌ clicking and‌ no‌ inventory slot for‌ food.</grad></shadow>
[!tip] It holds a lot‌ and‌ one slaughter factory‌ produces more‌ meat than‌ any‌ player‌ can eat. This‌ is‌ a permanent fix to‌ food.
<typewriter><grad from=#D2503C to=#D2503C>A hunger‌ bar‌ that fills‌ itself</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#D2503C to=#F5A99B f=0.6>Meat Feeder</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#4FD9CE to=#BFF5F0 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Burns‌ Food</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Eight crops‌ around‌ a‌ cooked steak, on‌ a </grad><grad from=#4FD9CE to=#BFF5F0 f=0.8>Simple‌ frame</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Any food works, and both‌ numbers scale‌ with‌ the food‌ itself. Burn time‌ is </grad><grad from=#4FD9CE to=#BFF5F0 f=0.8>nutrition‌ times‌ 160</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, power is </grad><grad from=#4FD9CE to=#BFF5F0 f=0.8>saturation‌ times 80</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Golden carrots and‌ cooked‌ steak are excellent. Cookies‌ are not.</grad></shadow>
[!tip] Point‌ a Plant‌ Gatherer‌ at‌ a pumpkin farm‌ and‌ you have‌ infinite‌ food‌ and infinite‌ power from the‌ same field.
<typewriter><grad from=#4FD9CE to=#4FD9CE>It‌ eats your‌ dinner</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#4FD9CE to=#BFF5F0 f=0.6>Culinary Generator</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#A85A46 to=#E3A794 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Printing‌ Mobs</shadow></grad>
[!warn] This‌ pack‌ charges‌ 5000 energy‌ per operation instead‌ of the‌ mod's 400. Twelve‌ times‌ the‌ bill. Give it‌ a real‌ power line.
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>Exact copy‌ mode is‌ switched off pack-wide, so duplicates come‌ out as‌ fresh mobs, not carbon‌ copies‌ of the‌ one‌ you caught.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Plastic, nether‌ wart, two magma cream, two‌ emeralds, redstone‌ and‌ an </grad><grad from=#A85A46 to=#E3A794 f=0.8>Advanced frame</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Load‌ a </grad><grad from=#A85A46 to=#E3A794 f=0.8>Mob‌ Imprisonment Tool</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> with something‌ in it, fill the tank‌ with </grad><grad from=#A85A46 to=#E3A794 f=0.8>essence</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, and‌ it spawns copies‌ in its‌ area.</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#A85A46 to=#E3A794 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>The Costs</shadow></grad>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Essence‌ per‌ spawn‌ is the‌ mob's‌ health </grad><grad from=#A85A46 to=#E3A794 f=0.8>times twelve</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. A zombie is‌ 240, a blaze‌ is‌ 240, a wither‌ skeleton is‌ 240.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>It‌ spawns </grad><grad from=#A85A46 to=#E3A794 f=0.8>one‌ to four</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> at‌ a time, depending on how‌ much‌ essence is banked.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>It‌ stops if‌ there are‌ already </grad><grad from=#A85A46 to=#E3A794 f=0.8>more‌ than‌ 32</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> of that mob‌ in‌ the area.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#A85A46 to=#A85A46>Essence in, copies out</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#A85A46 to=#E3A794 f=0.6>Mob Duplicator</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#9B6BFF to=#D9C8FF f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>The End Of‌ The Line</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>In‌ the‌ Dissolution Chamber: two‌ plastic, a </grad><grad from=#9B6BFF to=#D9C8FF f=0.8>Supreme frame</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, two‌ netherite‌ ingots, two‌ diamond gears‌ and a </grad><grad from=#9B6BFF to=#D9C8FF f=0.8>nether star</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, sitting in </grad><grad from=#9B6BFF to=#D9C8FF f=0.8>500‌ ether‌ gas</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. Thirty seconds.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>It produces </grad><grad from=#9B6BFF to=#D9C8FF f=0.8>25,000,000‌ energy every‌ tick</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and buffers‌ a‌ hundred‌ million. It will fill‌ an‌ Infinity tool‌ to‌ Legendary‌ in under‌ three minutes.</grad></shadow>
[!danger] It only‌ runs while‌ all sixteen‌ Mycelial‌ generators‌ have fuel. One‌ empty generator‌ anywhere in your‌ world and‌ the Reactor stops dead.
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>That is‌ the whole‌ design. It is not‌ a‌ machine, it is‌ a‌ scoreboard that pays out‌ when‌ you have finished‌ the‌ mod.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#9B6BFF to=#9B6BFF>Twenty‌ five million‌ a‌ tick</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#9B6BFF to=#D9C8FF f=0.6>Mycelial Reactor</grad></shadow>

# <grad from=#D2503C to=#F5A99B f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Step One</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Two pink‌ slime‌ ingots, plastic, a meat feeder, a‌ diamond gear, a‌ furnace and‌ an </grad><grad from=#D2503C to=#F5A99B f=0.8>Advanced‌ frame</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>One‌ ore item‌ plus </grad><grad from=#D2503C to=#F5A99B f=0.8>100‌ Liquid Meat</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> becomes </grad><grad from=#D2503C to=#F5A99B f=0.8>100 Raw Ore‌ Meat</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, and the‌ fluid‌ remembers which‌ ore it‌ came‌ from. Five‌ seconds a‌ go.</grad></shadow>
[!tip] This is the machine‌ that‌ makes the whole‌ cow farm‌ worth building. Liquid‌ Meat‌ is‌ the input, and hostile‌ mobs‌ give twenty‌ times‌ more‌ of it‌ than animals do.
<typewriter><grad from=#D2503C to=#D2503C>Ore‌ goes in, ore‌ soup comes‌ out</grad>

# <grad from=#AFC3D8 to=#E6EFF8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Just‌ Smelt‌ It</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Dry Rubber goes‌ in‌ a‌ furnace, ten seconds, out‌ comes‌ Plastic. That is the‌ last easy step.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Look at‌ any‌ Industrial Foregoing recipe‌ and count‌ the plastic. Most‌ machines‌ want </grad><grad from=#AFC3D8 to=#E6EFF8 f=0.8>four‌ to six</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. The‌ frames‌ want two each. The good‌ tools want‌ a‌ lot more.</grad></shadow>
[!tip] Set‌ up the‌ tree, the‌ extractor, the‌ processing unit‌ and a furnace as‌ one‌ permanent line before‌ you build‌ anything else. You‌ will‌ never‌ stop needing it.
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>Sixteen‌ plastic‌ is roughly‌ 12,000‌ latex. Yes, really.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#AFC3D8 to=#AFC3D8>The‌ single most‌ important item in‌ the mod</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#AFC3D8 to=#E6EFF8 f=0.6>Plastic</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#C8AE86 to=#EBD9B8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>The Five‌ Things‌ That Are Always‌ True</shadow></grad>
5. <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#C8AE86 to=#EBD9B8 f=0.8>Redstone‌ control is‌ built in.</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> A little‌ button in‌ the corner of every machine‌ screen.</grad></shadow>
[!info] Machines idle‌ at almost no‌ cost. They‌ only spend‌ the‌ big number on the‌ tick‌ where they actually‌ do‌ something.

1. <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#C8AE86 to=#EBD9B8 f=0.8>Energy goes‌ in any‌ face.</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> No‌ cables‌ of its‌ own, no‌ preferred side. Use whatever power‌ mod you‌ already‌ like.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]

2. <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#C8AE86 to=#EBD9B8 f=0.8>Every side‌ is configurable.</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> Open‌ the‌ machine, click‌ the side‌ buttons, set each face to‌ push, pull‌ or nothing.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]

3. <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#C8AE86 to=#EBD9B8 f=0.8>Machines with‌ an area‌ show it.</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> Hold‌ one‌ in‌ your hand and‌ a‌ coloured box‌ appears‌ where‌ it will‌ work.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]

4. <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#C8AE86 to=#EBD9B8 f=0.8>Addon slots take‌ upgrades.</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> Speed, efficiency, processing and‌ range all‌ slot‌ in, and‌ they stack.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
<typewriter><grad from=#C8AE86 to=#C8AE86>Read‌ once, never think‌ about‌ it again</grad>
