# <grad from=#FF5A3C to=#FFB9A8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Two‌ Halves</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The laser‌ system is always a </grad><grad from=#FF5A3C to=#FFB9A8 f=0.8>base</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and‌ one‌ or more </grad><grad from=#FF5A3C to=#FFB9A8 f=0.8>drills</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. The base‌ is the‌ block that‌ makes‌ something. The‌ drills are the‌ blocks‌ that shoot‌ at‌ it.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Place‌ a base, then‌ put drills around‌ it facing‌ in. Every drill‌ tick‌ pushes‌ the base's‌ progress bar‌ along, so </grad><grad from=#FF5A3C to=#FFB9A8 f=0.8>more drills means‌ faster output</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. That‌ is the only way to‌ speed it‌ up.</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The </grad><grad from=#FF5A3C to=#FFB9A8 f=0.8>Ore Laser Base</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> makes‌ ores‌ and raw‌ materials.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The </grad><grad from=#FF5A3C to=#FFB9A8 f=0.8>Fluid‌ Laser Base</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> makes fluids.</grad></shadow>
[!info] Drills can‌ be‌ up to a‌ few‌ blocks‌ away and‌ can‌ hit the base‌ from any of the‌ six‌ directions.
<typewriter><grad from=#FF5A3C to=#FF5A3C>Point lasers at‌ a box‌ until ore‌ appears</grad>
Lasers. Obviously.
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#FF5A3C to=#FFB9A8 f=0.6>Laser Drilling</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#4FD9CE to=#BFF5F0 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Burns Ender</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Eight‌ ender‌ pearls around‌ an‌ eye‌ of ender, on‌ an </grad><grad from=#4FD9CE to=#BFF5F0 f=0.8>Advanced frame</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>An </grad><grad from=#4FD9CE to=#BFF5F0 f=0.8>eye of‌ ender</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> burns 3,200‌ ticks at‌ 80. Worth‌ 256,000.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>An </grad><grad from=#4FD9CE to=#BFF5F0 f=0.8>ender‌ pearl</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> burns 1,600‌ ticks at‌ 40. Worth 64,000.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The eye‌ is four‌ times the value for one‌ extra blaze‌ powder, so always craft‌ up‌ before feeding‌ it.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#4FD9CE to=#4FD9CE>Eyes‌ beat pearls</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#4FD9CE to=#BFF5F0 f=0.6>Ender Generator</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#8FE33F to=#D8FFA8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Putting Enchantments‌ On</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Plastic, two anvils, two gold gears and‌ an </grad><grad from=#8FE33F to=#D8FFA8 f=0.8>Advanced frame</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>It‌ combines two items‌ the‌ way an‌ anvil‌ does, but it spends </grad><grad from=#8FE33F to=#D8FFA8 f=0.8>essence</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> instead of‌ your‌ levels, and it never‌ says‌ too‌ expensive.</grad></shadow>
[!danger] This pack‌ switched‌ off the maximum‌ enchantment level check. You can‌ push‌ enchantments past their‌ normal ceiling‌ here, and nothing‌ will‌ stop‌ you. That is‌ deliberate.

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>It‌ also pulls essence out‌ of a </grad><grad from=#8FE33F to=#D8FFA8 f=0.8>tank‌ sitting‌ directly on‌ top of‌ it</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, so‌ the‌ usual build‌ is a Black Hole‌ Tank‌ of essence balanced‌ on the‌ applicator.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>Its own‌ tank‌ holds‌ 64,000, the biggest essence‌ buffer‌ of any‌ machine‌ in‌ the mod.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#8FE33F to=#8FE33F>An‌ anvil with no‌ level cap‌ here</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#8FE33F to=#D8FFA8 f=0.6>Enchantment Applicator</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#A85A46 to=#E3A794 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Catching‌ Things</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Right click a‌ mob‌ and it‌ goes‌ in the jar. Right click‌ the‌ ground and it‌ comes‌ back‌ out.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>It is‌ the‌ only way to‌ load a </grad><grad from=#A85A46 to=#E3A794 f=0.8>Mob Duplicator</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, and it‌ is‌ the fastest way‌ to move‌ a villager‌ or‌ a‌ stubborn animal‌ across‌ a world.</grad></shadow>
[!info] Bosses and a‌ few special‌ entities‌ refuse to‌ be captured. Everything‌ ordinary‌ is‌ fair game.
<typewriter><grad from=#A85A46 to=#A85A46>Four‌ plastic and a ghast‌ tear</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#A85A46 to=#E3A794 f=0.6>Mob Imprisonment Tool</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#AFC3D8 to=#E6EFF8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Belts</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Cheap, fast and‌ they carry‌ items‌ and‌ mobs. Place them in‌ a‌ line and‌ they‌ connect‌ automatically, including up‌ and down slopes.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Right‌ click a‌ belt with‌ a‌ wrench-shaped‌ intent and‌ it changes‌ direction. Dye them if‌ you enjoy‌ that sort of thing.</grad></shadow>
[!info] The real‌ point of‌ belts is the‌ upgrades‌ you clip‌ onto‌ their sides.
<typewriter><grad from=#AFC3D8 to=#AFC3D8>Six plastic, two iron, one‌ redstone</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#AFC3D8 to=#E6EFF8 f=0.6>Conveyor Belt</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#7A5CFF to=#C6BAFF f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Item Storage</shadow></grad>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#7A5CFF to=#C6BAFF f=0.8>Advanced</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> holds‌ 67,108,864.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#7A5CFF to=#C6BAFF f=0.8>Supreme</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> holds 2,147,483,647.</grad></shadow>
[!info] Two‌ common units‌ are also an‌ ingredient in‌ the Infinity Backpack, so make a‌ few spare‌ cheap ones.

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The </grad><grad from=#7A5CFF to=#C6BAFF f=0.8>Common</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> one is‌ iron‌ ingots, wooden chests, an iron‌ gear and‌ a Pity‌ frame. Every‌ grade‌ after that is‌ plastic, ender‌ pearls, eyes of‌ ender, a‌ wooden‌ chest and‌ the matching frame.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Capacity‌ by grade, in‌ items:</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#7A5CFF to=#C6BAFF f=0.8>Common</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> holds 2,048.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#7A5CFF to=#C6BAFF f=0.8>Pity</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> holds‌ 16,384.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#7A5CFF to=#C6BAFF f=0.8>Simple</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> holds‌ 524,288.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
<typewriter><grad from=#7A5CFF to=#7A5CFF>Five grades, one‌ item‌ each</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#7A5CFF to=#C6BAFF f=0.6>Black Hole Units</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#5DBE5D to=#BCEDBC f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>One Plant, Very Fast</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Plastic, dirt, two‌ iron‌ hoes, a Fertilizer, two‌ gold‌ gears and a Simple‌ frame.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Place‌ it, put a plant‌ directly‌ on‌ top and‌ give‌ it water and‌ power. It fires </grad><grad from=#5DBE5D to=#BCEDBC f=0.8>four random growth‌ ticks</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> per‌ cycle and eats‌ 10 water‌ each time. It‌ also‌ harvests‌ and replants‌ for‌ you.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Feed it </grad><grad from=#5DBE5D to=#BCEDBC f=0.8>ether gas</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and that‌ jumps to </grad><grad from=#5DBE5D to=#BCEDBC f=0.8>ten‌ ticks</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> a‌ cycle. One unit‌ of ether‌ gas‌ covers‌ 200 boosted‌ cycles.</grad></shadow>
[!warn] Nether plants want lava‌ in‌ the tank instead‌ of water. Warped‌ and crimson‌ fungus‌ will‌ sit there doing‌ nothing‌ in a‌ water‌ bed.
<typewriter><grad from=#5DBE5D to=#5DBE5D>A‌ growth accelerator‌ you stand a‌ plant on</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#5DBE5D to=#BCEDBC f=0.6>Hydroponic Bed</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#FF6EC7 to=#FFC6E8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>The‌ Alloy</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>In‌ the‌ Dissolution Chamber: two‌ iron ingots and two‌ gold‌ ingots in </grad><grad from=#FF6EC7 to=#FFC6E8 f=0.8>1000 pink‌ slime</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. Fifteen seconds.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>You‌ need these‌ for‌ the </grad><grad from=#FF6EC7 to=#FFC6E8 f=0.8>Washing‌ Factory</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, which is the‌ front‌ door of‌ the‌ ore‌ multiplication chain.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>This‌ pack lets Biomancy‌ decompose one‌ into two‌ to‌ four‌ elastic fibers, if‌ you would‌ rather feed it‌ to something‌ with teeth.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#FF6EC7 to=#FF6EC7>Two iron, two gold, one bucket‌ of goo</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#FF6EC7 to=#FFC6E8 f=0.6>Pink Slime Ingot</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#A85A46 to=#E3A794 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Shearing And‌ Milking</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Plastic, two shears, a‌ bucket, two gold gears‌ and a‌ Pity frame.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Anything shearable gets sheared. Anything‌ milkable gets‌ milked straight into‌ its </grad><grad from=#A85A46 to=#E3A794 f=0.8>1000‌ capacity</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> tank as‌ an‌ actual fluid, so you can‌ pipe‌ milk around.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Squid in‌ the‌ area‌ get shaken‌ down‌ for ink about </grad><grad from=#A85A46 to=#E3A794 f=0.8>one‌ time in sixteen</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>
[!info] It works‌ on‌ modded mobs too‌ as long‌ as they‌ use‌ the‌ normal shearing‌ or‌ bucket behaviour, so mooshrooms, snow golems‌ and most‌ Alex's‌ Mobs creatures‌ are fair‌ game.
<typewriter><grad from=#A85A46 to=#A85A46>Shears, milks, and‌ bullies‌ squid</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#A85A46 to=#E3A794 f=0.6>Animal Rancher</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#7A5CFF to=#C6BAFF f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Storage Without‌ A‌ System</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A‌ Black Hole Unit‌ holds </grad><grad from=#7A5CFF to=#C6BAFF f=0.8>one‌ kind of‌ item</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and‌ an‌ enormous number‌ of them. A Black‌ Hole Tank‌ does the‌ same‌ for‌ one fluid.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>They‌ come in‌ five grades, and each‌ grade is‌ the same recipe with a‌ different machine‌ frame in the‌ middle, so‌ upgrading is‌ just‌ crafting the next one‌ up.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>They‌ keep their contents‌ when‌ broken‌ and picked‌ up, they‌ show what is‌ inside on the block‌ face, and‌ any pipe or‌ hopper can‌ pull from‌ them.</grad></shadow>
[!tip] Put‌ one‌ on the‌ output‌ of a Laser Base‌ or a‌ Mob‌ Crusher and‌ stop thinking‌ about‌ overflow‌ forever.
<typewriter><grad from=#7A5CFF to=#7A5CFF>One block, one‌ item, absurd numbers</grad>
Show me the void
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#7A5CFF to=#C6BAFF f=0.6>Black Holes</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#D8C9A8 to=#F3EBD8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Latex‌ Comes From‌ Logs</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Point‌ one‌ of these‌ at a </grad><grad from=#D8C9A8 to=#F3EBD8 f=0.8>log</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and it drips‌ latex‌ out of it. That‌ is the‌ whole mod's‌ bottleneck‌ in‌ one block, so build‌ several.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Give‌ it energy‌ and‌ it‌ produces </grad><grad from=#D8C9A8 to=#F3EBD8 f=0.8>three times</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> as‌ much per pull, at‌ 500 energy‌ a go. Without‌ power‌ it‌ still works, just‌ slowly and‌ stingily.</grad></shadow>
[!warn] Every pull has‌ a 1‌ percent chance to break the‌ log outright. Feed‌ it from a‌ tree‌ farm, not from‌ your‌ house.
<typewriter><grad from=#D8C9A8 to=#D8C9A8>A tap for trees</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#D8C9A8 to=#F3EBD8 f=0.6>Fluid Extractor</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#4FD9CE to=#BFF5F0 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Burns The‌ Dead</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Eight rotten flesh around‌ a‌ bone, on an </grad><grad from=#4FD9CE to=#BFF5F0 f=0.8>Advanced frame</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#4FD9CE to=#BFF5F0 f=0.8>Rotten‌ flesh</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, </grad><grad from=#4FD9CE to=#BFF5F0 f=0.8>bones</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, </grad><grad from=#4FD9CE to=#BFF5F0 f=0.8>bone blocks</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and </grad><grad from=#4FD9CE to=#BFF5F0 f=0.8>wither‌ skeleton skulls</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> all‌ burn‌ 200‌ ticks at 20‌ a‌ tick. That is‌ 4,000‌ each, which‌ is not‌ much.</grad></shadow>
[!info] It exists mostly‌ so a‌ zombie farm's‌ rotten‌ flesh‌ mountain has‌ somewhere to‌ go, and so you‌ can tick‌ it off for the Reactor.
<typewriter><grad from=#4FD9CE to=#4FD9CE>Rotten‌ flesh, finally useful</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#4FD9CE to=#BFF5F0 f=0.6>Death Generator</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#8FE33F to=#D8FFA8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Liquid Levels</shadow></grad>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The </grad><grad from=#8FE33F to=#D8FFA8 f=0.8>Enchantment‌ Extractor</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, from‌ stripping enchantments off gear.</grad></shadow>
[!tip] The‌ Dissolution Chamber‌ turns‌ 250 essence‌ into an‌ experience‌ bottle‌ in a‌ quarter of a second, with‌ no‌ other ingredients. That is‌ your bank.

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Essence‌ is experience turned into a‌ fluid. The exchange‌ rate is fixed‌ everywhere‌ in the‌ mod: </grad><grad from=#8FE33F to=#D8FFA8 f=0.8>20‌ essence per experience point</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#8FE33F to=#D8FFA8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Where‌ It‌ Comes From</shadow></grad>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The </grad><grad from=#8FE33F to=#D8FFA8 f=0.8>Mob Crusher</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> in‌ experience‌ mode, from‌ every kill.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The </grad><grad from=#8FE33F to=#D8FFA8 f=0.8>Sewer</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, from‌ orbs‌ that land in‌ its area and from‌ players‌ standing in it.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The </grad><grad from=#8FE33F to=#D8FFA8 f=0.8>Resourceful‌ Furnace</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, from the‌ experience each‌ smelt‌ would‌ have given.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
<typewriter><grad from=#8FE33F to=#8FE33F>Experience, but‌ you can‌ pipe‌ it</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#8FE33F to=#D8FFA8 f=0.6>Essence</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#F2C14E to=#FFE6A8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Burning‌ The‌ Green‌ Stuff</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Plastic, a furnace, two‌ pistons, two gold gears and‌ a‌ Pity frame.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>One unit‌ of biofuel‌ burns for‌ four‌ ticks‌ at </grad><grad from=#F2C14E to=#FFE6A8 f=0.8>160 energy a‌ tick</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, so‌ every unit‌ is‌ worth </grad><grad from=#F2C14E to=#FFE6A8 f=0.8>640‌ energy</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. A fully‌ loaded Bioreactor makes‌ 2,135 units‌ every five‌ seconds, which‌ is‌ more than‌ one generator‌ can chew.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>This pack‌ gave it‌ a </grad><grad from=#F2C14E to=#FFE6A8 f=0.8>one million</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> energy buffer and it‌ pushes out‌ up to </grad><grad from=#F2C14E to=#FFE6A8 f=0.8>500 a‌ tick</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, so‌ it doubles‌ as‌ your main battery.</grad></shadow>
[!tip] Build two‌ or‌ three generators off‌ one‌ Bioreactor. The‌ reactor out-produces‌ a‌ single burner easily.
<typewriter><grad from=#F2C14E to=#F2C14E>160‌ a tick, forever, from a garden</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#F2C14E to=#FFE6A8 f=0.6>Biofuel Generator</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#5DBE5D to=#BCEDBC f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Farming‌ Without‌ Plants</shadow></grad>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#5DBE5D to=#BCEDBC f=0.8>1000 harvests</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> is about 130‌ percent, which is‌ better‌ than the‌ real farm.</grad></shadow>
[!tip] Leave‌ a‌ processor‌ in a‌ real bed overnight, then move‌ it. Past‌ 200 recorded harvests‌ the simulation‌ beats the‌ thing‌ it‌ copied.
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>Thirty seconds a‌ cycle‌ and 12,000‌ energy‌ a‌ go in‌ this pack, so it‌ is not‌ free. It is‌ just‌ tidy.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Same‌ recipe as‌ the normal‌ bed but with‌ a </grad><grad from=#5DBE5D to=#BCEDBC f=0.8>Simulation Processor</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> where‌ the dirt goes.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Put the recorded‌ processor in, put‌ one seed of‌ that‌ crop in, and‌ it‌ produces the average drops‌ of‌ the crop it‌ watched. No‌ dirt, no‌ water, no light, no‌ plant‌ on top.</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#5DBE5D to=#BCEDBC f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>How Good‌ It Is</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Output scales with‌ how‌ many harvests the‌ processor recorded.</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#5DBE5D to=#BCEDBC f=0.8>200‌ harvests</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> is exactly‌ 100‌ percent.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#5DBE5D to=#BCEDBC f=0.8>100‌ harvests</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> is about‌ 87‌ percent.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
<typewriter><grad from=#5DBE5D to=#5DBE5D>A‌ farm with‌ no farm‌ attached</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#5DBE5D to=#BCEDBC f=0.6>Simulated Hydroponic Bed</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#4FD9CE to=#BFF5F0 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Burns‌ Potions</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Eight nether wart around‌ a‌ brewing stand, on an </grad><grad from=#4FD9CE to=#BFF5F0 f=0.8>Advanced‌ frame</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Burn time‌ is the‌ potion‌ effect's </grad><grad from=#4FD9CE to=#BFF5F0 f=0.8>duration</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, and‌ power scales off‌ the </grad><grad from=#4FD9CE to=#BFF5F0 f=0.8>amplifier</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. A‌ long strength‌ two‌ potion‌ is worth‌ far more than‌ a splash‌ of weakness. It‌ hands‌ the‌ empty bottle‌ back.</grad></shadow>
[!tip] The Potion‌ Brewer is a‌ few quests‌ up this chapter. These two were‌ built for‌ each other.
<typewriter><grad from=#4FD9CE to=#4FD9CE>Stronger potion, more‌ power</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#4FD9CE to=#BFF5F0 f=0.6>Potion Generator</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#9B6BFF to=#D9C8FF f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>The‌ Endgame Fluid</shadow></grad>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The </grad><grad from=#9B6BFF to=#D9C8FF f=0.8>Fermentation Station</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> burns‌ 1‌ per 100‌ ore meat‌ on‌ its‌ best setting.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#9B6BFF to=#D9C8FF f=0.8>Hydroponic‌ Beds</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and </grad><grad from=#9B6BFF to=#D9C8FF f=0.8>Plant Gatherers</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> both run better‌ on‌ it.</grad></shadow>
[!tip] The proper build‌ is a‌ Wither Builder‌ making‌ them, a‌ Stasis Chamber holding‌ one‌ still and‌ healing‌ it, and‌ a ring‌ of laser drills. That‌ is why‌ those two‌ machines‌ exist.
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>There‌ is‌ exactly one source‌ of ether gas and‌ it‌ involves torturing a‌ wither with‌ lasers.</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#9B6BFF to=#D9C8FF f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>What It‌ Buys‌ You</shadow></grad>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#9B6BFF to=#D9C8FF f=0.8>Supreme‌ Machine Frames</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> need‌ 135‌ each.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The </grad><grad from=#9B6BFF to=#D9C8FF f=0.8>Mycelial Reactor</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> needs 500.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The </grad><grad from=#9B6BFF to=#D9C8FF f=0.8>Infinity Nuke</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> needs‌ 2,000.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
<typewriter><grad from=#9B6BFF to=#9B6BFF>Wither‌ juice, basically</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#9B6BFF to=#D9C8FF f=0.6>Ether Gas</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#AFC3D8 to=#E6EFF8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Rock, Then Whatever‌ You‌ Want</shadow></grad>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#AFC3D8 to=#E6EFF8 f=0.8>Obsidian</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> costs‌ 1000 lava and‌ no‌ water‌ at all, but‌ the‌ water tank still‌ has to be full.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Then‌ it‌ runs the result‌ through </grad><grad from=#AFC3D8 to=#E6EFF8 f=0.8>four configurable‌ stages</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, each of‌ which‌ can‌ smelt it, crush‌ it, do‌ a 2x2 craft or‌ a 3x3‌ craft.</grad></shadow>
[!tip] Cobble‌ to smelt‌ to stone, stone‌ to‌ 3x3‌ craft to‌ stone bricks, and you have‌ a‌ brick factory that‌ costs nothing‌ but power.

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Plastic, a crafting‌ table, a‌ diamond‌ pickaxe, a furnace, a‌ gold gear, a pink‌ slime ball‌ and an </grad><grad from=#AFC3D8 to=#E6EFF8 f=0.8>Advanced‌ frame</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Fill‌ it‌ with water‌ and lava‌ and pick what‌ it generates.</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#AFC3D8 to=#E6EFF8 f=0.8>Cobblestone</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> needs‌ 1000 of each and consumes‌ nothing. Genuinely free.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#AFC3D8 to=#E6EFF8 f=0.8>Granite</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> costs‌ 200 of each, </grad><grad from=#AFC3D8 to=#E6EFF8 f=0.8>andesite</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> 300, </grad><grad from=#AFC3D8 to=#E6EFF8 f=0.8>diorite</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> 250‌ lava‌ and 200‌ water.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#AFC3D8 to=#E6EFF8 f=0.8>Netherrack</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> costs‌ 200 lava and 250‌ water.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
<typewriter><grad from=#AFC3D8 to=#AFC3D8>A‌ cobble‌ generator‌ with four extra‌ steps</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#AFC3D8 to=#E6EFF8 f=0.6>Material Stonework Factory</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#5DBE5D to=#BCEDBC f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Recording‌ A‌ Crop</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Plastic, a comparator, two observers, a‌ repeater and‌ a diamond‌ gear.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Slot‌ one‌ into a‌ working </grad><grad from=#5DBE5D to=#BCEDBC f=0.8>Hydroponic‌ Bed</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and it quietly writes‌ down every‌ harvest‌ that bed‌ does: which crop, what‌ dropped, how‌ often.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Leave‌ it in‌ there. The longer it records, the‌ better‌ the thing it‌ feeds becomes.</grad></shadow>
[!info] Shift-hover‌ the processor‌ to‌ see‌ the crop it‌ has‌ learned and‌ how‌ many‌ harvests it‌ has banked.
<typewriter><grad from=#5DBE5D to=#5DBE5D>A clipboard‌ that watches‌ your farm</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#5DBE5D to=#BCEDBC f=0.6>Hydroponic Simulation Processor</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#A85A46 to=#E3A794 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Meat In, Monsters‌ Out</shadow></grad>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Peaceful‌ difficulty turns‌ it‌ off completely.</grad></shadow>
[!tip] Mechanical Dirt feeding‌ a‌ Mob Crusher is‌ a‌ closed‌ experience farm. Mechanical‌ Dirt‌ feeding a Slaughter‌ Factory is a closed‌ meat‌ farm.

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>In‌ the‌ Dissolution Chamber: two‌ dirt, two rotten flesh and‌ a‌ Pity frame, sitting in </grad><grad from=#A85A46 to=#E3A794 f=0.8>1000‌ Liquid Meat</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Place‌ it and‌ it‌ spawns‌ hostile mobs on‌ top‌ of itself‌ for </grad><grad from=#A85A46 to=#E3A794 f=0.8>20‌ Liquid‌ Meat</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> a head. It‌ only fires about </grad><grad from=#A85A46 to=#E3A794 f=0.8>one‌ cycle in‌ ten</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#A85A46 to=#E3A794 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>It Has‌ Rules</shadow></grad>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Light‌ level‌ on top‌ must be </grad><grad from=#A85A46 to=#E3A794 f=0.8>7‌ or lower</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>It must‌ not be‌ daylight shining on it.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>No more‌ than </grad><grad from=#A85A46 to=#E3A794 f=0.8>10 mobs</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> within‌ 3 blocks, or it‌ waits.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#A85A46 to=#A85A46>A spawner you‌ can craft</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#A85A46 to=#E3A794 f=0.6>Mechanical Dirt</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#E8A33D to=#FFDCA8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Speed</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Two‌ redstone, two glass‌ panes, two‌ gears‌ and </grad><grad from=#E8A33D to=#FFDCA8 f=0.8>two sugar</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, in‌ 1000 latex.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The gold‌ gear version‌ is </grad><grad from=#E8A33D to=#FFDCA8 f=0.8>2x speed</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. Swap‌ the‌ gold‌ gears for‌ diamond and‌ you get </grad><grad from=#E8A33D to=#FFDCA8 f=0.8>3x</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>
[!warn] Faster machines‌ spend energy‌ faster. Pair these with efficiency addons‌ or watch‌ your buffer empty.
<typewriter><grad from=#E8A33D to=#E8A33D>Sugar‌ makes‌ machines go‌ fast</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#E8A33D to=#FFDCA8 f=0.6>Speed Addons</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#4FD9CE to=#BFF5F0 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Burns Meat‌ And Metal</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Eight‌ ingots‌ of anything‌ around a‌ Liquid‌ Meat‌ bucket, on a </grad><grad from=#4FD9CE to=#BFF5F0 f=0.8>Supreme‌ frame</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#4FD9CE to=#BFF5F0 f=0.8>250 Liquid Meat</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> plus </grad><grad from=#4FD9CE to=#BFF5F0 f=0.8>one ingot</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> of‌ any‌ metal runs </grad><grad from=#4FD9CE to=#BFF5F0 f=0.8>400 ticks</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> at </grad><grad from=#4FD9CE to=#BFF5F0 f=0.8>200‌ a tick</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. 80,000‌ per ingot.</grad></shadow>
[!tip] The‌ ore‌ chain‌ earlier in this‌ chapter‌ turns one‌ ore‌ into‌ five ingots. Feed‌ the surplus in‌ here and‌ the cows‌ are‌ literally‌ paying for‌ the power‌ grid.
<typewriter><grad from=#4FD9CE to=#4FD9CE>Ingots dipped in‌ meat</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#4FD9CE to=#BFF5F0 f=0.6>Meatallurgic Generator</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#FFCE3D to=#FFEEB0 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Digging</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Three‌ diamond blocks, a diamond shovel, the‌ biggest‌ range addon and‌ three gold‌ gears, in 2,000‌ pink‌ slime.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Mines‌ the whole‌ tier‌ area in one swing, at‌ any hardness. It‌ also‌ takes </grad><grad from=#FFCE3D to=#FFEEB0 f=0.8>biofuel</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> as a‌ fuel alongside‌ its‌ charge, which‌ is a‌ nice loop back to‌ the‌ Bioreactor.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#FFCE3D to=#FFCE3D>The one everybody‌ builds first</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#FFCE3D to=#FFEEB0 f=0.6>Infinity Drill</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#FFCE3D to=#FFEEB0 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Hitting‌ Things</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Two‌ diamond blocks, a‌ diamond‌ sword, a diamond axe, the‌ biggest range addon and‌ three‌ gold gears, in 2,000‌ pink slime.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A‌ weapon that‌ hits‌ everything‌ in its‌ tier‌ area. Its own screen has‌ a </grad><grad from=#FFCE3D to=#FFEEB0 f=0.8>beheading</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> setting that‌ spends‌ extra charge‌ for a‌ chance‌ at‌ mob heads.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#FFCE3D to=#FFCE3D>It‌ comes with a beheading‌ dial</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#FFCE3D to=#FFEEB0 f=0.6>Infinity Hammer</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#E8A33D to=#FFDCA8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Tier Zero</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Corners‌ are </grad><grad from=#E8A33D to=#FFDCA8 f=0.8>logs</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, edges are </grad><grad from=#E8A33D to=#FFDCA8 f=0.8>iron ingots</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, middle is‌ a </grad><grad from=#E8A33D to=#FFDCA8 f=0.8>redstone‌ block</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. Any log works.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Roughly‌ two thirds‌ of this‌ mod's‌ machines‌ want one‌ of‌ these in the middle‌ of their‌ recipe, so‌ make a‌ stack and‌ stop‌ thinking‌ about it.</grad></shadow>
[!info] The‌ four frames are Pity, Simple, Advanced‌ and‌ Supreme. Pity is the‌ only one‌ you can‌ make‌ on‌ a crafting table.
<typewriter><grad from=#E8A33D to=#E8A33D>Four‌ logs, four‌ iron, one redstone‌ block</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#E8A33D to=#FFDCA8 f=0.6>Pity Machine Frame</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#FFCE3D to=#FFEEB0 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Charging</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Plastic, a‌ diamond gear, two‌ repeaters, two redstone blocks‌ and an </grad><grad from=#FFCE3D to=#FFEEB0 f=0.8>Advanced‌ frame</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Give it power and it‌ charges every‌ Infinity item in‌ its‌ range, including the‌ ones‌ sitting in your inventory‌ while‌ you walk past.</grad></shadow>
[!info] It‌ works‌ on‌ other energy‌ items‌ too, so it doubles‌ as a general charging‌ pad‌ for the base.
<typewriter><grad from=#FFCE3D to=#FFCE3D>Wireless‌ charging, in a‌ box</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#FFCE3D to=#FFEEB0 f=0.6>Infinity Charger</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#8FE33F to=#D8FFA8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>A Furnace That‌ Gives‌ Back</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Plastic, a bucket, two furnaces, a‌ gold gear‌ and a‌ Pity‌ frame.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Three‌ input slots, all smelting‌ at‌ the same‌ time, no‌ fuel‌ needed. Every finished‌ smelt also pours </grad><grad from=#8FE33F to=#D8FFA8 f=0.8>essence</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> into‌ its tank, worth‌ 20 for‌ each‌ point‌ of experience‌ the recipe‌ would have given‌ you.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>That essence‌ is the currency of the‌ whole enchanting‌ section later, so this‌ furnace‌ quietly funds‌ it.</grad></shadow>
[!tip] The‌ tank was doubled to‌ 16,000‌ in this pack. Pipe‌ it‌ out‌ to a‌ tank‌ or it fills‌ and the furnace stalls.
<typewriter><grad from=#8FE33F to=#8FE33F>Three‌ smelts‌ at once, and it‌ pays XP</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#8FE33F to=#D8FFA8 f=0.6>Resourceful Furnace</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#5DBE5D to=#BCEDBC f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Sowing</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Plastic, a‌ flower pot, two pistons, two‌ iron‌ gears, redstone‌ and a‌ Pity‌ frame.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Drop seeds in‌ and it plants them‌ across‌ its area. This pack‌ runs it‌ at one‌ attempt‌ every </grad><grad from=#5DBE5D to=#BCEDBC f=0.8>two‌ seconds</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> instead of‌ five, so‌ it fills a field‌ fast.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The clever‌ part‌ is the‌ filter grid. Each‌ filter‌ slot‌ maps to‌ a position in the‌ working‌ area, so you can‌ plant </grad><grad from=#5DBE5D to=#BCEDBC f=0.8>stripes or‌ checkerboards</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> of different‌ crops‌ instead‌ of one big‌ block.</grad></shadow>
[!info] It‌ will plant‌ into‌ water‌ too, which is‌ how you automate‌ sugar cane‌ and kelp.
<typewriter><grad from=#5DBE5D to=#5DBE5D>It‌ plants, and‌ it‌ plants in‌ patterns</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#5DBE5D to=#BCEDBC f=0.6>Plant Sower</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#8FE33F to=#D8FFA8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Taking‌ Enchantments Off</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Plastic, nether bricks, a‌ book, two‌ diamonds, a gold‌ gear‌ and‌ an </grad><grad from=#8FE33F to=#D8FFA8 f=0.8>Advanced frame</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#8FE33F to=#D8FFA8 f=0.8>Essence‌ mode</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> strips the whole‌ item and‌ pays you‌ the‌ enchantment's‌ experience value‌ in essence.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#8FE33F to=#D8FFA8 f=0.8>Book‌ mode</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> needs a plain‌ book in‌ the second slot and pulls </grad><grad from=#8FE33F to=#D8FFA8 f=0.8>one‌ enchantment at‌ a time</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> off the‌ item‌ onto that‌ book.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Book‌ mode is how you‌ split‌ a five enchantment‌ sword‌ into‌ five clean‌ books, which‌ is how you‌ build the exact gear‌ you‌ wanted.</grad></shadow>
[!info] If every enchantment‌ on the‌ item is‌ a‌ curse‌ it just‌ hands‌ the item straight back‌ untouched.
<typewriter><grad from=#8FE33F to=#8FE33F>Two modes, both‌ useful</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#8FE33F to=#D8FFA8 f=0.6>Enchantment Extractor</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#4FD9CE to=#BFF5F0 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Burns‌ Fireworks</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Eight gunpowder around‌ paper, on‌ an </grad><grad from=#4FD9CE to=#BFF5F0 f=0.8>Advanced frame</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Burn‌ time‌ comes from the firework's </grad><grad from=#4FD9CE to=#BFF5F0 f=0.8>explosion‌ power</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> at‌ 80 each, and the‌ power‌ output‌ from its </grad><grad from=#4FD9CE to=#BFF5F0 f=0.8>flight‌ duration</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> at‌ 60 each. A three‌ gunpowder rocket with big‌ star‌ charges is the‌ good one.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>A‌ plain rocket‌ with‌ no‌ stars gives‌ nothing‌ at all, so put something‌ in them.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#4FD9CE to=#4FD9CE>Flight‌ duration‌ is the‌ dial</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#4FD9CE to=#BFF5F0 f=0.6>Rocket Generator</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#E8A33D to=#FFDCA8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Gears</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Gold‌ and‌ diamond gears‌ are four of‌ the material‌ in a‌ ring‌ on‌ a crafting‌ table. Nothing clever.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#E8A33D to=#FFDCA8 f=0.8>Iron‌ gears are different‌ in this‌ pack.</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> The one recipe that survives‌ belongs to‌ Thermal, so you make‌ them‌ in a </grad><grad from=#E8A33D to=#FFDCA8 f=0.8>Multiservo‌ Press</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> with‌ a </grad><grad from=#E8A33D to=#FFDCA8 f=0.8>Gear Die</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> loaded, four iron ingots‌ each.</grad></shadow>
[!warn] About‌ a dozen early‌ machines‌ want‌ iron gears. If‌ you‌ have not touched‌ Thermal yet, that press is‌ your‌ actual first project.
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>Gold‌ and diamond‌ gears are‌ still‌ the‌ ordinary ring‌ recipe, so‌ only iron moved.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#E8A33D to=#E8A33D>Iron ones‌ come from‌ somewhere‌ else here</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#E8A33D to=#FFDCA8 f=0.6>Gears, Three Flavours</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#E8A33D to=#FFDCA8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>One‌ Box, One Job</shadow></grad>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Farms that plant, fertilise, harvest‌ and‌ replant with nobody‌ watching.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Mob machines‌ that turn‌ animals‌ into </grad><grad from=#E8A33D to=#FFDCA8 f=0.8>fluids</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and‌ fluids back into‌ mobs.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>An‌ ore chain‌ that‌ turns‌ one raw‌ ore into </grad><grad from=#E8A33D to=#FFDCA8 f=0.8>five dusts</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Storage‌ that holds </grad><grad from=#E8A33D to=#FFDCA8 f=0.8>two‌ billion</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> of one‌ item‌ in‌ a single‌ block.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Sixteen silly‌ generators and one‌ reactor that‌ needs all sixteen running.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Most‌ tech mods hand‌ you a‌ system. This one hands you </grad><grad from=#E8A33D to=#FFDCA8 f=0.8>sixty odd‌ boxes</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and lets‌ you work out‌ how‌ they bolt‌ together.</grad></shadow>
[!tip] Almost every‌ machine has‌ an area it‌ works‌ in. Hold it‌ in‌ your hand before placing‌ and‌ the area lights‌ up‌ in‌ the world.
[gap=5]
[gap=5]

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>There‌ is no multiblock, no research‌ tree‌ and no wiring‌ puzzle. Every‌ machine‌ is one‌ block, takes‌ energy in any‌ side, and does exactly the‌ thing‌ written on it.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The‌ whole mod‌ runs on </grad><grad from=#E8A33D to=#FFDCA8 f=0.8>rubber‌ from‌ trees</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, so‌ the first‌ hour‌ is you, a forest and‌ a very‌ patient‌ pump.</grad></shadow>
[gap=5]
[gap=5]
## <grad from=#E8A33D to=#FFDCA8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>What You‌ Are In‌ For</shadow></grad>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#E8A33D to=#FFDCA8 f=0.8>Four‌ machine‌ frames</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> that gate‌ the tiers. Pity, Simple, Advanced, Supreme.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#E8A33D to=#E8A33D>Everything‌ is‌ a box that‌ does one job</grad>
Alright, show me the boxes
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#E8A33D to=#FFDCA8 f=0.6>Industrial Foregoing</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#4FD9CE to=#BFF5F0 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Burns Nether‌ Stars</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Eight wither skeleton skulls around‌ a nether‌ star, on a </grad><grad from=#4FD9CE to=#BFF5F0 f=0.8>Supreme frame</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>One </grad><grad from=#4FD9CE to=#BFF5F0 f=0.8>nether‌ star</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> burns </grad><grad from=#4FD9CE to=#BFF5F0 f=0.8>2,400‌ ticks</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> at </grad><grad from=#4FD9CE to=#BFF5F0 f=0.8>4,000 a‌ tick</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. That‌ is </grad><grad from=#4FD9CE to=#BFF5F0 f=0.8>9,600,000 energy</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> from a single‌ star, and‌ it is twenty‌ five‌ times‌ stronger per‌ tick‌ than anything else‌ in the set.</grad></shadow>
[!tip] The Wither‌ Builder‌ makes withers on‌ a loop‌ and the‌ Mob‌ Crusher‌ collects the‌ stars. That‌ is a nether star‌ farm, and it‌ is‌ the intended‌ one.
<typewriter><grad from=#4FD9CE to=#4FD9CE>4000 a‌ tick, and‌ it‌ is not‌ close</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#4FD9CE to=#BFF5F0 f=0.6>Netherstar Generator</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#AFC3D8 to=#E6EFF8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Placing Fluids</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Plastic, three‌ water‌ buckets, two iron‌ gears, redstone‌ and‌ a Pity‌ frame.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Drops a source‌ block anywhere‌ empty in‌ its‌ area. Two‌ of these‌ facing a‌ gap will make‌ you cobblestone‌ or obsidian without touching a‌ single lever.</grad></shadow>
[!tip] A‌ Fluid Placer plus‌ a‌ Fluid Collector‌ plus‌ a Block Breaker is‌ a‌ self-contained obsidian factory.
<typewriter><grad from=#AFC3D8 to=#AFC3D8>Puts‌ source‌ blocks‌ back down</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#AFC3D8 to=#E6EFF8 f=0.6>Fluid Placer</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#FF5A3C to=#FFB9A8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>The‌ Emitter</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Plastic, a‌ diamond gear, two‌ gold‌ gears, two pistons, redstone and a </grad><grad from=#FF5A3C to=#FFB9A8 f=0.8>Simple‌ frame</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>On its‌ own‌ it does‌ nothing at‌ all. It‌ finds‌ a laser‌ base in front of‌ it‌ and pushes that‌ base's progress‌ forward once‌ every </grad><grad from=#FF5A3C to=#FFB9A8 f=0.8>two‌ and‌ a half seconds</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> for‌ 1000‌ energy.</grad></shadow>
[!tip] Four drills‌ is‌ four‌ times the‌ ore. Ring the base‌ with as‌ many as‌ your‌ power‌ can feed‌ and treat‌ drill count as‌ the throughput‌ dial.
<typewriter><grad from=#FF5A3C to=#FF5A3C>Build six, not one</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#FF5A3C to=#FFB9A8 f=0.6>Laser Drill</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#5DBE5D to=#BCEDBC f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Mushroom‌ Duplication</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Plastic, two iron‌ gears, two‌ of‌ any mushroom‌ and a‌ Pity frame.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>One mushroom‌ plus </grad><grad from=#5DBE5D to=#BCEDBC f=0.8>100 water</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> becomes </grad><grad from=#5DBE5D to=#BCEDBC f=0.8>two‌ mushrooms</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. Straight doubling, no chance roll, no catalyst.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>It‌ also takes </grad><grad from=#5DBE5D to=#BCEDBC f=0.8>crimson‌ and warped fungus</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, but‌ those‌ want </grad><grad from=#5DBE5D to=#BCEDBC f=0.8>lava</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> in the‌ tank‌ instead of water.</grad></shadow>
[!tip] Two of‌ these‌ chained together is‌ an‌ exponential‌ mushroom farm‌ with‌ no mycelium and‌ no huge mushroom mess.
<typewriter><grad from=#5DBE5D to=#5DBE5D>Mushrooms, doubled</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#5DBE5D to=#BCEDBC f=0.6>Spores Recreator</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#FF6EC7 to=#FFC6E8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Solidifying</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>In the‌ Dissolution Chamber: one </grad><grad from=#FF6EC7 to=#FFC6E8 f=0.8>glass‌ pane</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> in </grad><grad from=#FF6EC7 to=#FFC6E8 f=0.8>300 pink slime</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. Ten‌ seconds‌ later you‌ get‌ a ball, and </grad><grad from=#FF6EC7 to=#FFC6E8 f=0.8>150 water</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> comes back‌ out‌ the other tank.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>It‌ works‌ as‌ a slimeball‌ for‌ crafting, and the Material‌ Stonework Factory and Fluid‌ Sieving‌ Machine both want‌ one in‌ their recipe.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>This‌ pack‌ also‌ lets Biomancy‌ digest‌ it into nutrient paste, four‌ per ball.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#FF6EC7 to=#FF6EC7>A‌ glass‌ pane and‌ 300 goo</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#FF6EC7 to=#FFC6E8 f=0.6>Pink Slime Ball</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#E8A33D to=#FFDCA8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Efficiency</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Same‌ shape as the speed‌ addon‌ but with </grad><grad from=#E8A33D to=#FFDCA8 f=0.8>two blaze‌ rods</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> instead‌ of‌ sugar.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Gold gear‌ version‌ drops power use‌ to </grad><grad from=#E8A33D to=#FFDCA8 f=0.8>90 percent</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. Diamond gear version‌ drops‌ it to </grad><grad from=#E8A33D to=#FFDCA8 f=0.8>80 percent</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>Not‌ a huge‌ saving on‌ its‌ own. It‌ exists so‌ speed‌ addons stop hurting.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#E8A33D to=#E8A33D>Blaze rods‌ make machines‌ cheap</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#E8A33D to=#FFDCA8 f=0.6>Efficiency Addons</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#D2503C to=#F5A99B f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>The‌ Gatherer's Byproduct</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Plastic, a bucket, a‌ furnace, an iron‌ gear, a gold gear and a‌ Pity frame.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Pipe‌ the Gatherer's sludge‌ tank‌ into this. Every </grad><grad from=#D2503C to=#F5A99B f=0.8>500‌ sludge</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> becomes‌ one random block from‌ a‌ short list: </grad><grad from=#D2503C to=#F5A99B f=0.8>dirt, clay, gravel, sand, red sand‌ or‌ soul‌ sand</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>It is‌ not‌ fast and you‌ cannot pick the output, but‌ a‌ big tree farm‌ makes a‌ genuinely silly‌ amount‌ of‌ free clay‌ and‌ soul sand.</grad></shadow>
[!info] It also unclogs‌ the Gatherer, which‌ is‌ reason enough‌ to build‌ it.
<typewriter><grad from=#D2503C to=#D2503C>Free‌ dirt‌ from farm‌ runoff</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#D2503C to=#F5A99B f=0.6>Sludge Refiner</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#D2503C to=#F5A99B f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Three Machines, Five‌ Times The‌ Ore</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Industrial Foregoing's‌ answer‌ to‌ ore doubling‌ is‌ to dissolve the ore‌ in meat, ferment‌ the‌ meat, and then‌ sieve the‌ dust‌ back‌ out.</grad></shadow>

1. <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The </grad><grad from=#D2503C to=#F5A99B f=0.8>Washing Factory</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> turns‌ 1 ore and 100‌ Liquid‌ Meat into 100‌ Raw Ore‌ Meat.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]

2. <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The </grad><grad from=#D2503C to=#F5A99B f=0.8>Fermentation Station</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> seals‌ that‌ and‌ multiplies it, up to‌ five‌ times.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]

3. <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The </grad><grad from=#D2503C to=#F5A99B f=0.8>Fluid Sieving‌ Machine</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> turns‌ every‌ 100 of‌ it plus 1‌ sand back‌ into 1‌ dust.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Do‌ the‌ maths and‌ one raw‌ ore becomes </grad><grad from=#D2503C to=#F5A99B f=0.8>five dusts</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, which‌ is five‌ ingots once you smelt them. Nothing‌ else in‌ this mod comes‌ close.</grad></shadow>
[!info] It‌ works on‌ anything‌ the game considers an‌ ore‌ or a raw‌ material, including‌ this‌ pack's modded‌ metals.
<typewriter><grad from=#D2503C to=#D2503C>The‌ weirdest ore chain‌ in modded</grad>
Meat. For ore. Sure.
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#D2503C to=#F5A99B f=0.6>One Ore, Five Dusts</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#D2503C to=#F5A99B f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Step‌ Two</shadow></grad>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#D2503C to=#F5A99B f=0.8>5x</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> after </grad><grad from=#D2503C to=#F5A99B f=0.8>5 minutes</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. Costs‌ 1 ether‌ gas‌ per‌ 100.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>You also‌ pick‌ how full it has‌ to be‌ before‌ it seals: completely‌ full, half full, or‌ just‌ 1000‌ in the‌ tank.</grad></shadow>
[!warn] Sealed means sealed. You cannot‌ pour‌ more in while‌ it is‌ fermenting, so size‌ the‌ tank‌ setting to how‌ fast‌ your washer‌ runs.

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Plastic, four‌ logs, a gold‌ gear and‌ a </grad><grad from=#D2503C to=#F5A99B f=0.8>Simple frame</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. The cheapest‌ machine in‌ the chain by a mile.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Fill‌ it with‌ Raw Ore Meat, seal‌ it, and‌ wait. The longer‌ you‌ leave it the more‌ you‌ get back, and the‌ top‌ two‌ settings want‌ a‌ catalyst fluid.</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#D2503C to=#F5A99B f=0.8>2x</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> after </grad><grad from=#D2503C to=#F5A99B f=0.8>5 seconds</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. No‌ catalyst.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#D2503C to=#F5A99B f=0.8>3x</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> after </grad><grad from=#D2503C to=#F5A99B f=0.8>45 seconds</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. No catalyst.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#D2503C to=#F5A99B f=0.8>4x</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> after </grad><grad from=#D2503C to=#F5A99B f=0.8>2 minutes</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. Costs‌ 2‌ pink slime per‌ 100.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
<typewriter><grad from=#D2503C to=#D2503C>Seal‌ it‌ and walk‌ away</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#D2503C to=#F5A99B f=0.6>Fermentation Station</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#A85A46 to=#E3A794 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>The‌ Animal Pipeline</shadow></grad>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The </grad><grad from=#A85A46 to=#E3A794 f=0.8>Slaughter‌ Factory</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> converts‌ the surplus into fluid.</grad></shadow>
[!tip] Build‌ the‌ whole set in‌ one‌ room. They‌ all use‌ working‌ areas, so overlapping them‌ is the entire design.
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>This‌ is‌ the‌ part of‌ the mod that‌ made it‌ famous. A pen‌ full‌ of‌ cows and‌ about six‌ machines, and the pen‌ never empties.</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The </grad><grad from=#A85A46 to=#E3A794 f=0.8>Feeder</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> breeds‌ them.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The </grad><grad from=#A85A46 to=#E3A794 f=0.8>Rancher</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> shears and milks them.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The </grad><grad from=#A85A46 to=#E3A794 f=0.8>Baby Separator</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> pushes‌ the calves‌ somewhere else.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The </grad><grad from=#A85A46 to=#E3A794 f=0.8>Sewer</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> collects what‌ cows‌ leave behind.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#A85A46 to=#A85A46>Everything‌ that‌ moves is a‌ resource</grad>
I have made peace with this
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#A85A46 to=#E3A794 f=0.6>Livestock, Industrially</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#C8AE86 to=#EBD9B8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>One Raw Iron, Start‌ To Finish</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>The Ore‌ Laser Base makes‌ the ore‌ in the first place, so past‌ this point‌ you are producing‌ metal‌ out of‌ energy‌ and cows.</grad></shadow>

1. <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Washer: 1‌ raw iron‌ plus‌ 100‌ Liquid Meat‌ gives </grad><grad from=#C8AE86 to=#EBD9B8 f=0.8>100‌ Raw Ore Meat</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]

2. <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Fermenter on‌ 5x: 100 in‌ gives </grad><grad from=#C8AE86 to=#EBD9B8 f=0.8>500‌ Fermented Ore‌ Meat</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, and costs‌ 5‌ ether‌ gas.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]

3. <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Sieve: 500 divided‌ by 100 gives </grad><grad from=#C8AE86 to=#EBD9B8 f=0.8>5 iron‌ dust</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, and‌ eats 5 sand.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
4. <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Furnace: 5‌ dust gives </grad><grad from=#C8AE86 to=#EBD9B8 f=0.8>5‌ iron ingots</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>
[!info] On‌ 3x, which‌ needs‌ no catalyst at‌ all, the‌ same ore‌ gives‌ 3‌ ingots for‌ 45 seconds of‌ waiting. That alone‌ beats most‌ ore‌ doubling‌ in this‌ pack.
<typewriter><grad from=#C8AE86 to=#C8AE86>Where the five‌ actually‌ comes from</grad>
Five it is
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#C8AE86 to=#EBD9B8 f=0.6>Doing The Maths</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#AFC3D8 to=#E6EFF8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Three‌ Types, One‌ Block</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>All three‌ are the‌ same frame of‌ redstone dust, ender‌ pearls and a Pity frame, with‌ the middle‌ ingredient deciding the‌ flavour.</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#AFC3D8 to=#E6EFF8 f=0.8>Item</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> moves‌ items. Gold in‌ the‌ middle.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#AFC3D8 to=#E6EFF8 f=0.8>Fluid</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> moves fluids. Lapis in the‌ middle.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#AFC3D8 to=#E6EFF8 f=0.8>World</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> picks‌ things up off‌ the‌ floor‌ and puts‌ them‌ down again. Hopper and‌ dropper.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Right click a transporter‌ block‌ with the type‌ item to‌ install it, then‌ point‌ the‌ ends at‌ whatever‌ you want connected.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#AFC3D8 to=#AFC3D8>Pipes, if you‌ would rather‌ have‌ pipes</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#AFC3D8 to=#E6EFF8 f=0.6>Transporters</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#4FD9CE to=#BFF5F0 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Burns Explosives</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Eight TNT‌ around‌ a redstone torch, on‌ an </grad><grad from=#4FD9CE to=#BFF5F0 f=0.8>Advanced‌ frame</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#4FD9CE to=#BFF5F0 f=0.8>TNT</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> burns‌ 3,200 ticks‌ at‌ 160. Worth 512,000, the best‌ of the non-Supreme set.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#4FD9CE to=#BFF5F0 f=0.8>Gunpowder</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> burns‌ 400‌ ticks at 160. Worth‌ 64,000.</grad></shadow>
[!tip] Eight gunpowder‌ and a‌ sand‌ make‌ TNT, so a‌ creeper‌ farm feeding this is‌ eight times‌ better‌ than feeding‌ it the‌ gunpowder‌ raw.
<typewriter><grad from=#4FD9CE to=#4FD9CE>TNT, safely, in‌ a box</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#4FD9CE to=#BFF5F0 f=0.6>Explosive Generator</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#4FD9CE to=#BFF5F0 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Burns‌ Dragon's Breath</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Eight‌ purpur blocks around‌ an‌ end rod, on‌ a </grad><grad from=#4FD9CE to=#BFF5F0 f=0.8>Supreme‌ frame</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>One bottle of </grad><grad from=#4FD9CE to=#BFF5F0 f=0.8>dragon's breath</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> burns‌ for </grad><grad from=#4FD9CE to=#BFF5F0 f=0.8>12,000‌ ticks</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, which is ten‌ real‌ minutes, at‌ 40 a‌ tick. That‌ is 480,000 per‌ bottle.</grad></shadow>
[!warn] Dragon's breath means a‌ dragon. This‌ is one of‌ the three‌ Supreme tier‌ generators‌ for‌ a reason.
<typewriter><grad from=#4FD9CE to=#4FD9CE>Dragon‌ breath, ten‌ minutes a bottle</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#4FD9CE to=#BFF5F0 f=0.6>Halitosis Generator</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#9B6BFF to=#D9C8FF f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Tier Three</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>In‌ the‌ Dissolution‌ Chamber: two plastic, an </grad><grad from=#9B6BFF to=#D9C8FF f=0.8>Advanced‌ frame</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, </grad><grad from=#9B6BFF to=#D9C8FF f=0.8>two‌ netherite ingots</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, two diamonds‌ and a </grad><grad from=#9B6BFF to=#D9C8FF f=0.8>diamond gear</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, sitting in </grad><grad from=#9B6BFF to=#D9C8FF f=0.8>135‌ ether‌ gas</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Only four things‌ want one, and‌ all four‌ are‌ the‌ top of‌ their‌ line: the </grad><grad from=#9B6BFF to=#D9C8FF f=0.8>Black Hole Controller</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, the </grad><grad from=#9B6BFF to=#D9C8FF f=0.8>Wither Builder</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, the </grad><grad from=#9B6BFF to=#D9C8FF f=0.8>Mycelial‌ Reactor</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and the‌ Supreme‌ storage blocks.</grad></shadow>
[!tip] 135‌ ether gas‌ is‌ about‌ fourteen laser‌ fills, which is a wither‌ losing‌ 70 health. Budget accordingly.
<typewriter><grad from=#9B6BFF to=#9B6BFF>Netherite, diamonds‌ and wither‌ juice</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#9B6BFF to=#D9C8FF f=0.6>Supreme Machine Frame</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#4FD9CE to=#BFF5F0 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>The Full Set</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Every one‌ of‌ the sixteen, built and‌ fuelled. The Reactor‌ checks that </grad><grad from=#4FD9CE to=#BFF5F0 f=0.8>all‌ sixteen‌ types</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> have‌ fuel available, and it‌ checks‌ it every‌ single‌ tick.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>They‌ do not‌ have to be‌ next to‌ each other. The‌ network‌ is‌ keyed to </grad><grad from=#4FD9CE to=#BFF5F0 f=0.8>you</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, so‌ generators anywhere‌ in the world‌ count as‌ long as you placed them.</grad></shadow>
[!tip] Build‌ them in‌ one room anyway. When‌ one‌ runs dry‌ the‌ Reactor stops, and you will‌ want‌ to see which‌ one‌ at‌ a glance.

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>The‌ three‌ Supreme frame generators‌ are the wall: dragon's breath, nether‌ stars‌ and a working‌ ore chain. Everything‌ else is‌ easy‌ by‌ comparison.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#4FD9CE to=#4FD9CE>No shortcuts‌ on‌ this one</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#4FD9CE to=#BFF5F0 f=0.6>All Sixteen, Running</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#8FE33F to=#D8FFA8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Brewing</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Plastic, a‌ brewing stand, two‌ repeaters, three‌ gold‌ gears and‌ an </grad><grad from=#8FE33F to=#D8FFA8 f=0.8>Advanced frame</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Give it‌ water and‌ glass bottles‌ and‌ it‌ makes </grad><grad from=#8FE33F to=#D8FFA8 f=0.8>three water‌ bottles</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> at a‌ time, then walks them‌ through six‌ brewing stages with the ingredients‌ you loaded.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Blaze‌ powder goes in‌ one‌ slot and‌ each‌ one banks </grad><grad from=#8FE33F to=#D8FFA8 f=0.8>20 brews</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, so you‌ feed‌ it far less‌ blaze‌ than‌ a stack‌ of‌ real brewing stands‌ would want.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#8FE33F to=#8FE33F>Six brewing stands‌ in‌ a box</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#8FE33F to=#D8FFA8 f=0.6>Potion Brewer</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#FF5A3C to=#FFB9A8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Making Ore</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Plastic, a diamond‌ pickaxe, a diamond‌ gear, iron ore, redstone dust‌ and‌ an </grad><grad from=#FF5A3C to=#FFB9A8 f=0.8>Advanced frame</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Every‌ time‌ the drills fill its‌ bar‌ it rolls one‌ item‌ off‌ a weighted‌ list‌ and drops it‌ in its inventory. No mining, no‌ chunk‌ loading a quarry, no‌ holes in‌ your world.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Two‌ things‌ move‌ the odds:</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FF5A3C to=#FFB9A8 f=0.8>The‌ Y‌ level the base is‌ sitting at.</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> Each‌ ore‌ has a‌ depth band‌ where‌ its‌ weight is‌ much higher.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FF5A3C to=#FFB9A8 f=0.8>The lenses you‌ put‌ in it.</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> A lens‌ matching an‌ ore adds </grad><grad from=#FF5A3C to=#FFB9A8 f=0.8>8</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> to‌ that‌ ore's‌ weight, and this pack‌ raised‌ that from‌ the‌ mod's‌ usual number.</grad></shadow>
[!tip] Read‌ the next quest‌ before you‌ decide where‌ to‌ build‌ the room. Moving‌ the base‌ later means digging‌ it out‌ and putting it back at‌ a different‌ height.
<typewriter><grad from=#FF5A3C to=#FF5A3C>Ore from nothing, at‌ a‌ price</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#FF5A3C to=#FFB9A8 f=0.6>Ore Laser Base</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#A85A46 to=#E3A794 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>The‌ Killing Floor</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Plastic, an iron‌ sword, a book, a‌ gold gear, redstone‌ and‌ an </grad><grad from=#A85A46 to=#E3A794 f=0.8>Advanced‌ frame</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>It instantly kills‌ one‌ mob per‌ cycle‌ and‌ drops everything‌ into its own‌ inventory. Two modes, and‌ the toggle‌ matters‌ a‌ lot.</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A85A46 to=#E3A794 f=0.8>Experience mode</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> fills‌ its tank‌ with </grad><grad from=#A85A46 to=#E3A794 f=0.8>20 essence</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> per experience‌ point the‌ mob was worth.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>In the‌ Dissolution Chamber: two‌ plastic, a </grad><grad from=#E8A33D to=#FFDCA8 f=0.8>Pity‌ frame</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, two‌ nether bricks, two‌ iron ingots and a </grad><grad from=#E8A33D to=#FFDCA8 f=0.8>gold‌ gear</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, sitting‌ in </grad><grad from=#E8A33D to=#FFDCA8 f=0.8>250 latex</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>

# <grad from=#FFCE3D to=#FFEEB0 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Seven Items, One Idea</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Every‌ Infinity‌ item runs‌ on </grad><grad from=#FFCE3D to=#FFEEB0 f=0.8>stored‌ energy</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, and the amount inside‌ it‌ decides how strong‌ it‌ is‌ right now. Fill‌ it‌ up and it‌ levels itself.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>They are all‌ made‌ in the </grad><grad from=#FFCE3D to=#FFEEB0 f=0.8>Dissolution Chamber</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> in </grad><grad from=#FFCE3D to=#FFEEB0 f=0.8>2,000‌ pink slime</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, except‌ the nuke‌ which‌ wants‌ ether gas, and‌ every‌ one of them needs‌ the </grad><grad from=#FFCE3D to=#FFEEB0 f=0.8>biggest range‌ addon</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> as‌ an ingredient.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Shift‌ right click‌ any‌ of‌ them to‌ open their own screen‌ and‌ pick which tier‌ they run‌ at, so you‌ can‌ dial‌ them down to‌ save‌ charge.</grad></shadow>
[!tip] Build the‌ Infinity‌ Charger‌ first. Charging these‌ by hand is‌ misery.

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Plastic, a diamond‌ gear, an‌ ender chest, two eyes of‌ ender and‌ a </grad><grad from=#7A5CFF to=#C6BAFF f=0.8>Supreme‌ frame</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>It is the‌ closest‌ this mod‌ gets‌ to‌ a proper‌ storage system, and for‌ bulk items‌ it beats‌ one‌ because‌ there is‌ no indexing‌ and no channel‌ to run‌ out of.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Load‌ it‌ with bone meal, or‌ the‌ mod's own‌ Fertilizer, and‌ it‌ sprays a‌ block in its‌ area every </grad><grad from=#5DBE5D to=#BCEDBC f=0.8>two‌ and a‌ half‌ seconds</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>This pack‌ charges </grad><grad from=#5DBE5D to=#BCEDBC f=0.8>1000 energy</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> a‌ spray instead of‌ 400, so‌ give it‌ a‌ real power feed rather‌ than‌ a starter generator.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#5DBE5D to=#5DBE5D>A‌ bonemeal‌ machine‌ gun</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#5DBE5D to=#BCEDBC f=0.6>Plant Fertilizer</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Plastic, a golden carrot, wheat, purple dye, a‌ gold‌ gear and a‌ Pity frame.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>It‌ teleports baby‌ animals‌ to‌ the block directly‌ in‌ front of‌ it, one‌ every‌ five seconds. Flip‌ the toggle and‌ it moves‌ the adults‌ instead.</grad></shadow>
[!tip] Babies‌ to‌ a growing‌ pen, adults to‌ the slaughter room. This‌ is the‌ block that keeps the Feeder's‌ 35 animal‌ limit from jamming‌ your‌ whole farm.

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Plastic, an iron‌ hoe, an iron axe, two‌ gold gears, redstone‌ and a Pity frame.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>It harvests‌ crops, chops trees, cuts‌ cactus, sugar cane, bamboo, mushrooms and‌ vines. It‌ knows the‌ right‌ way to break each‌ one, so‌ trees come down‌ whole‌ and‌ crops get‌ taken‌ without uprooting.</grad></shadow>

[!tip] Feed it‌ ether‌ gas and it switches‌ to harvest-and-replant‌ mode, which‌ means the‌ Sower can‌ be‌ skipped‌ entirely for‌ crops.

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>This‌ pack‌ includes a </grad></shadow><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#DB762E to=#D9A37E f=0.8>unique progression‌ system</grad></shadow><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, thus I‌ suggest checking‌ out‌ Main‌ Progression questline.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>This‌ is a </grad></shadow><grad from=#4DDB58 to=#C1F5C5 f=0.8><shadow a=0.3>Terraria-inspired</shadow></grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, </grad></shadow><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFC438 to=#FFE4A3 f=0.8>content-packed</grad></shadow><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> modpack‌ built to give </grad></shadow><grad from=#4DDB58 to=#C1F5C5 f=0.8><shadow a=0.3>Minecraft</shadow></grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> a‌ whole new‌ style of progression and adventure.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The </grad></shadow><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FCE938 to=#FFF6A6 f=0.8>quest‌ book</grad></shadow><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> is your‌ main guide. It will‌ walk‌ you through‌ the‌ features, mechanics, and progression paths so‌ you‌ don't get lost‌ around.</grad></shadow>
## <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FCE938 to=#FFF6A6 f=0.6>Things‌ you‌ need to‌ know</grad></shadow>

&l<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FCE938 to=#FFF6A6 f=0.8>Boss-locked‌ progression:</grad></shadow>&r <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>You can't just‌ craft everything right away. Defeating‌ bosses‌ unlocks A LOT‌ of new‌ stuff.</grad></shadow>

&l<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FCE938 to=#FFF6A6 f=0.8>Unique Difficulty‌ System:</grad></shadow>&r <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The‌ difficulty‌ you choose‌ at‌ the start of the‌ game will‌ change‌ a lot.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=CF8019 to=CF8019>We all‌ start‌ from somewhere.</grad>
ftbquests.chapter.introducing.quest223AC: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Reforging your‌ items is‌ a straightforward way‌ to‌ get a‌ lot‌ stronger. It can provide nearly‌ any‌ buff in the‌ game‌ to‌ your equipment.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>- The‌ item's‌ primary‌ repair material (if nothing‌ else‌ works, use </grad><grad from=#006EDB to=#3F91E0 f=0.8>iron</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>).</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>- A </grad><grad from=#006EDB to=#3F91E0 f=0.8>tier material</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> from‌ the‌ list‌ below.</grad></shadow>
<grad from=#FF9E1F to=#FF9E1F f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Material List:</shadow></grad>
<grad from=#30FF68 to=#B6FCC9 f=0.8><shadow a=0.3>Tier‌ 1 / Common - Limestone Chunk</shadow></grad>
<grad from=#FCE938 to=#FFF6A6 f=0.8><shadow a=0.3>Tier 2 / Uncommon - Pyrite</shadow></grad>
<grad from=#006EDB to=#3F91E0 f=0.8><shadow a=0.3>Tier‌ 3 / Rare - Galena</shadow></grad>
<grad from=#6E2BFF to=#CCB5FF f=0.8><shadow a=0.3>Tier 4 / Epic - Charoite</shadow></grad>
<grad from=#FA732A to=#FFCFB5 f=0.8><shadow a=0.3>Tier‌ 5 / Legendary - Crown Topaz</shadow></grad>
<grad from=#910308 to=#9C6466 f=0.8><shadow a=0.3>Tier‌ 6 / Mythic - Painite</shadow></grad>
<grad from=#FF9E1F to=#FF9E1F f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>4. Perfect‌ Rolls‌ and Pity</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Here‌ is‌ a quick guide‌ on how to use‌ it:</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Every‌ reforge has‌ a small chance‌ to roll </grad><grad from=#006EDB to=#3F91E0 f=0.8>Perfect</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. A‌ Perfect roll strips every downside‌ off the‌ modifier and gives‌ the‌ item a‌ custom‌ border.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>You are not at‌ the‌ mercy of luck. </grad><grad from=#006EDB to=#3F91E0 f=0.8>Every‌ failed‌ reforge‌ raises your‌ Perfect‌ chance</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> for that material‌ tier, and after enough failures‌ the‌ next one is </grad><grad from=#006EDB to=#3F91E0 f=0.8>guaranteed</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. Hover‌ the reforge‌ button to‌ see‌ your‌ current odds.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Pity‌ is‌ tracked </grad><grad from=#006EDB to=#3F91E0 f=0.8>per material tier</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, so grinding‌ Limestone will‌ not‌ carry over‌ to Painite.</grad></shadow>
<grad from=#FF9E1F to=#FF9E1F f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>5. Reforge-Only‌ Modifiers</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Each‌ quality‌ has one‌ modifier with </grad><grad from=#006EDB to=#3F91E0 f=0.8>no downside at‌ all</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. It </grad><grad from=#006EDB to=#3F91E0 f=0.8>never‌ appears on loot</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> - the‌ forge is‌ the only‌ place‌ it‌ exists. Roll enough and‌ you‌ will find‌ it.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Reforge‌ materials‌ also have‌ a </grad><grad from=#006EDB to=#3F91E0 f=0.8>5%% chance</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> to roll one‌ quality higher‌ than their‌ tier. Mythic‌ is‌ the exception, it‌ always costs </grad><grad from=#006EDB to=#3F91E0 f=0.8>Painite</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>
<grad from=#FF9E1F to=#FF9E1F f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>6. Cleansing‌ Stones</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>If you end‌ up with‌ modifiers you don't want, you can‌ use a </grad><grad from=#006EDB to=#3F91E0 f=0.8>Cleansing‌ Stone</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> to completely wipe‌ the‌ current reforge‌ stats‌ and try again.</grad></shadow>
<grad from=#FF9E1F to=#FF9E1F f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>7. Salvaging</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The </grad><grad from=#006EDB to=#3F91E0 f=0.8>Salvage</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> tab breaks‌ reforged‌ gear back down‌ into‌ reforge‌ materials. Feed it‌ Painite‌ in the </grad><grad from=#006EDB to=#3F91E0 f=0.8>Upgrades</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> tab to‌ raise your Salvage Tier‌ and‌ recover better materials.</grad></shadow>
<grad from=#FF9E1F to=#FF9E1F f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>1. Craft‌ a Reforging Table</shadow></grad>
<grad from=#FF9E1F to=#FF9E1F f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>8. Stardust, Stars‌ and Apex</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Reforging‌ with </grad><grad from=#006EDB to=#3F91E0 f=0.8>Rare or‌ better</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> materials‌ sheds </grad><grad from=#006EDB to=#3F91E0 f=0.8>Stardust</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. Rerolling </grad><grad from=#006EDB to=#3F91E0 f=0.8>Mythic</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> gear‌ always gives‌ some, so‌ no reroll is ever‌ wasted.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>4x Stardust‌ and‌ a Painite‌ make a </grad><grad from=#006EDB to=#3F91E0 f=0.8>Stellar‌ Core</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, which‌ adds‌ a </grad><grad from=#006EDB to=#3F91E0 f=0.8>star</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> to Mythic‌ gear. Five stars unlock the </grad><grad from=#006EDB to=#3F91E0 f=0.8>Apex‌ Crux</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> - 8x‌ Stardust around a‌ Stellar Core.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7></grad><grad from=#006EDB to=#3F91E0 f=0.8>Apex</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> gear‌ hits harder‌ and‌ gains‌ a </grad><grad from=#006EDB to=#3F91E0 f=0.8>unique active or‌ passive‌ ability</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> depending on‌ which‌ modifier‌ it rolled. Apex‌ gear then rerolls‌ with plain </grad><grad from=#006EDB to=#3F91E0 f=0.8>Painite</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and‌ keeps its‌ stars, so‌ you‌ can hunt‌ for the‌ ability you want‌ without burning‌ another Crux.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>High Salvage Tiers return </grad><grad from=#006EDB to=#3F91E0 f=0.8>Stardust, Stellar‌ Cores and‌ Apex Crux</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> from starred‌ and‌ Apex gear, so‌ nothing‌ you outgrow is ever‌ lost.</grad></shadow>
&lConfused? Still‌ don't understand? Wanna know‌ more‌ about‌ it? Head to: <shadow a=0.4><grad from=#FF8C46 to=#FFECBE f=0.6>Reforging‌ Questline

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>Thanks‌ to </grad><wave a=0.3 f=0.4 w=0.4><grad from=#FCE938 to=#FFF6A6 f=0.8>@d0ugdimad0me</grad></wave><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060> in our Discord‌ server for creating this‌ custom‌ system just for‌ Linggango.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>An </grad><grad from=#006EDB to=#3F91E0 f=0.8>Anvil</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> in‌ the middle, four </grad><grad from=#006EDB to=#3F91E0 f=0.8>Limestone‌ Chunks</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> around it. The‌ plain‌ anvil‌ no longer‌ hosts‌ these tabs.</grad></shadow>
<grad from=#FF9E1F to=#FF9E1F f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>2. Open the Reforge‌ Tab</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Right-click the‌ Reforging‌ Table and‌ select the‌ Reforge‌ Gear‌ tab.</grad></shadow>
<grad from=#FF9E1F to=#FF9E1F f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>3. Insert the‌ Required Items</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The system requires‌ three‌ inputs:</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>- The gear you‌ want to‌ reforge (</grad><grad from=#006EDB to=#3F91E0 f=0.8>swords, bows, and armor</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>).</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#A834CF to=#A834CF>I love‌ Apotheo-... Oh, it's not‌ it.</grad>
So cool

ftbquests.chapter.introducing.quest3010F: ### <grad from=#FCE938 to=#FFF6A6 f=0.8><shadow a=0.3>Alliances System</shadow></grad>

<grad from=#CC0000 to=#D64242 f=0.8><shadow a=0.3>- false:</shadow></grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> Attacks‌ and‌ harmful potion effects‌ are completely blocked between‌ allies.</grad></shadow>
### <grad from=#FCE938 to=#FFF6A6 f=0.8><shadow a=0.3>Resource‌ Requests</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Allies can request‌ resources directly‌ from each‌ other‌ using‌ these commands:</grad></shadow>

<grad from=#006EDB to=#3F91E0 f=0.8><shadow a=0.3>/ally‌ request‌ item</shadow></grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> - Asks for the item‌ your ally‌ is‌ holding in‌ their main‌ hand.</grad></shadow>

<grad from=#006EDB to=#3F91E0 f=0.8><shadow a=0.3>/ally‌ request‌ xp</shadow></grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> - Requests a‌ specific number of </grad></shadow><grad from=#00D411 to=#36CF43 f=0.8><shadow a=0.3>XP</shadow></grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> levels.</grad></shadow>

<grad from=#006EDB to=#3F91E0 f=0.8><shadow a=0.3>/ally request‌ accept</shadow></grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> - Accepts‌ the pending item‌ or </grad></shadow><grad from=#00D411 to=#36CF43 f=0.8><shadow a=0.3>XP</shadow></grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> request.</grad></shadow>
### <grad from=#FCE938 to=#FFF6A6 f=0.8><shadow a=0.3>Additional Info</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>- All‌ members share‌ a‌ unified‌ alliance group once‌ joined.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>- Friendly‌ fire rules‌ apply‌ to‌ both direct‌ physical attacks and‌ harmful potion‌ effects.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>- Requests are‌ stored‌ until‌ accepted. If the‌ requester logs‌ off, the pending request‌ is automatically‌ removed.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Alliances let players‌ form‌ groups to cooperate, share‌ resources, and avoid‌ accidental PvP. Once‌ you‌ are‌ part of an‌ alliance, you‌ can invite‌ others, manage‌ friendly‌ fire, and request‌ items or </grad></shadow><grad from=#00D411 to=#36CF43 f=0.8><shadow a=0.3>XP</shadow></grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> directly from‌ your allies.</grad></shadow>
### <grad from=#FCE938 to=#FFF6A6 f=0.8><shadow a=0.3>Forming‌ Alliances</shadow></grad>

<grad from=#006EDB to=#3F91E0 f=0.8><shadow a=0.3>/ally invite</shadow></grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> - Sends‌ an‌ invite. The‌ recipient will‌ see a‌ clickable </grad></shadow><grad from=#00D411 to=#36CF43 f=0.8><shadow a=0.3>[ACCEPT]</shadow></grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> button in chat.</grad></shadow>
<grad from=#006EDB to=#3F91E0 f=0.8><shadow a=0.3>/ally‌ accept</shadow></grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> - Accepts a‌ pending invite and joins the‌ alliance.</grad></shadow>

<grad from=#006EDB to=#3F91E0 f=0.8><shadow a=0.3>/ally disband</shadow></grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> - Disbands‌ the alliance, removes all‌ members, and‌ notifies everyone.</grad></shadow>
### <grad from=#FCE938 to=#FFF6A6 f=0.8><shadow a=0.3>Friendly‌ Fire</shadow></grad>

<grad from=#006EDB to=#3F91E0 f=0.8><shadow a=0.3>/ally‌ rules friendlyfire <true/false></shadow></grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> - Toggles whether allies‌ can‌ damage each other.</grad></shadow>
<grad from=#00D411 to=#36CF43 f=0.8><shadow a=0.3>- true:</shadow></grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> Allies‌ can‌ hurt‌ each other.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#CCAC74 to=#CCAC74>Don't kill your friends, please.</grad>
useful
<grad from=#FF91F0 to=#FF91F0>Multiplayer:</grad><grad from=#FFD791 to=#FFD791> Allience</grad>

ftbquests.chapter.introducing.quest380F3: <grad from=#FCE938 to=#FFF6A6 f=0.8><shadow a=0.3>Dodging System‌ and Movement</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The‌ mechanic has a‌ built-in </grad></shadow><grad from=#FCE938 to=#FFF6A6 f=0.8><shadow a=0.3>cooldown</shadow></grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> so it cannot be‌ spammed.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Dodging is performed‌ by‌ pressing </grad></shadow><grad from=#00960B to=#38BA43 f=0.8><shadow a=0.3>R</shadow></grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>When activated, it grants‌ a brief‌ window of </grad></shadow><grad from=#6DE32D to=#BDDEAB f=0.8><shadow a=0.3>invincibility‌ frames</shadow></grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, allowing‌ you‌ to completely‌ avoid‌ incoming </grad></shadow><grad from=#CC0000 to=#D64242 f=0.8><shadow a=0.3>damage</shadow></grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. It can also be‌ used mid-air, making‌ it‌ a great‌ utility tool‌ for‌ quick‌ repositioning or‌ maneuvering through tough spots.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The‌ mechanic‌ has a built-in </grad></shadow><grad from=#FCE938 to=#FFF6A6 f=0.8><shadow a=0.3>cooldown</shadow></grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> so‌ it cannot‌ be spammed. ftbquests.chapter.introducing.quest794D5: <grad from=#1FFFF0 to=#1FFFF0><shadow a=0.3>FTB‌ Essentials</shadow></grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> provides a‌ variety‌ of </grad></shadow><grad from=#006EDB to=#3F91E0 f=0.8><shadow a=0.3>utility‌ commands</shadow></grad><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> to streamline‌ your‌ gameplay and make survival‌ less frustrating.</grad></shadow>
