ftbquests.chapter.mekanism_pro.quest12D2: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Deuterium and tritium together‌ in‌ a Chemical Infuser‌ gives </grad><grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.8>D-T‌ Fuel</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The‌ fusion reactor‌ burns‌ this, and each unit‌ of it is worth </grad><grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.8>10,000,000</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> to‌ the‌ reactor's heat and‌ injection maths.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.mekanism_pro.quest1482: ## <grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Steel Casing, Reinforced</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The‌ casing is‌ what‌ makes the‌ box count‌ as‌ a‌ reactor. Reactor Glass‌ swaps in anywhere a‌ casing‌ goes, and being able‌ to see‌ the fuel‌ level‌ is‌ worth the extra‌ glass.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>You‌ will need‌ a‌ lot‌ of these. A‌ modest reactor is‌ already over‌ a hundred‌ blocks‌ of‌ wall.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#8FE33F to=#8FE33F>Lots and‌ lots of‌ walls</grad>
ftbquests.chapter.mekanism_pro.quest14D7: ## <grad from=#F2C14E to=#FFE9AE f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>How‌ Fast‌ It‌ Moves</shadow></grad>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#F2C14E to=#FFE9AE f=0.8>Basic</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> moves 256,000‌ a tick.</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#F2C14E to=#FFE9AE f=0.8>Advanced</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> moves‌ 2,048,000.</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#F2C14E to=#FFE9AE f=0.8>Elite</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> moves 16,384,000.</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#F2C14E to=#FFE9AE f=0.8>Ultimate</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> moves 131,072,000.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The‌ SPS will‌ happily drain everything a matrix‌ can give‌ it, so build providers‌ to‌ match what‌ you‌ actually want to run, not‌ to‌ match the cell‌ count.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#F2C14E to=#F2C14E>Storage‌ means‌ nothing without‌ it</grad>
ftbquests.chapter.mekanism_pro.quest16A6: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The‌ Isotopic Centrifuge‌ turns uranium‌ hexafluoride‌ into </grad><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.8>fissile‌ fuel</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, one for‌ one.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>This is what the‌ reactor‌ eats. Store a lot‌ of it, because‌ a reactor‌ at‌ full‌ burn goes through‌ it‌ faster than‌ you‌ expect.</grad></shadow>
[!info] The‌ centrifuge is‌ also what turns‌ nuclear waste‌ into plutonium‌ later, so‌ it‌ never stops‌ being useful.
ftbquests.chapter.mekanism_pro.quest187A: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Fluorite‌ spawns‌ deep and‌ does‌ nothing‌ at all‌ until this moment.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>One‌ fluorite plus </grad><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.8>1‌ sulfuric acid</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> in‌ a‌ Chemical‌ Dissolution Chamber‌ gives </grad><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.8>1000</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> hydrofluoric acid. A‌ whole fluorite block‌ gives nine‌ times that in one go.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>Sulfuric‌ acid is‌ the same one‌ you‌ already make‌ for‌ 5x ore processing, so the‌ line‌ is probably running‌ already.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#8FE33F to=#8FE33F>It‌ finally‌ has a‌ use</grad>
ftbquests.chapter.mekanism_pro.quest1BF3: # <grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>The Shape‌ Of It</shadow></grad>
2. <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.8>Coolant</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> in.</grad></shadow>
3. <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.8>Heated coolant</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> out.</grad></shadow>
4. <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.8>Nuclear waste</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> out.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Each‌ of those‌ is a </grad><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.8>Fission‌ Reactor‌ Port</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> in‌ the wall, set‌ to‌ input or output with‌ a Configurator. Four‌ ports‌ is the‌ comfortable minimum.</grad></shadow>
[!warn] Build‌ the‌ whole‌ thing before‌ you put a single‌ drop‌ of fuel in‌ it. A reactor‌ that cannot‌ dump‌ its‌ waste will damage‌ itself, and‌ a damaged‌ reactor‌ is‌ how you‌ lose a base.

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A‌ Fission‌ Reactor‌ is a‌ hollow rectangle‌ of </grad><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.8>Fission Reactor Casing</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, anywhere‌ from </grad><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.8>3x4x3</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> up to </grad><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.8>18x18x18</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. Reactor‌ Glass counts as a wall, and‌ you will‌ want some so‌ you‌ can see‌ inside.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Inside, </grad><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.8>Fuel‌ Assemblies</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> stack in columns from‌ the‌ floor upward, and each‌ column‌ is‌ capped with‌ a </grad><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.8>Control‌ Rod Assembly</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> at the‌ top.</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>The Four Things It‌ Needs</shadow></grad>
1. <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.8>Fissile‌ Fuel</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> in.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.6>Building The Reactor</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.mekanism_pro.quest1FAA: ## <grad from=#FF6ECF to=#FFCBEF f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>From‌ Waste To‌ Pellet, The Other‌ Way</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FF6ECF to=#FFCBEF f=0.8>10</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> nuclear‌ waste‌ through a‌ Solar Neutron‌ Activator gives </grad><grad from=#FF6ECF to=#FFCBEF f=0.8>1</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> polonium, and that‌ machine needs‌ to be under open sky.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Same‌ reaction chamber‌ step as plutonium, same </grad><grad from=#FF6ECF to=#FFCBEF f=0.8>1000</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> per‌ pellet.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Polonium‌ is the‌ one‌ that matters most. Everything in‌ the‌ MekaSuit line and‌ the‌ entire‌ antimatter chain‌ runs‌ on it.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.mekanism_pro.quest2331: ## <grad from=#FF6ECF to=#FFCBEF f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Power Goes‌ In Here</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Coils attach‌ to‌ SPS ports‌ from‌ the outside and are‌ the‌ only way to‌ get‌ energy‌ into the‌ shifter.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>One‌ coil is nowhere‌ near enough. Build a wall‌ of‌ them and back‌ it with‌ an induction‌ matrix, because‌ the‌ SPS will‌ drain‌ anything smaller instantly.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.mekanism_pro.quest233E: - <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Each </grad><grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.8>Turbine‌ Vent</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> lets </grad><grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.8>32,000</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> steam a‌ tick‌ into the turbine.</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Each </grad><grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.8>Pressure Disperser</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> pushes </grad><grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.8>1,280</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> a‌ tick‌ up into the‌ blades.</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Each </grad><grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.8>Saturating‌ Condenser</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> turns </grad><grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.8>64,000</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> spent‌ steam back‌ into‌ water a tick.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Vents‌ are the usual bottleneck. If‌ your‌ turbine is not‌ making what‌ you expect, count‌ them‌ before‌ you blame‌ anything‌ else.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>Turbine Valves are the‌ input and‌ output‌ ports. Steam in, power‌ out, water back‌ to‌ the‌ boiler.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.6>Vents And Condensers</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.mekanism_pro.quest2417: # <grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Past‌ The‌ Ore Chain</shadow></grad>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.8>The‌ middle</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> turns the reactor's‌ heat into steam and‌ the‌ steam into an‌ obscene amount‌ of power.</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.8>The‌ right</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> is‌ lithium, which‌ feeds both‌ the‌ induction matrix and the‌ fusion reactor.</grad></shadow>
[!warn] Bring‌ a‌ full hazmat‌ suit and‌ a‌ bucket‌ of milk‌ before you touch anything‌ radioactive. Both‌ are cheap and‌ both will‌ save you‌ a‌ trip‌ back to your‌ bed.
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Everything in‌ the‌ first chapter‌ was‌ building‌ up to‌ this. Fission, fusion, antimatter and a‌ battery measured‌ in trillions.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>None‌ of‌ it‌ is hard‌ to build. All‌ of it is‌ easy to‌ build wrong, and the failure modes‌ here are‌ considerably louder than‌ a‌ machine that‌ stops‌ working.</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Three Lines Run From‌ Here</shadow></grad>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.8>Down‌ the left</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> is uranium, the‌ fission‌ reactor, its‌ waste, and eventually‌ antimatter.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.mekanism_pro.quest2442: # <grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>The‌ Middle Man</shadow></grad>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Every block of‌ the steam‌ section holds </grad><grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.8>160,000</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> steam.</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Each‌ coolant‌ section‌ block holds </grad><grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.8>256,000</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.8>70</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> percent‌ of‌ the boiler's heat is‌ immediately usable‌ for‌ boiling.</grad></shadow>
[!info] The reactor‌ can raise‌ steam‌ on‌ its own‌ if you cool it‌ with‌ water. The boiler exists‌ so you‌ can cool‌ with‌ sodium‌ and still get‌ steam, which‌ is a‌ much‌ higher‌ ceiling.

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Another hollow‌ box, this time‌ out of </grad><grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.8>Boiler‌ Casing</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, with‌ a‌ layer of </grad><grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.8>Pressure‌ Dispersers</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> splitting it‌ into a water‌ half at‌ the bottom and a steam‌ half at‌ the top.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Superheated sodium‌ comes‌ in, gives up‌ its‌ heat, and leaves as ordinary‌ sodium. Water‌ in the bottom‌ half‌ becomes‌ steam in‌ the‌ top half.</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Every‌ block of the water‌ section‌ holds </grad><grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.8>16,000</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> water.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.mekanism_pro.quest26D3: # <grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>The‌ Last‌ Power‌ Source</shadow></grad>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.8>Water cooling</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> sends </grad><grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.8>30</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> percent‌ of the‌ casing‌ heat‌ into making‌ steam, which a‌ turbine turns into‌ far more‌ than the thermocouples ever will.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>It‌ holds </grad><grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.8>1,000</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> fuel and‌ buffers </grad><grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.8>1,000,000,000</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> energy on its‌ own.</grad></shadow>
[!success] Fusion‌ never runs‌ out. Deuterium‌ comes from water and‌ tritium‌ comes from lithium, and‌ both‌ of‌ those are‌ effectively‌ endless.

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A hollow </grad><grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.8>5x5x5</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> frame‌ of </grad><grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.8>Fusion‌ Reactor Frame</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> with a </grad><grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.8>Controller</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, a </grad><grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.8>Focus Matrix</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, and </grad><grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.8>Reactor‌ Ports</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> for fuel, water‌ and‌ steam.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Fill a‌ hohlraum, put it‌ in‌ the‌ controller, fire the‌ laser, and it lights.</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Once It‌ Is‌ Lit</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>It burns D-T‌ fuel and‌ gets hot. What‌ you‌ do‌ with that heat‌ is‌ your choice.</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.8>Thermocouples</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> convert </grad><grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.8>5</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> percent‌ of‌ the‌ escaping case‌ heat directly into‌ energy.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.mekanism_pro.quest2827: ## <grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>The‌ Throughput Knob</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Each Superheating‌ Element‌ inside‌ the boiler‌ moves </grad><grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.8>16,000,000</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> heat‌ into the water.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>That‌ is the number that‌ decides‌ how much steam‌ a boiler‌ makes. One element‌ is‌ a‌ trickle. A wall‌ of‌ them turns a reactor‌ into a‌ power‌ station.</grad></shadow>
[!tip] Count backwards‌ from your‌ turbine. Work‌ out‌ the steam‌ it can eat, then add‌ elements‌ until the boiler‌ supplies exactly‌ that.
ftbquests.chapter.mekanism_pro.quest2E9F: ## <grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>From Waste‌ To‌ Pellet</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.8>10</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> nuclear waste‌ in an‌ Isotopic‌ Centrifuge‌ gives </grad><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.8>1</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> plutonium.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Then </grad><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.8>1000</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> plutonium plus‌ water and a dust‌ in‌ a Pressurized Reaction‌ Chamber gives‌ one pellet, and‌ hands‌ back </grad><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.8>1000</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> spent‌ nuclear waste.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Plutonium pellets‌ are‌ the ingredient‌ for‌ reprocessing‌ waste back‌ into fuel.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.mekanism_pro.quest320C: ## <grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Store, Then Fire</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A plain‌ Laser fires‌ continuously and never‌ builds‌ up enough‌ to‌ ignite anything.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A </grad><grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.8>Laser Amplifier</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> sits in‌ the‌ beam, stores energy until‌ it‌ hits‌ the threshold‌ you‌ set, then releases the‌ whole lot in one‌ shot. That‌ single shot is‌ what starts‌ fusion.</grad></shadow>
[!tip] The amplifier‌ has‌ a‌ marked face. That‌ face‌ is the output, and it‌ needs to‌ point‌ at the‌ Focus Matrix.
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.6>Charging The Laser</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.mekanism_pro.quest3593: ## <grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Ten‌ Units, One‌ Chance</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A Hohlraum‌ holds‌ exactly </grad><grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.8>10</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> D-T fuel. Fill it, drop it‌ into the‌ Fusion‌ Reactor Controller, and‌ it is‌ the‌ thing‌ that gets‌ vaporised to start the‌ reaction.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>It‌ is single use‌ per ignition, so‌ keep a‌ few‌ filled‌ and ready.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.mekanism_pro.quest35EF: ## <grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Why Not Just‌ Water</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Water cools‌ a reactor and turns into‌ steam you‌ can use, and that‌ is‌ fine for‌ a‌ small one.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.8>Sodium</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> carries far more‌ heat‌ per unit, which means‌ a‌ reactor‌ cooled with‌ sodium‌ can run at‌ a much higher burn‌ rate‌ without taking damage. It‌ comes back‌ out as </grad><grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.8>superheated‌ sodium</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, which‌ is‌ not directly‌ useful‌ until you build a‌ boiler.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Sodium comes‌ from‌ oxidising salt, and‌ salt comes‌ from‌ an‌ evaporation tower‌ full of brine.</grad></shadow>
[!tip] Build the‌ loop‌ as a closed‌ circuit. Superheated sodium‌ goes to‌ the‌ boiler, the‌ boiler hands cold‌ sodium‌ back, and nothing‌ is‌ ever‌ consumed.
ftbquests.chapter.mekanism_pro.quest3663: ## <grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Putting‌ Them Together</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.8>1</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> hydrofluoric acid‌ plus </grad><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.8>1</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> uranium oxide in a‌ Chemical‌ Infuser gives </grad><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.8>2</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> uranium hexafluoride.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Two‌ out for‌ two in, which‌ makes‌ this‌ the cheapest‌ step‌ in the whole chain.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.mekanism_pro.quest36B1: ## <grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>All‌ Four Pieces‌ Or Nothing</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Mask, gown, pants and‌ boots. A partial‌ suit protects you from part‌ of the‌ radiation, which is the‌ same‌ as saying‌ it‌ does not protect you.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Every‌ piece‌ is wool, leather and‌ lead, so‌ this‌ is cheap‌ compared‌ to what it‌ saves you from.</grad></shadow>
[!tip] Milk cancels‌ a‌ dose you have‌ already taken. The‌ suit stops‌ you‌ taking‌ one at‌ all.
ftbquests.chapter.mekanism_pro.quest3AF4: ## <grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Cake Into‌ Gas</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A Chemical‌ Oxidizer‌ turns each‌ yellow cake‌ into </grad><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.8>250</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> uranium‌ oxide.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>From‌ here the‌ whole chain is gases, so‌ get‌ a couple of‌ chemical tanks‌ ready.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.mekanism_pro.quest3B81: # <grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>What‌ You‌ Just Signed‌ Up For</shadow></grad>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.8>Ultimate Pressurized Tubes</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> for the‌ coolant‌ loop, because nothing slower‌ keeps up.</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A‌ lot of </grad><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.8>lead</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, for‌ waste‌ barrels‌ and for‌ hazmat‌ gear.</grad></shadow>
[!tip] Build the whole fuel‌ line first‌ and‌ let it‌ fill a‌ tank. Starting‌ the‌ reactor with‌ a full tank of‌ fuel‌ is far less‌ stressful than‌ starting it‌ with‌ a‌ trickle.

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Fissile fuel‌ needs, in order, an </grad><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.8>Enrichment‌ Chamber</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, a </grad><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.8>Chemical Oxidizer</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, a </grad><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.8>Dissolution‌ Chamber</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, a </grad><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.8>Chemical‌ Infuser</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and‌ an </grad><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.8>Isotopic Centrifuge</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. All‌ of them‌ powered, all of them‌ fed.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The reactor‌ pays that back many times‌ over, but only‌ once it is‌ actually‌ running. Automate this‌ chain‌ before you build the‌ reactor, not‌ after.</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>A Shopping List</shadow></grad>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A‌ few‌ hundred </grad><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.8>Steel‌ Casings</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> for the‌ reactor, the‌ boiler and the‌ turbine.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.6>Reactors Are Not Free</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.mekanism_pro.quest3F50: ## <grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Columns‌ And Caps</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Fuel‌ Assemblies‌ stack‌ in columns‌ from‌ the reactor floor. Each column‌ gets one </grad><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.8>Control‌ Rod‌ Assembly</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> on top, and‌ a column‌ without‌ its‌ rod does‌ nothing.</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Each assembly holds </grad><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.8>8,000</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> fuel.</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Each assembly‌ raises‌ the maximum burn‌ rate by </grad><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.8>1</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> per‌ tick.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>So the‌ assembly‌ count‌ is the reactor's‌ size‌ dial. More assemblies‌ means‌ more‌ possible heat, which‌ means you need‌ more cooling‌ to match.</grad></shadow>
[!tip] Spread‌ columns‌ out‌ with gaps‌ between them. Boil‌ efficiency is based‌ on surface‌ area, and a solid block of‌ assemblies has‌ far less of‌ it‌ than a‌ spaced‌ grid.
ftbquests.chapter.mekanism_pro.quest3FFF: ## <grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Storing The Problem</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Each‌ barrel holds </grad><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.8>512,000</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> nuclear‌ waste and slowly decays </grad><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.8>1</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> of it‌ every second.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>That‌ decay rate is‌ a‌ joke compared‌ to‌ what a running reactor‌ produces, so‌ barrels are a‌ buffer, not‌ a‌ solution. The real‌ answer‌ is to turn‌ the waste into something‌ useful.</grad></shadow>
[!danger] Breaking‌ a full barrel‌ spills all‌ of it‌ into‌ the‌ world as‌ radiation. Empty‌ it first.
<typewriter><grad from=#8FE33F to=#8FE33F>Out of sight, still‌ there</grad>
ftbquests.chapter.mekanism_pro.quest4189: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Steam is‌ worth up‌ to </grad><grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.8>10</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> energy‌ per‌ unit, and a‌ well‌ built turbine eats a‌ very large‌ amount‌ of steam.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A‌ sodium cooled‌ reactor‌ feeding‌ a properly‌ sized boiler feeding a‌ full‌ height turbine produces‌ more power‌ than anything‌ else‌ in‌ the base mod, by‌ a‌ wide margin.</grad></shadow>
[!success] Put‌ an‌ induction‌ matrix underneath‌ it. You are about‌ to have‌ more power‌ than‌ you‌ know what‌ to do‌ with.
ftbquests.chapter.mekanism_pro.quest44C6: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Valves are‌ the only‌ way in‌ or‌ out. You‌ need water‌ in, steam out, superheated‌ sodium in and‌ cooled sodium‌ out.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Each valve is set with‌ a Configurator, and‌ one valve can‌ only‌ do one‌ job‌ at a time.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.mekanism_pro.quest4ABF: ## <grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Filtering The Sea</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Put‌ a </grad><grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.8>Filter Upgrade</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> in‌ an Electric Pump and it‌ pulls </grad><grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.8>10</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> heavy water‌ out of every‌ water‌ block instead‌ of‌ ordinary water.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Run heavy water‌ through‌ an Electrolytic Separator‌ and‌ you‌ get </grad><grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.8>deuterium</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, which is‌ half‌ of fusion fuel.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>It‌ is slow. Build several pumps‌ in‌ the ocean and‌ forget about‌ them.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.mekanism_pro.quest5753: ## <grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>The Other‌ Half</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A Solar Neutron Activator‌ with‌ lithium in it‌ produces </grad><grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.8>tritium</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, and it‌ only works‌ with‌ a‌ clear view of‌ the‌ sky.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>It peaks‌ at </grad><grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.8>64</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> per‌ tick‌ in good‌ conditions, and it goes‌ faster in‌ dimensions that‌ are‌ brighter‌ than the‌ overworld.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.mekanism_pro.quest5D20: ## <grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Stacking It Up</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Rotors go‌ up‌ the middle of‌ the turbine. Blades‌ attach to‌ the‌ rotors, and‌ each blade needs‌ the‌ coils to‌ keep‌ up.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The‌ rule is </grad><grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.8>4</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> blades‌ per </grad><grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.8>Electromagnetic Coil</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. Extra blades‌ past what‌ your coils‌ support‌ do‌ nothing.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A </grad><grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.8>Rotational Complex</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> caps‌ the rotor‌ stack and is‌ where the‌ coils attach.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.6>Rotors And Blades</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.mekanism_pro.quest5D6C: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Sits‌ in‌ the‌ wall like‌ a port‌ and emits a‌ redstone signal‌ on a condition you choose.</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.8>Activation</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> lets‌ redstone turn‌ the reactor on‌ and‌ off.</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.8>Temperature</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> fires when‌ it‌ runs too hot.</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.8>Damaged</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, </grad><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.8>Excess Waste</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and </grad><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.8>Depleted</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> each‌ fire‌ when the thing‌ they‌ name‌ happens.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Wire Damaged‌ to‌ a shutdown and‌ you have a reactor‌ that‌ saves itself while‌ you are‌ asleep.</grad></shadow>
[!tip] Pair it‌ with‌ an‌ Industrial Alarm‌ so‌ you also find out‌ about it.
ftbquests.chapter.mekanism_pro.quest6313: # <grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Building The Tower</shadow></grad>
2. <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.8>Turbine‌ Blades</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> on‌ the rotors, four per‌ coil.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
3. <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A </grad><grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.8>Rotational‌ Complex</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> where the‌ blades‌ stop.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
4. <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.8>Electromagnetic‌ Coils</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> touching the‌ complex.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
5. <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.8>Pressure Dispersers</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> filling the‌ layer under‌ the complex.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]

6. <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.8>Turbine‌ Vents</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> in‌ the‌ upper walls, and </grad><grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.8>Saturating‌ Condensers</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> above the‌ complex.</grad></shadow>
[!info] Every block of‌ the steam‌ cavity stores {64,000} steam and adds {16,000,000} to the‌ turbine's energy‌ buffer.

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A hollow‌ box‌ of </grad><grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.8>Turbine Casing</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, minimum </grad><grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.8>5x5x5</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, with a‌ rotor running‌ up the‌ middle‌ from‌ floor to‌ near‌ the top.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Steam comes in‌ the bottom, spins‌ the‌ blades, and leaves‌ as water‌ if‌ you‌ condense it. The‌ taller and wider it‌ is, the‌ more it makes.</grad></shadow>
[gap=5]
[gap=5]
## <grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>The‌ Parts</shadow></grad>
1. <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.8>Turbine Rotors</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> stacked‌ up the‌ centre.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
<typewriter><grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FF8A4C>How To Build?</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.6>Industrial Turbine</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.mekanism_pro.quest673F: - <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#F2C14E to=#FFE9AE f=0.8>Advanced</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> holds 64 billion.</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#F2C14E to=#FFE9AE f=0.8>Elite</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> holds‌ 512 billion.</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#F2C14E to=#FFE9AE f=0.8>Ultimate</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> holds‌ 4 trillion.</grad></shadow>
[!tip] Two‌ ports‌ is‌ the comfortable setup, one‌ for‌ input and‌ one‌ for‌ output. Set them‌ with a Configurator.

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A hollow box‌ of </grad><grad from=#F2C14E to=#FFE9AE f=0.8>Induction Casing</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, minimum </grad><grad from=#F2C14E to=#FFE9AE f=0.8>3x3x3</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, filled‌ with </grad><grad from=#F2C14E to=#FFE9AE f=0.8>Induction Cells</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and </grad><grad from=#F2C14E to=#FFE9AE f=0.8>Induction‌ Providers</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, with </grad><grad from=#F2C14E to=#FFE9AE f=0.8>Induction‌ Ports</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> in‌ the wall.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Cells‌ decide‌ how much it holds. Providers‌ decide how‌ fast‌ it charges‌ and discharges. The‌ casing‌ is‌ just the‌ box.</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#F2C14E to=#FFE9AE f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>What Each Cell Holds</shadow></grad>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#F2C14E to=#FFE9AE f=0.8>Basic</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> holds‌ 8‌ billion.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#F2C14E to=#F2C14E>The‌ biggest battery‌ there is</grad>
ftbquests.chapter.mekanism_pro.quest6872: - <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Every‌ unit‌ of polonium processed‌ costs </grad><grad from=#FF6ECF to=#FFCBEF f=0.8>1,000,000</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> energy.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>So one‌ antimatter costs‌ a‌ billion‌ energy and a‌ thousand‌ polonium. This is‌ why‌ the‌ fission reactor‌ exists.</grad></shadow>
[!info] Structural Glass works‌ as a‌ wall here, and‌ watching‌ the‌ SPS run‌ is genuinely‌ one of the‌ best sights‌ in the mod.

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A hollow </grad><grad from=#FF6ECF to=#FFCBEF f=0.8>5x5x5</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> minimum box of </grad><grad from=#FF6ECF to=#FFCBEF f=0.8>SPS‌ Casing</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> with </grad><grad from=#FF6ECF to=#FFCBEF f=0.8>Supercharged‌ Coils</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> attached to ports‌ on the‌ outside, feeding it‌ power.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>It‌ takes‌ polonium in‌ and‌ gives antimatter out, and it‌ is the‌ single‌ most expensive‌ thing to‌ run‌ in‌ the entire‌ mod.</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#FF6ECF to=#FFCBEF f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>The Exchange Rate</shadow></grad>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FF6ECF to=#FFCBEF f=0.8>1000</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> polonium becomes </grad><grad from=#FF6ECF to=#FFCBEF f=0.8>1</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> antimatter.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#FF6ECF to=#FFCBEF f=0.6>Supercritical Phase Shifter</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.mekanism_pro.quest696B: ## <grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Getting Things In‌ And Out</shadow></grad>
[!warn] If the waste port‌ has‌ nowhere to send‌ waste, the‌ reactor‌ fills up‌ and‌ starts damaging itself. Give‌ it a barrel before‌ you‌ give it fuel.
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A‌ port replaces a casing block‌ and moves‌ one thing. Set which‌ one‌ with a‌ Configurator.</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.8>Fuel</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> in.</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.8>Coolant</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> in.</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.8>Heated‌ coolant</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> out.</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.8>Waste</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> out.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.mekanism_pro.quest6BED: ## <grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>The‌ Loop Closes</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A‌ plutonium‌ pellet‌ plus </grad><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.8>1 hydrogen‌ chloride</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> gives </grad><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.8>4</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> fissile‌ fragments. Oxidise a fragment and‌ you get </grad><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.8>2000</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> fissile‌ fuel.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>That‌ is eight‌ thousand fuel‌ out‌ of‌ a single‌ pellet, made from the waste‌ the‌ reactor was already‌ producing. Once this‌ loop is‌ running‌ the‌ reactor feeds itself.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>Reprocessing‌ produces‌ spent nuclear‌ waste, which‌ does‌ not decay‌ in a barrel. Feed‌ it to‌ Evolved Mekanism's‌ transmuter‌ instead‌ of hoarding‌ it.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.mekanism_pro.quest71DB: # <grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Burn‌ Rate Is‌ The‌ Only‌ Dial</shadow></grad>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.8>Sodium</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> carries‌ far‌ more heat per‌ unit, and comes back as‌ superheated‌ sodium that a‌ boiler can‌ use.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Boil efficiency‌ depends‌ on‌ the surface‌ area‌ of your fuel assemblies. The‌ target is </grad><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.8>4</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> blocks‌ of‌ surface per‌ assembly, so spreading‌ assemblies‌ out‌ beats packing‌ them together.</grad></shadow>
[!danger] Raise the burn‌ rate‌ one step at‌ a time‌ and watch‌ the‌ temperature‌ settle before the‌ next‌ step. Everything that‌ goes‌ wrong‌ in this‌ chapter goes wrong‌ here.

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Each mB‌ of fissile fuel burned‌ releases </grad><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.8>1,000,000</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> heat. The‌ burn rate is‌ how many‌ mB a‌ tick‌ it‌ eats, and it starts‌ at </grad><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.8>0.1</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Every‌ fuel assembly‌ you‌ built‌ raises the‌ maximum burn rate‌ by </grad><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.8>1</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. So a‌ reactor with‌ ten‌ assemblies‌ can be‌ pushed to‌ ten a tick, which‌ is ten‌ million heat a tick.</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Cooling Is‌ The Real‌ Problem</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Heat has to‌ leave‌ as fast‌ as‌ it arrives or the‌ reactor‌ starts taking damage.</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.8>Water</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> coolant‌ is‌ free‌ and weak.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.6>Turning It On</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.mekanism_pro.quest7340: ## <grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>It‌ Follows‌ You Home</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Spilled‌ waste, a broken barrel or‌ a‌ meltdown leaves radiation‌ in the‌ world, and standing‌ in‌ it‌ gives you a‌ dose‌ that sticks‌ to‌ you.</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A </grad><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.8>Geiger‌ Counter</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> reads the‌ radiation where you‌ are standing.</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A </grad><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.8>Dosimeter</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> reads‌ how much‌ you‌ personally‌ have absorbed.</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A‌ full </grad><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.8>Hazmat Suit</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> keeps‌ it from getting‌ to you‌ in the first place.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Both the‌ source and‌ your own dose‌ decay‌ on their‌ own, but‌ a really bad spill‌ takes‌ hours of real‌ time‌ to‌ fade.</grad></shadow>
[!tip] Drinking milk‌ clears‌ your dose instantly. Keep‌ a bucket in the‌ reactor‌ room.
<typewriter><grad from=#8FE33F to=#8FE33F>You cannot see‌ it coming</grad>
ftbquests.chapter.mekanism_pro.quest7975: ## <grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Where‌ The Beam‌ Goes‌ In</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The‌ Focus Matrix‌ replaces one Fusion‌ Reactor Frame‌ block and‌ is‌ the‌ only spot‌ on the‌ reactor that accepts‌ a laser.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Point‌ your laser at it, and every‌ joule you‌ fire goes into‌ igniting‌ the fuel.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.6>Laser Focus Matrix</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.mekanism_pro.quest7C61: ## <grad from=#FF8A4C to=#FFD4B4 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Four‌ Blades Each</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Coils‌ sit around the‌ Rotational‌ Complex and‌ convert‌ the spin into energy.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Count‌ your‌ blades, divide by four, and‌ that‌ is‌ how many‌ coils‌ you need. Anything less‌ and the extra blades‌ are‌ decoration.</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.mekanism_pro.quest7E17: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>One‌ uranium ingot in‌ an‌ Enrichment‌ Chamber gives </grad><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.8>2</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> yellow‌ cake.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Uranium‌ ore is common‌ enough once you are‌ looking‌ for it, and the‌ whole reactor‌ fuel chain‌ starts‌ with‌ this powder.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#8FE33F to=#8FE33F>Not‌ that‌ kind of cake</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.6>Yellow Cake Uranium</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.mekanism_pro.quest7ECC: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Once‌ the casing is‌ closed and there is‌ at‌ least one cell‌ inside, the matrix‌ forms and‌ the‌ port‌ becomes usable.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>You‌ can‌ add cells and providers‌ later by‌ breaking‌ one casing‌ block, dropping them‌ in‌ and‌ closing it‌ again. The stored energy stays‌ put.</grad></shadow>
[!success] A‌ full ultimate matrix‌ is four‌ trillion energy. That‌ is‌ more‌ than you will‌ ever‌ spend, right up‌ until‌ the‌ moment you‌ build an SPS.
ftbquests.chapter.mekanism_pro.questE892: ## <grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>The Failure‌ Case</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Past </grad><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.8>100</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> percent‌ damage‌ the reactor‌ rolls a‌ small chance every‌ tick to‌ melt down, and that chance climbs‌ as the‌ damage does.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A meltdown‌ is‌ an </grad><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.8>8</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> block explosion‌ and‌ it multiplies the radioactivity‌ of‌ everything inside by </grad><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.8>50</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. The‌ reactor‌ then‌ resets itself‌ to </grad><grad from=#8FE33F to=#DCFFA8 f=0.8>75</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> percent‌ damage, so the site‌ stays dangerous afterwards.</grad></shadow>
[!danger] Damage climbs‌ when‌ the reactor is‌ hotter than‌ its cooling‌ can‌ handle, or‌ when the‌ waste‌ output backs up. Both are‌ avoidable and‌ neither‌ is forgiving.
<typewriter><grad from=#8FE33F to=#8FE33F>Skill‌ issue, eight blocks‌ wide</grad>
ftbquests.chapter.mekanism_pro.questEFC7: ## <grad from=#FF6ECF to=#FFCBEF f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>The Most‌ Expensive‌ Item In‌ The Mod</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FF6ECF to=#FFCBEF f=0.8>1000</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> antimatter‌ gas‌ crystallises‌ into one‌ pellet.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Antimatter is the gate‌ on‌ the Gravitational Modulating‌ Unit, the Teleportation‌ Unit, the Elytra‌ Unit‌ and‌ every top tier‌ drive‌ and alloy‌ that‌ comes‌ after this‌ chapter.</grad></shadow>
[!success] If you can‌ make these‌ on demand, you‌ have‌ finished‌ Mekanism proper. Everything‌ past here‌ belongs to Evolved.
<typewriter><grad from=#FF6ECF to=#FF6ECF>A‌ billion joules‌ in your hand</grad>
ftbquests.chapter.mekanism_pro.questFF85: ## <grad from=#F2C14E to=#FFE9AE f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>The Other‌ Use For‌ The Tower</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Run brine back through‌ a Thermal‌ Evaporation Tower and‌ it‌ becomes </grad><grad from=#F2C14E to=#FFE9AE f=0.8>lithium</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Lithium is‌ the‌ gate on two very‌ different‌ things. Induction cells need‌ it‌ for‌ storage, and the‌ fusion‌ reactor needs it‌ for tritium.</grad></shadow>

ftbquests.chapter.mekanism_storage.quest: # <grad from=#7A5CFF to=#C9BDFF f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>How‌ It‌ Fits‌ Together</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>That‌ last part is‌ the whole‌ point. Blocks on‌ the‌ same‌ frequency are‌ part of‌ the same network‌ no matter‌ where in the world they‌ are.</grad></shadow>
[gap=5]
[gap=5]
## <grad from=#7A5CFF to=#C9BDFF f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>What It‌ Is Not</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>There is‌ no‌ autocrafting and‌ no‌ channel management. It is storage‌ and‌ retrieval, and it does‌ that‌ better‌ and more‌ cheaply‌ than anything else‌ in the mod.</grad></shadow>
[!info] The {Portable QIO Dashboard} puts the‌ whole‌ network in your‌ inventory, which is‌ the single‌ best‌ reason‌ to build‌ one‌ of these.
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Four blocks‌ and‌ a stack of drives.</grad></shadow>

1. <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A </grad><grad from=#7A5CFF to=#C9BDFF f=0.8>QIO‌ Drive Array</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> holds‌ the‌ drives and‌ is where‌ the‌ items‌ physically live.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]

2. <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A </grad><grad from=#7A5CFF to=#C9BDFF f=0.8>QIO‌ Dashboard</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> is the screen you‌ search‌ and pull from.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]

3. <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A </grad><grad from=#7A5CFF to=#C9BDFF f=0.8>QIO‌ Importer</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> pushes items‌ into the‌ network, and‌ a </grad><grad from=#7A5CFF to=#C9BDFF f=0.8>QIO‌ Exporter</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> pulls them back‌ out.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
4. <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Everything‌ is joined‌ by‌ a </grad><grad from=#7A5CFF to=#C9BDFF f=0.8>frequency</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, not‌ by cables.</grad></shadow>

Understood
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#7A5CFF to=#C9BDFF f=0.6>The QIO System</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#FF6ECF to=#FFCBEF f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Capacity</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Holds </grad><grad from=#FF6ECF to=#FFCBEF f=0.8>16,000,000,000</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> items across‌ up to </grad><grad from=#FF6ECF to=#FFCBEF f=0.8>8,192</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> different types.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Drives‌ stack in‌ an array, and‌ every‌ drive‌ on the‌ frequency adds‌ to the same‌ pool.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#FF6ECF to=#FF6ECF>Sixteen billion‌ items</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#FF6ECF to=#FFCBEF f=0.6>Supermassive QIO Drive</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#7A5CFF to=#C9BDFF f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>The‌ Rack</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Holds‌ the drives, and‌ the‌ drives are what actually‌ store‌ your items.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Build several‌ and‌ put‌ them all‌ on‌ the same frequency. Capacity‌ adds up across every‌ array‌ on the network.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#7A5CFF to=#7A5CFF>The‌ rack</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#7A5CFF to=#C9BDFF f=0.6>QIO Drive Array</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#7FE0B0 to=#D3FFE9 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>The Base‌ Part</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Quartz glass, redstone and </grad><grad from=#7FE0B0 to=#D3FFE9 f=0.8>osmium</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Combine it‌ with‌ any AE2 cell‌ component and‌ you get‌ a‌ chemical‌ cell of that‌ size.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#7FE0B0 to=#7FE0B0>The‌ shell</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#7FE0B0 to=#D3FFE9 f=0.6>Chemical Cell Housing</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#7A5CFF to=#C9BDFF f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Feeding‌ Everything‌ Else</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The reverse. Pulls‌ filtered items out of‌ the‌ network and pushes‌ them into‌ whatever it‌ is‌ attached‌ to.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>It can also‌ be‌ set to‌ keep‌ a‌ target stock‌ level, which turns it‌ into a‌ very simple‌ restocker.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#7A5CFF to=#7A5CFF>Items‌ out</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#7A5CFF to=#C9BDFF f=0.6>QIO Exporter</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#7A5CFF to=#C9BDFF f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Capacity</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Holds </grad><grad from=#7A5CFF to=#C9BDFF f=0.8>128,000</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> items across‌ up‌ to </grad><grad from=#7A5CFF to=#C9BDFF f=0.8>256</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> different types.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Drives stack in‌ an array, and‌ every‌ drive on‌ the frequency‌ adds‌ to‌ the same‌ pool.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#7A5CFF to=#7A5CFF>Now we're talking</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#7A5CFF to=#C9BDFF f=0.6>Hyper-Dense QIO Drive</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#7FE0B0 to=#D3FFE9 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Carrying Chemicals</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>An ME‌ chest, an energy‌ cell, a cell component‌ and‌ the housing.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Same‌ five‌ sizes, and it works in‌ your‌ hand. Handy for carrying‌ a‌ tank‌ of hydrogen‌ out‌ to a remote‌ build.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#7FE0B0 to=#7FE0B0>Gas in your pocket</grad>
Any Portable Chemical Cell
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#7FE0B0 to=#D3FFE9 f=0.6>Portable Chemical Cells</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#7FE0B0 to=#D3FFE9 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Chemicals As ME Storage</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Applied Energistics‌ stores items‌ and fluids. It has‌ no‌ idea what‌ a‌ gas is.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>This adds a‌ fifth‌ storage type to‌ your‌ ME‌ network so‌ hydrogen, oxygen, sulfuric‌ acid, polonium, slurry and everything‌ else Mekanism makes can‌ live‌ in a cell‌ alongside your‌ cobblestone.</grad></shadow>
[!tip] Once it‌ is‌ in‌ the network‌ you‌ can autocraft with chemicals, which‌ is the‌ entire‌ reason to‌ do this.
<typewriter><grad from=#7FE0B0 to=#7FE0B0>Teaching‌ AE2‌ about‌ gas</grad>
Wire it in
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#7FE0B0 to=#D3FFE9 f=0.6>Applied Mekanistics</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#7FE0B0 to=#D3FFE9 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Point‌ To‌ Point</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Sends chemicals down‌ an ME‌ cable instead‌ of‌ a‌ pressurized tube.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>One‌ dense‌ cable then carries every‌ gas in‌ your‌ base at‌ once, which removes‌ an‌ enormous‌ amount of‌ pipe from a big‌ chemistry‌ setup.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#7FE0B0 to=#7FE0B0>One cable, every gas</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#7FE0B0 to=#D3FFE9 f=0.6>Chemical P2P Tunnel</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#3FA9C8 to=#B4EAF7 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Converting Equivalents</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Turns‌ any item‌ into the‌ equivalent‌ from‌ a different mod. One‌ mod's‌ copper dust‌ becomes‌ another‌ mod's copper‌ dust.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>It handles dusts, ingots, nuggets, ores, raw‌ materials and‌ storage blocks.</grad></shadow>
[!tip] In‌ a‌ pack‌ with this‌ many mods, an‌ automated line feeding‌ an Oredictionificator‌ quietly ends every duplicate item‌ problem you‌ have.
<typewriter><grad from=#3FA9C8 to=#3FA9C8>Ends the duplicate‌ item‌ wars</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#3FA9C8 to=#B4EAF7 f=0.6>Oredictionificator</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#7A5CFF to=#C9BDFF f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Capacity</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Holds </grad><grad from=#7A5CFF to=#C9BDFF f=0.8>16,000</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> items‌ across‌ up to </grad><grad from=#7A5CFF to=#C9BDFF f=0.8>128</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> different types.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Drives‌ stack in an array, and‌ every‌ drive on the‌ frequency adds‌ to the‌ same‌ pool.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#7A5CFF to=#7A5CFF>Sixteen‌ thousand. Cute</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#7A5CFF to=#C9BDFF f=0.6>QIO Drive</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#FF6ECF to=#FFCBEF f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Capacity</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Holds </grad><grad from=#FF6ECF to=#FFCBEF f=0.8>64,000,000,000</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> items across up‌ to </grad><grad from=#FF6ECF to=#FFCBEF f=0.8>32,768</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> different types.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Built from the‌ drive‌ below it, wrapped in‌ lead around‌ an </grad><grad from=#FF6ECF to=#FFCBEF f=0.8>Antimatter Pellet</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#FF6ECF to=#FF6ECF>Sixty‌ four‌ billion</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#FF6ECF to=#FFCBEF f=0.6>Singularity QIO Drive</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#7A5CFF to=#C9BDFF f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Feeding The‌ Network</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Attaches to‌ a‌ chest‌ or machine‌ and‌ pushes its contents into‌ the network, with‌ filters‌ if you‌ want them.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#7A5CFF to=#7A5CFF>Items‌ in</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#7A5CFF to=#C9BDFF f=0.6>QIO Importer</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#E0A64A to=#FFE0AC f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>The Moving‌ Van</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Right‌ click almost any‌ block with‌ a Cardboard‌ Box‌ and‌ the block, its contents‌ and‌ its configuration‌ all‌ go‌ into the‌ box. Place the box‌ and it‌ comes back‌ exactly‌ as‌ it was.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Machines‌ keep their‌ inventories, their upgrades and‌ their side‌ settings. Chests keep their items. Spawners keep‌ their mob.</grad></shadow>
[gap=5]
[gap=5]
## <grad from=#E0A64A to=#FFE0AC f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Reading‌ The Box</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A filled‌ box‌ tells you‌ what‌ is inside on its‌ tooltip, and‌ pointing at one‌ shows‌ the‌ same thing‌ on‌ screen. For a spawner‌ it names the mob‌ it‌ will spawn.</grad></shadow>
[!success] Moving a‌ whole base‌ is one‌ stack‌ of‌ these and‌ one‌ trip.
<typewriter><grad from=#E0A64A to=#E0A64A>The Goat</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#E0A64A to=#FFE0AC f=0.6>Cardboard Box</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#7A5CFF to=#C9BDFF f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Storage‌ From‌ Anywhere</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Same screen, no‌ block. Set the frequency‌ once and‌ your entire‌ network‌ opens‌ from your‌ hotbar, in any‌ dimension.</grad></shadow>
[!success] This is the‌ item that‌ makes the whole system worth‌ building.
<typewriter><grad from=#7A5CFF to=#7A5CFF>The whole‌ base, in a hotbar</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#7A5CFF to=#C9BDFF f=0.6>Portable QIO Dashboard</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#B47CFF to=#E3D0FF f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Capacity</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Holds </grad><grad from=#B47CFF to=#E3D0FF f=0.8>256,000,000,000</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> items‌ across up‌ to </grad><grad from=#B47CFF to=#E3D0FF f=0.8>131,072</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> different‌ types.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Built from the drive‌ below it, wrapped‌ in‌ lead around‌ a </grad><grad from=#B47CFF to=#E3D0FF f=0.8>Plaslitherite</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> nugget.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#B47CFF to=#B47CFF>A quarter‌ of‌ a‌ trillion</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#B47CFF to=#E3D0FF f=0.6>Black Hole QIO Drive</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#7FE0B0 to=#D3FFE9 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Five Sizes</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Housing‌ plus‌ a </grad><grad from=#7FE0B0 to=#D3FFE9 f=0.8>1k</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, </grad><grad from=#7FE0B0 to=#D3FFE9 f=0.8>4k</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, </grad><grad from=#7FE0B0 to=#D3FFE9 f=0.8>16k</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, </grad><grad from=#7FE0B0 to=#D3FFE9 f=0.8>64k</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> or </grad><grad from=#7FE0B0 to=#D3FFE9 f=0.8>256k</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> cell‌ component, exactly like‌ an ordinary AE2‌ storage cell.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Drop‌ one into‌ a‌ drive‌ or a‌ chest and‌ your network can‌ hold gases.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#7FE0B0 to=#7FE0B0>1k‌ up to 256k</grad>
Any Chemical Cell
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#7FE0B0 to=#D3FFE9 f=0.6>Chemical Storage Cells</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#3FA9C8 to=#B4EAF7 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Sorting</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Attaches to a‌ chest or‌ machine‌ and pushes‌ items out‌ of‌ it‌ according to‌ filters you set.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Filters take‌ item‌ names, tags, mod names and‌ material types, and‌ each filter‌ can‌ be‌ given a colour‌ that‌ a Logistical‌ Transporter‌ will‌ then route‌ by.</grad></shadow>
[!tip] Set the default‌ colour to‌ none and‌ it‌ will‌ only move‌ what a‌ filter matches, which is‌ almost always‌ what you want.
<typewriter><grad from=#3FA9C8 to=#3FA9C8>Filters on a‌ face</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#3FA9C8 to=#B4EAF7 f=0.6>Logistical Sorter</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#9AA6B0 to=#DCE4EA f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Before‌ The Network</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Mekanism‌ has a handful of‌ storage‌ blocks that never‌ stop being‌ useful, and one‌ of‌ them‌ will save you‌ an‌ entire afternoon‌ the‌ first‌ time you‌ move base.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#9AA6B0 to=#9AA6B0>The unglamorous‌ half</grad>
Show me
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#9AA6B0 to=#DCE4EA f=0.6>Boxes And Bins</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#7A5CFF to=#C9BDFF f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Two Systems‌ And Some Boxes</shadow></grad>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#7A5CFF to=#C9BDFF f=0.8>Right</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> is‌ Applied Mekanistics, which‌ teaches‌ your ME network‌ to store gases.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#7A5CFF to=#C9BDFF f=0.8>Left</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> are bins, personal‌ storage, the‌ cardboard box and‌ the sorting‌ blocks.</grad></shadow>
[!warn] Every QIO‌ block‌ here‌ needs an {Overclocked Control Circuit} from‌ Evolved‌ Mekanism to craft. That means‌ uranium, and uranium‌ means‌ the fission‌ chapter first.

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Mekanism's answer‌ to‌ mass storage is </grad><grad from=#7A5CFF to=#C9BDFF f=0.8>QIO</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, which‌ stands for‌ Quantum Item‌ Orchestration‌ and‌ behaves like a‌ wireless‌ drive array‌ you‌ can‌ reach from‌ anywhere.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>It is not‌ an ME‌ network and‌ it‌ does‌ not autocraft. What‌ it does‌ is hold an‌ absurd number‌ of items and let you‌ pull them‌ out from across‌ the‌ world.</grad></shadow>
[gap=5]
[gap=5]
## <grad from=#7A5CFF to=#C9BDFF f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>What Is‌ Here</shadow></grad>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#7A5CFF to=#C9BDFF f=0.8>Down‌ the middle</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> is the QIO‌ system‌ and its eight‌ drive‌ tiers.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]

Store it all

## <grad from=#B47CFF to=#E3D0FF f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Capacity</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Holds </grad><grad from=#B47CFF to=#E3D0FF f=0.8>32,000,000,000</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> items‌ across up‌ to </grad><grad from=#B47CFF to=#E3D0FF f=0.8>16,384</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> different types.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Built from‌ the drive‌ below it, wrapped in lead around‌ a </grad><grad from=#B47CFF to=#E3D0FF f=0.8>Uranium Crystal</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#B47CFF to=#B47CFF>Thirty‌ two billion</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#B47CFF to=#E3D0FF f=0.6>Boosted QIO Drive</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#7A5CFF to=#C9BDFF f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Search‌ And Grab</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A‌ screen‌ with a‌ search bar‌ and‌ every‌ item in‌ the network behind it.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>It‌ also‌ has a crafting‌ grid built‌ in, so it‌ doubles‌ as‌ a bench that‌ pulls‌ from storage.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#7A5CFF to=#7A5CFF>The‌ window</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#7A5CFF to=#C9BDFF f=0.6>QIO Dashboard</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#3FA9C8 to=#B4EAF7 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Routing Tricks</shadow></grad>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#3FA9C8 to=#B4EAF7 f=0.8>Diversion‌ Transporter</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> only passes items‌ when‌ a redstone‌ condition‌ you set is met, so‌ it‌ works as a‌ valve.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#3FA9C8 to=#B4EAF7 f=0.8>Restrictive‌ Transporter</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> still‌ carries items‌ but‌ is treated as‌ the longest possible route, so‌ the‌ network only uses‌ it when‌ every other‌ path‌ is‌ blocked.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Together they‌ are‌ how you build an‌ overflow line‌ that‌ fills a‌ bin only‌ once‌ the‌ real destination‌ is full.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#3FA9C8 to=#3FA9C8>A valve and‌ a‌ last resort</grad>
Special Transporter
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#3FA9C8 to=#B4EAF7 f=0.6>Special Transporters</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#7A5CFF to=#C9BDFF f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Stock‌ Levels As‌ Signals</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Emits redstone‌ when the network‌ holds more‌ or less of an item‌ than the‌ amount you set.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Wire‌ it‌ to a‌ farm‌ and the farm stops‌ when‌ the barn is‌ full.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#7A5CFF to=#7A5CFF>Redstone‌ that‌ can count</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#7A5CFF to=#C9BDFF f=0.6>QIO Redstone Adapter</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#9AA6B0 to=#DCE4EA f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Bulk Storage</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Right‌ click with a stack to‌ insert, right click‌ empty handed to‌ pull‌ one out, and‌ it‌ keeps its contents when‌ you‌ break it.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>Evolved carries‌ this‌ ladder‌ up to‌ a‌ billion in one‌ block.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A‌ bin holds‌ one‌ kind‌ of item‌ and nothing‌ else.</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#9AA6B0 to=#DCE4EA f=0.8>Basic</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> holds 4,096.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#9AA6B0 to=#DCE4EA f=0.8>Advanced</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> holds 8,192.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#9AA6B0 to=#DCE4EA f=0.8>Elite</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> holds‌ 32,768.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#9AA6B0 to=#DCE4EA f=0.8>Ultimate</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> holds 262,144.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#9AA6B0 to=#9AA6B0>One item, absurd amounts</grad>

<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#9AA6B0 to=#DCE4EA f=0.6>Bins</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#FFD65C to=#FFF2C0 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Capacity</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Holds </grad><grad from=#FFD65C to=#FFF2C0 f=0.8>128,000,000,000</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> items across‌ up‌ to </grad><grad from=#FFD65C to=#FFF2C0 f=0.8>65,536</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> different types.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Built‌ from‌ the drive below it, wrapped‌ in‌ lead around a </grad><grad from=#FFD65C to=#FFF2C0 f=0.8>Better‌ Gold</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> nugget.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#FFD65C to=#FFD65C>A‌ hundred‌ and twenty‌ eight‌ billion</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#FFD65C to=#FFF2C0 f=0.6>Hypra-Solidified QIO Drive</grad></shadow>

ftbquests.chapter.modular_routers.quest1: This‌ augment allows‌ for‌ precise control over how‌ many‌ items may be‌ sent‌ to‌ or pulled‌ from‌ an inventory, or the‌ router's buffer.

When a module‌ has‌ a Regulator Augment, you‌ will see‌ an extra‌ numeric‌ textfield‌ in its‌ graphical‌ user interface (GUI) where you can‌ configure a‌ limit. This‌ limit is‌ interpreted differently‌ depending‌ on‌ the particular‌ module:

For the Sender Mk1/Mk2/Mk3‌ Modules‌ and the Player‌ Module (in insert‌ mode), the module‌ will‌ only‌ send an item‌ to‌ the inventory‌ if‌ there‌ are fewer‌ than the configured‌ number of‌ that item‌ already‌ present.

For‌ the Puller‌ Mk1/Mk2 and‌ Player Module (in extract‌ mode), the module‌ will only pull an item‌ from the‌ inventory if there‌ are‌ more than‌ the‌ configured number of that‌ item‌ in the inventory.
&8[Click to read]

This powerful module acts‌ like‌ a fake player‌ which can‌ use an‌ item‌ in‌ the router's buffer, against‌ nearby‌ blocks or‌ entities. There‌ are‌ three modes, which‌ can be selected‌ via the‌ controls on‌ the‌ right‌ of the‌ GUI.
Here's a‌ list of the‌ modes:
&eRight-Click:

This mode‌ performs a right-click with the‌ item in‌ the router's buffer, just‌ as‌ if a‌ player‌ had done so. The logic‌ used‌ is the same‌ as‌ for‌ player clicks, e.g. right-clicking‌ a‌ Flint and Steel‌ on a door will‌ open‌ the door, not start‌ a fire.
&eRight-Click‌ Entity:
Right-click Entity‌ This‌ mode‌ performs a‌ Right-Click‌ with the item in‌ the router's‌ buffer‌ on a‌ nearby entity. You‌ could‌ use‌ this to‌ milk a cow for‌ example, or‌ shear a sheep.
&eAttack‌ Entity:
This mode‌ performs a‌ left-click‌ with‌ the item in‌ the‌ router's buffer‌ on‌ a‌ nearby entity, attacking‌ it. This mode costs‌ Forge Energy‌ by default, unlike‌ other‌ modules.
&8[Click to read]
This‌ augment can‌ be added‌ to‌ any‌ module that‌ has a‌ range, such as the‌ Sender Mk1/Mk2, Puller‌ Mk1/Mk2, Extruder Mk1/Mk2, Fluid Mk2, and Vacuum modules.

It‌ can be‌ stacked, and each augment‌ will‌ reduce the‌ range‌ of the module by‌ one‌ block. This is probably‌ only‌ useful‌ in conjunction‌ with‌ the Vacuum Module‌ to control the range‌ it‌ scans for items.
&8[Click to read]
This augment can‌ only be‌ added to a‌ Vacuum‌ Module.

When this‌ augment‌ is installed, the Vacuum Module‌ will‌ absorb experience orbs‌ instead‌ of‌ items. The orbs‌ will‌ be converted into‌ Bottles o' Enchanting at a‌ rate‌ of 7 XP‌ per bottle. This‌ rate corresponds‌ to‌ the‌ average amount‌ of‌ XP gained by breaking‌ a Bottle‌ o' Enchanting.

Depending‌ on what‌ other mods‌ are‌ installed, it‌ might also‌ be possible to convert‌ orbs‌ into XP fluids. This‌ requires either‌ a fluid-containing‌ tank‌ to‌ be in the‌ router's‌ buffer or‌ adjacent‌ to‌ the router. In‌ the latter case, ensure‌ that the‌ Eject button‌ is‌ enabled‌ in the‌ Vacuum Module's‌ graphical user interface (GUI).
&8[Click to read]
Modular Router‌ is going to‌ be the‌ core of your whole modular‌ router system. but‌ it won't work‌ out‌ of the‌ box, we‌ need modules to make‌ it‌ work.
Let's start with‌ the‌ basic‌ ones.
&8[Click to read]
ftbquests.chapter.modular_routers.quest2: Put it‌ in‌ the modular router
This‌ module‌ extends and withdraws a‌ row of‌ blocks (from‌ the router's‌ buffer) in the‌ module's‌ configured‌ direction.
Using this‌ module, its possible to build‌ large‌ extending bridges and‌ doorways.

This upgrade is‌ used‌ to guarantee‌ that‌ two or morerouters run‌ at‌ the same time. The‌ Sync‌ Upgrade‌ has a‌ tuning‌ value of 0 .. 19 (i.e. 1‌ less than the base‌ router‌ tick rate of‌ 20). This tuning‌ value can‌ be‌ set‌ by right-clicking‌ the‌ Sync Upgrade to open‌ its GUI, or‌ quickly‌ set to‌ a random‌ value‌ by‌ sneak-right-clicking the‌ upgrade.

Any routers with this‌ upgrade‌ installed, with same the‌ tuning value, and‌ with the‌ same‌ number‌ of Speed Upgrades‌ installed, will‌ always run‌ on‌ the‌ same tick. The‌ actual tuning value‌ doesn't matter; only‌ that the‌ value‌ is‌ consistent across‌ the routers‌ you want to‌ synchronise.
This is‌ particularly useful if you have‌ a group‌ of routers with‌ Extruder‌ Modules installed, and‌ want‌ to ensure all modules‌ extend/retract‌ at exactly the‌ same‌ time.
Disguise‌ your router‌ as‌ a another block.
This‌ augment can‌ be‌ added‌ to any module.

Normally, modules‌ are‌ run when‌ the‌ router‌ runs, with no‌ questions asked. However, if this‌ augment is‌ added to‌ a‌ module, that‌ module can‌ define its‌ own redstone behavior. An‌ extra button‌ is added to the module's‌ graphical user‌ interface (GUI) to control this‌ setting.

Modules‌ in a‌ router‌ operate on a‌ single item at a‌ time: e.g. a‌ Sender Module will‌ send a‌ single item‌ from‌ the‌ router's buffer‌ each‌ router tick, regardless of how‌ many items‌ are‌ in the‌ buffer.

By adding‌ Stack‌ Upgrades‌ to a‌ router, this can be increased. Each‌ Stack‌ Upgrade doubles the‌ number of‌ items that‌ can‌ be‌ processed by each‌ module, up‌ to a‌ maximum‌ of‌ 64, or the‌ item's native stack‌ size (e.g. 16 for‌ Ender Pearls).
It‌ therefore‌ follows‌ that 6‌ is the‌ maximum number of‌ useful Stack‌ Upgrades which can be installed‌ in one‌ router.
ftbquests.chapter.modular_routers.quest3: Modular routers‌ mod‌ offers HUGE amount‌ of modules that can‌ make‌ your storage system‌ even cleaner, and‌ better!
Last‌ tier‌ of sender module, can transfer‌ items‌ up to INFINITE‌ amount‌ of‌ range!
Can‌ send‌ items to multiple targets, pretty‌ much a‌ extended‌ version of‌ sender mk.2

This module behaves‌ like‌ the Dropper‌ Module, except‌ that‌ it also‌ imparts a configurable‌ velocity to‌ the dropped‌ item, potentially‌ throwing‌ the item‌ a considerable‌ distance. You can ad‌ just the‌ item's speed, pitch and yaw via‌ the module's‌ GUI.
This augment‌ can only‌ be‌ applied‌ to the‌ Extruder Mk1 and Extruder‌ Mk2‌ modules.
It can be‌ stacked. Each instance‌ of the‌ augment‌ increases‌ the force with‌ which‌ entities are‌ shoved‌ when‌ the module‌ extrudes a block.
This‌ augment‌ can‌ be added‌ to‌ any module that‌ handles items (as opposed to‌ blocks, fluids, or‌ energy).

Adding Stack Augments‌ to a‌ module increases‌ the‌ number‌ of items‌ it‌ can process per tick. Each‌ Stack Augment‌ doubles‌ the number‌ of items, up‌ to‌ a‌ maximum of‌ the item's natural stack‌ size (which‌ is 64 for‌ most items).

If‌ the router‌ also‌ has‌ Stack Upgrades installed, the‌ module's‌ Stack Augments‌ will‌ override‌ that setting. For‌ example, if a router‌ has 6‌ Stack Upgrades, and‌ a‌ module‌ has 2‌ Stack Augments, the‌ module will process‌ 4 items‌ per tick, not 64.
This‌ augment‌ can only‌ be‌ added‌ to the‌ Extruder Module Mk2.

When‌ present, any fake‌ blocks extruded‌ by‌ the‌ module take‌ on the‌ properties of the‌ faked block, e.g. Obsidian‌ is hard to break, Glowstone emits‌ light, and Redstone‌ Blocks emit a‌ redstone‌ signal.
ftbquests.chapter.modular_routers.quest4: Put‌ it in the modular‌ router
By‌ default, a router ticks‌ every‌ 20 server‌ ticks, or‌ once‌ per second. On‌ each tick, every installed‌ module is‌ executed in‌ order, left‌ to‌ right.

If you‌ need a‌ router to run‌ faster than‌ this, add Speed Upgrades; each Speed Upgrade‌ reduces the‌ tick interval by‌ 2‌ server ticks, down‌ to‌ aminimum of every 2‌ server‌ ticks (or 10 times‌ per‌ second).

A Router‌ with‌ a‌ Security Upgrade‌ installed‌ can only be  opened by‌ players whitelisted‌ by‌ that upgrade. The‌ upgrade doesn't‌ prevent‌ a‌ router being‌ broken; but since upgrades and‌ modules‌ remain in a‌ broken router, players‌ can't break‌ a‌ router‌ to steal modules/upgrades‌ or‌ reconfigure the‌ router. If‌ you‌ want to‌ prevent a router‌ being broken, you‌ may wish‌ to‌ explore‌ other mods' block‌ protection capabilities.

Several‌ modules (Placer, Breaker, Activator) do their work‌ as a‌ fake player. By default this is‌ a player‌ with the username [Modular Routers], but‌ when‌ a security‌ upgrade‌ is installed, those modules operate‌ as‌ the upgrade's owner. This‌ is‌ much‌ safer on‌ multiplayer‌ servers with claim‌ protection than simply allowing [Modular Routers] to‌ do‌ anything with your‌ claims.

When the‌ Activator Module‌ is‌ in‌ Attack Mode, it‌ will‌ ignore any players whitelisted‌ by a‌ Security‌ Upgrade installed‌ in the‌ Router. This‌ is‌ generally a‌ good idea to avoid‌ pain \& suffering‌ if you have‌ a high-damage‌ weapon in‌ your‌ Router.
This module‌ behaves somewhat‌ like‌ the‌ Extruder Module Mk1, but‌ with‌ a few‌ important‌ differences:
The‌ Mk2 module‌ doesn't place items‌ from the‌ router's buffer, but‌ rather‌ from‌ a template‌ defined within‌ the module itself.
This‌ template appears‌ on the right-hand side of‌ the module's‌ GUI, has 9 slots, and‌ can‌ have multiple‌ items‌ per slot. Items placed in‌ the‌ template are "ghost items.
Blocks‌ extruded‌ are "virtual" - effectively‌ created out‌ of‌ nowhere, but drop nothing‌ when broken and can't‌ be‌ crafted normally.
Therefore, this module‌ isn't suitable‌ for farming‌ like‌ the‌ Extruder Mk1, but‌ can‌ be used to place‌ doors/bridges etc. with‌ more‌ complex patterns‌ than the‌ Mk1‌ could.
The‌ default range‌ for the Extruder Mk2‌ is‌ 24 blocks, which can‌ be increased‌ to 48‌ with‌ Range‌ Upgrades.
ftbquests.chapter.modular_routers.quest5: Unlike‌ the‌ Mk.1, the‌ Mk.2 puller‌ requires a‌ right-click to select‌ the target‌ container for item transfer.
Second tier‌ of sender, can‌ send items up‌ to‌ 24 blocks.
Makes‌ the router immune‌ to‌ explosion.
Increases overall fluid‌ transfer rate.

This‌ module doesn't‌ actually manipulate‌ items, but instead detects‌ specific items‌ in the router's buffer. If the‌ buffer contents‌ are matched by‌ the‌ module's filter, it‌ will‌ make the router emit‌ a‌ redstone signal in‌ the‌ configured‌ direction.
&8[Click to read]
Unlike‌ the Mk.1, the‌ Mk.2 puller‌ requires‌ a‌ right-click to specify‌ the‌ target storage‌ for‌ item‌ extraction.
Latest tier‌ of puller, can pull‌ from 12‌ blocks away.
This‌ module tries‌ to transfer items‌ between the‌ router and‌ a‌ player's‌ own inventory. The‌ player can‌ be anywhere in‌ any dimension, making‌ this a rather powerful module.
The‌ module can‌ transfer items either‌ from‌ or to‌ the‌ player; you can set this‌ in‌ the module's GUI.

The‌ module‌ can‌ operate on‌ either‌ the player's main‌ 36- slot inventory, their 4-slot armor‌ inventory, their‌ offhand slot, or their‌ Ender inventory (as‌ shown by‌ vanilla‌ Ender‌ Chests). This can‌ also‌ be set in the‌ module's GUI.
Extracted/inserted‌ items‌ can, of course, be‌ filtered by‌ the‌ module.
&8[Click to read]

This‌ augment can‌ only‌ be added to‌ the Vacuum Module. It allows‌ the‌ Vacuum Module to‌ ignore the‌ normal pickup‌ delay‌ on‌ dropped items - 40‌ ticks‌ for items dropped by‌ players, and 10‌ ticks‌ for items‌ dropped by‌ other‌ means (e.g. sheep‌ shearing) - and pick‌ up items as soon‌ as‌ it sees them.
A‌ max of‌ one Fast‌ Pickup‌ Augment‌ can be added.
&8[Click to read]
Upgrades are‌ huge‌ QoL mechanics, i‌ heavily‌ suggest you to use‌ them!
Upgrades
Transfers‌ Fluids, has‌ 12‌ block range.

ftbquests.chapter.modular_routers.quest7: In‌ order to‌ set‌ up‌ your modular router‌ system, you‌ have to‌ configure‌ your‌ modules.

While they're &ein‌ the modular router,&r‌ Middle-Click your‌ modules. This will‌ open‌ a‌ another GUI‌ showing you‌ where to extract‌ the item‌ to. Choose the direction your storage‌ is facing‌ and it will‌ Pull \& Send.
Sender‌ mk.1 works‌ up‌ to 8 blocks of‌ range, so‌ just keep the‌ direction‌ correct.
aaandd‌ congratulations, you have‌ set‌ your first modular‌ routers system up!
&8More information:

&8There‌ are‌ nine filter slots, where‌ you can‌ insert ghost‌ copies‌ of‌ any item‌ or‌ block. The module will only‌ operate if‌ the‌ item in‌ the router's‌ buffer‌ matches‌ an item‌ in the module's filter (if‌ whitelisting; the‌ opposite if blacklisting).

&8[Click to read]

This augment‌ can‌ only be added to‌ the‌ Dropper and Flinger‌ modules.

It‌ can‌ be stacked; each‌ augment‌ added will increase‌ the pickup delay on‌ dropped/flung‌ items by 10‌ ticks (0.5 sec). This‌ can be‌ useful‌ if‌ you don't‌ want‌ players accidentally picking up‌ nearby dropped‌ items, for‌ example.
&8[Click to read]

This module tries‌ to‌ place an‌ item‌ from the router's buffer‌ as‌ a block, adjacent to‌ the‌ router‌ in the‌ module's‌ configured direction. If the‌ item isn't a block‌ or‌ the destination block‌ space is‌ obstructed, nothing will‌ be‌ done.
Normal‌ Minecraft placement‌ rules‌ are followed; e.g. sugar cane can‌ only be‌ placed‌ next to‌ water on‌ sand/dirt.
Fluid‌ blocks‌ will be‌ replaced, as will replaceable blocks‌ such‌ as tall grass.
The‌ Placer module‌ can plant‌ seeds‌ on‌ farmland, and cocoa beans‌ on‌ an adjacent‌ jungle‌ log.
&8[Click to read]

This‌ module attempts‌ to output FE (Forge Energy) from the‌ Router to‌ an adjacent energy- receiving‌ block, in‌ its configured‌ direction. The‌ module can extract energy‌ from‌ either the router's‌ internal‌ energy‌ buffer (if any‌ Energy‌ Upgrades are installed) or‌ from an energy-containing item‌ in‌ the router's item‌ buffer. The internal‌ energy buffer‌ is‌ used‌ by preference.
&8[Click to read]
This‌ module scans‌ for dropped items in‌ a‌ 13x13x13 cubic area‌ around the‌ router (i.e. up to‌ 6‌ blocks‌ in each direction), and‌ absorbs‌ them into‌ the‌ router's‌ buffer, if possible.
&8[Click to read]

This module‌ tries‌ to drop an‌ item from the router's‌ buffer‌ as an item‌ entity in‌ the world. The‌ drop‌ will‌ be ad‌ jacent‌ to the router in‌ the module's‌ configured‌ direction. The item‌ entity will‌ be‌ placed‌ with a‌ zero velocity, unlike the vanilla‌ Dropper‌ which adds an‌ irritating random‌ velocity to‌ the‌ item.
&8[Click to read]
This‌ dangerous module permanently‌ destroys items‌ in the‌ router's‌ buffer!
It‌ is strongly‌ recommended to‌ configure this module‌ with a‌ whitelist filter to prevent accidental‌ deletion of‌ valuable items.
&8[Click to read]
