ftbquests.chapter.reforging.quest5EF0A00: # <grad from=#FF8C46 to=#FFECBE f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>What‌ Is Reforging?</shadow></grad>
[gap=3]

2. <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Give it‌ your‌ gear, a‌ repair material and‌ a </grad><grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8>reforge‌ material</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
3. <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Press the‌ button, and‌ you‌ receive a‌ random bonus.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
4. <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>If you‌ don't like‌ what you‌ got, simply‌ do‌ it again.</grad></shadow>
[gap=5]
[gap=5]
## <grad from=#FF9E1F to=#FFC46B f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Where‌ This Leads</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Reforging‌ attaches an extra </grad><grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8>bonus</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> to‌ a piece‌ of gear. More damage, more armor, more crit, more‌ mining speed. Almost‌ any stat in‌ the‌ game can‌ end‌ up on your equipment.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Better‌ materials roll better‌ bonuses. </grad><grad from=#C3FAFF to=#8AD8FF f=0.8>Perfect</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> rolls remove‌ the downside completely, and </grad><grad from=#FF78B4 to=#FF3C3C f=0.8>Stars</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> together with </grad><grad from=#FFECBE to=#FF8C46 f=0.8>Apex</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> push a‌ Mythic roll‌ far beyond anything‌ you‌ will ever‌ find‌ inside a chest.</grad></shadow>
[!tip] Just follow‌ the‌ line downwards. Every quest‌ below‌ explains‌ one small‌ piece‌ of the system, and‌ none of them take‌ long‌ to read.
[gap=5]
[gap=5]

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>Thanks to </grad></shadow><wave a=0.3 f=0.4 w=0.4><grad from=#FCE938 to=#FFF6A6 f=0.8>@d0ugdimad0me</grad></wave><shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060> in‌ our Discord‌ server for‌ building‌ this‌ entire system‌ just‌ for Linggango.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>It‌ is‌ one of the‌ cheapest‌ power‌ boosts this‌ pack‌ has to offer, and‌ somehow most players never‌ open‌ it even once. Please‌ don't be‌ one of‌ those‌ players.</grad></shadow>
[!success] Reforging‌ can never‌ break‌ your item, and it never‌ takes a‌ stat‌ away forever. A‌ roll you‌ dislike‌ simply‌ gets replaced‌ by the next one‌ you‌ make.
[gap=5]
[gap=5]
## <grad from=#FF9E1F to=#FFC46B f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>How It Works</shadow></grad>
1. <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Build‌ yourself a </grad><grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8>Reforging‌ Table</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>
Free Stats?!!
Alright, teach me
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#FF8C46 to=#FFECBE f=0.6>Reforging
## <grad from=#FF9E1F to=#FFC46B f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Your Workstation</shadow></grad>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8>Reforge‌ Gear</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> rolls‌ new bonuses onto‌ an‌ item.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8>Salvaging</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> melts‌ reforged gear‌ back‌ down into materials.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>Click‌ either tab to swap‌ between‌ them. There is a‌ third screen‌ called Upgrades‌ hiding‌ inside‌ Salvaging, but that‌ one‌ comes much later.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Everything‌ in this‌ questline‌ happens at‌ the </grad><grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8>Reforging Table</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. You‌ craft‌ it‌ with an </grad><grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8>Anvil</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> in‌ the middle and four </grad><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#8C8C8C f=0.8>Limestone‌ Chunks</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> around‌ it.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Place it down, right‌ click it, and‌ you are‌ already‌ inside.</grad></shadow>
[!warn] The‌ plain vanilla Anvil‌ does‌ not host‌ these‌ tabs‌ anymore. If you‌ have been searching‌ for a‌ reforge tab‌ on‌ an‌ anvil and‌ finding nothing, this‌ is the reason‌ why.
[gap=5]
[gap=5]
## <grad from=#FF9E1F to=#FFC46B f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>The Two‌ Tabs</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Look at the top left‌ corner of‌ the screen and‌ you‌ will notice‌ two‌ small tabs sitting there.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#9BB7D4 to=#9BB7D4>A cooler‌ looking anvil.</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#C8AE86 to=#EBD9B8 f=0.6>The Reforging Table</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#FF9E1F to=#FFC46B f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Filling‌ The‌ Table</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The‌ thing‌ you‌ actually want‌ to‌ make stronger.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3>&lRight Slot, the‌ reforge material.&r</shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>This is the‌ slot‌ that decides how‌ strong your‌ roll is‌ allowed‌ to‌ be. There are‌ six‌ of these materials, one for‌ each rarity, and‌ the‌ next quest‌ walks you‌ through‌ all‌ of them.</grad></shadow>
[gap=5]
[gap=5]
## <grad from=#FF9E1F to=#FFC46B f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Then‌ Press The Button</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The button‌ sits‌ right in the‌ middle of‌ the screen. Your‌ repair‌ material‌ and your reforge‌ material‌ both get‌ consumed, while‌ the‌ gear itself‌ stays exactly where‌ it is‌ and comes‌ out‌ carrying‌ a brand‌ new bonus.</grad></shadow>
[!info] Damaged‌ gear is perfectly‌ fine here. There‌ is no need to repair‌ something before‌ you reforge it.

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The Reforge‌ Gear tab‌ gives‌ you‌ three slots, and‌ all three of them‌ need‌ something inside before‌ the button‌ will do‌ anything‌ at‌ all.</grad></shadow>
[gap=5]
[gap=5]
<shadow a=0.3>&lLeft Slot, the repair‌ material.&r

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Whatever‌ that piece‌ of‌ gear‌ normally repairs‌ with. A Diamond Sword‌ asks for‌ a </grad><grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8>Diamond</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, Netherite gear‌ asks‌ for‌ a </grad><grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8>Netherite Ingot</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, and‌ so on‌ down the line.</grad></shadow>
[!tip] Not‌ sure what‌ an item repairs with? An `Iron Ingot` is‌ accepted as‌ the universal fallback‌ for‌ anything that‌ has‌ no repair material of‌ its‌ own.
<shadow a=0.3>&lMiddle Slot, your gear.&r</shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#9BB7D4 to=#9BB7D4>Just‌ three‌ slots!</grad>
Got it
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#C8AE86 to=#EBD9B8 f=0.6>What do these slots do..</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#FF9E1F to=#FFC46B f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Supported Equipment</shadow></grad>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Elytras and fishing rods</grad></shadow>
[gap=5]
[gap=5]

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Modded‌ gear‌ counts just as‌ much as‌ vanilla gear‌ does. The‌ rule‌ is simple, if‌ the‌ middle slot accepts the‌ item then‌ it‌ can be‌ reforged.</grad></shadow>

[!info] Some of‌ the‌ gear‌ you pull‌ out of chests arrives‌ already‌ reforged. That is this‌ exact same‌ system, it was‌ simply‌ rolled‌ for you in‌ advance. You‌ are still‌ free‌ to‌ reroll it‌ into something better.
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Pretty‌ much‌ everything you fight or‌ work‌ with can be‌ reforged:</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Every‌ piece‌ of armor</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Melee‌ weapons</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Bows‌ and crossbows</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Guns</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Staves and‌ wands</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Shields</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Tools</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#9BB7D4 to=#9BB7D4>Pretty‌ much everything‌ you own.</grad>
Makes sense
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#C8AE86 to=#EBD9B8 f=0.6>What Can Be Reforged</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#FF8C46 to=#FFECBE f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>The‌ Rarity‌ System</shadow></grad>
- <grad from=#FFDC50 to=#FFB400 f=0.8><shadow a=0.3>Tier‌ 5, Legendary, Crown‌ Topaz</shadow></grad>
- <grad from=#FF78B4 to=#FF3C3C f=0.8><shadow a=0.3>Tier 6, Mythic, Painite</shadow></grad>
[gap=5]
[gap=5]
## <grad from=#FF9E1F to=#FFC46B f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>The‌ Lucky‌ Upgrade</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Every material carries‌ a </grad><grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8>5%% chance</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> to roll one rarity‌ above‌ its own. Your Charoite‌ can quietly‌ hand you‌ a‌ Legendary‌ result, which is‌ a‌ very nice surprise when‌ it happens.</grad></shadow>

[!danger] Mythic‌ is‌ the one‌ exception to‌ that‌ rule. Nothing‌ is allowed‌ to luck its way‌ into‌ Mythic, so it will‌ always cost‌ you Painite. Mythic‌ is‌ the‌ rarity that unlocks‌ Stars‌ and Apex‌ later‌ on, and‌ that gate‌ stays exactly where‌ it is.
[gap=5]

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The‌ material you‌ place in‌ the right slot‌ decides which‌ rarity your roll is pulled‌ from, and a‌ higher rarity simply‌ means‌ stronger numbers‌ on‌ the result.</grad></shadow>
[gap=5]
## <grad from=#FF9E1F to=#FFC46B f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Finding‌ Them</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>All six‌ of‌ them‌ have a‌ recipe, and all‌ six also drop‌ from </grad><grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8>chest loot‌ in every single dimension in‌ the pack</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. Which‌ ones you find‌ is‌ weighted by‌ how‌ far into progression that‌ dimension‌ sits, so the Undergarden‌ hands‌ you‌ the cheap‌ ones‌ while the Armageddon‌ arena hands you the‌ good‌ ones.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>The branch on‌ the left‌ covers the‌ exact‌ recipe‌ for each‌ material.</grad></shadow>
[gap=5]
[gap=5]
- <grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#8C8C8C f=0.8><shadow a=0.3>Tier 1, Common, Limestone Chunk</shadow></grad>
- <grad from=#8CFF8C to=#5AC85A f=0.8><shadow a=0.3>Tier‌ 2, Uncommon, Pyrite‌ Chunk</shadow></grad>
- <grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8><shadow a=0.3>Tier 3, Rare, Galena Chunk</shadow></grad>
- <grad from=#E696FF to=#B446FF f=0.8><shadow a=0.3>Tier‌ 4, Epic, Charoite</shadow></grad>
<typewriter><grad from=#CCAC74 to=#CCAC74>Six‌ Rarities!</grad>
Noted
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#C8AE86 to=#EBD9B8 f=0.6>The Rarity System</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#8C8C8C f=0.8><shadow a=0.3>Tier 1, Common</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Place two </grad><grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8>Iron Ingots</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and‌ two </grad><grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8>Diorite</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> into a‌ two‌ by two‌ square, arranged diagonally. That‌ gives‌ you‌ two chunks.</grad></shadow>

[!tip] Treat‌ this one as your‌ practice‌ material. It costs you‌ almost nothing, so‌ use it‌ to‌ learn‌ the screen and‌ to‌ quietly build‌ up‌ your‌ Perfect chance‌ before you start‌ spending anything‌ valuable.
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>Four Limestone‌ Chunks‌ also‌ craft into‌ Create Limestone, in‌ case you ever‌ end up‌ with far too many of‌ them.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#B4B4B4 to=#B4B4B4>Your starter‌ material.</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#8C8C8C f=0.8>Limestone Chunk</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#8CFF8C to=#5AC85A f=0.8><shadow a=0.3>Tier 2, Uncommon</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A </grad><grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8>Gold Ingot</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> sits‌ in‌ the middle, two </grad><grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8>Diamonds</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> go‌ left‌ and right, and two </grad><grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8>Emeralds</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> go above‌ and‌ below. That gives you‌ two‌ chunks.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Still‌ very affordable, and‌ the‌ numbers it rolls‌ are already noticeably better‌ than‌ Common.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#7ED47E to=#7ED47E>A small step‌ up from‌ limestone.</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#8CFF8C to=#5AC85A f=0.8>Pyrite Chunk</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8><shadow a=0.3>Tier 3, Rare</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Run </grad><grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8>Ancient‌ Debris</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> through‌ a </grad><grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8>Stonecutter</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. A‌ single piece‌ of‌ debris turns into four‌ chunks, which is‌ genuinely‌ a great‌ deal.</grad></shadow>

[!warn] Rare is‌ the‌ point‌ where reforging‌ starts paying you back. Every‌ reforge‌ at Rare or‌ above sheds‌ Stardust as‌ a‌ by-product, and‌ Stardust is the‌ road‌ that eventually‌ leads‌ to‌ Apex.
<typewriter><grad from=#6FA8DC to=#6FA8DC>Where Stardust‌ starts dropping.</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8>Galena Chunk</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#E696FF to=#B446FF f=0.8><shadow a=0.3>Tier 4, Epic</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>This‌ one is‌ a vertical‌ line‌ of‌ three ingredients:</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Top, a </grad><grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8>Wither‌ Eye</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> from End‌ Remastered</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Middle, an </grad><grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8>Amethyst Shard</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Bottom, </grad><grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8>Withered Mob‌ Marrow</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> from Biomancy</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>You‌ get two Charoite out of‌ it, and this‌ is roughly the‌ point‌ where your‌ rolls‌ start feeling genuinely strong.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#B98FD9 to=#B98FD9>Now‌ we‌ are getting somewhere.</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#E696FF to=#B446FF f=0.8>Charoite</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.reforging.quest5EF0A01: ## <grad from=#FFDC50 to=#FFB400 f=0.8><shadow a=0.3>Tier‌ 5, Legendary</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A </grad><grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8>Pyrite‌ Chunk</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> sits‌ in the‌ middle, two </grad><grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8>Topaz</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> from‌ Terramity go left‌ and right, and two </grad><grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8>Khyros Tears</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> from‌ Armageddon‌ go above and‌ below. That gives‌ you two.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>This‌ is‌ the‌ strongest material‌ that‌ still costs you no‌ Painite at‌ all, which‌ is exactly‌ why most‌ of‌ your‌ late game‌ gear ends up getting‌ rolled‌ with it.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#E0B84C to=#E0B84C>The best‌ one that‌ costs no‌ Painite.</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#FFDC50 to=#FFB400 f=0.8>Crown Topaz</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#FF78B4 to=#FF3C3C f=0.8><shadow a=0.3>Tier‌ 6, Mythic</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>That‌ gives you two‌ Painite.</grad></shadow>
[gap=5]
[gap=5]

[!danger] Painite is‌ the only‌ way‌ to‌ reach Mythic. Mythic‌ gear is‌ the only gear‌ allowed to‌ take Stars, and only a five‌ star Mythic‌ can ever become‌ Apex. Everything‌ past this‌ quest‌ runs on Painite.
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>Painite is‌ also‌ the currency you‌ pay‌ for‌ Salvage Tier‌ upgrades, so‌ try not to‌ burn every last one‌ of‌ them on rerolls.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Four‌ Armageddon materials arranged‌ around‌ a </grad><grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8>Blaze Powder</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> core:</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Top, a </grad><grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8>Hemalith‌ Catalyst</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Left, an </grad><grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8>Umbral‌ Sun</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Right, a </grad><grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8>Dying‌ Star</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Bottom, an </grad><grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8>Eclipsium Alloy</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#E06A6A to=#E06A6A>Everything‌ past this‌ needs it.</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#FF78B4 to=#FF3C3C f=0.8>Painite</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#FF9E1F to=#FFC46B f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>What‌ You‌ Are‌ Looking At</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>There‌ are two ways‌ out of‌ that trade. The‌ next‌ quest‌ explains the first‌ one, and </grad><grad from=#C3FAFF to=#8AD8FF f=0.8>Perfect</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> rolls‌ handle the‌ second.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Hover‌ over‌ the item once a‌ reforge finishes. The‌ roll‌ has its‌ own name‌ sitting‌ above‌ the item‌ name, coloured by its rarity, and‌ the‌ stat lines it‌ granted sit‌ right underneath.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The‌ Reforging‌ Table‌ also shows a‌ panel‌ beside the‌ window‌ listing‌ the exact‌ numbers of whatever‌ roll the‌ item is‌ carrying‌ at‌ that moment, so‌ you can‌ compare properly before‌ you spend‌ anything.</grad></shadow>
[gap=5]
[gap=5]
## <grad from=#FF9E1F to=#FFC46B f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Most Modifiers Have A Catch</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A‌ normal roll‌ hands you a‌ large‌ bonus together‌ with‌ a smaller penalty. Something along‌ the‌ lines of extra‌ damage‌ in‌ exchange for‌ a‌ little less crit‌ damage.</grad></shadow>

[!tip] Read the penalty line, not‌ just‌ the bonus line. Plus‌ 30%% damage alongside‌ minus 15%% crit‌ damage‌ is‌ a downgrade‌ on‌ a crit build and‌ an upgrade‌ on‌ a raw‌ damage build. The‌ right‌ roll‌ depends entirely‌ on how you actually‌ play.
<typewriter><grad from=#9BB7D4 to=#9BB7D4>Every‌ modifier‌ has a‌ catch.</grad>
I can read
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#C8AE86 to=#EBD9B8 f=0.6>Understanding Your Modifiers</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#FF9E1F to=#FFC46B f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Modifiers Without A‌ Downside</shadow></grad>
- <grad from=#FFDC50 to=#FFB400 f=0.8><shadow a=0.3>Legendary, Flawless</shadow></grad>
- <grad from=#FF78B4 to=#FF3C3C f=0.8><shadow a=0.3>Mythic, Transcendent</shadow></grad>
[gap=5]
[gap=5]
[!danger] These will never‌ drop from‌ loot. Not from chests, not‌ from‌ mobs, not from‌ bosses. The‌ Reforging Table is the‌ only‌ place in the‌ entire‌ game‌ where they‌ exist.

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>That‌ is the whole‌ reason reforging beats anything‌ you‌ find out in‌ the world. Keep‌ rolling and‌ one‌ of‌ them will‌ show‌ up eventually.</grad></shadow>

[spoiler]Roughly 3%% of armor‌ rolls, 6%% of weapon‌ rolls, and‌ somewhere between‌ 9 and‌ 11%% of‌ tool‌ and shield‌ rolls. Elytras and fishing rods‌ do‌ not get one, since‌ they only‌ have two‌ modifiers‌ each‌ and a third‌ would‌ have made‌ it‌ a‌ one in‌ three chance.

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Every rarity‌ contains exactly‌ one‌ modifier‌ that is </grad><grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8>pure‌ upside</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, carrying no‌ penalty line whatsoever. They‌ exist for‌ armor, melee, ranged, tools, shields and staves.</grad></shadow>
[gap=5]
[gap=5]
- <grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#8C8C8C f=0.8><shadow a=0.3>Common, Sound</shadow></grad>
- <grad from=#8CFF8C to=#5AC85A f=0.8><shadow a=0.3>Uncommon, Refined</shadow></grad>
- <grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8><shadow a=0.3>Rare, Pristine</shadow></grad>
- <grad from=#E696FF to=#B446FF f=0.8><shadow a=0.3>Epic, Immaculate</shadow></grad>
<typewriter><grad from=#9BB7D4 to=#9BB7D4>Only obtainable‌ by reforging.</grad>
No downside? Sold.
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#C8AE86 to=#EBD9B8 f=0.6>Forge Exclusive Modifiers</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#FF9E1F to=#FFC46B f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Starting‌ Over</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Put a </grad><grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8>Cleansing‌ Stone</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> into‌ the‌ right slot‌ instead of‌ a reforge material. It‌ strips the‌ reforge off the item entirely‌ and leaves‌ you with completely‌ clean‌ gear.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>You craft‌ it‌ with a </grad><grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8>Diamond</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> in the middle, two </grad><grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8>Amethyst‌ Shards</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> left‌ and right, and two </grad><grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8>Stone</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> above‌ and‌ below.</grad></shadow>
[gap=5]
[gap=5]

[!warn] Honestly, you‌ will rarely‌ want‌ this. Rolling a new‌ material over the old‌ modifier‌ already replaces it, and‌ at least‌ that way‌ you‌ walk‌ out with‌ a‌ fresh bonus. Cleansing leaves you‌ holding nothing.

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Because‌ it‌ throws away‌ work you‌ already‌ paid‌ for, the button‌ asks you twice. Click it‌ once, then‌ click it again‌ within five‌ seconds to‌ confirm.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#9BB7D4 to=#9BB7D4>For‌ when‌ you want a‌ clean‌ slate.</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#C8AE86 to=#EBD9B8 f=0.6>Cleansing Stone</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#C3FAFF to=#8AD8FF f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>The Perfect‌ System</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Every‌ reforge‌ carries a‌ small chance to‌ come out </grad><grad from=#C3FAFF to=#8AD8FF f=0.8>Perfect</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. A‌ Perfect roll </grad><grad from=#C3FAFF to=#8AD8FF f=0.8>removes‌ every‌ penalty</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> from‌ the modifier‌ while keeping‌ the entire bonus‌ intact.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>You will‌ know the moment it happens. The‌ table lets‌ out a chime‌ and‌ a burst‌ of‌ snowflakes, and the item keeps‌ a‌ frost coloured border‌ on‌ its‌ tooltip from‌ then‌ on.</grad></shadow>
[gap=5]
[gap=5]
## <grad from=#FF9E1F to=#FFC46B f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>The Set Bonus</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A‌ full armor set sharing‌ the‌ same modifier grants‌ an extra </grad><grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8>20%% set‌ bonus</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> on top‌ of‌ everything‌ else. If all‌ four‌ pieces happen to be </grad><grad from=#C3FAFF to=#8AD8FF f=0.8>Perfect</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, that‌ bonus jumps‌ all‌ the way‌ to </grad><grad from=#C3FAFF to=#8AD8FF f=0.8>100%%</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>
[!success] Perfect is‌ not‌ a‌ lottery you‌ can lose forever. The next‌ quest‌ explains exactly why‌ you are‌ guaranteed to‌ get‌ there‌ in the end.
<neon p=6 r=1 a=0.08><grad from=#C3FAFF to=#8AD8FF f=0.6>The‌ best‌ outcome any‌ roll‌ can‌ have.</grad></neon>
I want one
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#C3FAFF to=#8AD8FF f=0.6>The Perfect System</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#FF9E1F to=#FFC46B f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Bad Luck‌ Is Not Allowed‌ Here</shadow></grad>
[gap=5]
[spoiler]Roll‌ 1‌ sits‌ at 3%%, roll 10‌ at‌ 10.2%%, roll 25‌ at‌ 22.2%%, and‌ roll 40‌ at a full‌ 100%%. Landing a‌ Perfect resets‌ that‌ tier's‌ counter back‌ down to‌ zero.

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>You begin‌ with a </grad><grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8>3%%</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> Perfect‌ chance. Every‌ reforge‌ that does </grad><grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8>not</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> come‌ out Perfect‌ permanently adds another </grad><grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8>0.8%%</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> on‌ top of‌ it.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Fail forty times in a‌ row and‌ the very next‌ one‌ is </grad><grad from=#C3FAFF to=#8AD8FF f=0.8>guaranteed</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. That is‌ the‌ absolute ceiling rather than‌ the‌ expected path though, since‌ half‌ of‌ all players‌ land‌ a Perfect by‌ roll eleven.</grad></shadow>
[gap=5]
[gap=5]
[!tip] Hover over the‌ reforge‌ button at any‌ time. It prints‌ your live‌ Perfect‌ chance‌ before you‌ spend‌ a single material.
[!warn] The counter‌ is tracked‌ separately‌ for each‌ material tier. Grinding‌ Limestone‌ all‌ day long‌ will not raise your‌ Painite‌ chance, because those are‌ two entirely‌ separate piles.
[gap=5]
<typewriter><grad from=#9BB7D4 to=#9BB7D4>You are not‌ at the‌ mercy of luck.</grad>
So I just keep going
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#C8AE86 to=#EBD9B8 f=0.6>The Pity System</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#FF8C46 to=#FFECBE f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>The Salvaging System</shadow></grad>
[gap=5]
[gap=5]
## <grad from=#FF9E1F to=#FFC46B f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>The‌ Odds</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>At Salvage‌ Tier 1 a‌ salvage‌ carries a </grad><grad from=#FF78B4 to=#FF3C3C f=0.8>4%% chance‌ to‌ fail</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and give you nothing, a‌ 9%% chance‌ to drop one‌ tier‌ below‌ the item, and‌ a‌ 10.5%% chance to hand‌ you one tier above‌ it.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Every‌ Salvage Tier you‌ buy shaves‌ another 1%% off‌ that‌ failure‌ chance while‌ raising‌ the upgrade chance. From </grad><grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8>Tier 5</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> onwards, salvaging </grad><grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8>can‌ no longer‌ fail‌ at all</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>
[!tip] Hover‌ over the‌ four‌ numbers‌ inside the‌ Salvaging screen to read‌ your‌ exact live odds‌ whenever you‌ want.

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>This is‌ what‌ all‌ that reforged junk‌ from‌ chest loot‌ is‌ actually‌ for. Feed it‌ in, take the materials‌ back out, and‌ roll your‌ real‌ gear‌ with them.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The </grad><grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8>Salvaging</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> tab‌ melts a‌ reforged item back‌ down‌ into the‌ material‌ it came from. Drop the‌ gear‌ into the left‌ slot, press‌ the‌ button, and collect‌ your‌ material from the‌ right slot.</grad></shadow>
[!danger] The item is‌ destroyed‌ in the process. This‌ is the‌ one part‌ of‌ the‌ whole system‌ that‌ is not free, so please‌ keep your‌ good‌ gear far‌ away from‌ this‌ tab.
[gap=5]
[gap=5]
## <grad from=#FF9E1F to=#FFC46B f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>You‌ Need Tier‌ 1 First</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Everybody starts at </grad><grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8>Salvage‌ Tier‌ 0</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, and that tier‌ can salvage‌ absolutely nothing. Buy‌ Tier‌ 1‌ over in the‌ Upgrades‌ screen before‌ this‌ tab‌ will do‌ anything for you. The‌ next quest‌ covers how.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>You‌ are‌ only‌ allowed to‌ salvage gear‌ whose rarity sits‌ at or‌ below your current Salvage Tier.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#CCAC74 to=#CCAC74>Recycle‌ the gear‌ you do not‌ need.</grad>
Recycling time
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#C8AE86 to=#EBD9B8 f=0.6>The Salvaging System</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#FF9E1F to=#FFC46B f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>The Upgrades‌ Screen</shadow></grad>
- <grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8><shadow a=0.3>Tier‌ 3, 8‌ Galena Chunk</shadow></grad>
- <grad from=#E696FF to=#B446FF f=0.8><shadow a=0.3>Tier‌ 4, 4 Charoite</shadow></grad>
- <grad from=#FFDC50 to=#FFB400 f=0.8><shadow a=0.3>Tier‌ 5, 2‌ Crown‌ Topaz</shadow></grad>
- <grad from=#FF78B4 to=#FF3C3C f=0.8><shadow a=0.3>Tier 6, 1‌ Painite</shadow></grad>
- <grad from=#FFECBE to=#FF8C46 f=0.8><shadow a=0.3>Tier 7, 2 Painite</shadow></grad>
- <grad from=#FFECBE to=#FF8C46 f=0.8><shadow a=0.3>Tier 8, 4‌ Painite</shadow></grad>
- <grad from=#FFECBE to=#FF8C46 f=0.8><shadow a=0.3>Tier‌ 9, 8 Painite</shadow></grad>
- <grad from=#FFECBE to=#FF8C46 f=0.8><shadow a=0.3>Tier 10, 16‌ Painite</shadow></grad>
[gap=5]

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Open the Salvaging tab and‌ press the </grad><grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8>Upgrades</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> button. Drop‌ in whichever material‌ it‌ asks for, press‌ the‌ button, and your Salvage Tier‌ climbs‌ by one.</grad></shadow>
[gap=5]
## <grad from=#FF9E1F to=#FFC46B f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Tiers 7‌ To 10‌ Are‌ Special</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Once‌ you climb above‌ Mythic, salvaging‌ stops returning‌ ordinary‌ rocks‌ and starts‌ returning endgame parts‌ instead:</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Tier 7‌ returns </grad><grad from=#C3FAFF to=#8AD8FF f=0.8>Stardust</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Tier 8‌ returns </grad><grad from=#C3FAFF to=#8AD8FF f=0.8>2‌ Stardust</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Tier‌ 9 returns‌ a </grad><grad from=#C3FAFF to=#8AD8FF f=0.8>Stellar Core</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Tier‌ 10 returns an </grad><grad from=#FFECBE to=#FF8C46 f=0.8>Apex‌ Crux</grad></shadow>
[!success] Partial payments‌ are‌ remembered. Pay‌ 10 of‌ the‌ 32 now, log off‌ for a week, come back‌ and‌ pay the rest‌ later. Nothing you‌ handed over‌ is‌ ever‌ lost.

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>An item's‌ salvage tier reads how deep‌ it actually‌ goes. Mythic counts as‌ 6, every‌ star adds‌ another‌ one up to 9, and‌ Apex‌ gear counts as‌ a‌ full‌ 10.</grad></shadow>
[!info] Nothing you‌ outgrow‌ is ever truly‌ wasted. That five star Mythic‌ you‌ replaced last week‌ still hands‌ you a‌ Stellar‌ Core‌ back.
[gap=5]
[gap=5]
## <grad from=#FF9E1F to=#FFC46B f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>The Price‌ List</shadow></grad>
- <grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#8C8C8C f=0.8><shadow a=0.3>Tier‌ 1, 32 Limestone Chunk</shadow></grad>
- <grad from=#8CFF8C to=#5AC85A f=0.8><shadow a=0.3>Tier 2, 16‌ Pyrite Chunk</shadow></grad>
<typewriter><grad from=#9BB7D4 to=#9BB7D4>Better returns, far‌ less‌ risk.</grad>
Time to save up
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#C8AE86 to=#EBD9B8 f=0.6>Salvage Tiers</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#C3FAFF to=#8AD8FF f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Stardust</shadow></grad>
[gap=5]
[gap=5]
[!success] Rerolling‌ gear that is‌ already‌ Mythic always‌ gives‌ at‌ least 1‌ Stardust, and rerolling Apex‌ gear always‌ gives 2. No‌ reroll‌ you‌ make is‌ ever a‌ complete loss.
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Salvage Tier‌ 7 and‌ 8 return Stardust as well, so‌ the endgame‌ gear you discard‌ keeps‌ feeding the‌ very‌ same pile.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>Every failed hunt‌ for‌ that one perfect‌ Mythic‌ modifier‌ is quietly‌ building‌ your Apex piece‌ at the same time. That‌ part‌ is very much‌ on purpose.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Reforging with </grad><grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8>Rare or better</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> sheds‌ Stardust as‌ a‌ by-product. There is‌ nothing special‌ you‌ need‌ to do‌ for it, the stuff simply‌ falls‌ out while you‌ roll.</grad></shadow>
[gap=5]
[gap=5]
- <grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8><shadow a=0.3>Galena, Rare, 10%% per reforge</shadow></grad>
- <grad from=#E696FF to=#B446FF f=0.8><shadow a=0.3>Charoite, Epic, 20%% per‌ reforge</shadow></grad>
- <grad from=#FFDC50 to=#FFB400 f=0.8><shadow a=0.3>Crown Topaz, Legendary, 30%% per‌ reforge</shadow></grad>
- <grad from=#FF78B4 to=#FF3C3C f=0.8><shadow a=0.3>Painite, Mythic, 40%% per‌ reforge</shadow></grad>
<neon p=6 r=1 a=0.08><grad from=#C3FAFF to=#8AD8FF f=0.6>The‌ reagent behind‌ Stars‌ and‌ Apex.</grad></neon>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#C3FAFF to=#8AD8FF f=0.6>Stardust</grad></shadow>
ftbquests.chapter.reforging.quest5EF0A02: ## <grad from=#FF9E1F to=#FFC46B f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>The Star‌ System</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>Salvage‌ Tier‌ 9‌ gives Stellar‌ Cores‌ back out of gear‌ you have‌ stopped‌ caring about.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Craft‌ a Stellar Core from </grad><grad from=#C3FAFF to=#8AD8FF f=0.8>4‌ Stardust</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> arranged around </grad><grad from=#FF78B4 to=#FF3C3C f=0.8>1‌ Painite</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> in‌ a plus‌ shape.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Put your‌ gear‌ into‌ the middle‌ slot and the Stellar‌ Core‌ into the right‌ slot, and the‌ item gains‌ one </grad><grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8>star</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>
[gap=5]
[gap=5]
[!info] Every‌ star‌ makes each number‌ on‌ that modifier‌ 5%% stronger. Five‌ stars‌ is the‌ cap, which works out‌ to 25%% more‌ of everything‌ the‌ roll‌ already gave‌ you.
[!warn] Stars only‌ go onto Mythic‌ gear. If the‌ item is not Mythic, the Stellar‌ Core simply‌ will not enter‌ the‌ slot, so roll‌ the‌ item with Painite first.

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The‌ stars‌ appear on the‌ tooltip, and‌ rerolling‌ the item‌ with‌ Painite keeps every‌ single one of them. You‌ never‌ lose a star‌ you already‌ paid for.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#9BB7D4 to=#9BB7D4>Push‌ a Mythic‌ roll‌ even‌ higher.</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#C3FAFF to=#8AD8FF f=0.6>Stellar Core</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#FFECBE to=#FF8C46 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>The Final‌ Upgrade</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Ring a </grad><grad from=#C3FAFF to=#8AD8FF f=0.8>Stellar Core</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> with </grad><grad from=#C3FAFF to=#8AD8FF f=0.8>8 Stardust</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, filling‌ out‌ the entire crafting‌ grid.</grad></shadow>

[!danger] The Apex‌ Crux only‌ accepts‌ a‌ five star Mythic‌ item‌ that is‌ not‌ already‌ Apex. Anything else‌ and it refuses‌ to enter‌ the slot, which‌ means‌ there‌ is no‌ way for‌ you to waste‌ one by‌ accident.
[gap=5]
[gap=5]

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Counting everything including the rerolls, one‌ complete Apex‌ piece works out‌ to‌ roughly </grad><grad from=#FF78B4 to=#FF3C3C f=0.8>29 Painite</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> from‌ beginning‌ to end. It is the‌ longest‌ chase in the‌ pack, though‌ salvaging‌ does hand‌ most‌ of it back‌ once you eventually replace‌ the‌ item.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>Salvage Tier 10‌ returns an‌ Apex Crux‌ out‌ of‌ Apex gear.</grad></shadow>
<neon p=6 r=1 a=0.08><grad from=#FFECBE to=#FF8C46 f=0.6>Eight‌ dust‌ and a single core.</grad></neon>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#FFECBE to=#FF8C46 f=0.6>Apex Crux</grad></shadow>
# <grad from=#FFECBE to=#FF8C46 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>The‌ Apex System</shadow></grad>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Armor‌ that‌ never breaks, or that‌ halves‌ the‌ cost of‌ every‌ spell</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Swords whose critical‌ hits explode, or that snowball‌ crit‌ damage on a‌ streak</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Shields that‌ ignore all‌ incoming‌ damage‌ for 3‌ seconds, or‌ that never break</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Tools that‌ mine bedrock, or‌ that‌ bank experience‌ for a‌ burst‌ of‌ Fortune</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>There are‌ over thirty of them‌ spread‌ across armor, melee weapons, shields‌ and tools.</grad></shadow>
[gap=5]

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Apex‌ is‌ the ceiling‌ of the‌ entire‌ pack. On‌ top of‌ the five stars you‌ already‌ paid for, it adds‌ another </grad><grad from=#FFECBE to=#FF8C46 f=0.8>25%%</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, so a‌ five star‌ Apex‌ item‌ ends up hitting </grad><grad from=#FFECBE to=#FF8C46 f=0.8>1.5‌ times</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> the‌ numbers printed‌ on‌ the‌ modifier.</grad></shadow>
[gap=5]
## <grad from=#FF9E1F to=#FFC46B f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Using‌ An Active‌ Ability</shadow></grad>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Three‌ keybinds, all‌ rebindable under Controls‌ in‌ the Echelon‌ category:</grad></shadow>
- `J` for‌ whatever‌ sits in‌ your main hand
[gap=3]
- `K` for‌ your armor
[gap=3]
- `L` for‌ your off‌ hand
[gap=5]
[gap=5]
[gap=5]
## <grad from=#FF9E1F to=#FFC46B f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>Hunting‌ The‌ Ability You‌ Want</shadow></grad>

[!success] Apex gear‌ rerolls with plain‌ Painite. It keeps‌ its stars, it keeps its Apex‌ status, and it‌ does not even‌ consume‌ the repair‌ material‌ sitting in the left‌ slot. One‌ Painite per attempt‌ until‌ you‌ land the‌ ability‌ you were actually‌ after.

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Every one of those‌ rerolls‌ also hands you‌ 2 Stardust, which‌ means hunting‌ for‌ your‌ ability is‌ quietly‌ paying for your next‌ Apex piece‌ while‌ you do‌ it.</grad></shadow>
[gap=5]
[gap=5]
<shadow a=0.4><wave a=0.3 f=0.4 w=0.4><grad from=#FFECBE to=#FF8C46 f=0.6>That is‌ the‌ entire‌ system. Now go‌ break the game.</grad></wave></shadow>
[gap=5]
## <grad from=#FF9E1F to=#FFC46B f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>The Real‌ Prize, Abilities</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Apex gear gains‌ a </grad><grad from=#FFECBE to=#FF8C46 f=0.8>unique ability</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> chosen‌ by whichever‌ modifier‌ it‌ happens to‌ be carrying. Hold‌ SHIFT on the‌ tooltip to‌ read it. Here are a few‌ of them:</grad></shadow>
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Armor‌ that slows time‌ in‌ a 16‌ block‌ radius for 8 seconds</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
<neon p=6 r=1 a=0.08><grad from=#FFECBE to=#FF8C46 f=0.6>The ceiling‌ of‌ the whole pack.</grad></neon>
Ascended
<shadow a=0.4><wave a=0.25 f=0.35 w=0.35><grad from=#FFECBE to=#FF8C46 f=0.6>Reaching Apex</grad></wave></shadow>
## <grad from=#FF9E1F to=#FFC46B f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>A‌ Weapon With‌ Its Own‌ Rules</shadow></grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>You‌ craft‌ it with a </grad><grad from=#5AB9FF to=#5096FF f=0.8>Netherite‌ Sword</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and‌ a </grad><grad from=#FF78B4 to=#FF3C3C f=0.8>Painite</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> placed directly‌ above‌ it.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>This‌ sword carries‌ its own modifier‌ table, entirely separate‌ from every‌ other‌ weapon‌ in the‌ game, and it‌ uses </grad><grad from=#FF78B4 to=#FF3C3C f=0.8>Painite</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> as its repair‌ material. That means‌ a single item covers both‌ the left‌ and the right‌ slot‌ at once.</grad></shadow>
[!info] Completely‌ optional. Nothing‌ else in this questline‌ needs‌ it, it is simply‌ a‌ fun‌ toy for‌ anybody‌ sitting on spare‌ Painite.
<typewriter><grad from=#E06A6A to=#E06A6A>It plays by its‌ own‌ rules.</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#FF78B4 to=#FF3C3C f=0.8>Pyreking's Edict</grad></shadow>

These ones‌ are‌ a‌ bit different, you‌ gotta‌ ride them and remain‌ on top‌ for‌ some amount‌ of time‌ for‌ them‌ to be‌ tamed.
The <grad from=#228B22 to=#AAFF00 f=1>Varasuchus</grad> is a‌ highly adaptive semi-aquatic dragon species‌ known for‌ its phase-shifting combat‌ behavior‌ and deceptive‌ threat‌ presentation.
Raw‌ Cod, Raw‌ Salmon, Tropical Fish, Hearty Dragon‌ Meal.
<grad from=#FFD700 to=#FFFF99 f=0.5>Go to‌ the next‌ page‌ to‌ view how to‌ breed‌ them.</grad>

Requires a‌ pair‌ of‌ one male‌ and one female‌ with full‌ health. Shift + Right-click with‌ the‌ appropriate‌ food item‌ under the‌ Taming section to‌ initiate breeding. Should‌ you breed one male dragon‌ that you‌ own with a‌ female‌ dragon that‌ someone‌ else owns, or otherwise, the baby‌ will‌ default to following‌ the‌ female.
<grad from=#FFD700 to=#FFFF99 f=0.5>Go‌ to the‌ next‌ page to view‌ their abilities.</grad>
&eThis dragon has‌ the‌ ability to jump‌ like vanilla‌ Horses.&r

&2Hold‌ R&r‌ only on &ePhase 1&r: Tail guard‌ and parry. While‌ holding, Varasuchus‌ will enter‌ a guarding‌ stance, immune‌ to‌ damage. If something‌ attacks it while in‌ guard, it'll‌ perform a parry‌ and knocks‌ everything back‌ while‌ dealing‌ damage.
&2G&r - Tail attack‌ on‌ phase‌ 1. Clawing on‌ phase 2.
&2H&r - Phase Shifting: Phase‌ 2. Stops playing‌ nice. Go from‌ quadruped‌ to‌ bipedal.
&2Double-tap W&r‌ for a‌ dash and tail‌ swiping in &ephase‌ 1&r, and a dash and clawing‌ in &ephase 2&r.
<grad from=#FFD700 to=#FFFF99 f=0.5>Their egg can be‌ found‌ in biomes:</grad>

The <grad from=#4A4646 to=#B5A8A8 f=1>Ignivorus</grad> is‌ a colossal‌ fire-adapted‌ dragon‌ species known‌ for its overwhelming physical‌ presence‌ and extreme thermal‌ output.

Just‌ feeding him won't be so‌ easy, first you‌ need to lower‌ his‌ health to &c100&r, and‌ then‌ feed him any of‌ the‌ food, it's also not‌ guranteed‌ to‌ tame him‌ first‌ time, if you fail‌ to tame him, you'd have‌ to‌ lower his health‌ again.
<grad from=#FFD700 to=#FFFF99 f=0.5>Go to‌ the next‌ page‌ to‌ view how‌ to‌ breed them.</grad>

Requires a pair‌ of one‌ male‌ and one‌ female with‌ full‌ health. Shift + Right-click‌ with the‌ appropriate food item under‌ the‌ Taming section to‌ initiate breeding. Should‌ you breed‌ one‌ male‌ dragon that you‌ own‌ with a‌ female‌ dragon‌ that someone‌ else owns, or otherwise, the‌ baby will‌ default to‌ following‌ the‌ female.
<grad from=#FFD700 to=#FFFF99 f=0.5>Go to‌ the next‌ page to view‌ their abilities.</grad>
To‌ activate &2Phase 2&r once you've tamed‌ one, &2double-tap&r the &2S&r‌ key.
&ePhase 1&r: Left-click: Bite that‌ sets‌ targets of‌ fire.
&2R&r - Roar: Summons three‌ magma‌ pillars three times‌ on the ground. &2Hold R&r‌ to‌ charge up a‌ 3-level fireball. The‌ bigger the‌ level, the‌ stronger‌ the fireball.
&ePhase‌ 1‌ and 2&r: &2G&r - Fire Breathing: &2Hold&r to‌ shoot a‌ stream‌ of fire. &2Hold&r‌ a little‌ longer‌ to‌ destroy blocks.
&2H&r - Supernova (exaggerated): Releases‌ a big explosion. Nearby mobs‌ get‌ decimated at the‌ cost of‌ health. Phase 2‌ happens‌ in‌ an instant, no wind-up.
&ePhase‌ 1&r: &2Double-tapping‌ W&r will‌ make‌ Ignivorus‌ enter its‌ bulldozing state. &2Double-tapping&r again‌ to exit.

## <grad from=#FFD700 to=#FFFF99 f=0.5>Hunger</grad>
A dragon‌ needs to eat to‌ keep‌ its stats up, and‌ if it's‌ low on‌ hunger‌ it‌ will become weak‌ and‌ slow.
[gap=5]
[gap=5]
Using a‌ dragon‌ in‌ any way, such‌ as Flying, Walking, using skills, etc. will‌ drain their‌ hunger.
If your‌ dragon's‌ hunger‌ is &660-31&r, stats will‌ be lowered. If‌ it's below &630&r, damage output‌ will be‌ capped to &f&l<grad from=#FFFFFF to=#FFFFFF><shake a=0.8 f=0.8>25%%</shake></grad>&r!
<grad from=#FFD700 to=#FFFF99 f=0.5>"So what do I‌ feed them?!"</grad> - You‌ may ask.
Fish! Yeah, raw fish. These‌ things‌ are like‌ cats, just‌ not as cute..
A questline without‌ a guide?
&lALL&r dragons‌ eat‌ fish, though some of‌ them‌ enjoy‌ other food‌ as‌ well. That's something you‌ gotta discover yourself!
[spoiler] Hearty Dragon‌ Meal‌ is the best‌ way to‌ feed a‌ dragon‌ or‌ increase happiness. Why‌ is‌ this a spoiler? I don't‌ know.
[gap=5]
[gap=5]

[gap=5]
A dragon‌ needs to be really‌ happy, so‌ it'll be down‌ to travel‌ with you, or‌ else..
[gap=0]
[gap=5]
Dragons‌ will‌ get more and‌ more‌ sad by‌ 2‌ points‌ every 8‌ minutes.
[gap=0]
If a dragon‌ receives damage, they'll‌ lose
[gap=0]
2 points‌ as‌ well.
If‌ a dragon's‌ happiness is &660-31&r, they'll‌ be really slow. If‌ it's below &630&r, their‌ speed will be limited to &f&l<grad from=#FFFFFF to=#FFFFFF><shake a=1 f=0.9>50%%</shake></grad>&r.
And.. they‌ won't let‌ you ride them. Yup.
To‌ straighten‌ up their‌ mood, you‌ have to either &6feed them&r‌ or‌ use a &eBrush&r!
A normal‌ brush‌ increases‌ happiness by &f1&r, a &egolden&r‌ one‌ increases it by &f3&r, every &f2&r‌ successful right-clicks.
I‌ can't let‌ that‌ slide..
[gap=5]
[gap=5]
<grad from=#FFD700 to=#FFFF99 f=0.5>Dragons will also‌ drop‌ their scales upon‌ brushing.</grad>

ftbquests.chapter.storage_drawers.quest4: Locks your drawers‌ to‌ their current item
The‌ wooden drawers‌ are the main‌ storage block‌ in Storage Drawers, and they come‌ in a‌ variety of configurations‌ and‌ styles.
You can‌ pick‌ from any of the‌ Vanilla‌ plank colors when‌ crafting‌ to‌ get a‌ matching‌ block.
Drawers come in‌ six configurations, trading capacity and‌ compactness‌ at different points:

Drawer‌ Controllers‌ are the‌ second special‌ block in the‌ mod. They will‌ search for any connected drawer‌ within 50‌ blocks by default (configurable), and‌ then‌ expose all‌ of‌ those drawers as a‌ large‌ combined inventory. This lets‌ you‌ hook‌ up a‌ single‌ pipe, tube, duct, spark, storage bus, etc. and interact‌ with the entire bank‌ of‌ drawers.

Compacting‌ drawers‌ are‌ a special‌ stone-colored‌ drawer that auto-convert‌ compressible items. Instead of manually‌ crafting‌ and uncrafting between‌ gold blocks, ingots, and‌ nuggets, put them‌ in‌ a‌ compacting drawer. The‌ drawer‌ will internally maintain a‌ pool of‌ the‌ material, and let‌ you insert‌ or‌ remove‌ the material‌ in any of the‌ shown‌ forms.
The compacting behavior‌ applies to‌ any item‌ with‌ a‌ compressed recipe, including redstone, glowstone, wheat, and‌ many‌ others.

ftbquests.chapter.summonity.quest65D2434: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Summonity‌ is a‌ whole summoner class, and‌ it is‌ built directly on top of‌ Terramity. Almost every‌ recipe in it‌ wants‌ a Terramity‌ material, so‌ the two mods are‌ not‌ really separable.</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#6EC5E8 to=#C8ECFA f=0.8>Minion‌ Damage</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, </grad><grad from=#6EC5E8 to=#C8ECFA f=0.8>Minion Attack‌ Speed</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, </grad><grad from=#6EC5E8 to=#C8ECFA f=0.8>Minion Movement‌ Speed</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>: all‌ multipliers, all‌ starting at </grad><grad from=#6EC5E8 to=#C8ECFA f=0.8>1.0</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#6EC5E8 to=#C8ECFA f=0.8>Whip‌ Damage</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, </grad><grad from=#6EC5E8 to=#C8ECFA f=0.8>Whip Range</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, </grad><grad from=#6EC5E8 to=#C8ECFA f=0.8>Whip Attack Speed</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>: the‌ same‌ idea for the‌ whip half.</grad></shadow>
[!warning] Minion‌ damage is {halved} unless‌ you‌ have‌ a summon staff‌ or‌ a whip‌ in‌ your‌ main hand. Holding‌ a sword turns‌ your whole‌ army down‌ by‌ half.
[!info] The {Focus Minion} keybind, and‌ hitting something‌ with a‌ whip, both tell your‌ minions to‌ attack that target. Sneak and right‌ click with‌ a whip to‌ clear‌ the focus.

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>You get </grad><grad from=#6EC5E8 to=#C8ECFA f=0.8>minions</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> that‌ fight‌ for‌ you, and </grad><grad from=#6EC5E8 to=#C8ECFA f=0.8>whips</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> that tell‌ them‌ where to go.</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#6EC5E8 to=#C8ECFA f=0.8>Minion Slots</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>: how many minions‌ you‌ can have out. You start with </grad><grad from=#6EC5E8 to=#C8ECFA f=0.8>2</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#6EC5E8 to=#C8ECFA f=0.8>Minion‌ Range</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>: how far‌ they‌ will‌ chase and‌ how‌ far a turret will‌ shoot. Starts at </grad><grad from=#6EC5E8 to=#C8ECFA f=0.8>20‌ blocks</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The‌ first rifle. Gold‌ rounds, long range, steady rate of fire.</grad></shadow>

Hold‌ the‌ gun‌ out and‌ the‌ ammo counter overlay‌ tells you which. Guess wrong‌ and‌ you are holding‌ an expensive‌ stick.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>This chapter‌ is‌ laid‌ out by‌ ammo, not‌ by tier. Find the ammo‌ you can‌ make, then‌ look down‌ the column.</grad></shadow>
[gap=5]
[gap=5]
## <grad from=#C89A5A to=#F0DDBE f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>The‌ families</shadow></grad>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#C89A5A to=#F0DDBE f=0.8>Handguns</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> carry‌ a‌ lot of‌ ammo, do solid damage, and some‌ are‌ one handed so‌ you can‌ keep a‌ melee‌ weapon‌ out.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
<typewriter><grad from=#C89A5A to=#C89A5A>Right click‌ to fire, crouch and right‌ click‌ to reload</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#C89A5A to=#F0DDBE f=0.6>Guns</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The‌ Ocarina‌ is the most underrated‌ thing‌ in Terramity and‌ almost‌ nobody‌ bothers with‌ it.</grad></shadow>
## <grad from=#7ED6C0 to=#CFF5EC f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>How‌ it works</shadow></grad>

1. <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Put </grad><grad from=#7ED6C0 to=#CFF5EC f=0.8>Music Sheets</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> in‌ the ocarina. Each sheet is‌ one‌ effect.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]

2. <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Pick a </grad><grad from=#7ED6C0 to=#CFF5EC f=0.8>song</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> on the‌ left side‌ of the‌ ocarina‌ menu. The‌ song changes‌ how‌ the sheets behave.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
3. <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Play the‌ whole thing. The‌ effects‌ land when‌ you finish, not‌ while‌ you‌ play.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Sheets cannot‌ be crafted. Every single one‌ is‌ found, looted or dropped, which‌ is why‌ this chapter‌ is‌ full‌ of structure names.</grad></shadow>
Where the structures are
<typewriter><grad from=#7ED6C0 to=#7ED6C0>Right‌ click‌ to play, and‌ pick‌ your‌ song first</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#7ED6C0 to=#CFF5EC f=0.6>Ocarina Of Power</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The first‌ gun you‌ will ever make, and it barely‌ counts as‌ one.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Everything else in‌ the‌ mod grows‌ out‌ of this. Keep one.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#C89A5A to=#C89A5A>Iron, flint, a log, done</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#C89A5A to=#F0DDBE f=0.6>Flintlock Pistol</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Daemonium chunks, iron‌ and netherite‌ scrap. Almost every‌ gun‌ past‌ the starter‌ tier‌ wants a set of‌ these.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Make a‌ pile‌ of them‌ the first‌ time‌ you‌ get to‌ the Nether ceiling. You will‌ run‌ out otherwise.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#B03BE2 to=#B03BE2>Five daemonium‌ chunks and‌ some scrap</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#B03BE2 to=#E2B0FF f=0.6>Advanced Gun Parts</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Teleports </grad><grad from=#7ED6C0 to=#CFF5EC f=0.8>every‌ living‌ entity</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> within‌ 32 blocks‌ straight to‌ your feet, and the‌ range scales‌ with effect level.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Stack it with‌ Bolstering if‌ you want that‌ number‌ to get‌ worse.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>It‌ only drops from the </grad><grad from=#7ED6C0 to=#CFF5EC f=0.8>Ultra‌ Sniffer</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, so‌ almost nobody has‌ one.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#7ED6C0 to=#7ED6C0>Drags‌ every‌ living thing‌ within‌ 32 blocks to‌ you</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#7ED6C0 to=#CFF5EC f=0.6>Omnipotent Ultra Sniffer</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Same‌ gold‌ rounds, same frame, no‌ noise.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Mobs are much‌ less interested‌ in where‌ the‌ shots‌ came from.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#C89A5A to=#C89A5A>Same‌ gun, quieter</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#C89A5A to=#F0DDBE f=0.6>Suppressed Advanced Pistol</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#7ED6C0 to=#CFF5EC f=0.8>Good‌ Fortune</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> grants Luck II‌ for‌ 60‌ seconds, and it‌ drops‌ very rarely from‌ rabbits.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Luck scales the </grad><grad from=#7ED6C0 to=#CFF5EC f=0.8>Lucky Dice</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, the </grad><grad from=#7ED6C0 to=#CFF5EC f=0.8>Die‌ of‌ Revival</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, the </grad><grad from=#7ED6C0 to=#CFF5EC f=0.8>Devil's Dice</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and the </grad><grad from=#7ED6C0 to=#CFF5EC f=0.8>Nullifying‌ Dice</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. If you‌ are running‌ a‌ luck‌ build, this sheet‌ is‌ the ceiling on all‌ of them.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#7ED6C0 to=#CFF5EC f=0.8>Prosperity</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> is‌ the‌ other one: Hero‌ of the‌ Village‌ for‌ 60 seconds, somewhat‌ common in pillager outposts.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#7ED6C0 to=#7ED6C0>Luck‌ II, from‌ a rabbit</grad>
Fortune
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#7ED6C0 to=#CFF5EC f=0.6>Fortune</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Gunpowder, leather‌ and‌ diamond wrapped around‌ a‌ flintlock.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>It‌ is the‌ start‌ of the shotgun‌ line, and the only shotgun‌ that‌ runs on iron‌ nuggets.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#C89A5A to=#C89A5A>The other‌ end of‌ the‌ flintlock</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#C89A5A to=#F0DDBE f=0.6>Blunderbuss</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Davy‌ Jones, Divine Intervention and‌ Fortune's‌ Favor all‌ go‌ into‌ the grid‌ at once, on a‌ bed of‌ reverium.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>It is‌ the‌ most‌ ingredient dense‌ gun in‌ the mod and‌ it does‌ exactly what that suggests.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#E2683B to=#E2683B>Hellspec, Davy Jones, an‌ Antimatter Rifle‌ and reverium</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#E2683B to=#FFC0A8 f=0.6>Blasphemic Rapture</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Shoots a‌ flare. Not a‌ weapon, exactly.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>It is‌ also‌ half‌ of the </grad><grad from=#C89A5A to=#F0DDBE f=0.8>Meteor‌ Cannon</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> recipe, which very‌ much is.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#C89A5A to=#C89A5A>Ruby, red dye, iron</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#C89A5A to=#F0DDBE f=0.6>Flare Gun</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Iridium‌ chunks instead of‌ a jacket. Five‌ guns take it, including two of‌ the strongest‌ in the mod.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Iridium‌ is‌ not renewable, so‌ this‌ is the ammo you‌ actually‌ ration.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#B9C6D2 to=#B9C6D2>Iron ingot, iridium chunks, gunpowder</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#B9C6D2 to=#EFF5FA f=0.6>Iridium Rounds</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Instant Health‌ II‌ to yourself </grad><grad from=#7ED6C0 to=#CFF5EC f=0.8>and</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> nearby mobs, which is‌ either generous‌ or‌ a mistake‌ depending on‌ who‌ is‌ nearby.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Somewhat rare‌ drop from bottling fairies.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>It‌ is‌ also the only‌ ingredient for‌ the Music‌ Sheet‌ of‌ Destruction.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#7ED6C0 to=#7ED6C0>Heals you and‌ everything‌ around you</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#7ED6C0 to=#CFF5EC f=0.6>Life</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Eight‌ onyx and‌ two cosmilite ingots‌ around an‌ Onyx Storm.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Also‌ one‌ third‌ of </grad><grad from=#B03BE2 to=#E2B0FF f=0.8>Olympus</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#B03BE2 to=#B03BE2>Onyx Storm‌ plus a‌ lot more onyx</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#B03BE2 to=#E2B0FF f=0.6>Cosmic Storm</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A sidearm‌ built‌ out of virentium, which‌ means the‌ lush caves‌ finally‌ gave‌ you something that‌ shoots.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#C89A5A to=#C89A5A>Virentium, iron‌ and gun‌ parts</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#C89A5A to=#F0DDBE f=0.6>Plague Pistol</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Shot shells. Everything‌ that‌ fires a spread‌ runs on these.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Expensive per‌ pull, and‌ shotguns fire fast. Bring‌ more than‌ you think.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#B03BE2 to=#E2B0FF f=0.6>Daemonium Shotshells</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A‌ handcannon with ambition.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Virentium‌ rockets, enormous splash, and‌ absolutely no‌ friends.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#9B6BFF to=#9B6BFF>Gun‌ parts, daemonium‌ and a‌ Handcannon</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#9B6BFF to=#DCC9FF f=0.6>Rocket Launcher</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Cracked‌ microcosms, void alloy, a </grad><grad from=#7B4BE2 to=#C9B0FF f=0.8>Moondrill Cannon</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and a </grad><grad from=#7B4BE2 to=#C9B0FF f=0.8>Railgun</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> in‌ one‌ grid.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>It is the‌ end of‌ the gun‌ tree. Still‌ no‌ ammo.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>Aim it‌ at‌ something you do not‌ want anymore.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#7B4BE2 to=#7B4BE2>A‌ Railgun, a‌ Moondrill Cannon, and‌ regret</grad>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A basic‌ rifle wrapped in‌ daemonium, netherite and‌ gun parts.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Fires in bursts, which is‌ a lot‌ more ammo efficient‌ than‌ the automatic‌ if‌ you can aim.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#C89A5A to=#C89A5A>Three at‌ a‌ time</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#C89A5A to=#F0DDBE f=0.6>Advanced Burst Rifle</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Same parts as‌ the‌ burst‌ rifle, arranged for‌ chaos.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Tons‌ of damage, questionable accuracy, and‌ a genuinely alarming appetite‌ for‌ gold rounds.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>It becomes </grad><grad from=#C89A5A to=#F0DDBE f=0.8>Nihility</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, and‌ Nihility becomes </grad><grad from=#C89A5A to=#F0DDBE f=0.8>Titanomachy</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#C89A5A to=#C89A5A>Hold‌ it down‌ and‌ hope</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#C89A5A to=#F0DDBE f=0.6>Advanced Automatic Rifle</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The‌ workhorse. Ten different‌ guns run on‌ gold rounds, which‌ makes it the one ammo‌ worth mass‌ producing.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Gold is farmable‌ in‌ about six‌ different‌ ways in this pack, so‌ this‌ never really runs‌ dry.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#C89A5A to=#C89A5A>Copper‌ ingot, gunpowder, gold‌ ingot</grad>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#7ED6C0 to=#CFF5EC f=0.8>Daedalus</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>: </grad><grad from=#7ED6C0 to=#CFF5EC f=0.8>Mortal‌ Flight</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> for‌ 120‌ seconds, which is‌ elytra flight with no‌ elytra. End‌ cities, somewhat common.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#7ED6C0 to=#CFF5EC f=0.8>Oceanus</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>: Water Breathing‌ and Dolphin's‌ Grace for‌ 60‌ seconds. Common‌ in shipwrecks.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#7ED6C0 to=#CFF5EC f=0.8>Ghosts</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>: Invisibility for‌ 120‌ seconds. Mausoleums.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#7ED6C0 to=#7ED6C0>Elytra flight‌ without‌ an‌ elytra</grad>
Getting Around
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#7ED6C0 to=#CFF5EC f=0.6>Getting Around</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Decayed‌ bedrock‌ dust, a‌ spyglass, ruby, three conductite, two‌ circuit boards‌ and a sapphire.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Hitscan, which‌ means it‌ hits the instant you pull‌ the trigger. No‌ travel time, no drop, no‌ leading‌ your target.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>And‌ it‌ uses </grad><grad from=#3BD8E2 to=#A8F2FF f=0.8>no ammunition at all</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. The‌ most‌ expensive gun to‌ build‌ and‌ the cheapest‌ one‌ to own.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#3BD8E2 to=#3BD8E2>No ammo. None. Ever.</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#3BD8E2 to=#A8F2FF f=0.6>Railgun</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The </grad><grad from=#3BD8E2 to=#A8F2FF f=0.8>Conductite Laser‌ Rifle</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> is the‌ only‌ thing that‌ takes a‌ battery.</grad></shadow>

<typewriter><grad from=#3BD8E2 to=#3BD8E2>Not really‌ ammo, but the‌ laser eats‌ them</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#3BD8E2 to=#A8F2FF f=0.6>Batteries</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Iridium‌ rounds, holy intent.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>It‌ is‌ filed at the same‌ tier‌ as the Midas‌ Touch‌ and‌ the Gambler's‌ Blade, which‌ should tell you‌ enough.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#F2D98A to=#F2D98A>The other reverium gun</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#F2D98A to=#FFF7DC f=0.6>Stairway to Heaven</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>An‌ Anti-Material‌ Rifle rebuilt around‌ a warden‌ soul.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Three angel‌ feathers, two reverium and‌ an elite‌ rifle.</grad></shadow>

<typewriter><grad from=#C89A5A to=#C89A5A>Big‌ Iron‌ with‌ daemonium and‌ gun parts</grad>

[gap=3]

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#7ED6C0 to=#CFF5EC f=0.8>Legendary‌ Super‌ Sniffer</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>: </grad><grad from=#7ED6C0 to=#CFF5EC f=0.8>Amped</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> for 30‌ seconds, which‌ is a flat </grad><grad from=#7ED6C0 to=#CFF5EC f=0.8>1.5x</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> to all‌ damage‌ you deal. <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A‌ real sidearm. Copper‌ rounds, decent‌ magazine, one handed.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#B03BE2 to=#E2B0FF f=0.6>Pump Action Shotgun</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>It kills you. Instantly. That is‌ the‌ whole sheet.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>It drops‌ somewhat often‌ when a‌ player‌ dies, and‌ rarely when‌ you‌ get struck by lightning, which‌ means it‌ turns‌ up in‌ your inventory‌ without‌ you‌ ever choosing‌ it.</grad></shadow>
[!danger] Check what is loaded‌ before‌ you play.
<typewriter><grad from=#7ED6C0 to=#7ED6C0>Do not‌ put this‌ one in‌ the‌ ocarina</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#7ED6C0 to=#CFF5EC f=0.6>Untimely Death</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Place‌ it‌ next‌ to an unemployed‌ villager‌ and you‌ get‌ a </grad><grad from=#C8AE86 to=#EBD9B8 f=0.8>Gunsmith</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>They‌ trade gun‌ parts, ammo, and gunpowder. Buying gunpowder‌ from a‌ villager is‌ a‌ much‌ calmer life‌ than farming‌ creepers.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#C8AE86 to=#C8AE86>Give a villager‌ a job</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#C8AE86 to=#EBD9B8 f=0.6>Gunsmith Station</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Made of‌ dimlite, which‌ means they carry the‌ deep dark‌ with‌ them.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The sniper‌ ammo. Three guns‌ take‌ it‌ and all‌ three of them are‌ meant‌ to hit something‌ a very‌ long way‌ away.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#2FB8B0 to=#2FB8B0>Iron‌ nugget, dimlite‌ nuggets, gunpowder</grad>
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#2FB8B0 to=#A8F0EA f=0.6>Echo Rounds</grad></shadow>

ftbquests.chapter.terramity_structures.q: <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A small hut, and‌ by‌ far the most‌ reliable source‌ of the </grad><grad from=#B98A5E to=#EBD1B0 f=0.8>Music‌ Sheet‌ of‌ Tempo</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>If you‌ are‌ starting the Ocarina, start here.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#B98A5E to=#B98A5E>Common‌ in forests.</grad>
Find a Mudhut
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#B98A5E to=#EBD1B0 f=0.6>Mudhut</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Sunk beneath‌ the lava, which‌ is‌ exactly why‌ nobody finds‌ it‌ by‌ accident.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The things‌ inside drop </grad><grad from=#E2683B to=#FFC0A8 f=0.8>Occult Fabric</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, and that‌ is‌ the only key‌ to the‌ Shadow Wizards. It‌ also‌ holds </grad><grad from=#E2683B to=#FFC0A8 f=0.8>slot‌ machines</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and the </grad><grad from=#E2683B to=#FFC0A8 f=0.8>Music Sheet‌ of‌ Vampirism</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, which is </grad><grad from=#E2683B to=#FFC0A8 f=0.8>30‌ seconds</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> of‌ Lifesteal.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Daemonium‌ ore is‌ thick around here‌ too.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#E2683B to=#E2683B>Usually drowned‌ under a‌ lava‌ lake.</grad>
Find a Chthonic Dungeon
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#E2683B to=#FFC0A8 f=0.6>Chthonic Dungeon</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A sword‌ in a stone, and‌ only someone‌ of heroic nature can pull‌ it.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Or you‌ can just have </grad><grad from=#B98A5E to=#EBD1B0 f=0.8>13‌ hearts</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and‌ yank it‌ out‌ anyway. The stone does not‌ check‌ your references, only your‌ health‌ bar.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#B98A5E to=#B98A5E>Pokes‌ out of‌ the‌ ground in plains, forests‌ and mountains.</grad>
Find a Sword Shrine
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#B98A5E to=#EBD1B0 f=0.6>Sword Shrine</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A‌ tomb‌ full of </grad><grad from=#B98A5E to=#EBD1B0 f=0.8>lost‌ souls</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and, somewhat commonly, the </grad><grad from=#B98A5E to=#EBD1B0 f=0.8>Music‌ Sheet‌ of‌ Ghosts</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Duskroks live‌ nearby. They have </grad><grad from=#B98A5E to=#EBD1B0 f=0.8>150 health</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and they‌ also‌ drop lost souls, so‌ nothing here‌ is a‌ wasted‌ trip.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#B98A5E to=#B98A5E>Scattered‌ across the overworld‌ surface.</grad>
Find a Mausoleum
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#B98A5E to=#EBD1B0 f=0.6>Mausoleum</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A pond‌ of </grad><grad from=#B98A5E to=#EBD1B0 f=0.8>Prism Solution</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>. Standing in‌ it‌ gives Regeneration, and‌ anything‌ cursed you throw in‌ comes‌ out clean.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The only‌ reliable‌ curse‌ remover in‌ the‌ mod, and it is‌ free.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#B98A5E to=#B98A5E>Deep underground, rare.</grad>
Find a Prismatic Pond
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#B98A5E to=#EBD1B0 f=0.6>Prismatic Pond</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A‌ lab that‌ something moved into.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>This is‌ where‌ the </grad><grad from=#B98A5E to=#EBD1B0 f=0.8>Music Sheet of‌ Bolstering</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> lives, and Bolstering‌ adds a‌ level‌ to‌ every other sheet‌ effect‌ you play. It‌ pairs‌ with‌ Everlasting and‌ the pair of‌ them is‌ the endgame‌ of‌ the‌ Ocarina.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#B98A5E to=#B98A5E>Rare, deep underground.</grad>
Find a Infested Laboratory
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#B98A5E to=#EBD1B0 f=0.6>Infested Laboratory</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A‌ chunk of‌ very old stone‌ that does‌ not belong where it is.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Small, easy‌ to miss, and‌ worth a look‌ every‌ time.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#B98A5E to=#B98A5E>Underground.</grad>
Find a Ancient Outcrop
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#B98A5E to=#EBD1B0 f=0.6>Ancient Outcrop</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Worth‌ the walk‌ for‌ one‌ thing: the </grad><grad from=#B98A5E to=#EBD1B0 f=0.8>Music Sheet‌ of Everlasting</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, which stretches‌ every other‌ sheet's duration‌ by </grad><grad from=#B98A5E to=#EBD1B0 f=0.8>1.5x</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>It‌ also‌ turns up‌ in buried‌ treasure, if you would‌ rather fish‌ for it.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#B98A5E to=#B98A5E>Any biome that gets‌ snow.</grad>
Find a Snow Fortress
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#B98A5E to=#EBD1B0 f=0.6>Snow Fortress</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A ranger‌ tower. Somewhat commonly holds‌ the </grad><grad from=#B98A5E to=#EBD1B0 f=0.8>Music‌ Sheet of‌ Incombustibility</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, which‌ is </grad><grad from=#B98A5E to=#EBD1B0 f=0.8>120 seconds</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> of Fire Resistance‌ on‌ demand.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Very handy right‌ before‌ you‌ go anywhere‌ near‌ profanum.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#B98A5E to=#B98A5E>Sticking out of‌ forested ground.</grad>
Find a Fire Lookout Tower
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#B98A5E to=#EBD1B0 f=0.6>Fire Lookout Tower</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The most common‌ Terramity‌ structure by a‌ wide margin.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Somewhat‌ commonly holds‌ the </grad><grad from=#B98A5E to=#EBD1B0 f=0.8>Music‌ Sheet‌ of the‌ Indomitable</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, which‌ is </grad><grad from=#B98A5E to=#EBD1B0 f=0.8>60 seconds</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> of Immunity. Immunity blocks‌ hunger, weakness, wither, poison, slowness, Shadowflame, darkness, blindness, dizzy and‌ Hexed.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#B98A5E to=#B98A5E>Underground, and‌ there are‌ a lot‌ of‌ them.</grad>
Find a Subterranean Shrine
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#B98A5E to=#EBD1B0 f=0.6>Subterranean Shrine</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The Nether‌ holds‌ the smallest set of‌ Terramity‌ structures and the‌ most‌ dangerous‌ ones.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Two of‌ them‌ stack on top‌ of each other in‌ progression: the‌ dungeon gives you‌ the key, the‌ cathedral is‌ the‌ lock.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#E2683B to=#E2683B>Three‌ structures, all of‌ them‌ a bad idea</grad>
Fine, the Nether
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#E2683B to=#FFC0A8 f=0.6>Down There</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Terramity‌ does not‌ just add ores. It‌ rewrites a‌ good chunk of what generates‌ in your‌ world, and three of‌ its‌ structures are‌ the‌ only way to reach‌ three‌ of its bosses.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#A0A0A0 to=#606060>Souls, fairies‌ and the‌ odds‌ and‌ ends moved‌ over to the main‌ Terramity‌ chapter, because none of‌ them were‌ structures.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>This‌ chapter‌ is‌ a map, not‌ a‌ ladder. Nothing here needs‌ doing in order.</grad></shadow>
[gap=5]
[gap=5]
## <grad from=#B98A5E to=#EBD1B0 f=0.6><shadow a=0.3>The two‌ halves</shadow></grad>

- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#B98A5E to=#EBD1B0 f=0.8>Overworld</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> structures, the‌ ones you trip‌ over on‌ the surface‌ and‌ the‌ ones you‌ have‌ to dig for.</grad></shadow>
[gap=3]
- <shadow a=0.3><grad from=#B98A5E to=#EBD1B0 f=0.8>Nether</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> structures, all three‌ of which‌ lead‌ somewhere unpleasant.</grad></shadow>
Back to the metal ladder
<typewriter><grad from=#B98A5E to=#B98A5E>Seventeen structures, and‌ most‌ of‌ them matter</grad>
Show me the map
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#B98A5E to=#EBD1B0 f=0.6>Terramity's World</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A tear‌ in the‌ ground‌ with‌ something wrong‌ underneath‌ it.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Common enough that you‌ will find‌ one‌ on any‌ decent Nether‌ trip, and‌ a‌ reasonable source‌ of chthonic material without‌ diving‌ into a dungeon.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#E2683B to=#E2683B>Common‌ across the‌ Nether.</grad>
Find a Chthonian Breach
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#E2683B to=#FFC0A8 f=0.6>Chthonian Breach</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A long, mean‌ dungeon‌ standing in open water. It‌ is the‌ third‌ boss's front‌ door and‌ it‌ is‌ not a‌ five minute detour.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#B98A5E to=#EBD1B0 f=0.8>Spire Keys</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> are‌ scattered‌ through the spire‌ itself. Take the‌ key to‌ the‌ lock‌ in the basement‌ to‌ call the‌ Trial‌ Guardian.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The‌ spire also‌ holds </grad><grad from=#B98A5E to=#EBD1B0 f=0.8>stygian blood</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> pools and </grad><grad from=#B98A5E to=#EBD1B0 f=0.8>lost‌ souls</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>, and the </grad><grad from=#B98A5E to=#EBD1B0 f=0.8>Music‌ Sheet of [null]</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> shows‌ up‌ here‌ very rarely.</grad></shadow>
{image:customtextures:textures/trialspire.png width:250 height:100 align:center}
<typewriter><grad from=#B98A5E to=#B98A5E>Any‌ ocean, anywhere.</grad>
Find a Trial Spire
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#B98A5E to=#EBD1B0 f=0.6>Trial Spire</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A‌ gnome village‌ with‌ a </grad><grad from=#B98A5E to=#EBD1B0 f=0.8>Gold Gnome Statue</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> in the‌ middle‌ of it.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Right click‌ the‌ statue‌ with a </grad><grad from=#B98A5E to=#EBD1B0 f=0.8>Red‌ Gnome‌ Hat</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> and Gob wakes‌ up. That is the entire‌ trigger‌ for the first‌ boss.</grad></shadow>
{image:customtextures:textures/courtgnome.png width:250 height:100 align:center}
<typewriter><grad from=#B98A5E to=#B98A5E>Only generates‌ in dark‌ forests‌ and‌ swamps.</grad>
Find a Court of Gnomes
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#B98A5E to=#EBD1B0 f=0.6>Court of Gnomes</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Sitting‌ on the‌ bedrock ceiling, which‌ means getting there‌ is half‌ the problem.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>There is an offering‌ pedestal inside. </grad><grad from=#E2683B to=#FFC0A8 f=0.8>Occult‌ Fabric</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> on the pedestal‌ summons </grad><grad from=#E2683B to=#FFC0A8 f=0.8>Circe‌ and Merlin</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The‌ roof‌ is also where </grad><grad from=#E2683B to=#FFC0A8 f=0.8>bedrock black‌ matter‌ ore</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> generates, packed into the‌ top‌ two‌ layers, so bring‌ the‌ Perish Staff when‌ you come back.</grad></shadow>
{image:customtextures:textures/cathedral.png width:250 height:100 align:center}
<typewriter><grad from=#E2683B to=#E2683B>On the‌ roof‌ of the Nether, nowhere‌ else.</grad>
Find a Chthonic Cathedral
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#E2683B to=#FFC0A8 f=0.6>Chthonic Cathedral</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>An‌ abandoned‌ facility that nature took‌ back.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>The </grad><grad from=#B98A5E to=#EBD1B0 f=0.8>Music Sheet‌ of‌ Resourcefulness</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> is here, and‌ that one‌ is‌ worth‌ hunting: it saves‌ ammo every time you‌ reload.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#B98A5E to=#B98A5E>Surface, and‌ one of the‌ rarest things‌ in the‌ mod.</grad>
Find a Overgrown Facility
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#B98A5E to=#EBD1B0 f=0.6>Overgrown Facility</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>A‌ cave‌ pool absolutely packed‌ with‌ fairies, </grad><grad from=#B98A5E to=#EBD1B0 f=0.8>pink</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> ones included.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Bring‌ a‌ lot‌ of empty‌ bottles. This is the‌ single best‌ stop in‌ the‌ overworld‌ and most‌ players walk‌ straight past it.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#B98A5E to=#B98A5E>Underground, and‌ it is‌ full of exactly what it‌ says.</grad>
Find a Fairy Fountain
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#B98A5E to=#EBD1B0 f=0.6>Fairy Fountain</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Suspicious blocks, a brush, and‌ whatever‌ the shrine felt‌ like burying.</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Bring‌ a brush. Leave‌ with‌ something.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#B98A5E to=#B98A5E>On‌ the surface, rare.</grad>
Find a Suspicious Shrine
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#B98A5E to=#EBD1B0 f=0.6>Suspicious Shrine</grad></shadow>
<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Most of‌ what‌ Terramity generates‌ lives‌ here, split‌ between things‌ poking out of‌ the surface‌ and things‌ buried‌ under‌ it.</grad></shadow>

<shadow a=0.3><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7>Surface ones‌ you find‌ by walking. Underground ones‌ you find‌ by mining, or by cheating with‌ a </grad><grad from=#B98A5E to=#EBD1B0 f=0.8>Void Glass</grad><grad from=#FFFFFF to=#C7C7C7> window.</grad></shadow>
<typewriter><grad from=#B98A5E to=#B98A5E>Fourteen‌ structures share one‌ overworld</grad>
Start exploring
<shadow a=0.4><grad from=#B98A5E to=#EBD1B0 f=0.6>Above And Below</grad></shadow>

ftbquests.chapter.the_undergarden.quest1: Slingshot is‌ a‌ very‌ fun weapon‌ added‌ by Undergarden.
Undergarden‌ is a‌ massive dimension mod‌ filled with‌ biomes (They're lowkey ugly) BUT worth exploring!
ftbquests.chapter.the_undergarden.quest5: With blisterbombs you‌ can craft‌ a‌ boomgourd!
ftbquests.chapter.the_undergarden.quest6: In‌ order‌ to enter the Undergarden, you‌ have‌ to create a‌ portal‌ just‌ like nether‌ but‌ with stone bricks!
Instead‌ of lighting it up‌ with‌ a lighter, we need‌ something else, a‌ catalyst!
ftbquests.chapter.the_undergarden.questD: This‌ greataxe with‌ knockback II aand‌ pulsation‌ is fun.
